Do you understand complex business processes, question assumptions and turn real needs into solutions developers can build? Join our product team in Aarhus and help shape the in-house systems supporting global commodity trading, risk management and financial operations!

We are looking for an experienced Senior Business Analyst, who can bridge business stakeholders and our development team. You will get close to the users, understand how the business creates value and manages risk, and translate complex needs into clear, prioritized backlog items. The goal is simple: to ensure that we build the right things, not only build things right.

This is an operational and influential role in a collaborative product team. You will be expected to ask “why”, create clarity, speak up and help the team make pragmatic decisions in a complex domain. You will not be coding, but you have enough technical understanding to discuss services, data and integrations credibly with developers.

Your role and responsibilities

In this role, you will work directly with end users and business stakeholders to understand their processes, pain points and goals. You will constructively question requirements to uncover the real need behind requests and challenge initiatives that do not create sufficient value. Based on these insights, you will map and document business processes, data flows and system-supported capabilities, translating business needs into clear epics, user stories and acceptance criteria that the development team can act on.

In addition, you will:

• Partner closely with the Product Owner and support prioritization based on business value, risk and dependencies.

• Participate actively in refinement and act as the go-to person for business questions during development.

• Maintain the big-picture view of how changes affect services, integrations and downstream processes across the trade lifecycle.

• Use AI tools to accelerate analysis and documentation, while critically reviewing and improving the output.

• Help the team and the business identify practical, responsible ways of applying AI in everyday workflows.

The environment you will join

You will become part of an agile product team, with a closely involved Product Owner and a culture where decisions are made together. There is no ivory tower. We expect colleagues to contribute their perspective, challenge ideas respectfully and take shared ownership of the outcome.

The team builds and develops in-house systems covering the trade lifecycle from capturing derivative trades through risk management to invoicing. The users work within Global Risk Management, and the solutions operate in a service-oriented landscape based on .NET and Azure, with a combination of on-premises infrastructure and Kubernetes.

The role is based at our Aarhus office, where close day-to-day collaboration matters. Depending on business needs, you should also expect occasional visits to Middelfart.

What we are looking for

We imagine that you have several years of experience as a Business Analyst, Business Architect, Product Owner, Functional Consultant or in a comparable role. More importantly, you have repeatedly demonstrated that you can understand complexity and turn it into concrete, value-creating deliverables.

You have demonstrated the ability to understand complex business processes and translate them into clear, actionable deliverables. You are also comfortable writing user stories and acceptance criteria and contributing effectively in agile or Scrum-based product teams.

We also imagine that you bring:

• Practical use of AI tools in daily work, for example to analyze information, draft requirements, summarize stakeholder input or map processes, combined with sound critical judgement.

• Clear communication skills and the ability to bring business and technical stakeholders into alignment

• Ability to align stakeholders constructively, including at senior level

• Sufficient technical understanding to discuss services, data and integrations without needing to be a developer.

• Professional proficiency in English. Danish is an advantage because much of the team’s daily collaboration takes place in Danish.

It will be a strong advantage if you also have:

• Knowledge of commodity or energy trading, derivatives, risk management or financial back-office processes such as trade capture, settlement, invoicing or hedging.

• Experience with ETRM or CTRM systems.

• A background in software development or a hybrid technical/business role before moving closer to the business side.

Who you are

• Curious and motivated to understand how the business makes money and manages risk.

• Pragmatic and able to balance an ideal solution with what creates value now.

• Comfortable expressing an opinion, asking difficult questions and making complex topics understandable.

• Collaborative, accountable and motivated by being part of a product team rather than a separate analysis function.

• Interested in new tools, including AI, and thoughtful about where they genuinely improve quality and speed.

What we offer

At Bunker Holding, you will work in an international business where technology supports global trading and risk management. You will join experienced colleagues in Aarhus, gain direct access to both users and developers, and work with complex systems where your analysis helps shape priorities and solutions

You can expect a collaborative and practical environment, professional development opportunities, pension and health insurance, and flexible working arrangements that support a sustainable work life. Normal support hours are centred around the working day, and any holiday on-call coverage is handled through a rotating arrangement.

Ready to apply?

If this sounds like the challenge you are looking for, we would be happy to hear from you. Please upload your CV and application. We review applications on an ongoing basis and schedule interviews when we identify suitable candidates.

We believe diverse perspectives improve our decisions and solutions. Therefore, we encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every single preference listed above. For any questions about the position, feel free to reach out to Team Lead, Jane Ingildsen at +45 2791 6688.

Bunker Holding

Bunker Holding is a global leader in purchasing, selling and supplying marine fuel and lube oil, while also providing risk management and other vital services to the shipping industry. The company operates through more than 1,600 ports worldwide and is present in 33 countries with 56 offices and more than 1,400 employees.

Bunker Holding is the largest company in USTC, a family-owned group with activities across energy, shipping, logistics, risk management, mobility, IT and sustainable solutions.

Do you enjoy keeping a team moving without getting in the way? Are you the kind of producer who loves making work life easier for your team through process? And are you also quite silly?

We're expanding one of our games and looking for a Senior Producer to help drive new content and features for our players. You'll work very closely with the executive producer and game director, supporting them in setting a clear production plan within time and budget constraints, while making sure the team has everything they need to do their best work.

You'll also be part of a cross-studio producer team where you can exchange ideas, challenge each other, and share knowledge and complementary skills.

**Here's What That Looks Like Day To Day

**

• Implement and refine production processes and tools, shaping how we work and grow as a studio

• Drive the project forward by removing roadblocks and keeping delivery dates realistic

• Facilitate the team’s day-to-day rhythm (stand-ups, planning, reviews, post-mortems)

• Plan updates, roadmaps, and marketing beats together with the leads, and communicate plans clearly to stakeholders

• Manage the project long-term: priorities, scope, timelines, risks, and follow-up

• Take on team and people responsibility, including 1:1s, development reviews, and salary conversations

Last, but not least: There's plenty of room to shape this role to fit you.

**Must-haves

**

• Experience going through at least one full game production cycle

• Experience as a producer on at least one shipped game

• Experience with live service and online games

• Experience working with external stakeholders

• A deep understanding of the game development process

• A strong belief in nurturing team wellbeing because a sustainable pace and motivation directly shape the quality of what ships

• Experience with people management (development talks, hiring, 1:1s) and team production (version control, stand-ups, sprints, reviews)

• You’re ready to tell us where we’re going wrong and help us improve

**What Always Matters To Us At Triband

**We've always believed that games are made by teams, not solo superstars, and good ideas can come from anyone. We love people who bring curiosity, generosity, flexibility, and strong opinions, especially when those opinions come with reasoning, openness, and a willingness to validate ideas properly.

We also care a lot about experimentation. Sometimes the weird idea is not the right fit. Sometimes the weird idea is the entire game! The trick is being able to explore it together, learn from it, and not get too precious when the experience tells us we're wrong.

**Practicalities

**

• We don't offer relocation support or visa sponsorship for this role.

• We work a 37-hour work week, with core hours 10-15, and the freedom to start and finish anywhere between 7 and 18.

• We work on-site at our cozy office in central Copenhagen.

• No crunch. People over deadlines.

• Our working language is English.

**We offer

**

• Silly but ambitious projects, and the chance to work on and impact great games that reach millions of players.

• A playful and ambitious work environment where experimentation is encouraged.

• Friendly and kind colleagues who love making each other laugh as much as making games.

• A professional development budget to invest in your growth.

• Social activities like Friday bars, hobby nights, board game nights, team events, you name it.

• Daily lunch at a local restaurant just a walk across the lakes away, with plant-based options (and soft ice on Thursdays).

• Six weeks of vacation (five standard plus one extra on us).

• Paid parental leave at full salary for the periods covered by state reimbursement.

• Child's first sick day on us, no questions asked.

• Pension plan and private health insurance.

• Endless amounts of coffee.

**WHAT THE TRIBAND?

**Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, which is played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by our mission to make everyone laugh. To do so, we focus on exploring comedy through gameplay. We like to break player expectations, use wonderful music, slick art, and create a quirky atmosphere. We experiment a lot, and it doesn't always work out, but we always learn something.

We put people first and strive to create a safe and creative working environment. We believe that teams, not individuals, make games, and we believe diversity makes for better teams. For these reasons, we look for people who bring new perspectives and will challenge us and our way of doing things.

For more info about Triband, check out: triband.net/about

jobs.occupation: Technical expert in inks & coatings, plastics: Technical Product Specialist or Head of Product Development
jobs.description:
About Octarine

Octarine Bio is a Copenhagen-based biotech company making safe, sustainable, bio-based pigments. Our PurePalette™ platform uses precision fermentation and renewable raw materials to produce colourants that can replace petrochemical and mined pigments.

We are a team of around 15 people, working across pigment manufacturing, formulation and application development, and commercial development. As our pigment manufacturing processes reach full commercial scale, and our first pigment products are now in the hands of customers and partners, we are looking for someone with deep domain expertise in one or more of our core application areas (dyeing, printing, coatings and plastics) to make PurePalette™ work in real industrial applications and turn successful customer trials into lasting commercial products.

The role

You will be the technical owner of the PurePalette™ product range and the link between our lab and our customers. You will translate what the market needs into clear performance targets, work with our scientists to meet them, and make sure our pigment products perform once they reach a customer's processes.

We are looking for an applications expert in inks and coatings, plastics, or both, or in a closely related pigment application field. The title and scope will match your experience:

• Technical Product Specialist if you are earlier in your career and want a role with a lot of room to grow as the company scales.

• Head of Product Development if you have the experience to lead the product and applications function, shape the product roadmap and build a team.

In both cases you will report directly to our Chief Scientific Officer and work closely with our commercial team.

What you will do

Own the product, technically

• Be the technical expert for all PurePalette™ products and the first point of contact for technical questions from customers, partners and colleagues.

• Define the performance and quality parameters customers expect in each application, such as colour strength, dispersibility, heat stability, light and weather fastness, migration, rheology, and wash and rub fastness.

• Plan and coordinate the internal and external testing needed to prove each parameter, and turn the results into clear data packages for customers.

• Own, write and maintain our technical and product documentation, including Safety Data Sheets (SDS), Technical Data Sheets (TDS), Certificates of Analysis (CoA), product specifications and application guides.

Make our pigments work for customers

• Work with customers, distributors and partners to implement PurePalette™ products in their processes, from first lab trial to production run.

• Own the technical side of our partnerships with masterbatchers, ink manufacturers, dyehouses and research institutes. Set up project plans, manage technology transfer between parties, and troubleshoot problems until the product works in the target application.

• Handle technical customer feedback and complaints, find the root cause and feed lessons back into product and process development.

Decide what to develop next

• Identify where bio-based pigments offer real value to end users, and where they can genuinely meet customers' performance expectations.

• Work with Octarine scientists to map which applications our current pigments suit, and which applications we should target with future products.

• Work with our formulation and application scientists to refine formulations (dispersions, masterbatches, inks, dye and print pastes) to meet customer requirements.

• Work with our R&D and process teams to develop and implement strategies that improve pigment performance, for example through stabilisation, surface treatment or particle engineering.

• Benchmark our products against incumbent pigments and competing bio-based alternatives.

Connect technical and commercial

• Act as the bridge between Octarine's technical and commercial teams, translating customer needs into technical requirements and technical results into customer value.

• Join customer meetings, site visits and trade fairs as the technical voice of the company.

• Contribute technical content to sales materials, grant applications and investor discussions, and help capture new inventions for our IP portfolio.

What you bring

Pigment applications are many markets, not one. Printing inks alone span flexo, gravure, offset, screen and digital printing, and each places different demands on a pigment. The end markets differ just as much, from packaging and textiles to toys, consumer goods and coatings, each with its own performance, safety and regulatory requirements.

We need someone who knows this landscape in depth. You should understand the technical and performance requirements of each sub-application and market, judge where our pigments have a realistic and valuable fit, and work with our scientists to develop products that meet those requirements.

Specifically, we are looking for:

• An MSc or PhD in chemistry, polymer or materials science, chemical engineering, colour science or a related field, or equivalent industrial experience.

• Hands-on industrial experience applying pigments or colourants in textiles, inks and coatings, plastics and masterbatch, or a closely related field. For the Head of Product Development level, we expect around 5 or more years, including leading projects or people.

• A practical understanding of pigment dispersion and of how pigment properties such as particle size, surface chemistry and thermal stability affect performance in the final product.

• Experience with colour measurement (spectrophotometry, CIELAB, ΔE) and with standard ISO, EN or ASTM test methods for pigment and application performance.

• Experience writing or maintaining SDS, TDS and CoA documents, and working knowledge of REACH and CLP.

• Experience working directly with customers or external partners on trials, scale-up or technology transfer.

• The ability to explain technical results clearly to scientists, customers and commercial colleagues.

• A structured, self-driven way of working, and comfort with the pace and ambiguity of an early-stage company.

• Fluent written and spoken English.

• The confidence to take full ownership of the role from day one. You will set your own priorities, make decisions within your remit and drive projects to completion without close supervision, keeping the CSO informed rather than waiting for direction.

Nice to have

• Experience in both inks and coatings and plastics.

• Experience with textile dyeing or printing.

• Experience with organic pigments, natural colourants or other bio-based materials.

• Knowledge of food contact and product safety requirements, such as EU 10/2011, the Swiss Ordinance, EuPIA guidelines, EN 71-3 or ZDHC.

• Experience with quality systems such as ISO 9001, or with setting product specifications for a new product.

• An existing network in the European ink, coatings, masterbatch or textile industries.

What we offer

• A central role in bringing a new class of sustainable pigments to market, with real influence over which products we build and how.

• Direct work with the founding team and a short path from idea to decision.

• A small, highly skilled team of scientists across synthetic biology, fermentation, downstream processing, formulation and application.

• For earlier-career candidates, a role that can grow with the company. For senior candidates, the chance to build and lead the product function.

• Real autonomy and ownership of your work, and the chance to make a lasting impact at a fast-growing company developing new materials for industries that urgently need to change.

Practical details

Location: Copenhagen, Denmark. On-site is strongly preferred; hybrid working is possible for the right candidate.

Start date: As soon as possible

Reports to: Chief Scientific Officer

Employment: Full-time, permanent

Travel: Some travel to customers and partners within Europe

Right to work: Applicants must already have the right to live and work in Denmark. We are unfortunately not able to sponsor work visas at this time.

How to apply

Apply with your CV. Please highlight the pigment applications you have worked on and a technical problem you solved in a customer's process.

We review applications on a rolling basis and will fill the position as soon as we find the right person, so we encourage you to apply early.

We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and are happy to answer questions about the role before you apply.

Does it excite you to build the marketing engine for an upcoming obesity and metabolic health launch, and do you have experience with turning brand strategy into integrated, compliant go-to-market plans? If this sounds like you, and you are ready to take on a broad area of responsibilities, then you could be our new colleague.

**Your new position

**As Senior Director, Global Marketing Strategy, you will build and lead the marketing capabilities that bring Zealand Pharma’s medicines to healthcare professionals and patients. The role translates brand strategy into customer engagement, channel, and campaign plans, and creates the foundation for a scalable marketing organization. You will be the commercial voice in building the core brands towards a successful launch.

**We Offer Exciting Responsibilities

**

• Define brand strategy, including positioning, segmentation and brand building to a strong value proposition

• Develop the go-to-market and marketing strategy, translating brand strategy into integrated, multichannel plans

• Build the marketing function, including team structure, processes, and agency and vendor partnerships

• Own marketing planning, budgeting, and performance measurement

• Lead launch-readiness activities for marketing, e.g. campaigns, tools, and customer engagement models

• undefined

• Ensure promotional activities comply with regulatory and internal review requirements, in partnership with Medical Affairs and Legal

• Collaborate with Commercial, Market Access, and the U.S. organization to align execution across markets

**Your profile

**You are a strategic thinker who connects market, HCP and consumer needs into a compelling story. You influence without relying on authority, bring clarity in ambiguity, and enjoy building something new in a growing organization.

• Extensive experience in brand strategy within pharma or biotech, including senior leadership responsibility

• Track record from global or regional launches, ideally in obesity, diabetes, or other metabolic or specialty areas

• Experience with omnichannel and digital engagement strategies for healthcare professionals and patients

• Solid understanding of promotional compliance and review processes

• Experience managing budgets, agencies, and marketing analytics

• Experience working in matrixed, international settings, ideally with alliance or partner models

• Master degree, e.g. life sciences, business. MBA is a plus

• Fluency in English

**Your new team

**You will be a member of the global commercial organization reporting into the Senior Vice President. You will be part of building the area and will work closely with our external partners and with key stakeholders, e.g. Medical Affairs, R&D, Market Access, Alliance Management.

**Let’s bond and be bold

**We have a unique culture, characterized by excellent teamwork and strong engagement across the organization. And we want you to help us strengthen this culture.

Making bonds is at the core of everything we do. From discovering and developing the best new peptide drugs for patients, to engaging with our partners or connecting with each other. We bond through curiosity and playfulness as a team, allowing ourselves to challenge common thinking and drive future innovation. Join us and let’s bond and be bold.

Interested in bonding with us? Then please apply no later than 15 November 2026, or as soon as possible. The applications will be reviewed as they come in. While a cover letter is not required, please include a few sentences in your CV explaining your motivation for applying.

For further information, please contact Senior Vice President Mette Zacho, MZacho@zealandpharma.com .

We are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and welcome applications from all job applicants.

**About Zealand Pharma A/S

**Zealand Pharma A/S (Nasdaq: ZEAL) is a biotechnology company focused on advancing medicines for obesity and metabolic health. Combining more than 25 years of peptide R&D expertise with a proprietary data platform that leverages advanced data-driven and AI/ML approaches, Zealand Pharma aims to lead a new era in obesity and metabolic health. To date, more than ten Zealand Pharma-invented drug candidates have entered clinical development, of which two products have reached the market and three candidates are in late-stage development. The Company has collaborations with global pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners for research, development, and commercialization. Founded in 1998, Zealand Pharma is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, with a U.S. presence in Boston, Massachusetts. Learn more at www.zealandpharma.com.

Sophion Bioscience is looking for an ambitious, customer-focused Vice President of Research & Development to lead and further develop our R&D organization.

This is a central leadership role with responsibility for Sophion’s technology strategy, product development execution, engineering capabilities, and R&D organization. You will ensure that priorities, resources, budgets, and development activities are managed with clarity and discipline, enabling us to deliver high-quality products that create measurable value for customers.

You will report to the CEO and as a member of the Senior Leadership Team, you will contribute to Sophion’s overall direction and continued growth.

About the role

As VP R&D, you will lead and develop Sophion’s multidisciplinary R&D organization, setting a clear direction and creating the structure, leadership, and ways of working needed to deliver on our ambitions.

You will translate product and portfolio priorities into clear R&D priorities, roadmaps, and resource commitments, ensuring alignment and accountability across the organization. Working closely with Innovation, Market & Product Management, you will ensure R&D brings strong judgment and execution discipline to the development of differentiated and commercially successful products.

A key part of your mandate will be to strengthen the R&D organization and its leadership. You will develop leaders, build effective teams, establish clear governance and decision-making, and create a culture of collaboration, ownership, and delivery.

You will attract, develop, and retain talented people and ensure that R&D continues to grow in capability, maturity, and performance.

About Us

Since 2000 Sophion Bioscience has pioneered Automated Patch Clamping for ion channel research. Today, we specialize in automated solutions for pre-clinical life sciences.

We work closely with academic institutions, contract research organizations, and leading biotech and pharmaceutical companies to create effective assays for screening and characterization. Our solutions empower the study of drug targets and candidates at the bench, reducing development time in discovery and reducing risk in clinical trials.

Through the continued development of our Automated Patch Clamp portfolio (QPatch & Qube) and our new Organ on a Chip platform (Ethica), we offer uncompromised data quality in a user-friendly environment, from assay setup to advanced data analysis.

We are driven by curiosity, teamwork, and a genuine passion for helping scientists succeed. We work in an open and collaborative environment where people share knowledge freely, support each other across roles and borders, and take pride in doing things properly. Our culture is informal, trusting, and grounded in respect — for colleagues, customers, and the science we enable. Even as we grow globally, we remain a company where people feel welcome, included, and able to make a meaningful impact.

We are headquartered in Denmark and have subsidiaries in the United States, Japan, and China.

What You'll Do

• Set and execute Sophion’s R&D and technology strategy in alignment with the company’s overall direction and priorities.

• Lead and develop the R&D organization, including its structure, leadership capabilities, ways of working, and competencies.

• Clearly communicate R&D priorities, progress, risks, and trade-offs across Sophion and to the Leadership Team and Board.

• Own the R&D budget and ensure resources are allocated to the activities that create the greatest strategic and customer value.

• Drive portfolio and resource management, translating product priorities into actionable development roadmaps and execution commitments while balancing short- and long-term priorities.

• Ensure customer needs inform development decisions by driving broad R&D engagement with the market, key opinion leaders, and key accounts.

• Strengthen development governance, decision-making, accountability, milestones, KPIs, and transparent reporting.

• Drive continuous improvement in product quality, performance, reliability, and maintainability.

• Work closely with Innovation, Market & Product Management to assess opportunities and convert agreed priorities into robust and commercially viable products.

• Maintain appropriate quality and compliance standards across R&D activities.

• Build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders

Who You Are

You are a strategic and hands-on R&D leader who can turn complex scientific and technical opportunities into high-quality products.

You bring clarity to complex situations and combine strong judgment with disciplined execution. You build strong teams, set clear priorities, use resources effectively, and deliver commitments.

You are engaging and decisive, and you build trust through transparency, communication, sound judgment, and consistent follow-through. You are comfortable moving between strategic questions and operational details without losing sight of R&D and company priorities.

We expect that you:

• Master’s degree in science, engineering, technology, or a related field.

• Proven R&D leadership experience in complex, multidisciplinary product development, leading leaders and sizeable teams of specialized engineers and scientists across hardware, software, firmware & bioscience.

• Strong communicator with the ability to set the agenda, shape strategy, and communicate in a clear direction across the organization and with customers and investors.

• Track record of taking products from concept to successful global market use.

• Experience from life science tools, diagnostics, MedTech, laboratory instrumentation, or similar quality-critical environments is preferred.

• Demonstrated ability to improve execution, prioritization, organizational capability, and product quality.

• Strong strategic, customer, communication, and decision-making skills, with the ability to work effectively across functions and deliver results.

• Strong interpersonal, negotiation, and problem-solving skills, with professional English proficiency.

How to Apply

Please apply via LinkedIn.

If you have questions about the role, you are welcome to contact Helene Fife on hef@Sophion.com

Start Date

As soon as possible.

We review applications on an ongoing basis and close the recruitment process once we have found the right candidate. If this opportunity excites you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

_Please do not contact us or apply if you are a recruiter, consultant or outsourcing company.

**Deliver with focus. Scale with intent 🚀

**Are you a delivery leader who knows how to guide enterprise customers through complex set-ups without over-engineering the journey? Do you care deeply about building scalable, repeatable SaaS delivery rather than one-off custom projects?

At Performativ, we’re building the infrastructure layer for modern wealth management. As our Engagement Manager, you’ll lead the enterprise rollout of our SaaS platform helping customers onboard successfully through structured delivery, clear communication, and lightweight technical engagement.

This is not a professional services consulting role. You won’t be buried in endless customer-specific code or heavy customizations. Instead, you’ll work cross-functionally to help customers adopt our product the right way: cleanly, securely, and in line with platform best practices so they can scale on top of us, not around us.

**What You Will Do

**

• Own enterprise set-up programs end to end (kick-off through go-live and hyper-care) against an agreed plan and scope (Statement of Work).

• Enable customers to integrate Performativ via standard platform patterns (APIs, SSO, configuration) without custom buildouts, working with product and engineering to flag gaps early and advocate for scalable paths.

• Own plan, scope, and change control, keeping scope tied to contract and change visible and decided rather than quietly absorbed, and support the Technical Program Lead on requirements, design documents, and acceptance-criteria sign-off.

• Run customer communication, cadence, and governance with reporting that keeps meetings short, and manage risk, dependency, and issue tracking (including customer-side).

• Lead a clean handover to Customer Success at go-live or hyper-care exit, including train-the-trainer sessions and supporting materials.

• Represent the program in internal capacity and exception reviews, bringing requests the plan cannot absorb back as options rather than committing on the spot.

• Build repeatable playbooks, documentation, and artefacts that make the next program faster. You will be measured on this, not only on your own delivery.

**How You Will Work

**You will run multiple programs at once, in a delivery pod alongside the Technical Program Lead, Integration Engineers, Data Migration Specialists, and Product Engineers. None report to you. Rather you get things done through clarity and relationships, not authority. You will report to the COO. This is an in-office role based at our Copenhagen office.

**What We're Looking For

**

• 7+ years in program or engagement management, consulting, product management, or another delivery-facing role, with a track record of leading complex, multi-stakeholder implementations end to end.

• Comfort being firm with customers on scope and timeline while keeping the relationship stronger for it.

• Any industry background welcome. Experience with enterprise customers (banks, asset managers, regulated industries), balancing urgency against long-term maintainability highly advantageous.

• Structured and highly organized, producing written plans, governance cadences, and reporting that stakeholders can act on.

• Broad technical literacy across enterprise SaaS delivery: API-based integrations, SSO and security configuration, and data migration and mapping, including enough SQL to read and question a mapping. You do not build the integration, but you understand it well enough to scope it, question it, and know when something does not add up.

• Ability to build working fluency in the customer's business domain fast: within 90 days, able to discuss topics such as advice and suitability workflows and customer reporting without a subject-matter expert in the room.

• ITIL Foundation, PMP or PRINCE2 Certification would be beneficial.

**Technical Fluency

**

• You’re not, necessarily, a developer, but you’re comfortable with APIs, data structures, auth flows (OAuth/SAML), and deployment models.

• You can dive into logs, payloads, and basic SQL or Python when needed to unblock yourself or a customer - but you prioritize scalable fixes over tactical workarounds.

• You advocate for platform-aligned solutions, not special cases.

**What This Role Is Not

**This role sits in operations, not engineering or commercial, and is project-based: once delivery is complete, you roll on to the next engagement. As a SaaS provider, we do not build bespoke software; delivery works within the bounds of the product.

**We Can Offer

**

• Trust and responsibility to shape how Performativ delivers for its largest customers.

• A competitive salary and benefits package.

• A fast-growing, VC-backed fintech scaleup, working alongside professionals from leading institutions (Goldman Sachs, McKinsey, BCG, Amazon and others).

• Career acceleration through professional development and leadership opportunities.

jobs.description:
Unsolicited application Warehouse employee – Night shift (part time)

We are not currently looking for warehouse employees for night shifts, but you are very welcome to send us an unsolicited application.

**Can you work at night, perform in a busy environment, do you have experience from packing or from a warehouse and do you have a good physique?

About the job**

As a warehouse employee you are an important part of the business. You will pack products for our customers from refrigerated, dry, green and frost areas. We use pick-by-voice, and you will be walking around the warehouse, picking and packing orders throughout your entire shift. This requires that you have a good physique.

The packing department consists of more than 40 different nationalities and since it is a multicultural area it requires that you speak and understand English.

Work hours

Nemlig operates 365 days a year, and for this position you will be working two fixed night shifts during the weekend.

We are offering a flexible part-time contract of 15 -25 hours per week, consisting of 2 night shifts of 7.5 hours.  Your average working hours will be between 15 and 25 hours per week, calculated over a planned period of at least 4 weeks. Usually, you will be scheduled for 15 hours per week, spread across 2 working days Saturday and Sunday night. During busy periods, we may change your work schedule one month in advance, increasing your working hours by up to 25 hours per week. It is therefore important that you are flexible during busy periods, e.g. Christmas and New Years.

Your working hours will be:

• Saturday night / Sunday morning: 22:00 Saturday to 06:00 Sunday

Celare Quantum Communications is a Danish high-tech quantum technology company with a mission to radically improve cybersecurity and enable trusted global data sharing.

Our core product is Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution (CV-QKD), a unique, cutting-edge technology born from years of university research. This technology enables quantum-secure key exchange for protecting sensitive data across critical infrastructure.

Celare partners with national and international governments, telecom operators, data centers, banks, defense ministries, and leading academic institutions. Over the past year, our team has launched commercial pilot deployments of our technology.

The Celare Team

We are a highly specialized and ambitious team of quantum engineers, serial entrepreneurs, mathematicians, software engineers, IC and FPGA designers, and specialists in lasers, RF, and electronics.

Based in Copenhagen, we combine deep academic expertise with practical experience in launching complex, high-impact technology products.

The Role

In this role, you will get a unique opportunity to work at the cutting edge of quantum technology development. You will join our FPGA/ASIC team and work directly with FPGA design for high-speed data processing, testbench development, and the early stages of our ASIC development.

As part of a small and agile organization, you will contribute across the full product lifecycle — from early architectural decisions and prototyping to production and large-scale deployment. You will work both in collaboration with our team and independently as a specialist, sharing knowledge across disciplines.

This is a hands-on role with real responsibility and influence. It offers the chance to work in a dynamic, international, multilingual, and multicultural team with direct connections to academic research and state-of-the-art technologies.

The role is based on-site at our Copenhagen headquarters.

Responsibilities

• Contributing to the early stages of ASIC design, from architecture to RTL

• Designing and implementing high-speed data processing systems on FPGAs

• Developing self-checking testbenches and verification environments for FPGA/ASIC designs

• Developing and integrating IP cores

• Participating in system-level integration

• Bringing up, testing, and debugging hardware in the lab

Qualifications

• MSc in electrical engineering or similar

• 5+ years of hands-on FPGA/ASIC design experience, including IP core integration, FPGA timing closure, and floorplanning

• Proficiency in Verilog/SystemVerilog (or VHDL)

• Experience with ASIC-grade verification, e.g., UVM, constrained-random and coverage-driven testing, SystemVerilog Assertions, and bit-accurate reference models

• Experience implementing high-speed data processing on complex FPGAs (e.g., AMD/Xilinx UltraScale+) and their toolchains

• Experience with high-speed interfaces such as PCIe, JESD204B/C, and multi-gigabit transceivers

• Proficiency in scripting, e.g., Tcl, Bash, and Python

• Good understanding of high-speed signal integrity

Nice to have

• Experience with ASIC design flows, e.g., synthesis, static timing analysis, DFT, and gate-level simulation

• Experience with high-speed board design (schematic design, PCB layout, integration, and power delivery)

We Offer

This full-time position offers the opportunity to build and shape the future of quantum communication in collaboration with an experienced and dynamic team. We provide individual growth plans aligned with your personal preferences and motivation. We offer competitive compensation commensurate with qualifications and experience.

Contact

For more information, or to apply, send an email to jobs@celare-quantum.com with the subject line “FPGA/ASIC Design Engineer”.

jobs.occupation: Laser Engineer – High-Power Spectral Beam Combining
jobs.description:
The Mission: Build the Next Generation of SBC Systems

Ibsen Photonics develops Spectral Beam Combining (SBC) modules for high-power laser architectures, based on our in-house transmission gratings. We are looking for a Laser Engineer to join the High-Power Beam Combining team and contribute across design, assembly, and experimental optimisation of these modules — working closely with colleagues and international partners.

What you will do

• Design and assemble compact SBC modules based on Ibsen's transmission gratings, accounting for optical beam paths, thermal effects, and mechanical constraints

• Optimise optical alignment, mechanical stability, and thermal management at high power loads in iterative design–experiment–optimise cycles

• Characterise beam quality during power scaling, including M², wavefront sensing, and spectral analysis

• Support sourcing of optical and mechanical components and the transition from experimental prototypes to scalable, volume-ready designs

• Collaborate with internal teams and international partners, including occasional overseas visits for joint prototyping and testing

What you bring

You are a proactive problem-solver who thrives in a "build-test-learn" environment.

Ideally, you possess

• MSc or PhD in optics, photonics, laser physics, or a related field

• Documented laboratory experience with high-power optics and/or lasers

• Knowledge of high-power-capable optical design practices, including thermal lensing, runaway effects, and their mitigation, as well as Gaussian optics and beam propagation

• Knowledge of opto-mechanical design practices for high-power devices

• Hands-on experience with precise free-space and/or fibre optical alignment and experimental troubleshooting

• Experience with beam quality measurement and analysis

• Professional proficiency in English

Nice to have

• Experience with SBC or CBC techniques

• Mechanical design of tight-tolerance devices and familiarity with mechanical CAD

• Experience transitioning prototypes toward volume production

• Proficiency in optical simulation tools (e.g. Zemax)

Security and export control: This position is subject to defence-related export control and security requirements. You must be able to obtain the required Danish security clearance.

Why join Ibsen Photonics?

• Visible Impact: Your will work directly on the core technology and design behind next generation of SBC modules, with real autonomy over how you solve the tasks you are given. Your results will carry through from lab prototypes to finished products supplied to international customers

• Working culture: A supportive, flat organisation with short decision paths, open knowledge sharing, and a healthy work-life balance.

Ready to make a difference?

Submit your CV and cover letter via the link. We recruit as soon as possible and keep the position open until filled.

jobs.occupation: IT Product Owner for Scientific Solutions
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about finding technology solutions for drug development, so our scientists can focus on the science?

Do you have experience with IT product discovery and continuous development?

If so, now is your chance to join Ascendis Pharma as our new IT Product Owner for the Scientific Solutions team.

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients’ lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs in our Endocrinology Rare Disease and Oncology portfolios. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

Our context

This position is based in our Global IT organization. Over the past five years, we have built and matured a product-driven organization with a strong focus on product management and lifecycle thinking. Our long-lived teams take ownership from problem discovery through solution delivery and continuous improvement, ensuring that we address real business needs.

Our structure combines clear leadership intent with empowered teams. Each team member is supported by a People Leader focused on development and a Functional Leader guiding strategy and delivery. We foster autonomy and self-organization to enable fast flow, clear accountability, and minimal dependencies.

The Scientific Solutions team supports Product Innovation, Product Development, CMC, Nonclinical Development, and Global Medical business functions. Across these areas, the common objective is to identify and develop technology solutions that enable pharmaceutical product innovation.

We are seeking a passionate IT Product Owner to join our growing Scientific Solutions team. As a key member of Global IT, you will play a crucial role in shaping coherent technology offerings across applications, tools, and data for a broad scientific user group.

This is an exciting opportunity to work in a fast-paced environment and collaborate with cross-functional, global teams to achieve extraordinary results.

You will report to Jakob Monajemzadeh Thrane, People Leader in Global IT, and, from a functional perspective to Ivanna Rosendal, Global Head of Digitalization. The position is based at our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Ensure that a broad scientific user group has coherent technology offerings across applications, tools, and data that evolve with their needs.

• Communicate closely and frequently with users and leadership teams to create a clear, shared understanding of the most important needs and priorities.

• Translate business needs into technology deliverables and coordinate with relevant IT teams to ensure prioritization and completion.

• Prioritize and manage the Scientific Solutions team’s backlog and actively help remove impediments to technology delivery.

• Collaborate closely with other teams across Global IT to manage dependencies and align priorities.

Qualifications and skills:

You hold a relevant academic degree, at minimum a master’s degree, and have 5+ years of experience in a related role within a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or comparable scientific environment.

Furthermore, you have:

• A background that enables you to understand the translational stage of drug development.

• Hands-on experience managing and developing a technology product portfolio.

• Experience with product discovery and decision facilitation.

• Experience driving the successful delivery of digital products and platforms.

• Experience working in an agile team and continuously improving ways of working.

Key competencies:

You are a strong team player, innovative and curious, and have a can-do attitude.

You possess an entrepreneurial mindset and can thrive in an informal, open environment where innovation and change are key.

To succeed in this role, we also expect you to be a proactive self-starter who can identify opportunities for improvement and take initiative to move things forward.

Our team needs to scale to support the ever-growing demands, so we need team members who both can act pragmatically, and solution orientated for the short term, and at the same time are able to think long-term to ensure what we do today can grow to support us in the future.

Travel: 10-25 days per year

Office: Tuborg Boulevard 12, 2900 Hellerup

Apply now!

We evaluate applications as they are received, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Please note that we conduct interviews on a rolling basis and reserve the right to remove the job posting at any time.

To ensure your application is reviewed, please submit it through the specified platform. Applications sent by email or through other channels will not be evaluated.

For more details about the position or the company, please contact Jakob Monajemzadeh Thrane at jmt@ascendispharma.com or Ivanna Rosendal at imr@ascendispharma.com.

You can learn more about Ascendis Pharma by visiting www.ascendispharma.com.

Applications must be submitted in English and will be treated confidentially.

A note to recruiters

We do not allow external search-party solicitation. Presentation of candidates without written permission from the Ascendis Pharma HR team, specifically a Talent Acquisition Partner or Human Resources Director, is not allowed. If this occurs, your ownership of these candidates will not be acknowledged.

We’re looking for a product engineer to help us build better tools for legal research. You’ll work mainly on the backend, with a say in what we build and responsibility for taking it from an early idea to something customers use every day. That includes asking whether we’re solving the right problem, deciding what’s worth shipping first, and knowing when something needs more time.

About Pandektes

Our mission is to rebuild legal research from the ground up. Lawyers still lose countless hours to fragmented sources, outdated systems, and databases that fight them at every turn. We're building the largest AI-powered legal database in the world to make that friction disappear.

We're a team of 40+ based in our Copenhagen HQ, Zurich, London, and Hamburg. We’re a small team with high trust and flat structure. We move fast, argue our positions, and ship. If your input is good, it gets implemented - often within hours, not sprints.

We have has raised more than €4M, including a €2.9M seed round (Feb 2025) led by People Ventures, Interface Capital, and a strong bench of angels. We already serve 400+ customers across Denmark, Germany, and Switzerland, and we're just getting started.

What we value

“How fast can we ship this?” comes up a lot at Pandektes. So does “we should take our time with this one.”

Knowing which question to ask is a big part of being an engineer here.

Knowing when it’s good enough

We like getting things into customers’ hands quickly. That means making trade-offs, questioning scope, and accepting when something is good enough for now. There’s usually another approach to explore or another prompt to try. At some point, you have to ship.

We use AI throughout our development process. AI code reviews, feature flags, and remote coding agents running end-to-end tests help us move quickly with confidence. Deciding what to build, what to check, and when it’s ready still takes judgment.

We value people who can find a smaller version worth shipping, explain the trade-offs, and follow through once customers start using it.

Knowing when to slow down

Some decisions deserve more time. Getting them right makes everything that follows easier. Getting them wrong means paying for the same mistake repeatedly.

Our default is to move quickly, so slowing down takes discipline. Sometimes it means pushing back when the rest of us want to get something out. We value someone who can explain why the extra work matters, challenge an approach, and help us decide where to spend our time.

You’ll have room to make those calls here, and teammates who will question them. We expect you to do the same for us.

Make time to experiment

We enjoy trying things before we know whether they’ll work. A new tool, a different way to use an agent, an idea that might turn out to be useless. Finding out is part of the work.

Once a month, we get together to demo our setups, show what we’re experimenting with, and share what we’ve learned. Sometimes we invite people from outside the team to show us how they work. Those sessions have changed how we build software.

We value curiosity and the generosity to bring other people along. If you find something useful, show us. If an experiment fails, we’d like to hear about that too.

We try to watch this video once a month to keep this value top of mind.

The experience you’ll bring

You’ve built and operated backend systems that real customers depend on. You can work through questions about data, APIs, performance, and security, and explain the consequences of your decisions.

Our stack includes TypeScript, NestJS, GraphQL, Postgres, and Prisma. We also work with OpenAI and Turbopuffer. Experience with these tools is useful; we’re especially interested in what you’ve built with them and the decisions you made along the way.

You enjoy working through a product problem while it’s still taking shape. You ask questions, share unfinished work, and help decide what’s worth building. You’re comfortable taking a feature from those early conversations through implementation, testing, and delivery.

What we offer

You’ll join at a point where there’s still a lot to shape. We offer competitive pay and equity so you can share in the success you help create.

We are usually office based but we all work from home time to time. You’ll have your own Pleo card for the tools and work expenses you need, plus 25 vacation days a year, public holidays, and paid parental leave when your family grows.

We also make time to get together away from our usual work. Our last team trip was to Barcelona, and we’d love to have you along for the next one.

Pandektes is an equal opportunity employer

We believe diverse teams build better products and stronger teams. We embrace and encourage people from all backgrounds to apply regardless of race/ethnicity, colour, religion, nationality, gender, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, socio-economic status, culture or beliefs.

Legal professionals should be able to stand behind every answer. We build the foundation for that: verified legal data, complete across time and traceable to its source, with research tools built for confident legal judgment. Our vision is clear: to be the leading platform for legal information retrieval, enabling in-depth and accurate legal knowledge in a fast, efficient and user-friendly way using artificial intelligence.

jobs.occupation: Tenure track Assistant Professor/Associate Professor Position in the field of Sustainable Design and Manufacturing
jobs.employer_name: Technical Sciences - Institut for Mekanik og Produ
jobs.description:
The Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering (MPE) at Aarhus University is consolidating its research and teaching activities within the field of Design and Manufacturing and invites applications for a Tenure Track Assistant Professor/Associate Professor within the field of design and manufacturing from July 1st, 2027 or as soon as possible.

The MPE Department seeks an innovative and visionary researcher capable of establishing and leading an internationally recognized research group and delivering research-based teaching at the Bachelor, Master & PhD levels. The chosen candidate is expected to establish effective and visible research programs, develop local and international research collaborations, attract external funding, and contribute to our mechanical engineering bachelor and master programs with teaching at an international level

We welcome candidates with interdisciplinary research backgrounds who can help realize our vision of creating lasting impact by guiding the shift toward a resilient and sustainable industry, society, and planet.

For this open position, we are seeking candidates to advance research in resilient and sustainable design of products and manufacturing solutions.

We prefer candidates that can demonstrate the potential for industrial application of their research. The candidate should bridge existing fields in the section and department, and we encourage applicants to address potential synergies in our educational programs and research activities.

The selected candidate will be required to teach relevant courses in the MPE educational program at the B.Sc., M.Sc., and PhD levels of the Mechanical and Production Engineering programs. 

Expected start date 
July 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible.

To meet expectations in this role, we expect the candidate to fulfill the following requirements:
To meet expectations in this role, we expect the candidate to fulfill the following requirements:
- PhD or equivalent in Mechanical or Production Engineering or a closely related subject area.
- Substantial experience conducting high-quality research in the field of Sustainable Design and Manufacturing with publications in leading international journals that match career stage.
- Familiarity with experimental, computational, or theoretical research method.
- Interest in and prior experience with interdisciplinary collaboration across engineering disciplines and with industry is desired.
- For the position as associate professor, the applicants should, in addition, have:
- Documented teaching experience and a clear commitment to teaching and advancing mechanical engineering courses within the field of Sustainable Design and Manufacturing, from introductory undergraduate instruction through master’s and PhD-level study
- Documented record of self-directed research leadership, external funding acquisition, supervision of PhD students, and teaching and course development at university level.
- The candidate should have proficient communication skills in English.
- It is an advantage if the candidate has the ability or is willing to develop their communication skills in Danish.

Who we are
The engineering field in Aarhus University is evolving with a rapid growth in student population, major research initiatives as well as through the establishment of a number of new physical facilities in the city center of Aarhus. We have comprehensive plans for increased activities in research and education, as well as public and industrial cooperation. The Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering within the Faculty of Technical Sciences has cooperation with universities and advisory service providers in more than 20 countries. The engineering field at Aarhus University is well established with extensive research activities, over 700 mechanical engineering students and a long tradition of industrial cooperation that we wish to extend significantly.

What we offer 
The department offers:
- research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment 
- an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
- a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
- a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
- a workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance 

Place of work and area of employment 
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Mechanical and Production Engineering, Katrinebjergvej 89, DK-8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

Contact information
For more information about the position contact Deputy Head of Department for Research Charles Møller (charles@mpe.au.dk / +45 61677786) or Head of Section Ramin Aghababaei ( ra@mpe.au.dk / +45 93508956)

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than January 4th 2027.

Technical Sciences Tenure Track
Aarhus University offers talented scientists from around the world attractive career perspectives via the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme. Highly qualified candidates are appointed as Assistant Professors for a period of six years with the prospect of performance- based advancement to a tenured Associate Professorship. 

The aim of the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme is to:

• attract outstanding talented individuals that are competitive at an international level
• to promote the early development of independent research success early in the career of scientists
• to create transparency in the academic career path
As part of the tenure track position, the candidate is offered:

• access to research infrastructure
• capability development, including postgraduate teacher training
• a mentoring programme
• support to develop scientific networks and to secure interdisciplinary research at the highest level
As part of the Aarhus University Tenure Track Programme, the University carries out a mid-way evaluation to review the progress of the tenure track candidate after three years, according to the same criteria used in the final tenure review. The final tenure review is conducted after five and a half years. If the review is positive, the candidate will be offered a tenured position as Associate Professor at Aarhus University.

Please refer to the tenure track guidelines for the tenure review criteria and for the tenure review process.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation. 

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

The Environmental Microbiology Section at the Department of Environmental Science is currently looking for a VIP at the Associate Professor level who works on microbial degradation of pollutants in different environments who can provide novel dimensions, interpretation and project opportunities within contaminant microbial ecology. The new Associate Professor should also be able to interact and collaborate both within the department but also across the faculty with special emphasis on microbial ecology in industrial water.

1 April 2027 or as soon possible.

This is a permanent position.

Job description

We are especially interested in individuals whose research integrates microbial ecology under different redox potentials and thus can understand contaminant degradation processes in all elements of natural and engineered water systems from groundwater sediment to wastewater. Research focused on understanding the link between different omics techniques is particularly relevant here.

Applicants should have demonstrated experience in microbial ecology under different redox conditions and have a strong background in molecular microbiology and method development. Experience in defining and executing projects that involve water stakeholders is essential. Proficiency in a range of laboratory techniques, such as anaerobic culturing, pure culture characterization, antibiotic resistance genes and of metagenomic and meta-transcriptomic analysis, is desirable to fully utilize the analytical platforms available at Aarhus University (Risø campus).

The successful candidate will have a strong record of academic achievements at the international level and show potential to develop collaborative research within the university and with external partners. A demonstrated ability to attract external funding for advisory work and/or research from national and/or international funding agencies, public water administrative agencies or private companies is expected.

Responsibilities include:

- Apply for funding and conduct both basic and applied research, attract research-based advisory work for public agencies and industry

- Ensuring collaboration across the different sections at ENVS and different Departments to develop a research group in redox microbial ecology

- Supervision of PhD and Master students

- Participate and contribute to administration and committees within the department

Your profile

•   A PhD in Microbial Ecology or related fields

•   Demonstration of collaboration with environmental engineers through collaborative projects and/or common publications

•   Experience in supervision of PhD and Master students

•   Proficiency in a range of laboratory techniques, such as anaerobic incubation techniques, DNA /RNA extraction and sequencing methods, and PCR quantification is required to fully utilize the analytical platforms available at Aarhus University

•   Strong record of academic achievements at the international level within redox microbial ecology.

•   A demonstrated ability to attract external funding from national and/or international funding agencies is expected.

•   Show strong potential to develop collaborative research within the university and with external partners.

•   A collaborative mindset and strong problem-solving skills are a requirement.

•   Motivated by working in a highly collaborative and inclusive environment.

The Department of Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary department under the Faculty of Technical Sciences at Aarhus University. The expertise of the Department ranges from physics, chemistry, microbiology, social science, geography, economics, to policy analysis. Basic as well as applied research are conducted on some of the major challenges facing society, such as pollution and pollution control mechanisms, management of land, soil, water, air and biodiversity, protection of ecosystem services, and climate change. Advisory services within these areas are offered to ministries and other authorities. Currently, about 140 staff, postdocs and PhD students are working at the department. A day in your life with us

In Goods Handout, we are committed to giving customers the best possible experience when collecting goods ordered either in-store or online. We are confident working independently, while also knowing when to involve and support one another when needed. As part of our team, you will enjoy a varied range of tasks. Your responsibilities will include:

• Managing sold items that are unexpectedly out of stock.

• Scanning and quality-checking orders to ensure customers receive the correct products in good condition.

• Performing other ad hoc tasks as required.

Why we will love you

At IKEA, we are passionate about creating great customer experiences. That is why we are looking for someone who is passionate about delivering excellent customer service and is not afraid to take a hands-on approach. Your background may be varied; what matters most is that you enjoy meeting many people every day and are comfortable with physical work.

We also value that you:

• Enjoys meeting different people every day and makes customers feel welcome and cared for.

• Thrive in a role with routine tasks.

• Have strong logical thinking skills and attention to detail.

• Work independently and demonstrate discipline in your daily work.

• Stays calm in a busy environment and is comfortable making decisions that help both customers and the team.

• Speaks English and basic Danish.

Together, we work hard to create a great experience for every customer who visits us, and we collaborate closely with colleagues across the store every day.

This means you'll have the opportunity to work with many different people, build valuable relationships, and become part of a team where we support each other, share responsibilities, and succeed together. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can be themselves and feel welcome for who they are.

We will provide you with the training and support you need to feel confident, comfortable, and well-equipped to succeed in your role.

Questions and support? Let's connect!

Please note that we only accept applications submitted through our recruitment system and do not accept applications sent by email.

Your models might start in Python. Their impact goes far beyond it.

Your career in data science might only just be getting started. At NORDEN, you will apply it to real logistics challenges involving vessels, ports, terminals, weather and cargo flows.

At NORDEN, moving cargo from A to B involves vessels, ports, terminals, weather, cargo flows and countless operational constraints. Understanding how all those pieces interact can make a real difference to the decisions we make and at the end our base margin.

As our new Data Scientist in Maritime Logistics, you will turn that complexity into models we can explore, test and learn from, helping us make better operational and commercial decisions.

You do not need years of experience or deep shipping knowledge. What matters is a strong foundation in Python and supply chains and the curiosity to apply it to the real world.

Why this role?

Because you get to take problems that exist in the real world and build models that help us understand what could happen next.

You might be modelling how vessels move through a logistics network, exploring the capacity of a terminal or testing what happens when weather, congestion or operational constraints change. Other times, you could be looking at historical data, improving an existing model or helping colleagues understand what different scenarios could mean commercially and operationally.

A central part of your role will be translating complex logistics systems into simulations that allow us to ask better questions before decisions are made in the real world.

You will work closely with commercial and operational colleagues while learning from experienced colleagues within analytics and shipping. Our broader Quantitative Analytics environment works with Python and technologies including Prefect, Docker and Azure and you will also gain practical experience developing solutions and visualisations using Power BI.

What you will be doing

You will work where shipping, logistics and data science meet. Helping us continuously improve how we work with simulation, optimisation, analytics and software development.

To be more specific you will:

• Design and develop simulation models of supply chains and maritime logistics operations.

• Use discrete-event simulation and agent-based modelling to represent vessels, terminals, ports and other parts of complex logistics systems.

• Analyse logistics networks and explore opportunities to improve capacity, throughput, utilisation and operational efficiency.

• Use historical and operational data to calibrate, validate and continuously improve your models.

• Build analytical tools that allow colleagues to explore scenarios and understand their operational and commercial implications.

• Develop robust analytical models and simulation solutions in Python.

• Create visualisations that make complex outputs easier to understand and use.

What you bring

There is no need to understand every aspect of shipping or every modelling method from day one. What matters is that you have a good analytical foundation, an understanding of supply chains and logistics and the curiosity to keep learning.

Qualification we are looking for:

• Have 0–3 years of relevant professional experience.

• Hold a degree in Supply Chain Management and Logistics, industrial engineering, operations research or another relevant quantitative field.

• Have a good foundation in Python and are comfortable writing structured, maintainable analytical code.

• Are fluent in English, our working language.

• Are eligible to work in Denmark.

What matters just as much is how you work with people. You are curious about how complex operations actually work, you ask questions before jumping to the model and you can explain what your analysis means to colleagues who may never open a line of Python themselves.

Application

Please upload your motivation letter, resume and relevant diplomas via our website as soon as possible and no later than 22 November 2026. Your motivation letter helps us understand what drives you, why you are interested in the role, and how your skills and experiences could contribute to the team. We are especially interested in your motivation and transferable skills, not a recap of your CV. It is your opportunity to tell us the story behind your application.

We review and interview candidates on an ongoing basis.

We will do our best to get back to you at least within ten working days after the application deadline, 22 November 2026.

In NORDEN we value a range of perspectives, educational backgrounds and professional experience and encourages all qualified candidates to apply.

We are a global provider of ocean- based freight services for bulk and project cargo of all sizes. We integrate freight solutions with port logistics, helping our customers optimise and decarbonise supply chains. We provide tailored solutions built on flexibility, reliability, and intelligence.

Our agile business model ensures stability by continuously adapting our fleet to market developments and customer needs.

Founded in 1871, NORDEN is one of Denmark’s oldest internationally operating shipping companies. Incorporated in Denmark, we are listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen as part of the OMX Nordic Large Cap index.

With offices across 6 continents, we are a truly integrated part of global trade.
