jobs.occupation: Professor / Associate Professor / Senior Researcher taking lead in Catchment and Freshwater Ecosystem sciences
jobs.description:
Are you an engaged, leading scientist of international standing, with deep expertise in the research of catchments and freshwater ecosystems, and excellent science leadership skills? Do you have the scientific vision to guide the strategic direction for a nationally and internationally recognized research community working with catchments, wetlands, lakes, streams and nature-based solutions?

The Department of Ecoscience at Aarhus University invites applications for a full-time permanent scientific position (Full Professor, Associate Professor, or Senior Researcher) in the Catchment science and Freshwater Ecology (CaFE) focus area. We are looking for a scientist who enjoys taking lead and working strategically with organizational impact covering the range of research areas in CaFE.

Expected start date and duration of employment

This is a permanent position from 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible.

Job description

The position centers around research and research based advisory in catchment processes and freshwater ecosystems – including wetlands, streams and lakes and the landscapes like forests, agricultural areas etc. that surround them.  We expect the candidates to have expertise and track record with one or more of the key thematic areas:

• Hydrology and the retention and transport of nutrients and hazardous substances

• Biogeochemical processes and emissions of greenhouse gases from land and water bodies, including interactions with carbon and nutrient dynamics

• Freshwater ecology and the links between abiotic and biotic processes, including ecosystem functioning, biodiversity, and responses to human pressures and climate change

• Nature-based solutions and ecosystem restoration to strengthen biodiversity and resilience and reduce nutrient loss, limit greenhouse gas emissions and regulate water flow in the landscape

• Combining long-term monitoring data with novel research using laboratory, mesocosm and field experiments, in situ sensor data and catchment- and ecosystem modelling

At Department of Ecoscience, all scientific staff in general are expected to contribute to external income generation, dissemination of knowledge, and talent development. Your specific scientific responsibilities may also include:

• Taking the lead on the development and implementation of the CaFE focus area strategy as part of the Department’s strategy, Ecoscience 2030 – including formulating concrete goals and action plans for implementation in dialogue with colleagues and the Department’s management

• Setting the direction and fostering a strong and inclusive research environment across the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management, the Section for Freshwater Ecology and the Centre for Nature-based Solutions

• Bringing our research and knowledge to Danish ministries and agencies as well as to other relevant national, European and international decision makers through science-based advice, making an impact for the society around us

• Promoting innovation within the focus area and wider department by fostering use of new and/or novel technologies through closer dialogue and interaction with other sections/focus area within the department and across the faculty

• Supporting the scientific development and career paths of colleagues in the focus area

Your profile

We are looking for a scientist with a strong research track record as well as documented experience with science-based advisory work and leadership of research staff. You have expertise within catchment science and freshwater ecology, previous experience working in interdisciplinary teams and from broad sectoral collaborations. Applicants must hold a PhD in hydrology, limnology, freshwater ecology, biogeochemistry, environmental science, physical geography, environmental engineering or a closely related discipline. The level of appointment (Full Professor, Associate Professor or Senior Researcher) will be determined based on qualifications.

We value in particular:

• Excellent leadership experience from similar research environments; e.g., leading larger research groups and taking responsibility for strategic development of larger units (academic citizenship)

• Skills in strategic scientific coordination, strategy development, project management, and building research networks

• An established international network, collaborative skills and relationships within catchment science and/or freshwater ecology and nature-based solutions

• Documented experience in securing and leading externally funded research projects

• Documented experience with science-based advisory work and engagement with authorities and other stakeholders

Excellent written and spoken English; Strong Danish language skills are an advantage.

Who we are

The Department of Ecoscience, with approximately 300 employees in Aarhus and Roskilde, is one of Denmark's leading research environments in applied ecology, spanning terrestrial, freshwater, marine, and Arctic ecosystems. We conduct both fundamental and applied research and deliver Science-based advisory services to authorities in Denmark and Greenland. Our work is grounded in long-term monitoring, field-based data collection, and advanced modelling, and we pride ourselves on a research culture characterized by high scientific integrity, strong interdisciplinary collaboration, and societal relevance. Our values are impact, professionalism, curiosity, collaboration and trust.

CaFE is the department's focus area for catchment science and freshwater ecology, integrating the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management, the Section for Freshwater Ecology and the Centre for Nature-based Solutions. We are around 80 research and technical employees working to generate the data and knowledge that qualify decision-making on conservation and recovery of deteriorated wetlands and inland waters. Our vision is to maintain and expand our position as the key national focal point for applied research and modelling within catchment processes and freshwater ecosystem dynamics, helping authorities monitor, manage and mitigate human impacts on wetlands and freshwaters.

We combine long-term monitoring data with experimental approaches and modelling, and we have the strongest national scientific environment within modelling of nutrient transport, biogeochemical processes in wetlands, experimental freshwater ecology, lake ecosystem modelling and lake restoration. Key infrastructure includes a series of living labs in constructed wetlands, lakes, ponds and streams, including the semi-field mesocosm lake experiments at Lemming that have been running for more than 30 years.

Find out more about our current strategy, departmental values and more here: https://ecos.au.dk/en/about-us/au-ecoscience-our-strategy

What we offer

• A full-time permanent scientific position with an internationally competitive research environment and access to unique long-term datasets and world-class field and semi-field infrastructure

• A central role in shaping the scientific direction of CaFE, contributing actively to the focus area strategy under Ecoscience 2030 and beyond

• An interdisciplinary and dynamic working environment across catchment, freshwater, terrestrial, marine and Arctic research

• Highly engaged, motivated and positive colleagues and an innovative and dynamic working environment, where culture and values are important

• A working environment characterized by high scientific standards, trust, and well-being

• Close, trust-based relationships with Danish ministries and agencies and strong national and international research networks

• Access to professional support for international researchers and their families relocating to Denmark

For candidates with the right qualifications and experience in strategic research leadership, a temporary role as Deputy Head of Department with responsibility for the CaFE focus area of the Department of Ecoscience will be possible. This role includes participation in the Department’s management group. Further education/competence building in leadership will be offered. Contact the Head of Department (details below) for a more detailed description of this role.

Place of work and area of employment

The place of work is AU Campus Aarhus, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information

For further information about the position, please contact Head of Department Mikkel Tamstorf (mpt@ecos.au.dk; +45 53 57 50 44).

Application procedure

Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment.

Formalities and salary range

Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

• Collaborating with Finance departments, HR Business Partners and other colleagues across JYSK countries

WHAT SHOULD YOU BRING

You enjoy working with data and getting the details right, but you are also curious about the bigger picture behind the numbers. You take responsibility for your tasks, ask questions when something does not add up and enjoy finding better ways of doing things.

You do not need many years of experience. What matters to us is that you bring a strong analytical mindset, curiosity and a willingness to learn and contribute.

We are looking for a new colleague who:

• Has 0-3 years of relevant experience working with data, numbers or analytics, preferably in an international organisation

• Has an educational background within Finance, Economics, Organisation or a related field

• Works in a structured and analytical way with an eye for detail

• Understands why high-quality master data matters when making business decisions

• Is an advanced Excel user, while experience with SAP and BI tools is an advantage

• Takes initiative and enjoys working both independently and together with others

• Communicates confidently with colleagues across functions, countries and cultures

• Is fluent in written and spoken English

Additional Information

IS THIS YOUR NEXT OPPORTUNITY? Apply today!

If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact Sustainability & Total Rewards Director, Ditte Revsbæk Hansen at +45 3050 8125.

We kindly ask you to only attach your CV. With us, there is no need to write a traditional cover letter when applying for a job.

Instead, when you click “I’m interested/Apply”, you will have the option to write a brief message to the hiring team. If you wish, you can use this space to share your motivation for applying or highlight anything else you feel is relevant.

ABOUT US

We believe our employees are key to our success. That is why we strive to offer development and possibilities of growing and finding new challenges within JYSK. Since our founder, Lars Larsen, opened his first store in Denmark in 1979, JYSK has expanded our global presence with stores and web shops in countries around the world.

Our three fundamental JYSK Values – Tradesman, Colleague and Corporate Spirit – express the behaviour and attitude that we can expect from each other. We trust each other, and we believe in Empowerment and freedom with responsibility. We also take pride in rewarding engagement and a great effort among our employees. With the right attitude, opportunities abound in JYSK.

JYSK wants to include everyone, no matter the age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, and experience. Together, we secure our inclusive culture that encourages, supports, and celebrates the diverse voices of our employees. Because a great mix of minds, talents and unique personalities makes us a stronger team.

For more information, please visit our career page.

jobs.occupation: Business Controller, Netcompanys Group Finance team
jobs.description:
**Job Description

**We are seeking a Business Controller with strong motivation for the FP&A area for our Group Finance team. You are newly graduated or have 1-3 years of experience and will play a central role in ensuring timely and accurate management reporting, as well as in-depth analyses of our business and financial KPIs. _You will be part of a dynamic team where cross-functional collaboration and close interaction with a wide range of stakeholders are an integral part of everyday work.

_**Responsibilities

**You will join a high-performing and collaborative team where you will have plenty of opportunities to share ideas, learn from colleagues, and grow professionally. Working closely with the Head of Group FP&A and Forecasting, you will take ownership of key aspects of the monthly financial reporting process for senior leaders with global responsibilities. Your role will include monitoring business area performance, analyzing financial results, and preparing presentations.

In addition to responsibility for your own areas, you will also have a broad scope of engagement, where collaboration with other Shared Service departments in the business is an essential part. This position will give you a unique insight into the company's financial value drivers and an understanding of which financial parameters drive a business.

Your responsibilites will typically include:

• Conduct business analyses.

• Comment on monthly reports for your areas.

• Contribute to continuous improvement of the monthly reporting process.

• Participate with your own areas of responsibility in the development of our system structure.

• Actively participate in the budgeting and forecasting process.

**About You

**As a person, you are motivated by working with both complex and operational tasks, and you possess the ability to communicate across the organization. You have a proactive mindset and strong business acumen, combined with excellent analytical skills. You take initiative, identify opportunities for improvement, and are motivated by contributing to the development of the organization. With a keen eye for detail and a strong focus on quality, you take pride in delivering accurate results and meeting deadlines in a structured and reliable manner.

To succeed in this role, you:

• Are newly graduated or at the beginning of your career within a Cand.Merc. (Master of Science in Business and Economics), for example Cand.Merc.Fir, Cand.Merc.Asc, Cand.Merc.Aef., or similar education.

• Have experience working in Excel and processing large volumes of data.

• Are initiative-taking and are keen to contribute to improving and developing processes. At the same time, you have an eye for detail and work in a structured manner.

• Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken) is a must.

**Continue developing with us

**At Netcompany, we focus on your personal and professional development.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will guide you through your development and help you achieve your goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague helps ensure the well-being of each employee and provides you with concrete insights into the many different career opportunities as you build your experience.

**Join an inclusive community

**At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand and build a network early in your career.

**Send us your application

_All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

_We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment. Our recruitment processes are based on individual merit. If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support during the interview process, please email our recruiters at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com for assistance.

jobs.occupation: Lead Portfolio Manager to Support the Green Energy Transition
jobs.description:
Nordic RCC is a fast-developing company providing regional power system planning data and security analysis to support the national Transmission System Operators of Finland, Norway, Sweden and Denmark - to ensure the efficient operation of the Nordic Power System and high security of power supply at any time, with a vision of green transition by developing the relevant tools and data.

Right now, we are looking for a Lead Portfolio Manager who likes making a difference and supporting our journey of growth and organizational maturity.

**Job Description

**As a Lead Portfolio Manager, you will join a team of skilled colleagues and contribute to Nordic RCC ambitious goals of green transition together with our owners in the 4 Nordic countries.

The Portfolio team is sitting in the PMO organization, together with Nordic Project Support team and the local project management team. You will report directly to the Head of PMO and have a close collaboration with the other Senior Portfolio Manager, the local project management group and the manager of the Nordic Project Support team as well as the leadership team and Finance.

**Responsibilities

**Your tasks will include:

Portfolio management

• Drive continuous optimization of the Nordic RCC project portfolio with a focus on efficiency and strategic alignment.

• Lead financial budgeting and long-term planning in close collaboration with Finance, Experts, Project Manager and Team Leads to provide estimates for resource allocation both short- and long-term.

• Develop and deliver monthly portfolio reporting, including dependency tracking, to the leadership team and relevant stakeholders to provide an overview of critical deadlines and potential risks.

• Develop and deliver portfolio recommendation for Leadership team and Head of PMO

**Stakeholder Collaboration & Coordination

**

• Foster collaboration between internal and external stakeholders to enhance efficiency and ensure continuous project execution.

• Act as the central point of contact for project-related inquiries from local project managers and teams.

• Maintain a comprehensive overview of project dependencies and support departments in addressing organizational challenges related to products, processes, and resources.

**Governance & Best Practices

**

• Own and maintain the project Stage-Gate model, including governance structures and project management guidance.

• Ensure best practices are documented and prepare evidence for future audits.

• Drive continuous improvement by identifying inefficiencies, standardizing processes, and enhancing project governance within the PMO.

**Tools & Processes

**

• Oversee portfolio and resource management processes and tools, ensuring they support strategic decision-making and operational efficiency.

**Qualifications

**

• Hold a master’s degree in economics, engineering or a related field.

• Are proficient in English, both written and spoken. Additional languages are a plus.

• Exhibit strong problem-solving skills and the ability to make data-driven decisions.

• Value teamwork and have a collaborative mindset.

• Respectful of agreements, deadlines, other people’s time and ideas, and listening to customer needs.

• Structured in your work and approach to tasks, working in an orderly manner.

• Strong interpersonal skills

• Advanced Excel and data analysis skills, preferably combined with programming experience

**Requirements

**

• Have significant experience (more than 5-10 years) as a Project Portfolio Manager within an IT organisation, if possible a combination with knowledge from European renewable energy sector

• You bring a strong financial background and analytical mindset, enabling you to lead long-term planning and budgeting in close collaboration with Finance. Your financial insights make you a trusted advisor to the leadership team.

• You like to prepare and update management reports, presentations and follow up on activities.

• You like to gain and share knowledge/experience of various portfolio methods and processes.

• You have experience with both portfolio management and project management

**Employment conditions

**You will join a company of competent, diverse, and enthusiastic colleagues. We are currently more than 23 nationalities with more than 30% women (striving to improve this balance) and all ages.

Your daily workplace will be in our newly furnished office premises in Copenhagen Towers, Ørestad. We are offering workplace flexibility to ensure a healthy work-life balance including the possibility for working from home some of your worktime.

Our values of fellowship, curiosity, respect, and transparency have been defined by all employees. They identify how we behave and shape the way we work together, and we expect you to see yourself in them.

Note that as part of the recruitment process, the candidate must undergo a satisfactory background check. The position is also conditioned upon a national security clearance. Both will be facilitated by Nordic RCC. You can read more on security clearance here. Please also note that the process includes that any spouse, registered partner, cohabitant, steady partner, co-resident, child over 18 living at home and parent with the same address as the candidate must also consent to be examined.

**Application deadline and contact information

**Please apply online as soon as possible (in English) and no later than 15 November 2026. We may conduct interviews on a continuous basis.

To ensure a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly request that you do not include photographs in your CVs or application materials.

A cover letter is not required, but we kindly ask you to include a few sentences in your CV explaining why you are interested in the position. Applications are only accepted through our online recruitment system.

Link to apply: https://www.globesearch.dk/en/jobs/4463b01e-b1c7-4674-b81f-4b2cb44ef5df

Are you an experienced climate and restoration leader ready to shape strategy and turn it into practical results? Do you enjoy developing services, building partnerships and bringing international teams together around shared goals? If so, this role could be the right fit for you.

What You Can Expect

Preferred by Nature is looking for a Director of Climate and Restoration to lead our Climate and Restoration Programme within the Sustainability Certification division and coordinate climate and restoration work across our Advisory, Certification and Projects divisions.

Reporting to the Sustainability Certification Director, you will combine strategic and technical leadership with programme management, service development and external engagement. Our certification programme currently covers carbon project validation and verification, ecosystem restoration services, and verification of organisational and product carbon footprints. You will help this portfolio evolve in response to climate science, standards, regulation and market needs.

You will also lead our Climate Impact initiative, translating our ambition to build a strong portfolio of mitigation and adaptation services by 2028 into coordinated workplans and measurable progress.

Working with us is never routine, so in your first year you can expect the following areas to be central to your work.

• Lead the Climate and Restoration Programme, ensuring effective service delivery and progress towards financial and impact targets.

• Shape organisation-wide priorities for climate and restoration, aligning services, projects and expertise across divisions and regions.

• Develop services and delivery approaches that respond to stakeholder needs and create meaningful environmental and social impact.

• Oversee the systems, tools, templates and technical guidance needed for accreditation and credible service delivery.

• Build strategic relationships with clients, companies, NGOs, governments, donors, producers and assurance schemes.

• Identify and pursue business development, partnership and fundraising opportunities.

• Represent Preferred by Nature in conferences, technical networks, industry initiatives and other external forums.

• Lead and develop your team through clear priorities, capacity planning, regular feedback and professional development.

• Contribute to strategic planning, programme budgets, financial monitoring and reporting.

Your first year with us:

Within Three Months, You Will

• Develop a clear understanding of our climate and restoration portfolio, team capabilities, accreditation requirements and current commitments.

• Build working relationships with colleagues across Certification, Advisory, Projects and regional teams, alongside key external stakeholders.

• Review the Climate Impact roadmap and identify priorities, dependencies and opportunities for coordinated action.

Within six months, you will:

• Translate agreed strategic priorities into workplans with clear responsibilities, resource needs and progress measures.

• Work with relevant teams to advance priority service development, partnership and market engagement opportunities.

• Establish regular programme reviews covering delivery quality, financial performance, impact and team capacity.

• Put development priorities and training plans in place for your team.

Within twelve months, you will:

• Demonstrate progress against the agreed Climate Impact workplan and programme objectives.

• Have advanced priority services or partnerships that strengthen Preferred by Nature’s climate and restoration portfolio.

• Strengthen coordination across divisions, with clear ownership and effective use of technical expertise.

• Provide recommendations for the next planning cycle based on programme results, market developments and lessons learned.

Important that you:

• Have at least 10 years of relevant professional experience, including substantial experience in senior leadership, programme development, stakeholder engagement and climate or restoration services.

• Bring deep knowledge of climate mitigation, carbon markets, ecosystem restoration and related policy, market and regulatory developments.

• Have a proven ability to set strategic direction and lead complex initiatives across multiple teams and stakeholder groups.

• Can build alignment and deliver results in an international organisation where colleagues work across different functions and reporting lines.

• Have experience developing strategic partnerships and identifying opportunities that support organisational impact and growth.

• Bring professional credibility in the climate, carbon, restoration or wider sustainability sector, including experience representing an organisation in senior external forums.

• Understand business development and fundraising, and have experience contributing to budgets and financial management.

• Can lead and develop people, support teams through change and encourage collaboration, learning and accountability.

• Combine an entrepreneurial approach with practical judgement and a focus on measurable results.

• Share Preferred by Nature’s commitment to positive environmental and social impact.

Would also be great, but not necessary, if you:

• Have worked across several areas of our current portfolio, such as carbon project validation and verification, ecosystem restoration, and organisational or product carbon footprints.

• Have experience connecting assurance services, advisory work and project delivery within a shared organisational strategy.

If this sounds like you, we would love to hear from you!

What Sets Us Apart

• Global work culture

• High degree of flexibility – remote work, work from home.

• An in-depth onboarding and professional training that prepares you with the right skills and knowledge to thrive in this role.

• Excellent opportunities for growth and professional development

• Potential future international travel opportunities

• A friendly, international team of colleagues, with a pleasant work environment

• Start with 20 days of vacation leave per year

Preferred by Nature

Preferred by Nature is a non-profit, mission-driven organisation that works for sustainable land management and climate-friendly solutions. We develop practical solutions to drive positive impacts in production landscapes and supply chains, supporting better land management and business practices that benefit people, nature and the climate.

How To Apply

If you feel you meet the requirements of the role, please submit your application, including salary expectations, via the application form below. Application pre-screening will be conducted during the application period.

Preferred by Nature wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

**The Impact You'll Make

**As a Senior Data Engineer - AI & Databricks , you will help shape how AI is adopted across Danfoss Climate Solutions, especially within our global sales organization.

Working as part of a global team of data, analytics, and AI professionals, you will build and evolve a trusted, scalable, and well-governed Databricks platform that enables sales teams across multiple regions and functions to turn data into actionable insights. Your work will support use cases such as sales forecasting, pipeline visibility, and customer insights, helping teams make faster, data-driven decisions.

By ensuring the platform is secure, high-quality, and continuously improving, you will enable reliable data products and Generative AI solutions that drive business value. Working closely with data engineers, analysts, product owners, and business stakeholders, you will help establish best practices and scale AI adoption across the organization.

Success in this role means delivering trusted, AI-ready data products that strengthen governance, accelerate AI adoption, and support better business decisions.

**What You’ll Be Doing

**

• Own and improve Databricks governance, including Unity Catalog, data access, security, and data quality

• Design and maintain scalable data architecture, ensuring best practices across data models, tables, and pipelines

• Enhance Genie spaces (AI-powered knowledge tools) by improving content, entity matching, and answer quality for end users

• Partner with cross-functional teams to enable adoption of data products and AI solutions that support data-driven sales decisions

• Evaluate and implement new Databricks and AI capabilities to improve platform performance and deliver measurable business value

**What We're Looking For

**

• Experience with Databricks or similar cloud data platforms (e.g., Snowflake, Azure Synapse), including Unity Catalog and data governance practices

• Strong SQL and Python skills, with hands-on experience building scalable data models and modern ETL pipelines

• Proven ability to design and manage data platforms that enable analytics or AI use cases in a business environment

• Experience working with cross-functional stakeholders, translating data and AI capabilities into practical business solutions

• Fluent in English, with strong communication skills and a proactive interest in applying emerging AI technologies

**What You'll Get From Us

**

• Shape how AI is applied across global sales teams, driving measurable improvements in forecasting, pipeline visibility, and customer insights

• Work hands-on with Databricks, Unity Catalog, and Generative AI to build solutions used across multiple markets

• Influence how data and AI solutions are scaled globally, working with diverse teams and stakeholders

• Grow in a collaborative and international environment that supports continuous learning, innovation, and career development

• A competitive compensation package and flexible hybrid working model, with access to global opportunities

**Ready to Make a Difference?

**If you’re excited about building data platforms that power real-world AI applications and drive business decisions, we’d love to hear from you. Apply now and explore how your work can shape the future of AI at Danfoss.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or other protected category.

Want to build valuable business experience alongside your studies?

As a Student Assistant in the Supply Chain team at CRH Denmark, you will have the opportunity to work with data analysis, suppliers, tenders, and contract management. You will become part of an international company where you gain hands-on experience, take ownership of your own tasks, and collaborate with stakeholders across the organization.

The Role

You will support larger sourcing activities and contract management initiatives across CRH Denmark. Through analysis, reporting, and documentation, you will contribute to structured procurement processes, stronger decision-making, and reduced commercial risk.

You will collaborate with functions such as Category Management, Strategic Sourcing, Legal, Finance, Logistics, Operations, and HSEQ. In doing so, you will help translate business needs and category strategies into competitive agreements and measurable value.

Key Responsibilities

• Support sourcing and tender activities, including collecting quotations and comparing supplier solutions.

• Contribute to supplier onboarding, maintenance of supplier data, and follow-up on deliveries and supplier performance.

• Manage contract documentation, procurement data, and other procurement-related records.

• Prepare reports, dashboards, and analyses covering spend, savings, KPIs, and supplier performance.

• Assist with process mapping, improvement initiatives, and the development of templates and frameworks within procurement and supply chain.

Who Are You?

You are analytical and structured, with strong attention to detail while maintaining an understanding of the broader business context. You are curious about procurement and supply chain management and motivated by turning data into actionable insights.

You take ownership of your responsibilities, work independently, and enjoy collaborating across different functions. We do not expect you to know everything from day one, but we do value a proactive mindset and a willingness to learn.

We Imagine That You:

• Are currently pursuing an HD, Bachelor's, or Master's degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Procurement, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.

• Possess strong analytical capabilities and an interest in commercial topics, procurement, and supplier management.

• Have solid Excel skills and an interest in tools such as Power BI, TARGIT, ERP systems, or other data analytics platforms.

• Are proficient in Microsoft Word and PowerPoint and can present data and conclusions in a clear and structured manner.

• Communicate professionally in both Danish and English, verbally and in writing.

How Do You Succeed?

During your first months, you build a solid understanding of our procurement and supply chain processes. You are able to independently manage defined analysis, reporting, and documentation tasks while contributing to a stronger data foundation for the team's decision-making.

In the longer term, you succeed by creating structure and momentum in your work, delivering reliable analyses, and helping transform data into tangible improvements. At the same time, you contribute to greater quality and transparency in the management of tenders, suppliers, and contracts.

The Team

You will become part of CRH Denmark's Supply Chain organization, where we are constantly striving to raise the bar. We rarely accept "the way we've always done it" or standard solutions if there is a better alternative.

The team works proactively across the entire CRH Denmark organization and internationally to remove barriers in our value chain and mitigate disruptions across our supply chain.

Meet Your New Manager, Ulrik

I believe the best results are created through trust, collaboration, and a shared commitment to learning and improving. I encourage curiosity and new ideas, and I see mistakes as a natural and valuable part of developing new skills, improving processes, and driving innovation through a data-driven mindset.

As a Student Assistant, I don't expect you to have all the answers from day one. What matters most is that you're eager to learn, take initiative, ask questions, and gradually take ownership of your responsibilities. I hope you'll bring your own perspective, challenge us with fresh ideas, and contribute to the team's development as you grow in the role.

My role is to provide direction, sparring, and support so that you can succeed, deliver results, develop your skills, and take the next step in your career. I value open and honest dialogue, where we challenge each other, learn along the way, and turn good ideas into action and results.

What We Offer

• A relevant student job with meaningful responsibilities and real business impact.

• Practical experience in procurement, supply chain management, and contract management.

• Opportunities to work with Excel, Power BI, TARGIT, and ERP-based data.

• Collaboration with a broad range of business functions and subject matter experts.

• The opportunity to participate in projects across CRH Denmark.

• Flexibility in planning your working hours to accommodate your studies.

Application Material

Please submit your resume and include a short profile telling us about your studies, your areas of interest, and why this opportunity appeals to you.

Are you passionate about? Do you have experience within Procure to Pay and automation?

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients' lives. • Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities in a dynamic international environment

Key competencies:

You are a strong team player, analytical, and have a can-do attitude.

Travel: 5-10days per year.

Office: Denmark, Tuborg Boulevard 12, 2900 Hellerup

Apply now.

processes and applications.

**Suggested candidate profile

**Ambu – a visionary and international workplace where your efforts matter

•

A Salesforce Application or System Architect certification, or similar

LYDER DET SOM NOGET FOR DIG?

Så tøv ikke med at kontakte os og sende dit CV- vi har brug for dig!

English Version

Weisleder Nedrivning is looking for reliable, motivated demolition workers to join their growing team. Candidates should be physically fit, hands-on, flexible, and able to work independently as well as in a team. Experience in demolition and environmental remediation is preferred. The company offers varied tasks, a good working environment, opportunities for professional development, and competitive pay based on qualifications. Immediate start is possible, and applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

About Driversnote

Driversnote is a profitable, product-led SaaS company based in Copenhagen that helps over 4.5 million users simplify mileage tracking, with paying customers in 100+ countries. Our core product is a freemium mobile app, often paired with our iBeacon hardware for precise, automated mileage logging, and backed by a powerful web platform.

We’re a close-knit team of 50 working together across design, mobile and web development, marketing, support, sales and customer success. We’ve quadrupled our ARR in the last three years by staying focused on delivering real value to our users, and we’re now expanding from B2C into B2B, building advanced features for teams.

Our Customer Success and Support team is locally anchored in Denmark, Canada and Australia. Customers get help in their own time zone from people who know their market, its rules and how its businesses work.

The role

As Customer Success Manager for EMEA, you own a portfolio of our larger business customers and make sure they get real value from Driversnote, renew, and grow.

This is an outcome-led role, not a usage-monitoring one. Teams today can build their own tracking or buy a system that includes it, so we win by helping customers save money, stay compliant and run their mileage process with less effort. You’ll be the person who makes that happen for your accounts.

Success looks like this after your first year:

• 
Your accounts renew, and you know why the few that leave did

• 
New accounts are live and in use within weeks, not months

• 
Your accounts grow in licences and use more of what we offer

• 
Customers see you as a trusted adviser on mileage, reimbursement and compliance, and Driversnote is built into how they work, from their mileage policy to their payroll and AI tools

What you’ll do

• 
Own retention and renewals. Manage renewals for your accounts from start to finish, spot risk early and act on it.

• 
Get new accounts live. Run onboarding for new teams, with kickoffs for admins, managers and drivers, so the first year sets them up for success.

• 
Grow your accounts. Find expansion opportunities where it makes sense, help teams roll out to more drivers and pass qualified leads to Sales.

• 
Lead outcome-focused reviews. Run annual and quarterly business reviews built around what customers achieve, not just how much they use the app.

• 
Be the expert. Advise customers on mileage reimbursement policy, tax compliance and audit-readiness in your markets.

• 
Get Driversnote deeper into their processes. Help customers improve how they handle mileage end to end: shaping their mileage policy, connecting Driversnote to payroll, finance and AI tools, and removing manual steps, so we become part of how they work, not just an app they use.

• 
Help shape new services. Work with us as we build new offers, such as fleet mileage reports, CO2 reporting and compliance checks.

• 
Keep the data clean. Use HubSpot, health scores and AI tools to manage your portfolio, and log why customers leave so we can learn from it.

• 
Be the customer’s voice. Share what you hear with Product, Sales and Support to improve the product.

What we’re looking for

• 
A few years’ experience in customer success, account management or implementation, ideally in B2B SaaS

• 
Experience owning renewals or a revenue target, or helping customers get live with a new system

• 
Native or near-native English, written and spoken, since many of our customers are in the UK

• 
A commercial mindset: you can turn a customer’s goals into a reason to renew and grow

• 
Comfortable with data, CRM tools and AI; you use numbers to spot risk and show value

• 
A real interest in using AI to create more value, not just to work faster. We take AI seriously here, not as a buzzword: you’ll use and help shape the AI agents and workflows our team relies on every day

• 
Clear, warm communication with everyone from drivers to finance directors

• 
The role is based in our Copenhagen office, and you need a valid permit to work in Denmark

Nice to have

• 
Experience with expansion and upsell in existing accounts

• 
Additional languages are a plus

• 
Knowledge of mileage reimbursement, fleet management, payroll or tax compliance

• 
Experience with HubSpot

This role is probably not for you if…

• 
You want to stay at a strategic distance. This is a hands-on role: you’ll run onboardings, dig into data, fix problems and talk to drivers as well as finance directors.

• 
You only want large accounts. Your portfolio will be a mix of smaller teams and large accounts, and you need to enjoy both.

• 
You’re looking for enterprise sales. We don’t do long, complex corporate sales cycles. If large enterprise selling is what drives you, this isn’t the right fit.

What we offer

• 
Ownership from day one: a high-impact role where you own our B2B customers in the EMEA region.

• 
Shape how we do it: help build the B2B success motion for an established, profitable company.

• 
People to learn from: work with a team of highly experienced entrepreneurs and tech people, across Denmark, Canada and Australia.

• 
Growth: a clear career path in Customer Success, with specialisations as our services grow.

• 
Balance: a healthy work-life balance.

• 
Location and benefits: our Copenhagen office, pension and a learning budget.

We work in a relaxed environment in new offices near the Meatpacking District. Every day there’s a tasty, freshly cooked lunch (with a vegetarian option) and great coffee. We also have cosy Friday drinks and great events, from our running club and gaming nights to our epic Christmas and summer parties.

How to apply

Fill out an application here

We review applications and respond to candidates on an ongoing basis, so apply soon. We aim for a start date of 1 December or 1 January, depending on your availability, but finding the right fit matters more to us than a deadline. Expect a case during the interview process: it represents the kind of work you’ll do with us.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Role Overview

The High School Psychologist / Social-Emotional Counsellor is a member of the Student Support Team and shares responsibility for student wellbeing, inclusion and mental health across the High School. The role provides direct counselling, psychological support, consultation, and system-level guidance to students, families and staff, with particular attention to students who are socially, emotionally or psychologically vulnerable. Working hours and days are flexible and can be arranged to fit your existing schedule. You have the freedom to allocate your working hours across the week in a way that suits your availability while meeting the needs of students and the school.

Key Responsibilities

• 
Provide individual social-emotional counselling to students aged 15–19, supporting their mental health, resilience, relationships and academic wellbeing.

• 
Design and implement preventive and systemic interventions at class and year-group levels to promote student wellbeing and positive group dynamics.

• 
Develop, implement and review individual student support plans in alignment with the IB Access and Inclusion Policy.

• 
Collaborate with the student wellbeing team, student support staff, teachers and parents to coordinate appropriate support.

• 
Guide students and families through the Danish public and private healthcare and youth support systems, including PPR, specialist clinics and pathways to diagnostic assessment.

• 
Prepare professional referrals and supporting documentation for external assessments, including neuropsychological or psychiatric evaluations, within the scope of professional competence.

• 
Follow safeguarding, confidentiality and data protection requirements; identify students requiring specialist intervention and coordinate appropriate follow-up and support.

Qualifications and Experience

• 
Relevant qualifications and training in psychology, counselling or social-emotional support. A qualification as a psychologist, including assessment and diagnosis, is preferred; demonstrated expertise in social-emotional counselling will also be considered.

• 
Knowledge of the Danish healthcare and youth support systems, including PPR.

• 
Experience with psychological screening and assessment tools such as WISC, WAIS, BASC, and BRIEF is an advantage.

• 
Experience working within the International Baccalaureate (IB) system is desirable but not required.

Position Details

• 
Reports to: High School Principal / Programme Principal

• 
Works closely with: the Learning Support Team, Student Wellbeing Team, teaching staff, parents and external specialists

• 
Position: Part-time (50%)

• 
Start date: January 2027, or by agreement

• 
Closing date for applications: 20 November 2026

**Senior Utility Engineer – Plant Engineering (Søborg)

****Keep life-changing therapies moving by keeping our utilities running.

**Location: _Søborg, Denmark. Please note that AGC Biologics does not offer relocation assistance. Applicants must already reside in Denmark or the Greater Malmö area in Sweden.

_AGC Biologics is expanding its Utility team in Søborg and is looking for an experienced Senior Utility Engineer with strong expertise in GMP-regulated pharmaceutical water systems. You will play an important role in ensuring the safe, reliable and compliant operation of utility systems that support our 24/7 research, development and production activities.

**About The Department

**The Utility team is responsible for critical utility systems that support production and laboratory operations at our Søborg site. These include pharmaceutical water systems and other essential utilities. You will work closely with Production, QA, Validation, Maintenance and Project teams in a regulated environment where reliability, compliance and patient safety are key priorities.

**The role

**As Senior Utility Engineer, you will take technical ownership of GMP-critical water systems across the site. This is a hands-on, operational role focused on compliance, troubleshooting, risk reduction and continuous improvement. You will work alongside two skilled technicians who carry out scheduled and unscheduled maintenance, while you focus on system performance, technical oversight and long-term improvements.

**Your Responsibilities Will Include

**

• Ensuring the stable, compliant and efficient operation of pharmaceutical water systems.

• Taking technical ownership of systems and driving improvements to reliability and performance.

• Maintaining technical documentation, including SOPs, P&IDs and maintenance plans, in line with GMP requirements.

• Leading troubleshooting, root cause analysis, risk assessments and CAPA activities.

• Supporting commissioning, qualification and handover of utility projects to Operations and Maintenance.

• Providing technical input to CAPEX and OPEX projects.

• Representing Utilities during audits and inspections.

• Acting as the senior technical contact for water systems and providing guidance to colleagues across the site.

Most work takes place during regular business hours, although occasional evening or weekend work may be required to support our 24/7 production environment.

Initially, your primary focus will be pharmaceutical water systems. Over time, your responsibilities may expand to include black and clean utilities, allowing you to contribute more broadly across the Utility team.

**Experience And Competences

**We are looking for an experienced Senior Utility Engineer with substantial experience working with pharmaceutical water systems in a GMP-regulated environment.

**To Succeed In The Role, You Have

**

• An engineering degree in mechanical, electrical or chemical engineering, or a similar field, or an equivalent technical background combined with relevant experience.

• Strong knowledge of pharmaceutical water systems and applicable GMP/GxP requirements.

• Experience with troubleshooting, maintenance and optimisation of technical systems.

• Experience with technical documentation, deviations, CAPAs, risk assessments and regulatory inspections.

• The ability to take technical ownership, solve complex problems and drive improvements independently.

• The ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and communicate technical information clearly.

Experience with GMP utilities, project handovers, black and clean utilities, regulatory audits and mentoring colleagues is an advantage.

**As a person, you are

**You are proactive, independent and comfortable taking ownership of your responsibilities. You are structured and solution-oriented, with a strong focus on quality and compliance. You communicate clearly, collaborate effectively across teams and enjoy sharing knowledge with colleagues. You are comfortable balancing operational priorities with technical documentation and continuous improvement.

**AGC offers

**At AGC Biologics, you will work with critical utility systems in a dynamic pharmaceutical production environment. You will join a collaborative team where knowledge sharing, ownership and practical problem-solving are valued. The role offers the opportunity to develop your technical expertise and contribute to the reliable operation of systems that support our production activities around the clock.

**How To Apply

**Please submit your application and CV through the AGC Biologics career site. We do not accept applications by email.

Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, and we reserve the right to close the vacancy before the deadline if a suitable candidate is found.

Please note that AGC Biologics does not offer relocation assistance. Applicants must already reside in Denmark or the Greater Malmö area in Sweden.

We look forward to receiving your application!

**Who We Are

**AGC Biologics is a global Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization with a strong presence in Denmark. From our Søborg site, we develop and manufacture life‑changing advanced biologics for some of the world’s most innovative pharmaceutical companies. Together with our team members across Europe, the U.S., and Japan, we deliver development and manufacturing of mammalian and microbial-based therapeutic proteins, plasmid DNA (pDNA), messenger RNA (mRNA), viral vectors, and genetically engineered cells therapies. Across our global network, we are united by one mission: To work side by side with our customers in order to improve patients’ lives by bringing new biopharmaceuticals to market.

Applicants are invited for a double degree PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Biological and Chemical Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

The position is part of the MSCA project TagTIC - Target mining for the development of therapeutics against pathogen-induced cancers, ID: 101311627, Call: HORIZON-MSCA-2025-DN-01-01. Project website: tagtic.eu

Note that this is a double degree PhD project within an MSCA Joint Doctorate. Under the currently planned arrangement, the candidate will work for approximately three years at TissueGnostics GmbH in Vienna, Austria, and one year at Aarhus University, Denmark.

Research area and project description:

Microbial infections are increasingly recognized as important contributors to cancer, but identifying the spatial tissue features and molecular signatures associated with infection-driven disease remains challenging. Integrating tissue imaging with spatial transcriptomics and microbiome information offers opportunities to characterize disease-associated patterns and improve biomarker discovery.

Consortium: This PhD postion is part of the interdisciplinary TagTIC consortium, which brings together expertise in microbiology, virology, oncology, immunology, medicinal chemistry, imaging, AI, and bioinformatics, with support from associated partners in biotech, diagnostics, and science communication. Its collaborative structure allows doctoral candidates to work within a network where discovery science, technology development, training, and societal impact are closely connected.

Project DC11: This PhD is part of the TagTIC consortium. It combines machine learning with image analysis to support precision oncology. The aim is to develop AI algorithms that integrate tissue imaging, spatial transcriptomics and microbiome data (multiomics) to identify biomarkers and predict disease progression.

Project description: For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please simply copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Salary, holiday payment, pension contributions and the like include all employer and employee's taxes and contributions. Thus, figures are before taxes are paid, and taxes may differ depending on individual circumstances. Salary and terms of employment are in accordance with applicable collective agreement and national rules of the employing institution. You enjoy asking the right questions, challenging existing processes and finding practical solutions to complex business needs. You communicate clearly, take ownership and thrive in an international environment where knowledge-sharing, teamwork and continuous improvement are key.

We offer more than just a job

**We wish to be the best at what we do, and everything we do is based on our values of “Winning Attitude, Customer Orientation, and Getting it Done”. We offer flexible working hours and numerous employee benefits, counting a healthy canteen, take-away, free fruit, and fitness facilities. Moreover, we have an active employee association that invites us all to play paddle, badminton, board games etc. and to join the yearly DHL relay race.

Ready to apply?

If you have questions or want to know more about the team, please reach out to Team Lead, Kim Faarbæk, at kifa@wrist.com or by phone on +45 2097 3050

jobs.occupation: Research Assistants in Medical Robotics (Navigation & Control)
jobs.description:
The Department of Computer Science invites applications for one-year research assistant positions focused on developing innovative robot control and navigation techniques using simulation-based learning for medical robotic endoscope devices.

  Project Background
 This project addresses two critical challenges in the field of medical robotics to improve patient care through advanced simulation and control:

   	
• Image-Based Navigation: Creating reward functions for scoring navigation policies for medical robotic devices moving inside the human body, relying solely on image information and accounting for environment changes through interaction models. 	
• Soft Robot Control: Developing learning-based methods to control a soft robot endoscope via high-level navigation policies to perform clinical procedures inside the human body, including quality assessment of these methods during in-vivo interventions.   The successful candidates will join a multidisciplinary and collaborative team renowned for cutting-edge research in medical imaging and simulation technologies, operating within a global network across France, Germany, and Spain.

  Roles and Responsibilities
 The successful candidates will play a central role in the project’s technical and scientific success. While the level of autonomy will vary by position, both roles will share the following core responsibilities:

   	
• Technical Development & Implementation: Designing and implementing machine learning methods for motion planning and control. This includes integrating simulation-based learning frameworks and demonstrating the resulting systems on real robotic hardware and soft robot endoscopes. 	
• Research & Scientific Contribution: Contributing to the project’s core objectives by producing impactful research outputs. This includes writing high-quality papers for peer-reviewed journals and presenting findings at international conferences. 	
• Collaboration & Knowledge Exchange: Facilitating collaborations with industrial partners and academic collaborators to ensure that the developed methodologies are meaningful and translatable to real-world clinical practice. 	
• Professional Growth & Mentorship: Engaging in a high-growth research environment. The positions can be extendable and towards a PhD depending on the future funding status. The project has a trackrecord of landing members in top PhD program and faculty positions. 	
• Interdisciplinary Integration: Actively participating in team discussions and workshops to integrate expertise across medical imaging, physics simulation, and robotics control.   Profile
 We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience:

  Essential experience and skills

   	
• MSc in the fields mentioned above. 	
• You have a strong foundation and track record in robotics simulation, robot control, computer vision and/or machine learning for physical systems. 	
• You are highgly experienced in numerical optimization algorithms, preferably applied to motion planning or reinforcement learning. Hands-on experience on real robots especially soft robot systems is a plus. 	
• Proficient scientific computing and programming (C++/Python) and experience with libraries such as PyTorch, JAX, Warp, Taichi, or ROS. 	
• Excellent communication skills and a high level of motivation to work in a multidisciplinary, international research environment.   Desireable experience and skills

   	
• Experience in publishing peer-reviewed research in top-tier robotics or AI venues. 	
• Familiarity with physics simulation such as MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, Newton Physics, SOFA etc.   Terms of employment
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 1 year. The starting date is 15 February or after agreement

  Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025. 

  Questions
 Further information on the Department is linked at http://www.science.ku.dk/english/about-the-faculty/organisation/. Inquiries about the positions can be made to kenny@di.ku.dk and hayi@di.ku.dk.

  Application procedure

   	
• Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format 	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• A certified/signed copy of a Master of Science certificate. 	
• List of publications.   Deadline for applications: 30 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.
 We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

   

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: PhD Project in Photonic Quantum Error Correction
jobs.description:
The Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) is expanding its talented and international team to add to its cutting-edge quantum programme in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. At the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, we are running an international quantum computing programme, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, that drives research and innovations at multiple levels - from developing scalable quantum processor technologies to quantum algorithms and applications. The long-term mission of the programme is to develop fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware and quantum algorithms that solve life-science-relevant chemical and biological problems.

  NQCP invites applicants for a PhD fellowship on fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing with qudits and group surface codes.

  Start date 1 April 2027 or after agreement.

  The project
 Quantum computers promise to solve problems beyond the reach of conventional computers, but their fragile quantum states are easily disturbed by noise. Quantum error correction protects information against these errors. This project will explore new error-correction methods for quantum computers that use photons, the particles of light. In particular, it will investigate photonic qudits, which can carry information in more than two states, and a promising family of error-correcting codes called group surface codes.

  You will develop theoretical models and software to investigate how these codes can be implemented using photonic circuits. Through numerical simulations, you will study how well they protect information, how they allow computations to be performed reliably, and what resources they require. The aim is to identify approaches that could make large-scale photonic quantum computers more efficient. The work focuses on theory, programming and numerical simulation, while maintaining a close connection to photonic hardware. The project is supported by the Danish e-Infrastructure Consortium (DeiC).

  Who are we looking for?
 We are looking for a motivated candidate with a background in physics, quantum information, computer science, mathematics, photonics or a related field, and a strong interest in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

  Relevant qualifications include:

   	
• A solid foundation in quantum mechanics and quantum information. 	
• Strong programming skills, preferably in Python, and an interest in scientific software development and numerical methods. 	
• Knowledge of quantum error correction, quantum computing architectures, quantum optics or topological quantum codes. Experience in one or more of these areas is an advantage. 	
• Experience with numerical simulations, decoding algorithms or high-performance computing is an advantage. 	
• A curious mindset, the ability to work independently and collaboratively, and a structured approach to research. 	
• Good written and spoken English and strong communication skills.   Applicants are not expected to have prior experience in all aspects of the project. Relevant research projects, software contributions, publications and other professional activities will be considered in the assessment.

  Our group and research - and what do we offer?
 The group is part of the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen. We are located in Copenhagen.We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment hosted by NQCP at. You will be part of the photonics research environment and collaborate closely with researchers working on quantum computing architectures, quantum error correction and photonic quantum technologies.

  Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Stefano Paesani, Niels Bohr Institute, stefano.paesani@nbi.ku.dk. The co-supervisor will be Professor Apoorv Tiwari at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU). The project will involve close collaboration between the two institutions, with regular joint supervision meetings and in-person visits.

  Joining NQCP now, you will get involved in a well-established and ambitious programme, which offers excellent opportunities to build a career in advancing quantum computing. We want to make Denmark a world leader in quantum research, and we hope to attract people from all over the world.

  Life in Denmark is supported by strong social services, including universal healthcare, free or subsidised language courses, paid parental leave, subsidised day care and excellent public schools. Our work culture is egalitarian and prioritises work-life balance. Copenhagen offers excellent infrastructure, extensive cycling networks, a thriving food scene, museums and access to beautiful natural surroundings.

  The PhD programme 
 Depending on your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelors´s degree.

   Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Physics For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure. 

  Appointment will be subject to a security clearance.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

   Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme 

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor´s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database. 

  Terms of the integrated programme
 To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes in Physics.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see: www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year.

  A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7.426 before tax.
 
 When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Appointment will be subject to a security clearance.

   Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme  (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme) 	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision    	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project. 	
• Relevant publications. 	
• Relevant work experience. 	
• Other relevant professional activities. 	
• Curious mind-set with a strong interest in Physics. 	
• Good language and communication skills. 	
• A structures approach to work.   Application and Assessment Procedure
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor of Science or Master of Science and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if possible) 	
• Reference letters (if available)   When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

  The deadline for applications is 22 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified, whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the principal supervisor.

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

   

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

Are you passionate about leading high-performing teams and delivering business-critical technology solutions? BEC Financial Technologies is looking for a Development Manager to join our Document Lifecycle Management team at our office in Roskilde.

Our team develops, maintains, and operates core document management and archiving platforms used by Danish banks. These solutions support essential banking processes and enable secure, compliant, and reliable document handling throughout the document lifecycle.

As Development Manager, you will lead a distributed team of specialists based in Denmark and Poland and manage strategic vendor relationships. Reporting to the Head of Document Lifecycle Management, you will drive delivery, ensure operational stability, and support the continued evolution of critical platforms that operate around the clock, every day of the year.

Working closely with business stakeholders, architects, vendors, and other technology teams, you will play a key role in shaping the future of document lifecycle management at BEC.

At BEC, we prefer to collaborate often in the office, while also offering the opportunity to work remotely on average up to 1 day per week.

Primary tasks and responsibilities:

• Be accountable for the team’s contribution to the domain roadmap and delivery against agreed objectives.
