jobs.occupation: Rethinking Converter Synchronization: 2-Year Postdoctoral Position in Battery Energy Storage Systems
jobs.description:
Are you eager to contribute to a bold experimental research project at the forefront of power electronics and energy storage? We are offering an exciting 2-year postdoctoral position for a talented researcher to investigate advanced converter synchronization and control methods for Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), with particular emphasis on exploiting naturally occurring acoustic and vibration information. The project combines converter control, sensing, signal processing, and experimental validation to explore new approaches toward simpler, more robust, and scalable BESS operation. This position is expected to start from 1st of January 2027, or as soon as possible hereafter.

About the project
The position is affiliated with the VILLUM Experiment project A-choir and the EMI/EMC In Power Electronics research group at AAU Energy. The project investigates new synchronization concepts for multi-converter BESSs by combining power electronics, sensing, signal processing, and control. A particular focus is placed on whether physical signatures naturally generated during converter operation can provide useful information for synchronization and coordination. 

You will join a research environment working across power electronics, EMI/EMC, converter control, multi-physics analysis, and experimental validation with applications including battery energy storage systems and other converter-dominated energy systems, with opportunities for collaboration across disciplines. The position also offers opportunities for international scientific exchange, participation in leading conferences, and may include research visits to relevant academic or industrial partners.

Your work tasks
You will:

• Develop and investigate synchronization and coordination methods for power electronic converters.
• Develop sensing and signal-processing methods for acoustic and vibration measurements.
• Establish and evaluate relationships between physical signatures and converter switching/operating behaviors.
• Implement and validate the developed methods using real-time control platforms, HIL, and experimental converter setups.
• Assess the proposed approaches under representative BESS operating conditions, including robustness to interference and multi-converter interactions.
• Contribute to the coordination of related research activities, and disseminate results through scientific publications, conferences, and project deliverables.
The position may also include a limited amount of teaching and supervision in areas related to your expertise.

Your competencies
We expect you to have:

• A PhD in Electrical Engineering, Energy Engineering, or a closely related field.
• Documented experience in power electronics, power converter modelling and control, converter synchronization, signal processing, EMI/EMC, or related areas.
• Strong programming and experimental skills using DSP, MATLAB/Simulink, PLECS, hardware-in-the-loop implementation or comparable tools.
• Experience with one or more relevant methods, such as synchronization and coordination control, digital signal processing, time-frequency analysis, data-driven modelling, or machine learning.
• Good knowledge of battery storage systems or multi-converter systems; experience with synchronization control, hierarchical control, hardware design, or AI-assisted signal would be an advantage.
• A strong scientific publication record appropriate to your career stage.
• The ability to conduct independent research, collaborate across disciplines, and communicate effectively with academic and industrial partners.
• Excellent written and spoken English.
You are not expected to be an expert in all technical areas covering power electronics, acoustic/vibration sensing, signal processing, or machine learning. Strong competence in power converter control and synchronization, together with solid experimental skills and the ability to work across sensing, EMI/EMC, and system-level interactions, is particularly important. We value scientific independence, critical thinking, strong experimental skills, and a rigorous approach to modelling, implementation, validation, and documentation.

Who we are
The position will be based in the section for “Applied Power Electronic Systems” at Department of Energy in Aalborg University (AAU Energy). AAU Energy is an international research department at Aalborg University dedicated to developing clean and sustainable energy systems across electrical, thermal, and mechatronic energy technologies. We offer an interdisciplinary research environment, advanced laboratory facilities, and extensive collaboration with industry and academic partners. The department has campuses in Aalborg and Esbjerg; this position is based at the Aalborg campus. Read more at www.energy.aau.dk

Qualification requirements 
Appointment as postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level.

How to apply  
Your application must include the following:

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

**Do you want to help ensure reliable documentation for electrical infrastructure projects? Can you bring structure to complex documentation flows and secure complete project records? And do you have at least five years of experience in document control? Then join COWI as our new Document Controller.

****Create the solutions that will enable a better tomorrow

**We are looking for a Document Controller to join COWI and support our customer's electrical infrastructure projects. You will help ensure that both internal project documentation and supplier documentation are collected, organised and securely archived. Following an introduction to the relevant processes, methods and systems, you will work with minimal supervision to ensure complete project documentation through to final handover and project closure.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Set up archiving structures in the customer's electronic document and records management system and clarify which documentation must be collected and retained.

• Collect and secure internal project documentation from customer-managed SharePoint sites, as well as photographic documentation and other project records.

• Collect and secure supplier documentation, including collaborating with the customer's IT team on developing APIs or automation tools where needed.

• Ensure that final as-built documentation is complete, that projects comply with the customer's archiving guidelines, and that sites and platforms are closed down at project completion.

**Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

**The first step to success in this role is that you are eager to collaborate with the people around you, whether they are colleagues, partners or customers. Developing ties with others is something you do by acting respectfully and delivering on your promises. And you never get set in your ways, but keep exploring new insights and ways to improve.

On top of that, you will have:

• At least five years of experience in document control.

• Experience with electronic document management (EDM) systems, an aptitude for IT and a good working knowledge of Microsoft Office

• Experience managing electronic workflows and as-built documentation.

• Good written and verbal communication skills in both Danish and English.

• A structured and thorough approach, enjoyment of process-oriented tasks, and a service-minded, collaborative and practical attitude. You are motivated and engaged, with a focus on helping projects succeed

Your official COWI office location will be either Lyngby, Vejle or Aarhus. However, your primary workplace will be at Energinet in Erritsø, but Ballerup could also be an option, with some travel to Erritsø. You will report to Head of Discipline, Ioana Nicoleta Tuglui, who is based at COWI's headquarters in Lyngby.

**A place to work and so much more

**At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers.

We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home.

With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

**Before you apply

And we take diversity and inclusion into account in all relevant decisions and processes and when setting teams and fora. We do it because it is part of our values and because it is simply the right thing to do.

jobs.occupation: Partnership Officer for Driving Strategic Industry Collaboration and Research Funding within Energy - DTU Offshore
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about connecting cutting-edge research with industry needs?

We are looking for an experienced and commercially minded Partnership Officer to strengthen and expand our collaboration with industry partners and authorities across the energy sector.

In this strategic role, you will be responsible for building, developing, and nurturing long-term relationships with companies and other external stakeholders, translating opportunities into research collaborations, innovation projects, and industry-funded activities.

You will work closely with our researchers, technical experts and leadership team as well as both new and potential partners to identify industry challenges that can be addressed through research and development, while ensuring that our competencies, facilities, and expertise create value for our partners and society.

This position is ideal for someone with a strong technical background in energy related topics and a proven ability to establish trusted partnerships that result in funded research and innovation projects.

Key Responsibilities

• Contribute to developing and executing a strategy for industry engagement and partnership development in collaboration with relevant employees at DTU Offshore.
• Build and maintain relationships with key stakeholders across the energy sector, including utilities, developers, technology providers, consultancies, and public organizations.
• Identify opportunities for collaborative research, innovation, testing, demonstration, and consulting activities.
• Facilitate and negotiate industry-funded research and development projects.
• Work closely with researchers to translate scientific capabilities into compelling value propositions for industry partners.
• Expand and strengthen DTU Offshore’s network within the energy ecosystem.
• Secure external funding through strategic partnerships, contract research, consortium participation, sponsorships, and innovation initiatives.
• Represent the organization at conferences, industry events, networking forums, and stakeholder meetings.
• Support the development of long-term strategic alliances with national and international companies.
• Participate in monitoring industry trends, emerging technologies, and market needs to identify new collaboration opportunities together with researchers and technical experts at the centre.
Your Profile
We are looking for a highly motivated professional who combines technical insight with strong relationship-building and business development skills.

Qualifications

• Master's degree or higher in Engineering, Applied Sciences, Energy Technology, or a related technical field.
• Strong technical understanding of geo-engineering and energy production, especially offshore energy, renewable energy, hydrogen, energy storage, CCS or related fields as well as the broader energy transition landscape.
• Several years of experience working in the energy sector, research organizations, innovation environments, or technology-focused businesses.
• Demonstrated success in attracting industry funding, establishing externally funded research and development activities or selling technology development and innovation.
• Proven track record of developing strategic partnerships and long-term customer or stakeholder relationships.
• Extensive professional network within relevant parts of the energy industry.
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
• Strong ability to engage with both senior industry executives and leading researchers.
• Experience with contract negotiations, collaboration agreements, or business development activities is a plus.
Personal Competencies - you are:

• A network builder who enjoys connecting people and opportunities.
• Strategic and proactive, with a strong results-oriented mindset.
• Credible in technical discussions while comfortable engaging commercially.
• Collaborative and able to build trust across organizational boundaries.
• Skilled at translating industry needs into impactful research opportunities and successfully establishing commercial agreements with the industry.
• Motivated by creating societal and industrial impact through research and innovation.
What We Offer

• A unique opportunity to shape strategic collaborations between academia and industry in a developing organization with an entrepreneurial spirit and “can do” attitude. 
• A dynamic and international research environment at the forefront of energy innovation.
• Close collaboration with leading researchers and industrial partners.
• Significant influence on the development of industry collaborations and the development of the centre.
Salary and appointment terms
Salary and the appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). You are employed as Senior Executive Officer. In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for academic staff employed in technical-administrative positions at DTU (AC TAP): https://www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures 

The workplace is DTU Offshore, Lyngby Campus.

Application and contact
Please submit your online application no later than 3 December 2026. Open the “Apply now” link, fill out the form and attach your motivated application, CV and exam certificates.

If you would like additional information about the position, please contact New Projects Director, Charlotte Nørgaard Larsen, +45 93511536 or Centre Director, Elena Pachkova, +45 93511464. You can read more about DTU Offshore at https://offshore.dtu.dk/ 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

About DTU Offshore
DTU Offshore is Denmark's national R&D centre for offshore technologies, developing research-based solutions for the energy transition. We address critical challenges across CO₂ storage, water treatment, energy production and storage, abandonment, island energy systems, and impact on the marine environment. Through close collaboration with industry partners, regulatory authorities, and research institutions, we deliver applied innovations that support responsible on- and offshore energy operations. Our multidisciplinary approach combines decades of experience in the North Sea with world-class laboratory facilities.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Investment Performance Business Partner, Copenhagen, Helsinki or Stockholm
jobs.description:
Are you a finance or investment professional with the capability to change outcomes and directly impact the business? Would you like to work with talented individuals in an innovative company where you can influence your own responsibilities and build close partnerships across portfolio management, transactions & asset management?

**About The Role

**As an Investment Performance Business Partner at Urban Partners, you will be part of the wider CIO Office team and report to the Investment Performance Director.

Joining the Investment Performance team, you will play an important role in driving performance and decision making. You will act as a tactical and strategic partner to investment owners and portfolio management across Urban Partners. As our team expands, we are searching for the right candidate to join.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Drive bi-annual Re-Underwriting process for selected countries, ensuring quality & completeness.

• Own delivery of reporting, analysis, and insights to your stakeholders.

• Execute deep dives on investments or portfolios as nominated or flagged.

• Build scenario & sensitivity analysis on investment & portfolio level.

• Support development & expansion of Inv. Perf. team capabilities.

• Develop and advance analysis framework and AI adaptation.

Your Experience & Skills In this role, you hold a relevant Master's degree and bring 2-4 years of experience from investment management, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), forecasting, finance consulting, audit, controlling, or a similar analytical finance environment. Relevant backgrounds include Big Four firms, finance advisory, real estate controlling, and investment management. The role requires technical skills in modelling and a sound finance understanding.

**We Expect You To Bring

**

• Hands on experience and confidence working with financial statements and driver-based projections.

• Experience in investment modelling with the ability to rebuild a cash flow.

• Experience with projection/forecasting process execution.

• The ability to run analytical process, scenario analysis and sensitivity tests.

• Operational interest and understanding.

• AI application and curiosity.

• Excellent English communication skills, both written and verbal. Professional proficiency in local language, with the ability to understand and engage in day-to-day business discussions, is required. Additional Nordic language skills are considered an advantage.

Your character

• Collaborative and clear in your communication, able to build a strong connection with business stakeholders.

• Comfort with disagreement. The job is to challenge experienced colleagues constructively and repeatedly, and to be welcome in the following quarter.

• Curiosity about what drives a number rather than whether it ties. A reconciler will be unhappy in this role and unhelpful in it.

**What We Offer

**Make a difference by helping create urban spaces and places that enrich people’s lives in the most sustainable way

Lead the industry with an innovator that is pioneering new approaches while raising standards and inspiring the industry

Learn and grow as part of a powerhouse of brilliant people where teamwork, feedback and different ways of thinking are at the core

Be your whole self in a purpose-driven culture with a strong sense of belonging, based on trust, celebration and caring for each other

**About Us

**This role is closely connected to colleagues in Copenhagen and to teams across the investment-performance data flow. Active collaboration and regular in-person presence are important to making those relationships work well.

The Investment Performance team sits within the CIO Office and is responsible for the methodologies, analytics, and platforms that support investment decision-making across Urban Partners. Working at the intersection of investments, data, technology, and business processes, the team drives performance management, business partnering, platform ownership, and continuous improvement to help create a scalable and future-fit investment platform

**Join us

**If this opportunity interests you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible, as applications are reviewed and interviews conducted on an ongoing basis. Application deadline: 17 November. For questions, please contact Jerker Gustafsson (Investment Performance Director) at jegu@urban.partners.

We look forward to hearing from you!

**Description

**Factbird helps manufacturers turn real-time production data into decisions they can actually act on. Since 2016, we've helped manufacturers in 28 countries cut waste, boost uptime, and run smarter — from the shop floor to the boardroom. Over 300 companies trust us to make sense of their operations, and we're a team of 80+ people across Copenhagen and the US who care about making complex things simple.

We're creating a new role at the top of our Engineering career ladder: Lead Architect. It's the senior end of our Technical Track — the rung above Tech Lead — and today it's a role we've deliberately left lightly defined, because we want the first person in it to help define it. You'll set Factbird's technical direction: architecture, tooling, and the multi-year technology bets that shape where the product goes next.

This is our most senior technical role, with no direct reports — your authority comes from judgment and track record, not the org chart. You'll work alongside our Tech Leads in Factbird's technical leadership group, partner closely with our Director of Engineering, and be the person other senior engineers go to when a decision is genuinely hard to reverse.

**About the Role

**As Lead Architect, you own Factbird's company-wide technical vision: the architecture our services run on, the tooling and standards our engineers use every day, and the multi-year technology strategy that ties it all together. You make — or sign off on — the high-stakes, hard-to-reverse architecture calls, and you're accountable for getting them right with the full context of where the business is headed, not just where the code is today.

You'll work across a team built on Rust, React, Node.js, and AWS, with AI-assisted development already a core part of how we ship. Some of what this role owns is already well-defined — reviewing RFCs, stewarding language and platform standards, setting the team's AI-tooling strategy. Some of it isn't yet: Factbird is still a growing company, and part of the job is helping us figure out what technical leadership at this level should look like as we scale.

You'll thrive here if you'd rather be trusted with genuinely hard calls than manage a team, and if you can hold both the technical detail and the commercial context — cost, risk, market direction — well enough to make a technology bet you can still defend a year later.

**

What you'll do

**Architecture & technical strategy

• Own Factbird's multi-year technology strategy, and make the high-stakes architecture calls that are hard to reverse — with cost, risk, and business context factored in, not just engineering elegance

• Author and drive major RFCs from proposal through to an actual decision, and review the highest-risk architecture changes across the team

• Act as steward for our core languages and frameworks — setting standards, library choices, and the platform's overall shape

• Make build-vs-buy calls for new technical capabilities, and bring a clear point of view on emerging technologies worth adopting

• Define the observability, reliability, and security posture the platform is held to

**

Tooling & standards**

• Set the team's technical tooling and platform standards, and keep them evolving as the stack and the company grow

• Define Factbird's strategy for AI-assisted development — which tools we adopt, how we balance velocity against code quality, security, and IP risk, and where we draw the line

• Shape engineering-wide quality philosophy and help set the technical bar used in hiring interviews

• Help define shared components and reference architecture that other engineers build on, rather than reinvent

• Give input into technical org design and team topology as Engineering scales

**

Technical leadership & mentorship**

• Act as the trusted technical advisor to our Director of Engineering and the technical leadership group, partnering with Tech Leads and Product Leads on cross-team alignment

• Mentor senior engineers and Tech Leads toward architect-level thinking, without formal ownership of their people management

• Communicate technical vision and trade-offs clearly to non-technical stakeholders, including leadership

• Identify technical risks to the business early, and say so before they become expensive

• Represent Factbird's technical thinking externally where it makes sense — a talk, a blog post, an open-source contribution — though this isn't a requirement on day one

**What we’re looking for

**We're looking for someone who's already earned this kind of trust somewhere else — someone whose technical opinions carry weight because they're right more often than not, and who'd rather solve the interesting, ambiguous problem than manage the team solving it.

**

The ideal background**

• 8+ years of hands-on engineering experience, including real time spent as an architect or equivalent senior technical authority, not just a senior engineer with a bigger title

• A track record of owning multi-year technology strategy or platform architecture decisions that other teams had to live with — and that held up

• Has led major RFCs or architecture proposals cross-team, through genuine pushback, to an actual decision

• Comfortable making build-vs-buy and technology-adoption calls that account for cost, risk, and where the market is heading, not just what's technically interesting

• Experience mentoring senior engineers or Tech Leads toward architect-level thinking, without needing formal authority to do it

• Practical, current experience with AI-assisted development, and a clear point of view on where it genuinely helps versus where it creates risk

**Why Factbird?

**People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

**

Here's what you can look forward to:**

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn't one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Thoughtful, human onboarding: We'll support you step by step, giving you the context, tools, and guidance you need to feel confident from day one.

• A career path that grows with you: Through bi-yearly Individual Development Plan conversations, we'll work together to shape a career journey that fits your ambitions.

• Company-wide gatherings & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what's next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We're proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.

**

We'd love to hear from you

**If this role feels like a match, we'd be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit — feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Have questions? You can always reach out to Cristina Vartej at **crva@factbird.com

**_

At Factbird, we believe that great work starts with people feeling respected, valued, and included. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

__All employment decisions at Factbird are made based on business needs, role requirements, and individual qualifications, without discrimination based on gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital or family status, nationality, ethnic or social origin, religion or belief, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected under applicable European and local employment laws.

_We celebrate diversity in all its forms and believe that different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences make our teams stronger and our work better. We warmly encourage all qualified candidates to apply and to bring their whole selves to Factbird.

We are looking for a Head of Retail to lead and grow Tekla's retail business as it accelerates internationally. This is a senior commercial role, with full responsibility for the performance, consistency, and growth of our stores, from the shop floor through to clienteling, retail marketing, and new store openings.

Reporting directly to the Commercial & Merchandising Director, you will have direct management and commercial responsibility for all owned stores, with real accountability for retail KPIs. You will work closely with partners managing stores in some markets, as well as our internal operations, marketing, and merchandising teams.

This is a unique opportunity to shape how Tekla scales retail. As our roll-out accelerates, new locations bring more complexity and a diverse mix of operating models. You will build the routines and standards that make this expansion consistent and commercially disciplined.

While our preferred location for this role is Copenhagen, we are also open to applications from candidates based in London. Please note that, in both cases, regular travel across stores and departments will be required.

Key responsibilities of the role include, but are not limited to:

Commercial performance and store management

• Hold direct management and full commercial responsibility for all owned stores and staffed department store spaces, currently Copenhagen and London, with a growing portfolio ahead.

• Extend the same commercial oversight to partner-operated locations, ensuring consistency in practice and driving performance even where day-to-day management sits with the partner.

• Own retail KPIs across every door, including revenue, conversion, footfall, AOV, and profitability, and manage each location towards its individual target.

• Build and embed weekly and monthly performance routines that drive both engagement and consistency across the retail portfolio.

• Lead, coach, and develop store teams, setting clear standards for service, engagement, and commercial performance.

Clienteling

• Lead and implement Tekla’s clienteling strategy across all stores, building the high-value customer base that underpins the retail model.

• Own the clienteling tool: adoption, daily workflows, and reporting.

• In collaboration with marketing, define and implement a clienteling calendar, to ensure high-value customers are engaged with in a meaningful way

• Define and track the clienteling KPI set, from appointments and outreach through to follow-up quality and revenue attribution.

• Ensure high-value client relationships are developed consistently, and to the same standard, across locations.

Retail marketing and activations

• In close collaboration with marketing, own the in-store events calendar as a primary driver of qualified traffic and brand engagement, spanning clienteling events, seasonal brand moments, and cultural programming.

• In collaboration with the PR & Community team, build local partnerships and community relationships in each market to generate reach, acquisition, and repeat engagement.

• Work with the trade team to ensure the stores are best leveraged as platforms to engage with architects and interior designers.

• Overall, use each store as a live platform for brand storytelling and customer acquisition, not only as a point of sale.

Store openings and expansion

• Coordinate store opening projects end-to-end, including site readiness, operational workflows, recruitment, and onboarding.

• Adapt the operating model to different setups, from HQ-managed to partner-operated and local-lead formats.

• Build scalable routines and playbooks so that each new opening is faster and more consistent than the last.

Retail operations

• Manage the retail operations function to ensure perfect synchronisation between the front and back end of the business, across stock, systems, POS, and fulfilment.

• Ensure consistency in tools, processes, and reporting across an increasingly complex, multi-format retail portfolio, and continuously sharpen our reporting to drive diagnosis and action across the network of stores.

• Partner with operations, technology, merchandising, and e-commerce to drive process and tool improvements as the business scales, and to deliver a seamless omnichannel experience for the customer.

We’d love to hear from you if you are/have:

• A retail leader with deep experience running stores, ideally across multiple regions or markets.

• Experience managing a clienteling tool and driving a clienteling strategy. This is essential to the role.

• A proven record of driving retail KPIs and building the performance routines that lift both engagement and results across multiple doors.

• Experience in retail marketing, including events, local partnerships, and activations that generate traffic and build the brand.

• Comfortable owning store opening projects, including recruitment and onboarding, across different operating models.

• Commercially disciplined and operationally strong, able to hold consistency across a portfolio of stores with different setups.

• Ideally, a premium or luxury retail background, with a genuine feel for service, experience, and brand representation.

• Genuinely drawn to Tekla's approach to product and brand; an appreciation for considered, quality home textiles matters.

Reviewing applications and conducting interviews will take place on an ongoing basis, with the aim for the successful candidate to join us as in January. If you have a genuine interest in connecting with clients through retail, an appreciation for Tekla’s approach and a commercial mindset, we encourage you to apply.

We are seeking a Financial Controller to own the integrity of Tekla’s financial reporting across the group. The role combines technical control work, balance sheet reconciliations, consolidation and eliminations, with ownership of a growing set of tax and trade compliance obligations spanning packaging tax, EU and global VAT and customs duties.

The Financial Controller is responsible both for meeting these obligations accurately and on time, and for building the processes, controls and automation that make them repeatable as the business scales. The role sits within an AI-first function focused on operational excellence, so we are looking for someone with a strong digital mindset and a proactive approach to using AI and automation tools to enhance reporting and improve efficiency.

This is a hands-on role, instrumental in ensuring financial accuracy and supporting Tekla's profitability and growth objectives. Reporting to the Finance Director and working closely with the Accounting Manager, the Financial Controller will also contribute to a range of ad hoc financial projects and initiatives across the function.

This is a full-time position based in our open-plan, curated office in Copenhagen.

Key responsibilities of the role include, but are not limited to:

Financial Controlling & Reporting

• Design, implement and manage the group's balance sheet reconciliations, including building standardised templates and processes across multiple entities

• Prepare the monthly and year-end group consolidation, including intercompany eliminations, foreign currency translation and consolidated reporting packs

• Ensure the general ledger is supported by complete, reviewed and documented reconciliations in every period. While taking a hands-on approach to booking journals and ad hoc analysis.

Tax & Trade Compliance

• Own end-to-end packaging tax obligations, including data capture, calculation and filing

• Perform compliance reviews over packaging tax, taking a proactive approach as Tekla's global footprint grows

• Analyse customs and import duties, covering tariff classification, country of origin, preferential rates and duty paid versus duty due, and identify recovery and savings opportunities

Financial Analysis & Performance

• Monitor cash flow, working capital, and financial performance metrics

• Perform variance and accuracy analyses to validate forecasts, budgets, and data integrity, encouraging transparency and accountability

• Investigate material variances and implement process improvements that enhance forecasting precision and analytical rigour

• Provide insightful financial analysis to support business planning, cost efficiencies and strategic priorities

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support business objectives

Process Improvement & Automation

• Drive continuous improvement by leveraging AI and emerging technologies to enhance financial processes, systems, and reporting tools

• Support the automation programme within the accounting team, including Intrastat and VAT reporting

• Review and implement continual improvements in Business Central, including VAT code configuration, VAT statements and financial reports

• Strengthen documentation and controls across all owned processes so they are auditable and transferable

We'd love to hear from you if you are / have:

• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field

• Strong knowledge of accounting principles, financial reporting standards and tax regulations

• Demonstrable experience of group consolidation and intercompany eliminations in a multi-entity, multi-currency environment

• Strong working knowledge of global VAT and sales tax concepts

• Exposure to packaging tax regimes is an advantage

• Experience designing and operating a balance sheet reconciliation control framework

• Confident ERP user, ideally Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central

• Demonstrable experience using AI tools such as Claude to optimise and automate financial processes and reporting, for example building reporting dashboards, automating reconciliation and compliance workflows, or analysing large transactional data sets

• Advanced Excel skills and comfort working with large transactional data sets

• Experience from a high-growth business within fashion, textiles or luxury consumer goods is an advantage

• An entrepreneurial mindset with strong interpersonal skills

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English

Applications will be reviewed and interviews conducted on an ongoing basis, with the aim of the successful candidate joining us as soon as possible.

Tekla makes high-quality home textiles, with a focus on craftsmanship, sustainability, and timeless design. We sell through our own e-commerce platform, our stores in Copenhagen and London, and wholesale partners around the world. As we grow across channels and markets, we are building the operational and technological foundation to support that growth.

We are looking for a Data Analytics Engineer to bring our data in-house and build the foundation the whole company relies on. This is a new role and our first dedicated data hire. Today an external partner builds and runs our data platform. You will take it over, own it end to end, and shape how everyone at Tekla works with data and AI.

Reporting to the Technology Lead, you will form Tekla's core technology team together. Data only creates value when it drives action, so you will spend a good share of your time with colleagues across the business, making sure what you build answers real questions and becomes part of how people work. In your first year, the priority is to bring the data foundation in-house, then to support analytics, then to open up data to AI.

Data and AI

• Strong SQL and dimensional modelling skills.

• Experience building dashboards in a common tool such as Power BI, Looker, or Tableau.

Curious about how technology powers everything we do at Arla Foods, from farm to fridge? Join our IT Graduate Programme and kickstart your career with hands-on experience, real projects, and guidance from experienced colleagues and mentors.

Over two years and two rotations, you’ll build a strong foundation in IT & Digital, develop your ability to work closely with the business, and gain broad experience across our organisation while helping shape the digital future of Arla.

About our IT Graduate Programme

The IT Graduate Programme is a two-year opportunity designed to kickstart your career after graduation. Through two different rotations, you’ll gain a broad and well-rounded experience across Arla’s IT & Digital organisation, build your professional and personal skills, and explore different areas of IT & Digital.

The programme opens up broad career possibilities and will help prepare you for future opportunities within Arla IT & Digital after completing the programme.

“The IT Graduate Programme provides a unique opportunity to experience different areas of the business, build a strong network, and grow both professionally and personally. Besides building your technical skills, each rotation also offers a new perspective on the business, helping you understand how different teams collaborate to create value. The strong support network of mentors, buddies, development managers, and fellow graduates makes the journey both rewarding and fun, while helping you build connections across the entire organisation”, says Gergana Biserova Atanasova, IT Graduate in IT&Digital Foundation Operational Technology Infrastructure.

How will you make an impact as an IT Graduate?

As an IT Graduate, you’ll become part of a highly competent and diverse IT & Digital organisation, contributing to both daily operations and projects that help move our global business forward.

Throughout the programme, your two rotations will give you different perspectives and opportunities to develop:

First rotation

Before joining Arla, you’ll already know where your graduate journey will begin and who your manager will be. Your first rotation will focus on building a strong foundation in core IT & Digital capabilities.

• Depending on your role, this could mean working with data to identify trends or improve reporting, supporting the development or implementation of an IT solution, helping strengthen the reliability or security of our systems, improving an existing digital process, or contributing to a technical project together with experienced colleagues.

Second rotation

Your second rotation will focus on developing your business co-creation skills, giving you the opportunity to work closely with the business and strengthen your stakeholder engagement capabilities. You’ll see how Arla’s IT & Digital organisation supports the business from end to end, including areas such as Supply Chain, Commercial and Cross-functions.

• Here, the challenge might be understanding a problem faced by colleagues in Supply Chain, Commercial or Cross-functions and helping shape a technology solution, exploring how a manual process could be automated, using data to support better decision-making, or helping introduce a new digital solution for users across the business.

As part of your graduate journey, we’ll provide you with broad and well-rounded experience across Arla’s IT & Digital organisation. Your rotations could take you into areas such as data science, solutions consultancy, network consultancy, cybersecurity, or others.

By experiencing different parts of IT & Digital, you’ll start to understand not only the technology behind a global organisation, but also the people and business needs it supports. You’ll leave the programme with broader experience, a strong network and a clearer understanding of where you want to take your career at Arla.

What will make you a successful IT Graduate?

We’re looking for curious, motivated individuals with a genuine interest in IT and a strong desire to learn and grow. While we welcome graduates from diverse educational backgrounds, your mindset and motivation matter most.

You are:

• Aspiring to build a career in IT

• Living in Denmark

• Holding a bachelor’s or master’s degree in a STEM field, completed within two years before the programme starts in September 2027

• Analytical and structured in your approach, with strong problem-solving skills and a willingness to learn, explore, and take on new challenges

• Curious about how technology and digital solutions can support and create value for the business

• Open to new people and perspectives, comfortable communicating with others, and motivated to be an active part of the graduate community

Why join Arla’s IT Graduate Programme?

As part of our IT Graduate Programme, you’ll receive a variety of development opportunities every step of the way. To support your professional and personal development, you’ll benefit from:

• 
Responsibilities from day one, enabling on-the-job learning across two different rotations

• 
Graduate development camps taking place in different markets together with your graduate colleagues

• 
One-to-one mentoring and sparring with senior leaders

• 
A supportive graduate community across Arla’s graduate programmes

• 
Exposure to different areas of IT & Digital and opportunities to collaborate with colleagues across our global business

Important information before applying

Join Arla’s IT & Digital Graduate Programme and take the first step towards a meaningful, dynamic career in a global company that values innovation, collaboration, and your personal growth.

The application period for the IT Graduate Programme runs from 2nd November 2026 to 3rd January 2027.

Before applying, please make sure that you have prepared your CV in English. Cover letter is optional. You will be asked different questions on the application page, so we recommend that you start the application process from a computer rather than a mobile phone.

For additional information, read more about the IT Graduate Programme on our website. Here, you can get inspiration from some of our previous and current graduates and learn more about the programme. You can also read more about what to expect from the recruitment process.

Read more about the programme here

Shape the Future of Dairy

Arla is a global leader in the dairy industry, committed to enabling good food choices that make life better, providing people with nourishment, while taking care at every step to ensure Arla is a choice they can feel good about. If you are looking to shape the future with an ambitious global cooperative that truly cares about your growth, where everyone feels valued and empowered, and collaboration is the core of culture, Arla is a choice you can feel good about.

We’re looking for an experienced Financial Controller to take full ownership of our numbers as we scale. You’ll run a tight month-end close, get our SaaS revenue accounting airtight, and build the finance processes that let us grow fast without drowning in manual work. If you like turning messy into robust, read on.

**About Pandektes

**Legal research hasn’t changed much in decades. Lawyers still spend countless hours navigating fragmented sources, outdated systems, and complex databases just to find the information they need.

At Pandektes, we’re changing that.

Our ambition is to build the leading global platform for legal research and the largest AI-powered legal database. By combining artificial intelligence, intelligent search, and continuously updated legal sources, we’re redefining how legal knowledge is accessed, understood, analyzed, and applied.

Pandektes has raised more than _€_17.5 million and most recently closed a _€_13.5 million Series A round (October 2026) led by Alstin Capital, PROfounders and Scale Capital. Pandektes already serves more than 450 customers across Denmark, Germany and Switzerland.

We’re still early in the journey, and joining our team now means you’ll have big impact on shaping how we scale.

**About The Role

**This is a hands-on role responsible for ensuring the accuracy and integrity of financial information, overseeing the month-end close, management accounts, financial reporting and statutory compliance, while continuously improving financial processes, systems and internal controls and working closely with Senior Management, external service providers and the wider business teams. The role will combine strong technical accounting expertise with a proactive, solutions-focused approach and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

**What You’ll Do

**

• Own the monthly and annual close – reviewing journals, accruals, prepayments, provisions and balance sheet reconciliations, and delivering accurate trial balances and financial statements on time

• Make sure our SaaS revenue (subscription, usage-based and implementation) is recognised correctly, and reconcile revenue schedules to billing, contracts and the general ledger

• Produce reliable monthly P&L, balance sheet and cash flow reporting

• Take over revenue billing from the sales team and run it within finance

• Manage our outsourced service providers and review the reconciliations they prepare – bank, intercompany, payroll, fixed assets and other control accounts

• Design and maintain financial policies, controls and approval limits across payments, expenses, procurement and system access

• Oversee AP, AR and cashbook accounting, manage payments through Corepay, and keep an eye on working capital

• Lead statutory accounts and external audits, and oversee VAT, corporate tax and compliance with our tax advisers

• Coordinate intercompany accounting and reporting across our entities in Denmark, Germany, Switzerland and the UK

• Improve finance processes, systems and automation – and over time, build and develop a small accounting team

**What You’ll Bring

**

• 7+ years in commercially focused accounting roles, ideally with previous experience as a Financial Controller

• A recognised Danish accounting qualification (or equivalent, e.g. ACA, ACCA or CIMA)

• Hands-on experience with subscription and deferred revenue, including month-end revenue reconciliations

• A track record of independently running the month-end close and producing accurate management accounts

• Experience with intercompany balances, foreign currencies and reporting across international subsidiaries

• Exposure to international tax, VAT and transfer pricing, and experience running a local audit process

• A strong grasp of internal controls, segregation of duties and fraud risk

• Experience improving finance operations in a growing, scaling business – and a love for systems and automation

• A sharp eye for detail and the analytical instinct to tell a real business issue from an accounting error

**How We Work

**We place great value on a vibrant, inspiring, and challenging company culture. This is achieved through a talented and passionate team that believes in achieving great things together.

We value curiosity and the generosity to bring other people along. If you find something useful, show us. If an experiment fails, we’d like to hear about that too.

We believe that ownership is what brings us the best teams – you can expect a lot of freedom and responsibility. The key is open communication, trust, and a shared passion to transform the legal world.

We are a growing team based in Copenhagen, Hamburg, London and Zurich. This role will be based in our Copenhagen HQ.

**What we offer

**

• Competitive compensation + an attractive warrant program

• A collaborative work environment where your input is not only valued but often implemented within hours

• A central office in Copenhagen, where you can work closely with an ambitious and growing team

• International team events – last time we went to Barcelona, and we’d love to have you join us next time

• 25 vacation days per year + public holidays

• Your own Pleo card for necessary work expenses

• Paid parental leave

**Pandektes is an equal opportunity employer

**_We believe diverse teams build better products and stronger teams. We embrace and encourage people from all backgrounds to apply regardless of race/ethnicity, colour, religion, nationality, gender, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, socio-economic status, culture or beliefs.

jobs.occupation: Optimizing grazing management for biodiversity in semi-natural habitats: evidence from monitoring, remote sensing and field experiments
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Ecoscience programme. The position is available from 1 March 2027.

Research area and project description:

How can grazing management be optimized to benefit both biodiversity and nature-based beef production? This PhD project will address this question through analyses of long-term biodiversity monitoring data, development of digital biodiversity indicators, and field experiments in Danish semi-natural habitats.

Grazing is a key ecological process in many ecosystems. However, biodiversity outcomes depend on how grazing is managed, including grazing intensity and timing. Despite its widespread use as a conservation tool, important knowledge gaps remain regarding which grazing strategies deliver the greatest biodiversity benefits and how these outcomes can be documented in a robust and scalable way.

The PhD project is part of the interdisciplinary Nature&Beef initiative and will combine ecology, biodiversity monitoring, remote sensing and data science. The selected candidate will work with unique datasets from the Danish national biodiversity monitoring programme (NOVANA), field experiments, drone imagery and other digital monitoring approaches.

The project will focus on four interconnected themes:

• 
Identifying grazing practices associated with positive biodiversity outcomes using long-term monitoring data.

• 
Evaluating the effects of grazing intensity and grazing season on biodiversity in a large-scale field experiment.

• 
Developing and validating image-based indicators of vegetation structure and biodiversity condition from field and drone imagery.

• 
Contributing to the development of AI-based methods for mapping vegetation and habitat condition from drone images.

The project offers an opportunity to contribute to evidence-based conservation and the development of practical tools that can support land managers, farmers, conservation practitioners and value-chain actors in documenting biodiversity outcomes. The findings will help build a stronger scientific foundation for biodiversity-friendly grazing practices and nature-based beef production.

Qualifications and specific competences:

Applicants to the PhD position must have a Master’s degree (120 ECTS) in biology or equivalent. The applicants have documented experience in botanical surveys including species identification skills of North-European flora. The applicant must have a driver license applicable in Denmark. Demonstrated proficiency in data management and analysis, image analysis, and experience using R.

Place of employment and place of work:

The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is C.F. Møllers Allé 8, building 1110, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark.

Contacts:

Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:

• Senior researcher, head of section Camilla Fløjgaard, e-mail: camf@ecos.au.dk (main supervisor)

For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:

• admission.gradschool.tech@au.dk

How to apply:

Please follow this link to submit your application.

Application deadline is 1 December 2026 23:59 CET.

Preferred starting date is 1 March 2027.

For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Please note:

• Only documents received prior to the application deadline will be evaluated. Thus, documents sent after deadline will not be considered.

• The programme committee may request further information or invite the applicant to attend an interview.

• Shortlisting will be used, which means that the evaluation committee only will evaluate the most relevant applications.

Formalities and salary range

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8. As a PhD fellow you will also receive a monthly non-pensionable allowance.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via the online recruitment system, which can be accessed under ‘How to apply’.

jobs.occupation: Senior Manager, Clinical Trial Disclosure & Transparency
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**Job Description

**Genmab is committed to transparency of clinical trial research. We recognize the scientific and ethical value of sharing clinical trial information in a non-biased and timely manner to benefit patients and other external stakeholders. The Clinical Trial Disclosure & Transparency (CTD&T) team resides within Clinical Trial Delivery, which hosts key functions for ensuring successful conduct and reporting of clinical trials.

We are now looking for a new Senior Manager to join our CTD&T team. The role offers a meaningful blend of operational and strategic tasks in a collaborative environment where quality, shared purpose, and cross-functional support are central to how we work.

In the role as Senior Manager of CTD&T, you will be executing against the global and national disclosure regulations and requirements across the entire Genmab portfolio. This role engages with internal and external stakeholders to ensure consistent and responsible disclosure and transparency practices. The position requires strong expertise in disclosure requirements and regulatory processes, coupled with strong organizational and communication skills, while maintaining a commitment to quality, integrity, and advancing Genmab’s mission.

Do you get excited by the shape of a whole world: the districts, the landmarks, the routes between them, and the little details that make a place feel lived in? Then you might be exactly who we're looking for.

Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by a simple mission: to make everyone laugh.

We're growing! Triband is working on our most ambitious project to date: a new systemic open-world game built around a beloved IP, with our own spin on it. A bold new direction for us! And we're just getting started. Now we're looking for a Senior World Designer to plan, prototype, and build this world. You'll shape the big picture (the areas, how they connect, and how players find their way around) and work hands-on in the engine to bring it to life together with artists, designers, and the rest of your team. If maps and dots and their connections make you happy, you’ll probably like what comes next.

**Here's What You'll Do Day To Day

**

• Plan the world and lead its conceptualization, keeping a clear overview and vision for the whole map and for each new area before we start building it

• Create distinct spaces, biomes, and sections of the world (grounded in the real world), working closely with the art team to make each one feel unique

• Collaborate with artists and your team on environmental storytelling that gives each region its own identity

• Design how players navigate the world, using landmarks and the systems behind them

• Establish and maintain the world-creation pipeline, workflows, and hierarchy structures

• Work with developers on the tools that help build the world, such as traffic networks

• Gather needs from across the team and make sure they land in the right places in the world

• Build and implement hands-on in the engine like the rest of the team

**You're a great match if

**

• You have extensive in-engine experience. We use Unity, so that's preferred, but experience with other engines works too

• You've worked as a world or level designer on an open-world game as part of a team, and you know the common pitfalls of open-world design

• You have a strong macro-level design approach, balancing ideas and needs from different team members to create spaces that are believable, navigable, and fun

• You have experience establishing and maintaining detailed world and content documentation, and you like maps and spreadsheets

• A tidy hierarchy makes you happy, and you keep the small details and the big picture in view at the same time

• “Let’s try it out” is your favorite way to solve a problem

• You iterate on your work and stay open to changing it as the project evolves

• Balancing the needs of artists, designers, and programmers is a puzzle you enjoy rather than a chore

**Nice to have

**

• You enjoy building moment-to-moment, concrete level design too

• You can make people see a space before it exists, through a mood board, a rough walkthrough, or the story of a player’s first hour there

• You have an interest in urban planning and/or architecture

• You keep up with industry norms in open-world games

• You're drawn to casual, family-friendly, quirky universe building and storytelling

• You have experience prototyping mini games and activities

**What Always Matters To Us At Triband

**

• You thrive in taking ownership of your area: you spot problems, seek advice when needed, and implement creative solutions that push projects forward.

• You're motivated by collaboration, mutual respect, inclusiveness, and creativity, and you actively contribute to sustaining that culture.

• You believe games are made by teams, not solo rockstars, and that good ideas can come from anyone.

• You bring curiosity, generosity, and flexibility, along with strong opinions, especially when they come with reasoning, openness, and a willingness to actually test them.

• You're up for experimentation, and at the same time you don't get too precious when the experience tells you you're wrong.

• You value a positive work environment and contribute to keeping the studio a fun and supportive place.

**Practicalities

**

• We work on-site at our cozy office in central Copenhagen.

• This role is based in the Greater Copenhagen area, and we're not offering relocation for this one.

• We work a 37-hour work week, with core hours 10-15, and the freedom to start and finish anywhere between 7 and 18.

• Our working language is English.

• Most importantly: no crunch. People over deadlines.

**We offer

**

• A shot at shaping the world of a live game played by millions

• A tight, collaborative team where your ideas actually make it into the game

• A playful work environment where trying the silly idea is encouraged

• Friendly and kind colleagues who love making each other laugh as much as making games

• A professional development budget to invest in your growth

• Social activities like Friday bars, hobby nights, board game nights, and whatever else Tribanders turn into a tradition

• Daily lunch at a local restaurant, with plant-based options and soft ice on Thursdays

• Pension plan and private health insurance

• Child's first sick day on us, no questions asked

• Endless amounts of Cocio

jobs.occupation: Optimizing grazing management for biodiversity in semi-natural habitats evidence from monitoring, remote sensing and field experiments
jobs.description:
Optimizing grazing management for biodiversity in semi-natural habitats: evidence from monitoring, remote sensing and field experiments
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Ecoscience programme. The position is available from 1 March 2027.

Title:
Optimizing grazing management for biodiversity in semi-natural habitats: evidence from monitoring, remote sensing and field experiments

Research area and project description:
How can grazing management be optimized to benefit both biodiversity and nature-based beef production? This PhD project will address this question through analyses of long-term biodiversity monitoring data, development of digital biodiversity indicators, and field experiments in Danish semi-natural habitats.

Grazing is a key ecological process in many ecosystems. However, biodiversity outcomes depend on how grazing is managed, including grazing intensity and timing. Despite its widespread use as a conservation tool, important knowledge gaps remain regarding which grazing strategies deliver the greatest biodiversity benefits and how these outcomes can be documented in a robust and scalable way.

The PhD project is part of the interdisciplinary Nature&Beef initiative and will combine ecology, biodiversity monitoring, remote sensing and data science. The selected candidate will work with unique datasets from the Danish national biodiversity monitoring programme (NOVANA), field experiments, drone imagery and other digital monitoring approaches.

The project will focus on four interconnected themes:
1) Identifying grazing practices associated with positive biodiversity outcomes using long-term monitoring data.
2) Evaluating the effects of grazing intensity and grazing season on biodiversity in a large-scale field experiment.
3) Developing and validating image-based indicators of vegetation structure and biodiversity condition from field and drone imagery.
4) Contributing to the development of AI-based methods for mapping vegetation and habitat condition from drone images.

The project offers an opportunity to contribute to evidence-based conservation and the development of practical tools that can support land managers, farmers, conservation practitioners and value-chain actors in documenting biodiversity outcomes. The findings will help build a stronger scientific foundation for biodiversity-friendly grazing practices and nature-based beef production.

Qualifications and specific competences:
Applicants to the PhD position must have a Master’s degree (120 ECTS) in biology or equivalent. The applicants have documented experience in botanical surveys including species identification skills of North-European flora. The applicant must have a driver license applicable in Denmark. Demonstrated proficiency in data management and analysis, image analysis, and experience using R.

Place of employment and place of work:
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is C.F. Møllers Allé 8, building 1110, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher(s) in Digital Media, Computational Methods and Democracy
jobs.description:
The Department of Communication and Arts at Roskilde University invites applications for one or two postdoctoral position(s) in a new research project on digital media and the conditions for democratic debate. The position is a full-time appointment for 24 months, starting on 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

We welcome candidates with backgrounds in digital methods, computational social science, science and technology studies (STS), sociology, communication studies, political communication, media studies, information studies, digital humanities, or related fields in the humanities and social sciences.

About the project
The postdoc position is associated with an ambitious three-year project funded by the Politiken Foundation (Politiken-Fonden) through its largest ever research initiative, which seeks to investigate how digital technologies are shaping democratic debate. You will be part of a team researching how digital news media, search engines, social media, and AI chatbots present pressing issues in Danish public debate. Our central concern is the scope of public issues as they are represented online, how this varies between platforms and between people's actual online experiences, and how digital media shape the range of perspectives citizens encounter. While much research and public debate focuses on misinformation, disinformation, polarisation and hate speech, another fundamental question is whether digital media expose us to a sufficiently diverse range of actors, arguments, and viewpoints to support a productive democratic conversation. Do digital platforms broaden the range of concerns and perspectives that can enter democratic debate, or do they narrow the ways in which public issues are represented and understood?

The project will answer this by developing two complementary research tools:

• The Democratic Debate Meter: A public-facing digital tool that systematically tracks and compares how selected public issues — such as hybrid warfare, agricultural taxation, health services, or school reform — are represented across digital platforms. Using computational digital methods, including text analysis and simulated searches, we investigate which actors and topics become visible.
• The Live Data Donation Lab: A participatory research initiative that combines data donations with browser-based capture of digital content. Working with citizens, journalists, and policymakers, we investigate how personalised digital environments shape people's encounters with and sensemaking around public issues and involve participants in interpreting findings and developing our analytical approach.
By combining computational analysis with qualitative and participatory methods, the project aims to advance research on digital media and democracy. We are focused on producing publicly accessible findings, reports and tools that contribute to wider debates about the role of digital platforms in democratic life, while also contributing to cutting edge academic research at the highest international level.

The position
As a postdoctoral researcher, you will play a central role in the project's research activities, working closely with the project leaders and other team members. You will contribute to the collection and analysis of digital data, the development of methods for comparing representations of public issues across platforms, and the interpretation and communication of findings. Depending on your background and interests, there will be opportunities to contribute to computational text analysis, methodological development, public-facing data visualizations, qualitative research, participatory workshops and public dissemination. You will also contribute to the project's research publications and its public-facing outputs, including the Debate Meter and reports on the scope of issue representation across digital media.

The position offers an opportunity to develop an independent research profile while collaborating on a bold interdisciplinary project that connects methodological innovation with an important question for contemporary democracy. You will be part of an enthusiastic and supportive research environment at Roskilde University, with opportunities to participate in international conferences, workshops and research collaborations. In recent years, faculty have enjoyed a highly successful record of obtaining research grants for large national and international projects broadly focused on questions around digitalisation and democracy, meaning you will be joining a department where young and senior scholars are actively collaborating on a number of ambitious research initiatives in these areas.

The position is based at the Department of Communication and Arts, with affiliation to the Centre for Digital Citizenship and the Digital Media Lab. You will work closely with the project leader, Associate Professor Andreas Birkbak, and the co-investigator Professor Chris Peters.

Qualifications
We are looking for a researcher who is curious about how digital technologies shape public debate and who is interested in developing innovative ways to study these processes. Applicants must hold a PhD, or expect to obtain one by the time of appointment, in a relevant field within social science, the humanities, or data science.We are particularly interested in candidates who bring some combination of the following:

• Computational and digital methods: Experience with, or a strong interest in developing, computational approaches to digital data, especially text analysis and digital trace data and the comparative analysis of online content. Experience with qualitative, participatory or interpretive methods is also an advantage.
• Research on media and democracy: An interest in how digital media shape public debate, democratic participation and the visibility of different actors, issues and perspectives.
• Theoretical and methodological breadth: Familiarity with relevant approaches in STS, digital methods, media and communication studies, platform studies, controversy mapping, or related fields.
• Research communication: An interest in communicating research beyond academia, including through public reports, digital visualisations, workshops, or engagement with journalists and other societal actors.
• Good command of Danish is essential, as the project analyses Danish-language media content and public debate. Good command of English is also required, including the ability to write and publish research in English.
We do not expect candidates to be equally experienced in all these areas. We welcome applicants with complementary profiles who can contribute their own expertise while developing new skills through collaboration with the project team.

Responsibilities
The successful candidate(s) will be expected to:

• Contribute actively to the design and implementation of the project's research activities.
• Collect, process and analyse digital media data, including contributing to computational text analysis.
• Develop and apply analytical methods, in dialogue with the project's theoretical and empirical concerns.
• Contribute to research publications, both independently and in collaboration with the project team.
• Help communicate research to wider audiences through reports, digital outputs and other activities.
• Participate in workshops, conferences and collaborations with academic and non-academic partners.
• Contribute to the department's collegial and interdisciplinary research environment.
Assessment
In assessing applicants, particular consideration will be given to:

• The relevance and quality of the applicant's research experience and publications
• Potential for contributing to computational and digital methods and methodological innovation.
• The applicant's established theoretical and empirical interests on digital media and democracy.
• Experience with interdisciplinary collaboration and communicating research to wider audiences.
• Potential to contribute to the project and to the wider research environment at Roskilde University.
Further information
For further information about the position or the project, please contact the project leader Associate Professor Andreas Birkbak, at andreasbi@ruc.dk or +45 28 79 93 16. We expect job interviews to be held in February 2027.

The position will be filled according to the Agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC) and Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. 

According to the Pay Transparency Directive, the salary ranges for the various job categories at Roskilde University are listed here. 

Application procedure 
After the deadline for applications the Head of Department will shortlist applicants for assessment with assistance from the recruitment committee including the chairperson of the assessment committee.

Shortly after the application deadline all applicants will be notified whether or not their application has been selected for assessment.

The shortlisted applicants will be informed about the composition of the assessment committee, and each applicant will be given the opportunity to comment on the composition of the committee and - later on - their assessment.

Once the recruitment process is completed, all applicants will be informed of the outcome of their application.

Application 
To apply for the position go to www.ruc.dk/en/job/ 

Only applications in English are accepted. 

Applications must include: 

1. Cover letter 

2. CV 

3. Documentation of education 

4. A complete list of publications

5. A maximum of 5 relevant scientific works that you want included in the assessment 

If any of the publications that you want included in the assessment are the result of a joint effort, the extent and the nature of your contribution to each individual work must then be clarified in a co-author statement (find template here) 

6. If duties include teaching: Teaching portfolio (read more about teaching portfolio at Roskilde University here)

Please submit your application no later than January 10, 2027.

Material received after this date will not be taken into consideration. 

Roskilde University wishes to reflect the diversity of society and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background. 

The hiring process at Roskilde University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.
