Build software at scale. Influence how we build it. Help shape the next generation of development at Dalux.

Dalux is growing, and we are looking for experienced software developers who want significant technical ownership while continuing to build software hands-on.

You will work on products used by professionals around the world, contribute to architectural and technical decisions, and help us improve how we develop software – including how we use agentic AI to make capable developers more effective.

Your role

As an Experienced Software Developer, you will take ownership of complex product and technical problems from idea to production.

You will work in a product team with other developers, a Product Manager, and a Product Designer. We expect experienced developers to contribute beyond their individual tasks by making good technical decisions, improving our architecture and development practices, and sharing knowledge with others.

Your work can include:

• Owning complex features and technical problems end-to-end

• Designing scalable, maintainable solutions and contributing to architectural decisions

• Improving our codebase, tooling, developer workflows, and technical quality

• Driving or contributing to initiatives around DevOps, CI/CD, infrastructure, architecture, or developer tooling

• Sparring with and mentoring other developers

• Working closely with Product Management and Design to understand problems and find the right solutions

• Bringing new ideas and technologies into Dalux when they can improve our products or how we build them

We expect experienced developers to have opinions, challenge existing solutions, and be comfortable having their own ideas challenged in return.

Developing software with agentic AI

We are significantly increasing our use of agentic AI in software development.

We use and explore AI across the development lifecycle – from understanding problems and navigating codebases to implementation, testing, debugging, refactoring, and review.

We are looking for developers who already use agentic AI as part of their development workflow. The specific tools matter less than how you use them: providing the right context and direction, critically evaluating the output, and knowing when to intervene or take a different approach.

Strong engineering fundamentals remain essential. AI can increase what a capable developer can achieve, but you remain responsible for the architecture, correctness, maintainability, and quality of the software you build.

At Dalux, you will help us take these ways of working further by experimenting, sharing what works, and helping establish effective practices for agentic software development.

Technologies we work with

Our platform is built on a distributed cloud architecture using AWS. Our primary technologies include:

• C# / .NET

• Angular / TypeScript

• GitHub Copilot

• MSSQL

• Elasticsearch

• AWS

• Optionally, Android / iOS development using .NET MAUI

You may also encounter parts of our C++ codebase.

Experience with our exact technology stack is useful, but strong software engineering fundamentals and the ability to understand and improve complex systems matter more.

Product development at Dalux

Our developers do more than implement specifications.

Developers, Product Managers, and Product Designers work together to understand problems and find solutions that balance user value, usability, technical feasibility, business viability, and long-term technical health.

Our products are relied upon by professionals worldwide, making performance, stability, maintainability, and quality important parts of everyday engineering.

Your background

We expect that you:

• Have solid professional software development experience

• Have at least six months of practical experience using agentic AI as part of your software development workflow

• Hold a university degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, IT, or a related technical field

• Have strong software engineering fundamentals

• Are comfortable owning complex technical problems and decisions

• Can navigate and improve an established codebase and architecture

• Care about maintainability, reliability, performance, and quality

• Enjoy technical sparring and sharing knowledge with other developers

• Understand the trade-offs between short-term delivery and long-term technical quality

Experience with C#/.NET, Angular, or cloud development is useful, but we do not expect you to match every technology we use.

What You Can Expect From Dalux

Dalux is a software company at heart. As an experienced developer, you can expect:

• Significant ownership and real influence on technical solutions

• Skilled colleagues who enjoy technical discussion and constructive challenge

• Close collaboration between Engineering, Product Management, and Design

• Short paths from ideas to decisions and implementation

• Opportunities to improve engineering practices beyond your immediate product work

• An environment actively investing in agentic AI for software development

• High levels of trust and freedom in how you solve problems

jobs.occupation: Event & Experience Manager – Bring Axlab’s customer experiences to life
jobs.description:
Can you turn a showroom visit, a reference site tour or an industry exhibition into an experience that makes a lasting impression?

In collaboration with Actief Hartmanns, Axlab is looking for an Event & Experience Manager who combines creative design with hands-on delivery and a clear commercial focus.

In the position you will own Axlab’s customer-facing experience programme: reference site visits, the headquarters showroom, Axlab Academy, and industry exhibitions. This is an opportunity to combine concept development with practical execution, shaping how visitors experience Axlab’s solutions and building the calendar, materials and processes that ensure consistent quality and continuity.

Your role goes beyond logistics: you will design welcoming, relevant experiences that help visitors understand how Axlab’s solutions work in practice. You will also build the calendar, materials and documented processes that make the programme consistent, scalable, and less dependent on any one individual.

You will be part of the Marcom team and work closely with Sales, Product Management, and external partners. Together with the Graphic Designer & Event Coordinator, you will translate ideas into a strong exhibition presence and cohesive creative execution.

What you will take ownership of

• 
Develop and deliver reference site visits, showroom tours, Academy days and exhibitions that connect customer needs with Axlab’s automated pathology workflows.

• 
Establish and continually improve the showroom experience and reference site concept for prospective and existing customers.

• 
Manage programmes and events from concept to delivery, aligning internal teams, external agencies, and production partners.

• 
Build and maintain the activity calendar, supporting materials, briefings, and documented processes.

• 
Manage suppliers, budgets, and negotiations, with close attention to production details and on-site logistics.

• 
Track event performance and work with Sales and within Marcom to ensure effective lead handling and handover.

• 
Help support the development of a sustainable webinar approach that contributes to sales opportunities.

What you bring

You have at least five years of experience in event management, experiential marketing, or customer experience, ideally combining large-scale exhibitions with smaller, hosted experiences. Exhibition or trade show experience is essential, together with relevant experience from the medical device industry. You can demonstrate that you have designed and delivered premium customer or partner experiences, not simply coordinated the logistics.

• 
A bachelor’s degree or higher in marketing, communications, business, hospitality, or event management, or equivalent experience.

• 
Experience establishing and improving a showroom for a company providing anatomic pathology equipment or a medical device company.

• 
Experience developing and refining reference site concepts for prospective and existing customers.

• 
Strong end-to-end project management skills and the ability to collaborate with Sales, Product Management, and external partners.

• 
Experience managing vendors, suppliers, and budgets, including negotiations with agencies and production partners.

• 
Confidence reporting on event performance, handling leads and coordinates their handover.

• 
Fluency in English. Danish is an advantage when working with headquarters and the local reference site network.

Experience developing a webinar strategy that generates sales opportunities is a plus. Alternatively, you are comfortable learning this skill quickly, as you will work closely with your future colleagues in Marcom on this.

Regular travel should be expected, and in busy periods, this can be 50% or more.

A thoughtful host with a hands-on mindset

You make people feel genuinely welcome and adapt naturally to different visitors and situations. You stay calm when plans change, take pride in the details and are just as comfortable shaping an experience concept as managing the on-site logistics. Open and approachable, you build trust with colleagues, suppliers and senior stakeholders, communicate clear briefs, and know who needs which information — and when.

You bring creativity, initiative and a collaborative approach. You are curious about what works, use data and feedback to improve the programme and look for ways to make each visit or event meaningful rather than routine.

Axlab’s Marcom team works to build recognition of the Axlab brand for bringing innovation and automation to pathology laboratories in its direct markets. Through consistent brand storytelling, impactful events, customer experiences and digital channels, the team connects colleagues and customers with that ambition. In this role, you will have ownership of the experiences that show what it means in practice.

What we offer

We are a small yet ambitious growth company where our shared values — Decency, Innovation, Commitment, and Responsibility — form the foundation of everything we do. We offer a flexible, hybrid, and trust-based full-time position where you will have influence on both your own role and the continued development of our Marcom function . Occasional travel activity must be expected as part of the role.

• 
Competitive salary and employment conditions

• 
A highly visible role with direct access to senior leadership

• 
Influence on business decisions and strategic initiatives

• 
Professional and personal development opportunities

• 
An international and collaborative working environment

• 
Welcoming and comfortable office space with everyday perks including free refreshments and daily lunch buffet

• 
Social activities and annual global events

Does it excite you to work with complex inventory flows, including cross-border movements and transactions, and the indirect tax implications, such as VAT, that follow them? Your main contribution will be a robust financial, operations, tax and internal controls framework relevant to Zealand Pharma, leading to a successful external audit.

The position combines hands-on accounting with process ownership, giving you the opportunity to shape how financial operations scale in a growing biotechnology company. Besides owning these day-to-day areas, you will also take a big part in our SAF-T and ViDA reporting readiness project. You will work closely with colleagues in Finance and across the organization.

**

• Own inventory accounting, including valuation, cost accounting and period-end reconciliations

• Manage tax and VAT accounting, including reconciliations, reporting and compliance support

• Take a leading part in our SAF-T and ViDA reporting readiness, from process design and implementation through to optimization

• Oversee bank and treasury accounting, including cash, foreign exchange and investment transactions

• Manage intercompany accounting, including transactions and recharges

• Take part in building and continuously improve a robust financial operations, tax and internal controls framework

**Your profile

You find it an exciting challenge to build and keep an overview of the VAT setup in the countries where Zealand Pharma operates, you are curious about each country's rules, and you take satisfaction in setting up processes that keep the company compliant in all countries. You work independently as well as across teams, and you communicate clearly with colleagues who are not finance specialists.

• Relevant accounting experience, preferably from life sciences

• Hands-on experience with inventory, tax and VAT, bank and treasury, and intercompany accounting

• Experience from implementing and optimizing finance processes, ideally in connection with SAF-T, ViDA or similar tax reporting requirements

• Proficiency in ERP systems, preferably D365, and advanced Excel skills

• Analytical skills and fluent written and spoken English

**Your new team

We work closely with colleagues across the organization and take pride in clear processes, strong controls and continuous improvement.

Let’s bond and be bold

Making bonds is at the core of everything we do. From discovering and developing the best new peptide drugs for patients, to engaging with our partners or connecting with each other. We bond through curiosity and playfulness as a team, allowing ourselves to challenge common thinking and drive future innovation. Join us and let’s bond and be bold

**Zealand Pharma A/S (Nasdaq: ZEAL) is a biotechnology company focused on advancing medicines for obesity and metabolic health. Combining more than 25 years of peptide R&D expertise with a proprietary data platform that leverages advanced datadriven and AI/ML approaches, Zealand Pharma aims to lead a new era in obesity and metabolic health. **Rewards/Benefits

**

Kolding

Energy is our contribution to quality of life – day after day. With around 21,000 colleagues Vattenfall provides comprehensive electricity and heating offerings to several million customers in northern Europe. For the work ahead we need people who are fully dedicated to our customers and to a sustainable society – people like you.

Company Description

Vattenfall is a leading European energy company driving the transition to a sustainable energy system. We have been electrifying industries, powering homes and transforming life through innovation for more than 100 years. We employ around 21 000 people mostly in our core markets in Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, and the UK.

Business Area Wind is responsible for Vattenfall’s Onshore and Offshore Wind as well as other renewable activities such as solar PV and batteries. We develop, construct and operate wind generation and we have a clear strategy to develop our solar PV and battery operations further.

At Aalborg University, The Technical Faculty of IT and Design, Department of Architecture, Design and Media Technology (Copenhagen Campus) a full-time position as Postdoc is available for a period of 2 years from February 1, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The Department of Architecture, Design, and Media Technology has as its goal the development of an innovative cluster of engineering-based environments for education and research which integrate creativity, engineering and technology within the disciplines of architecture, urban design, industrial design, lighting design, digital design and interactive media. The department is a leading research and educational environment in Denmark that addresses the challenge of the interplay between creativity and technology and develops new areas in research and education directed towards the end-user.

Your work tasks    The successful candidate will contribute to research, supervision, teaching, and semester coordination within Lighting Design at the Department of Architecture, Design and Media Technology, Aalborg University, Copenhagen.

Research activities will be conducted with the transdisciplinary Lighting Design Lab and will primarily contribute to externally funded research projects addressing societal challenges through lighting design, technology, and human-centric approaches.

Supervision responsibilities will primarily be associated with the MSc program in Lighting Design, which includes approximately 60 international students. Students work in project groups on semester-based lighting design projects and individually or in groups on master theses. The projects are grounded in a strong understanding of design-research processes and integrate theories, methods, and approaches across relevant academic disciplines. The position will also include coordination of semesters and related educational activities.

Teaching will primarily focus on the engineering and technical aspects of lighting design, particularly within courses such as Lighting Fundamentals and Evidence-Based Lighting Design. Topics include fundamental photometric and colorimetric concepts, lighting laws and principles, measurement quantities and methods, international standards, and objective methods for the measurement, observation, analysis, and evaluation of lighting conditions.

**Your competencies

**The successful candidate is expected to demonstrate the ability to identify emerging societal challenges and translate them into future competence and skill requirements for the lighting design profession. The candidate should also demonstrate an understanding of how these competences and skills can be integrated into teaching and research in lighting design at the highest academic level.

The candidate should demonstrate the ability to attract external research funding and to lead or contribute to interdisciplinary research projects involving multiple partners and stakeholders. Experience with innovation and cross-sector collaboration between academia, industry, and public-sector organizations is considered particularly relevant.

The candidate must have experience in relevant teaching and supervising diverse student groups, with a focus on developing an understanding of transdisciplinary design processes supported by relevant technical skills and a strong scientific foundation.

The candidate must demonstrate strong collaborative skills and the ability to work effectively as part of an international and interdisciplinary team of lighting designers, architects, engineers, and other researchers within the Lighting Design Lab in Copenhagen.

Who we are

The Lighting Design Lab brings together lighting designers, engineers, architects, and researchers who work collaboratively to advance teaching and research in lighting design. The Lab supports a two-year international MSc programme in Lighting Design and a strong transdisciplinary research environment.

Our work integrates architecture, engineering, AI, and media technology and is often conducted in collaboration with private-sector partners to address relevant societal challenges. Research and experimental activities combine contextual and architectural analysis of the light environment, including daylight and electric lighting, with consideration of human visual and non-visual needs and dynamic lighting conditions.

Design solutions are based on a perceived understanding of light environments supported by advanced technologies such as lighting control, sensing systems, sky scanners, and smartphone-based applications, while remaining grounded in human and societal needs. The Lab also maintains a strong international network and collaborates with leading universities and research environments within lighting design.

You may read more about the department here: https://www.create.aau.dk/om-create

Qualification requirements Appointment as postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level.

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma)

• List of publications, with an indication of the attached publications that you wish to be taken into account in the assessment. You may attach a maximum of five publications.

• Documentation of teaching qualifications if relevant.

• Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc.

• Additional qualifications in relation to the position

• References/recommendations

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. International staff are encouraged, with support from the university, to learn Danish during their employment in order to support their integration into the workplace and Danish society.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact associate professor Ellen Kathrine Hansen, ekh@create.aau.dk Phone: 0045 21723181

Further information

Read more about our recruitment process here

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Salary and terms of employment  The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Postdoc”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

About Userlink

Userlink runs AI agents in production at several hundred Nordic webshops, including Bahne, XL-BYG, Coolshop and Bygma. The agents handle the customer dialogue before and after the purchase, and every conversation ends up as structured data on demand and purchase barriers. The team is based in Odense.

The product and the direction

Today we sell chat. Email is rolling out now, and phone and social follow. On top of that we are building the brain: a system that brings together every signal about a webshop and its customers, understands why people buy, and why they do not, and acts on it while the buyer is still on the page. The effect is measured against a control group, so the shop can see what it means for revenue.

That moves the sale from a customer service tool to a conversation about growth, and revenue per customer can become several times what it is today.

The role

Ownership of the entire go-to-market in one place: lead generation, new business, partners and existing customers. You run the process from first contact to signature, find out what works and write the sales process the rest of the company will follow.

Lead generation is yours as a minimum. You own where the meetings come from: the customer profile, the lead lists and the sourcing of the right webshops, outbound and the campaigns that have to fill the pipeline. You measure what a meeting costs to acquire and which channels carry, and you shut down the ones that do not. You build it yourself at first and set direction for marketing and meeting booking as they come on board.

The partner channel has to be built. Agencies and platform partners need to be found, judged realistically and sold alongside until they can do it on their own.

Growth in the existing customer base is part of it, especially as email, phone and the brain roll out, measured against clear monthly and quarterly targets.

Price, pitch, customer profile and process are yours. They change when they do not work, and the team is built as the numbers allow. Denmark is home turf, but we already have customers and partners in DACH and the Netherlands, and those markets grow from here.

Decisions are made on arguments, not titles. Ideas get challenged regardless of where they come from, and the best one wins.

Why founding

You do not step into a finished sales organisation. You build the commercial side together with the founder, and what you decide on price, pitch, process and the first hires is what Userlink will sell on for years.

That is why the role comes with equity. You help build the company, and you own part of what you build. In return we expect you to take responsibility like a co-owner, also when things are unclear or go wrong.

Profile

• Has built sales in a B2B SaaS company as one of the first salespeople, with own meetings and own closes

• Has built lead generation from scratch, through outbound, partners or marketing, and knows what pipeline costs to acquire

• Has had a budget and hit it, and can explain in detail how

• Sells personally and teaches others to do it at the same time

• Experience selling outside Denmark, and a feel for what changes when you do

• Strong product and technology understanding, and uses AI every day in their own work

• Danish at native level, confident on calls, in meetings and in demos

• Fluent English is mandatory. English is the office language at Userlink

The person

• Dreams of owning and building a company

• Ideally has tried starting something and knows what it takes

• Thinks like a founder, not an employee

• Happily gives more than a regular job asks for, because it is fun

• Says things as they are, and can take the same in return

• Takes ownership and looks for solutions rather than excuses

• Curious, learns fast and has a positive mindset

What we offer

• Competitive salary plus uncapped commission

• Equity

• Short decision paths and close collaboration with product and engineering

• Office at Storms Pakhus in Odense, where we are every day

Application process

We take the time it takes to find the right match.

• Introductory conversation

• Conversation about expectations and terms

Write to jobs@userlink.ai about a SaaS product you helped scale, where the meetings came from, and what you personally did to make it happen.

jobs.occupation: Senior Software Engineer — Wealth Management Systems
jobs.description:
_Please do not contact us or apply if you are a recruiter, consultant, or outsourcing company.

_Join a team of fintech heroes! 🚀

Performativ is changing the way investment advisors and financial institutions operate. We are building a modern platform for portfolio management, reporting, compliance, trading, and client engagement—replacing fragmented systems, manual workflows, and technology built for another era.

Our customers include wealth managers, asset managers, family offices, and financial institutions across Europe and beyond. We are on an ambitious scaling journey, supported by leading global venture capital investors, and are working to become the platform on which modern wealth management runs.

You can read more about our product at performativ.com.

As our new Senior Software Engineer — Wealth Management Systems 📈

You will help the team solve some of the hardest product and data problems across Performativ’s investment platform.

You will work where financial workflows, product decisions, and technical systems meet: portfolio data, reporting, fees, reconciliation, instruments, transactions, cash, performance, and trading. Your contribution will be turning that complexity into coherent solutions that work across customers rather than becoming a collection of one-off customisations.

This is not a narrowly scoped position. We work as one team, and you should be willing to tackle any important problem within our area.

• You will apply deep experience from wealth management, asset management, private banking, portfolio management, investment operations, trading, custody, or related financial infrastructure to develop sound product and system designs.

• You will investigate problems that cross financial data, calculations, APIs, integrations, operational processes, and production systems—determining their root causes and delivering reliable solutions that others can understand and extend.

• You will bring product thinking to ambiguous requirements, working closely with users and customer-facing colleagues to distinguish reusable platform needs from customer-specific preferences.

• You will use AI agents to produce much of the implementation. We expect you to design the solution, direct agents effectively, challenge their assumptions, review their output, and establish the tests and evidence needed for safe production deployment.

• You will lead when your knowledge makes you the right person to lead, follow through on what you take on, contribute to the work of others, and help teammates succeed.

Experience with performance calculations, valuations, fees, reporting, reconciliation, corporate actions, or portfolio-management systems would be particularly valuable.

We value your passion 🔥

At Performativ, we are builders first. We have ambitious goals and value the time, judgment, and effort people put into their work. You will be trusted to make your mark and help shape how we solve difficult problems.

We do not divide the platform into personal territories. People develop deeper context in different areas, but we solve problems as a team. Autonomy works only when paired with initiative, collaboration, sound judgment, and follow-through.

AI increases our delivery speed, but it does not reduce our engineering standard or our accountability for the result. You must be technically strong enough to recognise weak abstractions, incorrect assumptions, missing edge cases, security problems, and unsafe production behaviour.

This role is based in Copenhagen. We work together primarily from our city-centre office, with flexibility to work from home when it makes sense. You should already be based in Copenhagen or be ready to relocate.

What we can offer you 🌱

• Trust and meaningful responsibility from your first day, with the opportunity to influence both our platform and how we build it.

• Difficult and consequential problems involving financial data, product design, reliability, security, and real operational workflows.

• The opportunity to define an AI-native approach to developing complex financial software and see your work reach customers quickly.

• An ambitious, collaborative team with experience from leading technology companies, consultancies, and financial institutions.

• Strong opportunities for professional development as Performativ grows into a European market leader.

**About 3Shape

**Things have moved fast at 3Shape ever since our founding in 2000. 3Shape specializes in developing 3D scanning and software technology solutions that enable dental and hearing professionals to treat more people more effectively, and with improved care. Every second of every day, a 3Shape scanner is used all around the globe. A number which is skyrocketing and cementing our position as technology and industry leader, Danish growth comet and unicorn company. We are a truly international workplace with 50+ nationalities and more than 2200 employees globally. We are headquartered in Denmark in the center of vibrant Copenhagen at Kongens Nytorv.

**About The 3Shape 2-Year Graduate Program

**3Shape’s two-year Graduate Program serves as a launchpad for a high-impact career. Graduates rotate through three different departments within the Technical Track, with the possibility of an international assignment. This program gives talented and motivated young professionals the chance to acquire new knowledge, expand their skillset, and gain valuable expertise from the very beginning. Graduates gain unique insights into the core of our business and play an essential role in our strategy to develop future leaders and specialists at 3Shape.

**Become Our Next Technical Graduate

**As a 3Shape Graduate, you will be a valued team member, tackle complex business challenges, and become part of an extensive network of professionals in a global organization. We offer a steep learning curve and expect a lot from you, but in return, you will have opportunities to grow both professionally and personally.

• Rotate through three departments (8 months each) working with e.g., UX/UI, Software Development, Computer Science, IT, Data, Discovery, Regulatory Affairs, Product Management, and Production and Supply Chain.

• Play an essential role in an international and innovative organization that is constantly evolving.

• Lead and contribute to real projects with measurable impact.

• Broaden your horizons by working as part of integrated teams across the globe and collaborating with people from diverse backgrounds.

• Join a well-established, social, and friendly community of current and former Graduates.

• Receive ongoing feedback, coaching, and support from rotation managers, a mentor, and a buddy.

**We Fuel Your Career With

**

• Comprehensive onboarding - including an offsite, teambuilding, and networking with the Senior Leadership Team.

• Regular meetings with your Graduate Manager focused on your development and well-being.

• Multiple training sessions (such as Case Challenge, People Module, Technical Training, etc.).

• A production visit to our site in Poland.

• Quarterly Graduate-community activities with Graduates from our two cohorts

**What Makes a 3Shape Graduate?

**You are about to complete or have just completed a master’s degree. You have achieved top academic results and are highly proficient in English. You are enthusiastic, focused, and eager to learn.

• An excellent collaborator with an empathetic approach and a global mindset.

• Versatile and adaptable.

• Thrives in an international environment.

• Motivated to take responsibility.

• Strong analytical thinker with solid problem-solving skills.

• Brings positive energy and is eager to apply knowledge and make an impact.

**What 3Shape Offers

**

• A vibrant, international environment with social, diverse, and highly skilled colleagues - over 20 nationalities represented in our Denmark-based office.

• An attractive healthcare package

• Daily breakfast, Friday juices, and healthy lunches prepared by our private chefs.

• A good social work environment with many optional activities and clubs, from wine and beer tastings to board games, running, and paddle.

• Modern offices and R&D labs in downtown Copenhagen, near Kongens Nytorv, Nyhavn, and the Copenhagen Canals.

**Application Process

**

• Application deadline: 15/12/2026

• Graduate Program start date: 01/09/2027

• Applications are reviewed on a continuous basis – please apply as soon as possible.

• After a successful application and initial video call screening, candidates will be invited to our headquarters in Copenhagen for an assessment center on Friday, January 29th.

• If you have questions about the position or process, contact people@3shape.com.

We encourage all relevant applicants to apply. We are committed to celebrating human diversity, and we trust that the best way to reach outstanding business results, is by welcoming diverse people into our community.

**About Us

**3Shape started with a simple idea - to make 3D scanning better. First, we applied it to the hearing industry, then we succeeded in dentistry. Twenty years later, 3Shape has 2,000+ employees globally. With the help of dental professionals and amazing colleagues we’re creating award-winning scanning and CAD/CAM solutions to change dentistry together! Together, we contribute to a better world. jobs.occupation: Technical Lead - Substation Automation and Communication Systems
jobs.description:
Do you have experience with automation and communication systems for high-voltage substations? Can you lead technical work packages and coordinate specialist contributions to deliver an integrated solution? Join COWI as our new Technical Lead and contribute to the development of Denmark’s electricity transmission infrastructure.

Take technical responsibility for substation automation projects

We are looking for an experienced engineer to take technical responsibility for substation automation and communication systems in high-voltage substation projects. You will work on projects ranging from new substations to extensions, refurbishment and replacement of systems at existing sites. You will coordinate specialist contributions, manage technical interfaces and ensure that individual work packages meet the requirements of the overall substation automation solution.

The role combines technical expertise with responsibility for coordinating engineering activities, monitoring progress and ensuring the quality of technical deliverables. You will work closely with the project manager, technical specialists and other engineering disciplines throughout project execution.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Lead and coordinate the technical delivery of substation automation and communication systems.

• Plan and follow up on engineering activities, technical deliverables and milestones within your scope.

• Coordinate specialist contributions and ensure consistency across technical work packages.

• Ensure that technical solutions and documentation comply with project requirements, customer specifications and applicable standards.

• Manage technical interfaces between automation, communication systems, protection systems, primary equipment and auxiliary systems.

• Identify and resolve technical issues in collaboration with specialists and other engineering disciplines.

• Participate in project meetings and advise the project manager on technical matters, dependencies and risks within your area of responsibility.

• Coordinate technical activities with customers, suppliers and other project stakeholders.

Your expertise

You combine a strong technical foundation with a structured approach to planning and coordination. You can assess how individual systems and specialist contributions fit together, communicate technical requirements clearly and follow through on agreed actions.

You work independently and build effective working relationships with colleagues, customers and project partners.

You will also bring:

• A degree in electrical engineering or an equivalent technical qualification, together with more than five years of relevant experience in automation for high-voltage substations.

• A solid understanding of substation automation systems, including control and monitoring functions, communication networks and interfaces to protection equipment.

• An understanding of how substation secondary systems interface with high-voltage primary equipment.

• Experience coordinating technical work packages, planning engineering activities and following up on specialist deliverables.

• The ability to assess technical solutions, manage interfaces and maintain an overview of quality, progress and dependencies.

• Professional proficiency in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

• The ability to obtain the required security clearance and fulfil the requirements for the designated on-site role of “holdleder” at high-voltage substations.

Your place of work

Depending on project requirements, you may work from one of COWI’s offices in Denmark, at Energinet project locations or partly from home. Travel within Denmark is expected.

A place to work and so much more

At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers.

We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home.

With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

Got more questions?

If you have any unanswered questions about the role or what we have to offer, please reach out to Head of Discipline Carsten Sass Husum at CSHU@COWI.COM.

Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

Before you apply

All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture.

Equal opportunity employer

COWI provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability or genetics. In addition to federal law requirements, COWI complies with applicable state and local laws governing non-discrimination in employment in every location in which the company has facilities. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

Join us as Executive Protection Advisor at Maersk

Maersk’s Protective Services function helps keep our executive leadership, their families and designated senior leaders safe, connected and able to lead the business with confidence. We do this through intelligence-led advice, structured programmes and discreet coordination across the countries where Maersk operates.

We are looking for an Executive Protection Advisor to take ownership of our Executive Protection and Event Security programmes; co-own the executive scope of our Travel Risk Management programme and the family coverage within our Expat and Family Security Programme; and act as a trusted advisor to senior executives across Maersk and A.P. Moller Holding, as well as designated family members.

This role is for someone who leads through structure and judgement rather than visibility. You can balance operational delivery with programme development, build trust with senior stakeholders, and translate exposure into proportionate, discreet and workable solutions.

The role in brief

The Executive Protection Advisor is the trusted operational and advisory point of contact for our executive population and their closest support functions. The role sits at the centre of a global Protective Services team and works directly with the Head of Protective Services.

Approximately 60% of the role is operational. You will advise on executive travel, events, residences and family security situations; manage incidents and threats when they arise; and coordinate with Regional Heads of Security, vendors and authorities to ensure the right support is in the right place at the right time.

The remaining 40% is strategic. You will own and continuously develop the Executive Protection Programme and the Event Security Programme. You will also co-own the executive scope of Travel Risk Management and the coverage for families of Maersk’s executive leadership within our Expat and Family Security Programme, while contributing to the continued professional maturity of the function.

International travel is part of the role, including support for events, oversight of site visits, and the development and maintenance of vendor relationships. The role is based in Copenhagen.

What you will do

Programme ownership and development

·  Own the Executive Protection Programme (EPP), including its appendices, procedures and workflows, and ensure it remains current and operationally usable.

·  Own the Event Security Programme (ESP), including triggers, templates, planning standards and governance.

·  Co-own the executive travel scope of our Travel Risk Management programme and the family coverage within our Expat and Family Security Programme.

·  Prepare decision-ready executive briefings for leadership review and approval.

Executive, family and residential advisory

·  Act as the trusted contact for senior executives and designated family members on protective services matters.

·  Conduct individual exposure assessments and translate findings into proportionate, discreet, and practical measures.

·  Coordinate residential security across alarms, access control, surveillance, physical improvements and vendor delivery.

Executive travel and event coordination

·  Coordinate protective services for senior executive travel.

·  Plan and oversee event security for leadership events, off-sites and public engagements.

·  Coordinate with Regional Heads of Security, local offices, vendors and authorities to ensure consistent delivery.

Incident, threat and harassment case management

·  Lead the initial assessment of threats, harassment or incidents affecting executives, family members, or company locations.

·  Coordinate with Global Threat Intelligence, Cyber Security, Legal, HQ Security, and relevant authorities.

·  Maintain clear documentation, follow-up actions, and After-Action Reviews.

Intelligence, vendors and authorities

·  Define Protective Services’ intelligence requirements and coordinate with Global Threat Intelligence.

·  Support vendor evaluations, RFP processes and procurement collaboration across executive protection, residential security, event security and intelligence suppliers.

·  Build and maintain professional relationships with Danish and international police, authorities and security partners.

Training and onboarding

·  Deliver security onboarding and briefings for new members of Maersk’s executive leadership, Executive Assistants and relevant support functions.

·  Develop audience-appropriate awareness materials, briefings, and checklists.

About you

You are a trusted advisor, not a frontline operator. You bring the composure of someone who has worked closely with senior leadership, and you understand that judgement and discretion matter more than visibility in this environment.

You are structured, take ownership and follow matters through to closure. You are comfortable with ambiguity, able to bring orders to incomplete information, and confident in turning it into a workable plan.

You are proactive and anticipate what is coming. You engage early with Executive Assistants, regional partners and vendors, ensuring Protective Services remains a step ahead.

You communicate with clarity and confidence. You can turn a complex security topic into a concise, decision-ready briefing for a senior leader, and you can raise concerns respectfully but firmly when the situation requires it.

You will provide regular one-to-one support for a 9-year-old boy with autism and an intellectual disability. He needs close support, clear structure and a calm approach that helps create predictability.

The boy is energetic, enjoys being active and particularly likes outdoor play, trips to the playground and running in the woods. You may be a qualified pedagogue/social educator or have relevant experience working with children with special needs. You approach the child with calmness, patience and clarity, and you enjoy an active working environment where you take part in play and physical activities.

Phanofi is a DTU spin-out building the next generation of optical communication infrastructure. We design integrated photonic interconnect chips that dramatically reduce power consumption and increase data throughput for AI datacenters, quantum computing, and space applications. As a diverse team of 15 people, we are at an exciting inflection point, and we are looking for a senior leader to drive our commercial growth.

As Head of Business Development, you will own Phanofi's commercial trajectory. Reporting directly to the CEO, you will define and execute the go-to-market strategy, forge high-value industry partnerships, lead the company's funding and grant initiatives, and represent Phanofi on the global stage. This is a senior, highly visible role with the opportunity, and expectation, to build the business development function from the ground up.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Strategy & Commercial Leadership: Define and execute Phanofi’s business development strategy, establish commercial goals and KPIs, and drive market expansion across AI datacenters, quantum computing, and space sectors.

• Industry Relationships & Partnerships: Build and maintain strategic relationships with key stakeholders across the data communications, semiconductor, and photonics industries, while leading partnership discussions and negotiations.

• Market Intelligence & Business Insights: Conduct market research, monitor industry trends and competitive developments, and translate technical innovations into compelling business opportunities and commercial strategies.

• Brand Representation & External Communications: Represent Phanofi at industry conferences, trade shows, and networking events, while supporting thought leadership, public relations, and external communications activities.

**What We Are Looking For

**

• Experience: You bring a minimum of 5 years of experience in business development, or commercial leadership within the photonics, semiconductor, deep-tech, or related technology industries. You have a proven track record of securing strategic partnerships, commercial agreements, or major funding opportunities.

• Technical Background: You have a strong engineering or scientific background, preferably in photonics, integrated optics, electronics, communications, or a related field, enabling you to engage confidently with technical teams and customers.

• Skills: You possess strong business development, partnership management, negotiation, and market analysis skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into compelling business value propositions.

• Leadership & Soft Skills: You are a strategic and entrepreneurial leader who can influence cross-functional teams, communicate effectively with both technical and commercial stakeholders, and thrive in a fast-paced deep-tech startup environment. **The Perks

**We care about your long-term growth and well-being. We offer performance-based stock options, healthcare insurance, professional development support, and a positive culture with free snacks. You will also enjoy standard Danish benefits, including 5 weeks of paid holiday and maternity/paternity leave.

**How To Apply

**If you are interested in joining us on our entrepreneurial journey, we encourage you to submit your CV and a cover letter. We look forward to hearing from you!

Phanofi is committed to providing a workplace where equal opportunity and non-discrimination are fundamental principles. Founded by engineers — and customer obsessed — we leap at every opportunity to solve technical challenges, from designing next-gen UI/UX for interfacing with data to scaling our services and infrastructure across millions of virtual machines. As a software engineer with a backend focus, you will work with your team to build infrastructure for the Databricks platform at scale.

Department: Cloud

Location: Copenhagen

**Description

**Factbird helps manufacturers turn real-time production data into decisions they can actually act on. Since 2016, we've helped manufacturers in 28 countries cut waste, boost uptime, and run smarter — from the shop floor to the boardroom. Over 300 companies trust us to make sense of their operations, and we're a team of 80+ people across Copenhagen and the US who care about making complex things simple.

We're growing our engineering team and hiring several Full Stack Cloud Engineers — people who can move confidently across our stack: React on the front end, Rust and Node.js on the back end, and a multi-account AWS underneath it all.

**About the Role

**We're open on where your strengths sit. Some of these roles will lean more toward the back end — APIs, data pipelines, cloud infrastructure. Others will lean more toward the front end — the interfaces our customers use every day. What matters is that you're genuinely full stack: comfortable owning a feature end to end, and willing to work across the stack when the team needs it. We're not looking for anyone who only does front end or only does back end.

We’re looking for confident independent contributors that lean into ownership, are keen to shape architecture, and invest in mentoring others.

You'll fit right in if you've got a pragmatic, get-it-done mindset, a good instinct for testing and clean design, and you're just as happy explaining a technical trade-off to another engineer as to someone outside engineering.

**

What you'll do

**Building & shipping

• Operate within a Nix-backed ecosystem from development tooling to cross-compiled build artifacts

• Own features end to end — from a rough idea or user story through to a shipped, tested, monitored piece of production software

• Build and maintain frontend features in React and backend services in TypeScript on Node.js and Rust, backed by a multi-account orchestrated AWS environment (Lambda, API Gateway, RDS, DynamoDB, EKS, and more, depending on the team)

• Write infrastructure as code (e.g. AWS CDK) for the systems you build

**

Team & growth**

• Take part in code reviews — giving and receiving feedback that makes the codebase better

• Contribute to sprint planning, story breakdown, and demos

• Design systems and data pipelines from scratch, mentor other engineers, author RFCs and architecture decisions, and help set technical standards for the team

**About you

**We're looking for engineers who've seen more than one way of doing things, and who'll bring that perspective to challenge how we do things here — with a pragmatic, get-it-done mindset that can turn ambiguity into a plan.

**

The ideal background**

• At least three years experience since graduating from a relevant Masters program

• Solid, hands-on experience across the full stack — frontend (React or equivalent) and backend (Rust/Node.js, or equivalent) — even if you have a natural preference for one side

• Comfort working with AWS or another major cloud provider

• A track record of shipping features independently, with a good instinct for testing, code quality, and clean design

• Good communication — you can explain a technical trade-off clearly, whether you're talking to another engineer or someone outside engineering. And you can do all this with strong English fluency.

• Experience designing systems from scratch, mentoring other engineers, or driving architecture decisions through to a decision

We welcome applicants from people eager to move to Denmark so long as you already have the legal right to live and work here. We can contribute to relocation costs for the right candidate.

**Why Factbird?

**People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

Here's what you can look forward to:

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn't one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Thoughtful, human onboarding: We'll support you step by step, giving you the context, tools, and guidance you need to feel confident from day one.

• A career path that grows with you: Through bi-yearly Individual Development Plan conversations, we'll work together to shape a career journey that fits your ambitions.

• Company-wide gatherings & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what's next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We're proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.

**

We'd love to hear from you

**If this role feels like a match, we'd be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit — feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Have questions? You can always reach out at **khma@factbird.com

**_

At Factbird, we believe that great work starts with people feeling respected, valued, and included. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

__We celebrate diversity in all its forms and believe that different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences make our teams stronger and our work better. We warmly encourage all qualified candidates to apply and to bring their whole selves to Factbird.

Tech-first. Ego-free. User-obsessed.

Over one million Danes use Skatteguiden to understand and optimise their taxes. We automate tax tracking, surface deductions people didn't know they had, and give users the insights they need to make better financial decisions — all directly connected to the Danish tax authority.

We're an independent company of around 50 people based in Copenhagen, with a 4.7-star App Store rating and a simple mission: make financial insight accessible to everyone, not just those who can afford an accountant.

**About The Role

**Path to Plus is the engine that converts users into paying members and keeps them there. As a Backend Engineer on this team, you'll be building and shipping features as part of a cross-functional product team with a direct commercial mission — not executing on a spec handed down to you, but helping shape what gets built and why.

This is a product engineering role. The team owns the problem, not just the delivery. That means getting involved before requirements are written, connecting your technical work to user and business outcomes, and iterating based on real feedback. You'll work closely with engineering leadership — not as a follower, but as a collaborator who contributes to the plan. If you've worked that way before — or you're actively looking to grow into it — this is the right environment.

What you'll do

• End-to-end features. Ship features as part of the team's product cycle, from problem shaping to production.

• Multi-broker architecture. Stock tax support is live. The next challenge is redesigning the current model to support multiple brokers — a real architectural problem you'll be part of solving.

• Observability. You'll help us own the health of critical business flows and catch issues before users do.

• Azure migration. We're migrating our systems in the coming months. Cloud architecture thinking will be an active part of the role.

• Tech debt on the roadmap. We believe tech debt belongs on the roadmap, not hidden under it. You'll help identify, prioritise, and plan for it alongside the team.

What we're looking for

You're a backend engineer who takes reliability and code quality seriously, and you can move fast without cutting corners. We care more about how you build and think than about which stack you've used. If most of this sounds like you, apply, even if you don't tick every box.

• Strong backend experience in production. You've built and run services that real users depend on, in Java, Kotlin, Go or a similar language. Our stack is Java and Spring Boot. If you haven't used it, we expect you to be keen to learn it quickly, and we'll help.

• Comfort with distributed systems. You've worked with message queues, relational databases, or both, and you understand the trade-offs.

• A product mindset. You care why something is built, not just how. You're happy to question a requirement, suggest a simpler path, and judge your work by its effect on users and the business.

• Good engineering habits. You can read an unfamiliar codebase, spot its strengths and weak spots, and improve it over time without needing a perfect plan first. You think about reliability and data, and you're realistic about making change in a production environment.

• Practical use of AI tools. Every engineer here uses Claude in daily work. You don't need to be an expert, but you should be curious and willing to make it part of how you work.

Bonus points

None of these are hard requirements.

• Java, Spring Boot, JUnit, RabbitMQ or MySQL specifically

• Kubernetes, Argo, GitHub Actions, Grafana or Loki

• Running services in Azure or another cloud, including tuning resources and cost

• Experience with fintech, payments, subscriptions or regulated data

Why join us

• Visible impact. You're joining a team with a full pipeline, and your work will show results quickly.

• A company serious about engineering quality. We're actively investing in elevating engineering practices across the organisation. You'll be part of that, not just a passenger.

• Solid company. Independent, profitable, growing. No VC pressure, no bloated roadmap. Just a clear mission and a team that cares.

• Good people. We take the work seriously without taking ourselves too seriously. The culture is professional, informal, and genuinely collaborative.

• Room to grow. The scope of the work and the team's ambitions mean there's real room to step up.

Practical details

Location: Copenhagen. We're an office-first company, and it's a deliberate choice. We're moving fast, we have big ambitions, and we genuinely believe that being physically together is one of the things that makes that possible. Things move quicker when you can turn your chair and talk to someone.

The office is a five-minute walk from Rådhuspladsen and stocked with everything from fruit to fizzy drinks to afternoon snacks. Lunch is at Claus Meyer's canteen just across the street — proper food, not an afterthought. If you're putting in a long day, dinner is covered too.

Start: As soon as possible.

Salary: Competitive and based on your experience.

Reporting to: Engineering Manager.

Our hiring process

• Screening call with the hiring manager (30 min) — online

• Technical interview: build something together with a Backend Engineer and the Engineering Manager (60 min) — onsite

• Culture conversation with the Engineering Manager and CTO (60 min) — onsite

• Meet the CEO (30 min) — onsite

jobs.occupation: Biostatistician and Research Computing Specialist for The National Center of Excellence PREDICT
jobs.description:
The National Center of Excellence PREDICT at Aalborg University in Copenhagen is looking to recruit a motivated and dedicated biostatistician with an interest in the technical part of research to join our international and interdisciplinary group of researchers in a double role as biostatistician and technical contact person. The position is for 3 years, full-time (37 hours per week) and is open for appointment from March 1st 2027.

Your work tasks

As biostatistician in PREDICT you will be involved in epidemiological studies of risk factors for IBD, pre-clinical disease development and treatment of IBD. You will join an active group of dedicated biostatisticians and data scientists ensuring knowledge sharing and continuous professional development.

You will contribute to study planning, take responsibility for data management and statistical analyses of nationwide register data and large datasets collected in PREDICT, and contribute to the interpretation and reporting of the results, including co-authoring of scientific papers.

In addition to the biostatistical task, the position also includes the role of the primary technical contact person on our data infrastructure hosted on the National Genom Center’s HPC system. You will coordinate technical support, manage user access and onboarding, and assist researchers with data management, troubleshooting, and computational workflows. The role also involves ensuring secure handling of research data and contributing to the development and optimization of technical workflows.

Your competencies

Ideally, you have the following qualifications:

•    A master’s degree in statistics or equivalent

•    Experience conducting statistical analyses in epidemiological research

•    Knowledge about time-to-event analysis and related statistical methods.

•    Strong programming skills in R and/or Python

•    Experience in working with Linux-based computing environments

•    Experience working on High Performance Computing (HPC) systems

•    Experience with shell scripting for workflow automation and troubleshooting

•    Strong problem-solving skills and ability to support colleagues with technical challenges

•    Excellent communication and collaboration skills

Note that you must be qualified for both parts of the position to be taken into consideration.

Who we are

PREDICT was founded in 2021 and is at the forefront of international research to unravel the cause and prognosis of inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), which are chronic and disabling conditions affecting millions of people worldwide. The Center is composed of biologists, clinicians, epidemiologists, and data scientists working with collaborators nationally and internationally to push the boundaries of precision medicine research and create real-world impact in IBD. We have state-of-the-art facilities within the center and this means through PREDICT you will be part of a well-funded research environment equipped with the latest technologies, unique data, and a world-leading network of collaborators.

PREDICT has grown to become a world-renowned center, organized as a broad, national and interdisciplinary collaboration between Aalborg University and Aalborg University Hospital, with a multidisciplinary team of immunologists, geneticists, data scientists, clinicians and many more disciplines. PREDICT also has strong international collaborations across the world.

You can read more about PREDICT here: www.predictibd.dk

About the Department of Clinical Medicine

The Department of Clinical Medicine provides research-based teaching across all disciplines of the

medical degree programme and conducts research within the clinical specialties.

Read more about the Department of Clinical Medicine here

How to apply

Your application must contain the following:

• A brief motivated application describing your professional and personal competences and the experience qualifying you particularly for the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Examination certificate

• Any other relevant appendices

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Do you have any questions?

If you have any questions about the position, you are welcome to contact Chief Statistician, Group Leader Gry J. Poulsen, gryjp@dcm.aau.dk

Further information Read more about our recruitment process here.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

**

Salary and terms of employment

**Your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the Collective Agreement for Academic Staff Employed in the State Sector with the classification academic officer or special consultant. Classification is based on competence, experience and seniority, with the possibility of negotiating qualification-based supplements.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Technical and administrative positions Academic (AC-TAP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the sections entitled “Academic Officer” and “Special consultant”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

A Snapshot of Your Day

Join us as a DevOps & Platform Engineer, where you will play a pivotal role in building, operating, and continuously enhancing the platforms and services that drive product development, testing, validation, deployment, and operations within Siemens Gamesa’s digital ecosystem. Imagine developing automation solutions, enhancing CI/CD pipelines, and collaborating with software teams to elevate the developer experience and operational efficiency. You will work closely with product development, validation, architecture, and infrastructure teams to ensure that our platforms remain reliable, secure, and scalable. Whether you are modernizing platform services or contributing to cloud-enabled solutions, your efforts will significantly accelerate how engineering teams deliver innovative solutions. Become part of an international team that values ownership, innovation, and knowledge sharing in a culture driven by a strong engineering mindset.

How You’ll Make an Impact

• Design, build, and operate platform services that support product development, testing, validation, and deployment activities.

• Develop automation solutions that enhance reliability, scalability, security, and operational efficiency.

• Build and maintain Infrastructure as Code, automated deployments, CI/CD pipelines, and platform tooling.

• Develop integrations and automation using APIs, scripting, and modern DevOps practices.

• Improve observability through monitoring, logging, alerting, dashboards, and operational analytics.

• Support and evolve virtualization and platform technologies while contributing to modernization initiatives and future cloud capabilities.

• Collaborate closely with software engineers, architects, product teams, and infrastructure specialists to enhance developer productivity and platform capabilities.

• Contribute to platform standardization, self-service capabilities, and continuous improvement initiatives.

What You Bring

Must Have

• Experience in Platform Engineering, DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Software Engineering, or Infrastructure Automation.

• Strong experience with automation technologies such as Ansible, PowerShell, PowerCLI, Python, Git, Infrastructure as Code, and CI/CD tooling.

• Proven ability to create and maintain automation frameworks, deployment pipelines, APIs, integrations, or platform services.

• Familiarity with virtualization and platform technologies like VMware vSphere, vCenter, vSAN, ESXi, Proxmox VE, or similar enterprise platforms.

• Knowledge of Linux and/or Windows administration, scripting, troubleshooting, and system integration.

• Experience with monitoring, observability, logging, incident management, performance analysis, and service reliability practices.

• A proactive mindset with a passion for automation, continuous learning, and building reliable platform services.

Nice to Have

• Exposure to cloud-native technologies, containers, Kubernetes, Microsoft Azure, AWS, or hybrid cloud platforms.

• Experience in Agile environments using Scrum or SAFe methodologies, along with tools such as Jira, Confluence, and Git-based workflows.

• Familiarity with platform modernization, self-service platforms, developer experience initiatives, or Infrastructure as Code practices.

• Experience supporting engineering applications, industrial systems, SCADA environments, or operational technology solutions.

About the Team

You will join the Infrastructure Performance & Operations (IPO) team within Digital Products & Solutions. This team is dedicated to developing, operating, and evolving the digital platforms that support product engineering, validation, testing, and business operations across Siemens Gamesa. Our focus areas include platform engineering, automation, virtualization, CI/CD, observability, service reliability, infrastructure modernization, and operational excellence. We collaborate closely with product teams to simplify operations through automation, enhance developer experience, and provide scalable platform capabilities that support the development, validation, and delivery of digital products in the wind energy sector. Working in an Agile environment, we utilize Scrum and SAFe practices, ensuring alignment across development, infrastructure, architecture, validation, and product organizations. As our digital landscape evolves, the team is also shaping future platform capabilities, cloud adoption opportunities, and next-generation Digital Foundation services. We value collaboration, technical curiosity, knowledge sharing, continuous learning, and engineers who thrive on solving complex challenges through code, automation, and modern platform engineering practices.

Who is Siemens Gamesa?

Siemens Gamesa is part of Siemens Energy, a global leader in energy technology with a rich legacy of innovation spanning over 150 years. Together, we are committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. As a leading player in the wind industry and manufacturer of wind turbines, we are passionate about driving the energy transition and providing innovative solutions that meet the growing energy demand of the global community. At Siemens Gamesa, we are constantly seeking talented individuals to join our team and support our focus on energy transformation. Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Gamesa: Working at Siemens Energy: Careers & Job Opportunities

Our Commitment to Diversity

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity, we generate power. We run on inclusion, and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character—no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences.

Rewards/Benefits

Here are examples of the rewards and benefits Siemens Energy offers:

• Opportunities to work with a global team

• Opportunities to work on and lead a variety of innovative projects

• Medical benefits

• Hybrid (3x per week in the office) / Flexible work

Are you passionate about shaping a more sustainable future and would you like to play a key role in Vattenfall’s transition to cleaner energy? Vattenfall is looking for a Senior Consent Manager to strengthen its Offshore Consenting team in Denmark.
