We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

We are looking for a Department Manager to join one of our Electrical & Instrumentation (E&I) departments. As part of our E&I organisation, you will divide your time between project execution and department management, ensuring both successful project delivery and the continued development of your team.

Electrical & Instrumentation (E&I) plays a key role in designing and delivering safe, reliable, and efficient pharmaceutical production facilities. Our work connects the physical production process with the systems that monitor, control, and safeguard it throughout the entire engineering lifecycle, from conceptual and detailed design to procurement, construction support, testing, commissioning, and qualification.

Your contribution will be important in developing people, strengthening technical excellence, and supporting the continued growth of our E&I capabilities as demand for complex pharmaceutical engineering solutions increases.

• Leading and developing a team of approximately 11 employees and consultants

• Contributing to projects while providing technical and managerial leadership

• Managing resource allocation across projects and portfolios

• Driving employee, discipline, and competency development together with senior specialists

• Strengthening collaboration with colleagues in Denmark and Bangalore, India

Who you are

We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you are:

• Skilled at bringing people together around a common purpose

• Result-oriented with a structured and proactive approach to leadership

• Focused on employee growth, engagement, and development

• Able to build strong professional relationships with customers and stakeholders

• Agile and comfortable prioritising in a dynamic project environment

jobs.occupation: Senior Director, Alliance Management and Strategic Partnerships
jobs.description:
Does it excite you to work with partners to bring new medicines to the market and to patients, and do you have experience with taking partnerships from early science through to launch? If this sounds like you, and you are ready to take on a broad area of responsibilities, then you could be our new colleague.

Your new position

This Senior Director position reports to the SVP for Alliance Management, within a growing area of Commercial. The ambition is to evolve the mandate from ensuring partnerships are well governed and deliver against contractual obligations to maximizing the strategic, scientific and commercial value of our external partnerships across the asset lifecycle: from early science through development, regulatory approval, launch and lifecycle management. As we grow, the position offers the opportunity to build a "partner-to-market" value proposition for the entire organization and to shape the area that delivers it.

We offer exciting responsibilities:

• Shape and drive the partner-to-market agenda, keeping the route to market in focus and contributing to the strategy, operating model and growth of the area

• Lead strategic partnership assessments, from partner identification and deal thesis development to close collaboration with Business Development and the identification of portfolio and capability gaps that partnerships can address

• Maximize the value of partnered assets through strong alliance governance, timely milestone delivery and proactive risk management across the partnership portfolio

• Drive cross-functional alignment between Zealand teams and partners, and resolve escalations and conflicts constructively and swiftly

• Prepare partnerships for commercial success through launch readiness, market access collaborations and co-commercialization models

• Unlock lifecycle expansion opportunities with partners, including new indications that extend the value of Zealand assets

Your profile

You are motivated by the path from molecules to market, and by combining Zealand's strengths with those of our partners to reach patients faster and further. Alliance management experience is a strength, and you have a genuine motivation to drive partnership progress with the patient always in view. You are a strategic and commercially minded partner who builds trust easily, influences without relying on formal authority, and is energized by building something new in a growing organization. Curiosity, resilience and a bold, collaborative approach come naturally to you.

• Minimum 10 years of experience in biopharma or big pharma, within partnering, business development, alliance management, commercial or development roles

• Deep understanding of drug development and commercialization, demonstrated through hands-on experience from regulatory approval, launch readiness, market access or co-commercialization, and the ability to connect early scientific decisions to commercial outcomes

• Strong strategic and commercial acumen, including deal structures, partnership economics and deal thesis development, with the ability to assess where a partnership creates the most value for patients and for Zealand across the asset lifecycle

• Solid understanding of US market dynamics, including pricing, payer and market access considerations that shape partnered commercial strategies

• Solid understanding and experience working with Chinese market is an advantage

• Ability to challenge early science and clinical development programs with the end product in mind, ideally with experience within obesity and metabolic health

Your new team

Alliance Management reports to the Executive Vice President for Commercial and works at the interface between our partners and our internal functions across research, development, regulatory, commercial and business development

Let's bond and be bold

We have a unique culture, characterized by excellent teamwork and strong engagement across the organization. And we want you to help us strengthen this culture.

Making bonds is at the core of everything we do. From discovering and developing the best new peptide drugs for patients, to engaging with our partners or connecting with each other. We bond through curiosity and playfulness as a team, allowing ourselves to challenge common thinking and drive future innovation. Join us and let's bond and be bold.

Interested in bonding with us? Then please apply no later than 12 November 2026 or as soon as possible. The applications will be reviewed as they come in. While a cover letter is not required, please include a few sentences in your CV explaining your motivation for applying.

We are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and welcome applications from all job applicants.

About Zealand Pharma A/S

Zealand Pharma A/S (Nasdaq: ZEAL) is a biotechnology company focused on advancing medicines for obesity and metabolic health. Combining more than 25 years of peptide R&D expertise with a proprietary data platform that leverages advanced data-driven and AI/ML approaches, Zealand Pharma aims to lead a new era in obesity and metabolic health. To date, more than ten Zealand Pharma-invented drug candidates have entered clinical development, of which two products have reached the market and three candidates are in late-stage development. The Company has collaborations with global pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners for research, development, and commercialization. Founded in 1998, Zealand Pharma is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, with a U.S. presence in Boston, Massachusetts. Learn more at www.zealandpharma.com.

Research organizations across the public sector, higher education, regions, banking and insurance, and find the right people to talk to

A few years into RevOps, most people end up choosing between staying close to admin and reporting, or moving towards building automations and the AI tools that now sit on top of the CRM. The second path is hard to get onto if you haven't done it somewhere first.

In this job you'd do both, in a commercial team that already works with AI day to day through assistants connected to Salesforce, support tickets and product data, while marketing is being rebuilt the same way. You'd build on that, starting next to the person who set most of it up and taking over the technical side from them. You'd also keep the CRM and the data underneath it in good order. That's a lot of upkeep, like permissions, data cleanup and renewal notices to thousands of customers, and there's no ops team to share it with.

Airtame makes wireless screen-sharing devices and the cloud software that manages them, used in schools and workplaces around the world. Most of our volume goes through distributors on several continents, sometimes to customers our own reps sent them. Our sales team also works deals directly, and smaller orders come through our Shopify store. Running all three through one Salesforce makes for a harder data model than most RevOps roles come with.

We're around 55 people, headquartered in Copenhagen, and we'd prefer you to work from the office there. Remote from elsewhere in the EU works too. You'd report to our Director of Customer Experience & Revenue Operations, who sets the roadmap with you and owns the metric definitions, and you'd work with sales, customer experience, marketing and product every week.

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

Own the Commercial Stack: By the end of the year the technical side has moved over to you, including the AI tools the team uses. You bring the roadmap to your manager and build it, and when sales or support want a system changed, you decide how it's done.

Send the Right Renewal Message: Thousands of customers receive renewal notices. We're starting to ask customers in our cloud software how they intend to renew, and you'd build the email flows that act on it, with a separate path for each way of renewing. If a notice doesn't go out, you know within hours.

Make the Numbers Agree: Pipeline, bookings, ARR, renewals and churn come out the same in every dashboard and every AI assistant, whether the sale came through Shopify, a rep or a distributor. Your manager sets the definitions, and you make sure every system uses them.

Automate the Manual Work: Find the processes worth automating and keep shipping them, tested in a sandbox first with a way back if something goes wrong. The first one is turning the pricing claims our distributors send, in all sorts of formats, into line-item pricing in Salesforce with an audit trail. As AI assistants get better at connecting to things on their own, part of this is also deciding what's still worth building ourselves.

Bring Support onto Intercom: We're moving customer support from Zendesk to Intercom. Depending on when you join, you'd help finish the move or pick it up just after go-live, then own Intercom, including its Salesforce sync and the AI setup that gets customer feedback to the product team.

Who You Are

• You know Salesforce from the inside. A few years of hands-on admin, including Flow Builder, permissions and the data model. You write SQL and SOQL and can model data for a report yourself.

• You ask why before you build. You can tell us about a request you pushed back on, or a process you changed or dropped instead of automating it as asked, and what it was for in the first place.

• You work with AI by default. You use AI tools every day to write flows and queries, and you keep up with what's new on your own. When a new connector makes something we built unnecessary, you're happy to retire it. If you've connected tools through their APIs or written some Python or JavaScript, that's a strong plus.

• You've run a commercial system on your own. At some point you've been the only or main admin of a Salesforce org or a similar system, and you left documentation behind that someone else could take over from. Here there's no ops team behind you, so a broken sync in the morning and a dashboard request in the afternoon are both yours.

Why Airtame?

• Building on Top of Admin: You'd keep the CRM running and build automations and AI tooling on top of it, starting next to the person who set most of it up.

• Most RevOps roles are purely SaaS or purely e-commerce. Here, you get to solve the unique intellectual challenge of bridging a hardware supply chain with a high-velocity digital subscription model.

• A healthy work-life balance.

• Five weeks paid vacation and 5 days of extra paid AirtameFlex days.

• Pension and private health insurance (on FTE Copenhagen contract).

• Flexible work environment, with a hybrid mindset.

• Catered lunch in the office.

Airtame is an equal opportunity employer. We have colleagues across the globe, with both in-office and full-time remote workers. This feeds into our international hybrid mindset, with people from 25+ nationalities that make up the Airtame team.

Our work-life cultural balance is key to our success. Our team encompasses our values of trust and open communication to support each other and to collaborate in a fun and collective way.

jobs.description:
We're looking for a senior AI engineer with hands-on experience in generative AI, API integrations, and advanced agent-based applications. The ideal candidate brings a mix of full-stack, AI, and cloud engineering experience.

**What You'll Do

**This role cuts across multiple tech stacks and is a central part of how we deliver AI solutions for our clients.

**In This Role, You'll

**

• Translating early ideas into working prototypes and iterating them into production-ready solutions using modern full-stack frameworks

• Designing and deploying generative AI applications and autonomous agents using LLM APIs and established agent frameworks

• Integrating AI capabilities into client systems and managing deployment pipelines in cloud environments

• Collaborating with engineering, product, and business stakeholders to build solutions that address real needs

• Mentoring junior engineers and keeping pace with emerging AI and software engineering paradigms

**What You'll Bring

**We're looking for someone with at least five years of software development experience, including at least two in generative AI and agent-based applications, and a master's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field.

**

Relevant AI or cloud certifications are a plus. English is our corporate language; however, proficiency in one or more additional languages is a plus for this role.

_Do you want to shape how the world’s largest dedicated fund manager within greenfield renewable energy uses AI to deploy capital? If so, CIP Fund Solutions (CIP FS) is looking for a Product Manager to join our Digital & AI team in Copenhagen, Denmark.

_**Team

**As Product Manager, you will join the Digital & AI team in CIP Fund Solutions, reporting to the Investment Lifecycle Lead. You will be part of a new delivery unit, developing and rolling out digital and AI solutions that will bring efficiency to CIP’s investment teams.

As Product Manager, you will find where AI saves the investment teams the most time or improves their decisions and turn that into products they use every day. Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

The Opportunity

Veo runs on a fast-growing estate of devices, SaaS tools and offices across Copenhagen, Berlin and Miami. As the first operational IT security hire, you'll own the security of that environment: the devices our people use, the identities and access that connect them to our tools, and how we respond when something goes wrong.

This isn't a "follow the runbook" role. You'll sit in our IT team, assess where we are today, set the direction, and build the processes and tooling that keep Veo secure as we scale.

What You Will Do

• 
You'll be hands-on across endpoint, identity, and operational security, and you'll be the go-to person for IT security across the business.

• 
Own endpoint security across our macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS and Android devices, including EDR, MDM, patching, encryption and hardening baselines

• 
Define and enforce our BYOD approach, using conditional access, device compliance checks and data separation so people can work flexibly without putting company data at risk

• 
Run SSO, SCIM and MFA across our SaaS applications, and own onboarding and offboarding so access is granted and removed on time, every time.

• 
Build identity governance, including regular access reviews, least-privilege access, and clear ownership of who has access to what

• 
Lead IT incident response from detection and triage through containment, investigation and post-incident review, and keep our playbooks sharp

• 
Monitor and respond to CVEs affecting our endpoints and SaaS tools, assessing risk, prioritizing fixes, and making sure patches are applied on time

• 
Plan and run phishing simulations and security awareness training that change behavior, and measure the results

• 
Drive day-to-day operational security, including alert monitoring, vulnerability management, SaaS vendor assessments, and keeping policies and runbooks current

• 
Lead our IT security work for GDPR and NIS2, from implementing controls to maintaining documentation and evidence, together with Legal and GRC

• 
Help lay the groundwork for future SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certification

• 
Own our office security systems, such as CCTV and door access, working with our Office Manager

What You Could Bring

• 
You've likely spent several years in IT security or security operations, ideally in a growing tech company, and you're comfortable being the person who owns security end-to-end.

That experience tends to show up in several of the following:

• 
Endpoint and device security: hands-on with EDR and MDM tools such as CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Hexnode, Intune or Kandji, across desktop and mobile, including securing BYOD environments

• 
Identity and access: deep experience with Google Workspace and Entra rolling out SSO, SCIM, and MFA, and running joiner/mover/leaver processes and access reviews.

• 
Incident response: you've led real incidents end-to-end and can stay calm and clear under pressure.

• 
Vulnerability management: you track CVEs, judge real-world risk quickly, and get fixes rolled out.

• 
Security culture: you've run phishing awareness programs and can explain risk in plain language to people who aren't technical.

• 
Compliance in practice: you've applied GDPR and NIS2 requirements in an operational role. Experience with SOC 2 or ISO 27001 is a strong advantage as we work towards them.

• 
Linux: administration and hardening experience is highly valued.

Nice To Have

• 
Scripting and automation (Python, PowerShell, Bash)

• 
SIEM experience

• 
Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, OSCP, or GIAC

How We Work

You'll be part of the IT team within Administration & Finance and work most closely with GRC, the Security Enablement Team, and Legal. We're pragmatic; we prioritize what matters most, and we favor simple solutions that help people work securely without slowing them down.

If you match on several of these areas but not all, apply anyway. We care more about how you think and what you'll own than about ticking every box.

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger

outcomes.

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to make meaningful contributions.

Perks and benefits

This job comes with several perks and benefits

Free lunch

Free lunch

Flexible working hours

Flexible working hours

Free coffee / tea

Free coffee / tea

Social gatherings

Social gatherings

Free office snacks

Free office snacks

Free friday beers

Free friday beers

Working at

Veo Technologies

Veo is the world’s leading AI powered and affordable football camera solution. We want to enable all teams around the world recording their football matches without the obstacles of finding a cameraman. Democratizing football, by giving access to video analysis, that in the past only were available for the few. The innovative dual-lense camera technology records the entire pitch at all times, with two 4K high resolution sports action lenses. Our intelligent software automatically follows the ball to create a broadcast view, while allowing you the controls with a simple click of you mouse. Our solution is developing better athletes. We know players are visual learners, seeing themselves play rather than being told of their mistakes is more effective and likely to produce results.

At a big company, the platform layer is a hundred engineers, and you own a slice of it. A driver. A subsystem. A corner of the release pipeline. You go deep, but you rarely get to hold the whole thing. With us you will. One team owns the entire layer: the operating system and firmware on every Airtame, the streaming stack underneath it, the releases that reach devices in the field, and the work of turning new hardware into a shipping product.

The role is roughly 60% hands-on the hardest problems and 40% growing the engineers who work on them.

**About Airtame

**We're around 55 people, headquartered in Copenhagen, and you'd work from there or remotely from within the EU. We make the hardware and the software that runs on it, so a change you make to the firmware ships to every Airtame in the field. The team is cross-functional and spread across Europe, and it reaches a global market from a small base.

Year one outcomes

Take AirPlay and Miracast from beta to default. They're in beta today. A year from now they should be solid enough to ship on by default across the Airtame product line, so customers get them without opting in and never have to think about which protocol they're using. Judge it by connection success rates on the fleet, and by how many customers rely on them day to day.

Make firmware releases boring. The best release is the one nobody has to think about: a predictable cadence, an automated quality bar, and shipping to the whole fleet as routine. A year from now, cutting a release should be a low-drama process the team trusts, and that should let you ship improvements more often. Judge it by release frequency, and by the confidence behind each one.

Turn the next board into a shipping Airtame. New silicon has to boot, hold a network, manage its heat, and run conferencing well enough to sell. By year-end there's a repeatable path from a board landing on a desk to a build QA can test, and you own it. Judge it by how long that path takes, and whether the thermal and acoustic targets hold.

Lead the team. You'll run the 1:1s, set the technical bar, and support team members' growth. The measure is simple: a year in, the team runs on your leadership day to day.

Push AI-assisted development further. The team already builds with AI daily. You'll lead the next step: sharper workflows, better tooling choices, new patterns that make the whole group faster. By year-end, the team's AI practices should be visibly ahead of where they started.

Who you are

• The player-coach. You've set a team's technical direction: the architecture calls, the reviews where the hard problems get caught. And you want the people side too. Growing engineers, running 1:1s, hiring. You're not looking to trade one for the other. Maybe you've been a staff engineer or tech lead ready to own a team, or a manager who never stopped writing code. Either way, 60/40 sounds about right to you.

• At home where software meets hardware. Embedded Linux is your familiar ground: the kernel, the BSP, userspace, C and C++ running on the device itself. You've spent time close to the metal: wireless stacks, streaming protocols, drivers. You can reason about a bug whether it lives in the firmware, the network, or the silicon.

• You ship to hardware you can't reach. When it's firmware on a device mounted in someone's meeting room, a bad release doesn't just roll back with a hotfix. You've owned software that ships to the field, so staged rollouts, over-the-air updates, and testing on the devices themselves come naturally. "Works on my bench" isn't the finish line for you.

• You've turned new hardware into a product. Bare silicon arrives, and someone has to make it boot, talk to the network, manage its heat, and eventually stream. You've done that kind of bringup, or worked close enough to it to lead the people who do.

• You use AI as a daily tool. You write code with it, debug with it, prototype with it. You've formed your own view on where it speeds things up and where it gets in the way, and you help the people around you do the same.

**Logistics

**Location: Remote in Europe, or hybrid from our Copenhagen office.

Employment type: Full-time preferred. We're also open to a project-based contract scoped to delivering the native protocol implementations.

****Why Airtame:

• A shift worth architecting. Airtame's software is moving onto a widening range of devices, including hardware from partners. Leading Platform now means designing for that spread, a bigger and more open problem than keeping one hardware line running.

• A span you can hold. From the bootloader to the release that reaches the field, the whole layer is one person's to shape here, at a size where you can still keep it in your head.

• A healthy work-life balance.

• Significant responsibility and ownership over projects and your field of expertise.

• Five weeks paid vacation and 5 days of extra paid AirtameFlex days.

• Flexible work environment, with a hybrid mindset.

• Pension and private health insurance (on FTE Copenhagen contract).

Airtame is an equal opportunity employer. We have colleagues across the globe, with both in-office and full-time remote workers. This feeds into our international hybrid mindset, with people from 25+ nationalities that make up the Airtame team.

Our work-life cultural balance is key to our success. Our team encompasses our values of trust and open communication to support each other and to collaborate in a fun and collective way.

****What Our Employment Decisions Are NOT Based On

****Race, colour, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, disability, ethnicity, national origin, marital status, family or parental status, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other legally protected classification or status. And we will not tolerate discrimination or harassment.

****What Our Employment Decisions ARE Based On

****Business needs, job requirements, individual qualifications, and candidates potential for growing with Airtame.

jobs.occupation: Tech Lead, Video Conferencing & Screen Sharing
jobs.description:
Most companies that do conferencing hand you one slice of it. The desktop app, or the media pipeline, or, maybe, the join flow. Everything else you pass over a wall to another team. Not in this case. One team owns the whole path across the Airtame platform: Airtame 3, Airtame Go, Virtual Airtame, and browser, desktop, and mobile apps that go with them. The bar remains at an effortless experience. Someone walks into a room, and starts sharing. No app to hunt for, no login to chase.

The team is four engineers, and we're hiring their technical and people lead: someone who spends about 60% of time hands-on with the hardest problems, and the rest growing the engineers around them.

**About Airtame

**We're around 55 people, headquartered in Copenhagen, and you'd work from there or remotely from within the EU. We make the hardware and the software that runs on it, so a call you make about the streaming stack ends up in a product bolted to a wall in meeting rooms around the world. The team is small, works across disciplines, and reaches a global market from a small base.

Year one outcomes

Make joining a call one step that works. Today, getting an authenticated meeting started from a room takes too many turns: personal logins, manual entry, a different quirk on every platform. A year from now, starting a scheduled call on Teams, Zoom, Google Meet, or Webex should be something a room just does. Judge it by how often it works on the first try, and how rarely it reaches support.

Take the friction out of screen sharing. The browser path loses first-time users: too many clicks, not enough signposting. You'll own getting a newcomer from a short code to their screen on the wall without a stumble, and getting Miracast and AirPlay stable enough to turn on by default.

Make it behave the same everywhere. The experience varies between Airtame 3, Virtual Airtame, browser, desktop, and mobile today. By year-end, sharing and calling should feel like one product no matter which surface you're on, with real-time quality that holds up on whatever network the room happens to have.

Lead the team. You'll run the 1:1s, set the technical bar, and support team members' growth. The measure is simple: a year in, the team runs on your leadership day to day.

Push AI-assisted development further. The team already builds with AI daily. You'll lead the next step: sharper workflows, better tooling choices, new patterns that make the whole group faster. By year-end, the team's AI practices should be visibly ahead of where they started.

Who you are

• The player-coach. You've owned a team's technical direction: the architecture calls, the reviews where the hard problems get caught. And you want the people side too. Growing engineers, running 1:1s, hiring. You're not looking to trade one for the other. Maybe you've been a staff engineer or tech lead ready to own a team, or a manager who never stopped building. Either way, 60/40 sounds about right to you.

• Comfortable across the stack. Real-time media is second nature to you: WebRTC, streaming, the way audio and video behave over a network you don't control. You've gone deep somewhere, whether a media pipeline, native protocols, or a cross-platform client, and you can hold your own everywhere else, on browser, desktop, and mobile.

• You've made stubborn systems cooperate. Half this job is getting software to play nicely with platforms you don't own: Teams, Zoom, Meet, Webex, the operating system's own media APIs, each with its own idea of how things should go. You've done that kind of integration, and you keep your head when every platform behaves differently.

• You measure yourself by the room. Your bar is the person standing at the "share" button. Someone who's never seen an Airtame, getting their screen up first try with no help. That's what you optimize for, and it steers the calls you make when something has to give.

• You use AI as a daily tool. You write code with it, debug with it, prototype with it. You've formed your own view on where it speeds things up and where it gets in the way, and you help the people around you do the same.

**Logistics

**Location: Remote in Europe, or hybrid from our Copenhagen office.

Employment type: Full-time preferred. We're also open to a project-based contract scoped to delivering the native protocol implementations.

****Why Airtame:

• The defining calls are still ahead. Airtame's collaboration software keeps spreading across more devices and form factors, so the shape of the next phase is still open, and you'd be the one setting it.

• At our size, a major call you make shows up in front of customers within weeks, so the feedback comes back fast.

• A healthy work-life balance.

We’re looking for a commercially minded Legal Counsel to join us on our journey to become one stronger, more integrated SaaS business. You’ll work across commercial contracts, privacy and cybersecurity in the European and North American market, partnering with colleagues across the organisation to find practical solutions and support our growth.

Reporting to our General Counsel, you’ll work at the intersection of commercial law, privacy, cybersecurity and business transformation. You’ll play a key role in enabling business growth, supporting complex customer deals, and ensuring that our legal commitments are practical, proportionate and aligned with how we operate.

Whether you’re building on your experience in private practice or looking to grow further in an in-house role, this is an opportunity for you to take ownership, learn along the way, and make a real difference.

We are open to on-site (offices in Copenhagen and Wrocław), hybrid, and remote working within two time zones of our offices (CET), plus the US East Coast.

**About Us

**Cookie Information, Piwik PRO, and Sheltr, are leading SaaS brands specialising in privacy-first compliance and analytics. Together, we’re building intuitive, user-friendly products that help organisations navigate data privacy and marketing insights. With headquarters in Copenhagen and an office in Wrocław, our teams have been working across various industries to build trusted data privacy solutions since 2011.

We’re bringing our brands closer together to build one company with a shared identity in the group, a clear focus and ambitious plan for the future. The Legal, Compliance and Cybersecurity team has a core role to play in making that happen.

The role

These will be your main tasks:

Handle commercial contracts, particularly sales contracts

• Draft, review and negotiate customer contracts for EU and US customers.

• Support partner, reseller and supplier agreements, as well as more specialised regulatory requirements such as DORA-related terms and US healthcare BAAs.

• Work closely with Sales and Account Management to find solutions that support our commercial goals while managing legal risks.

Privacy compliance and cybersecurity

• Support GDPR compliance, international data transfers, sub-processor management and relevant UK and US privacy requirements.

• Work with our Cybersecurity team on NIS2 compliance and related contractual requirements.

• Help our Cyber Security and Compliance teams to respond to customer privacy and security questionnaires, audits and due diligence requests.

• Advise Product teams on privacy, consent and data protection, helping ensure that our commitments reflect how we actually work.

Help shape the way we work

• Improve legal templates, processes and ways of working as the business grows.

• Collaborate with colleagues across Sales, Product, Security, Finance and Operations.

• Contribute to shaping our legal function and how we support the wider business.

**About You

**You’re a structured, independent, and commercially minded lawyer who enjoys working with people and finding practical solutions. You combine sound legal judgement with a practical understanding of how a business operates. You’re comfortable challenging assumptions, thinking creatively and making decisions, even when the answer isn’t entirely straightforward.

You know that good legal advice is not just about identifying risks; it’s about helping the business understand those risks and finding a way forward.

You bring:

• 2-5 years of experience with commercial contracts, gained in-house or at a law firm.

• An understanding of B2B contracting and an interest in SaaS or technology businesses.

• Working knowledge of GDPR and privacy law in a commercial context, or relevant experience with HIPAA and US privacy law.

• The ability to communicate clearly, and comfortable working directly with Sales on live deals and making pragmatic judgement calls.

• Fluency in English (C2).

Nice-to-haves

• Experience with cybersecurity regulations (NIS2 and/or DORA).

• Experience with HIPAA, including negotiating BAAs.

• Knowledge of corporate governance, employment/HR legal matters (DK, PL, DE, and/or US).

• Experience with US customers and US commercial contracting, including state privacy laws and/or wiretap/tracking litigation risk.

• Experience building processes and templates in a growing legal function.

What we offer

• The opportunity to make a real impact. You’ll help shape a growing international SaaS business as it evolves towards a more integrated, enterprise-ready organisation. You won’t simply be maintaining existing processes; you’ll help develop the legal and commercial foundations for our next stage of growth.

• International exposure and commercial ownership. You’ll work on customer and partner relationships across the US and Europe, gaining exposure to complex commercial negotiations and a broad range of legal and regulatory challenges.

• The chance to broaden your expertise, take ownership of meaningful projects and grow with the business.

• Professional development budget, health insurance, and other benefits.

• A positive, informal workplace.

Application process

We’re looking to fill the position as soon as possible and will be inviting candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis, so don’t hesitate to send your application today.

This is what our recruitment process looks like:

• A brief screening call with our Talent Partner (online, approx. 30 mins)

• An in-depth interview with the General Counsel and a stakeholder from the company (online)

• A final interview with our General Counsel including a live case (online or in-person, TBD)

Our Commitment to Diversity & Inclusion

At Cookie Information & Piwik PRO we value diversity as a cornerstone of our success. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, religion, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability. We recognise that certain groups are underrepresented in the tech industry, and we encourage everyone to apply and help us shape a more inclusive workspace.

With an IoT platform connecting more than 6 million units — and growing — Trackunit is building the platform that will enable the construction industry to work faster, smarter, and more securely. And we need you to help run and scale it.

As an SRE, you will join our Europe-based team and be part of a global SRE organization spanning Europe and Canada. This is a hands-on role focused on the daily operation and continuous improvement of our platform, with room to grow into larger design and architecture work as you build depth.

The platform owned by SRE consists of an AWS cloud, Kubernetes clusters (EKS), and our IaC setup running Terraform and Terramate, as well as a GitOps delivery platform built on Argo CD and Atlantis.

We support engineering teams with 150+ developers. You will help keep a platform used by 15,000+ active users every day secure, available, and easy to build on.

We're looking for someone curious and collaborative — happy to share knowledge and ask questions as well.

Experience level: roughly 2–5 years in an SRE, DevOps, platform, or infrastructure operations role. If you're further along and the day-to-day scope appeals to you, apply anyway — we'll have the conversation.

With locations in the heart of Copenhagen, Kolding, Aarhus, and Aalborg, we offer a flexible setup with the possibility to work from one of our locations — or remotely from anywhere in Denmark.

**What's in it for you?

**

• International environment with regular check-ins and social events across teams, departments and borders.

• We take your personal and professional development goals seriously and we support them through training, coaching, and mindfulness as well as with an open feedback culture to enable you to identify your strengths and opportunities.

• Flexibility and hybrid working is not just a cliché to us or something we state in a job posting. We offer a flexible setup because we believe you know best how to structure your work. Once you have chosen how you work best, let us know what you need: we got you covered with the IT equipment you need for your work.

• Turning the Tide. At Trackunit, we aim to create and contribute to an inclusive workplace. And this priority starts with our hiring — we do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity, sexual orientation, personal expression, ethnicity, religious belief, or disability status. We only assess candidates on their qualifications and merit. Learn more about TIDE and other DE&I initiatives here.

**What You'll Do

**Your week will be a mix of keeping things running well and making them better.

• Operate and improve the platform. Monitoring, alerting, capacity, cost, and the steady stream of small improvements that keep a large AWS and Kubernetes estate healthy.

• Work in code, not consoles. Infrastructure changes go through Terraform and Helm, reviewed as pull requests and delivered through Atlantis and Argo CD.

• Keep the platform secure. Patching, vulnerability remediation, base image updates, and closing findings — a recurring, meaningful part of the job rather than a side task.

• Take part in incident response. You'll join our on-call rotation (SRE team, business hours) and contribute to incidents and follow-up work.

• Handle triage and requests from developer teams. Understanding what they need, unblocking them, and spotting when a repeated request could be automated.

**Who You Are

**We think you'll need

• Hands-on experience running workloads on AWS.

• Basic knowledge with Kubernetes.

• Basic knowledge about infrastructure as code, ideally Terraform.

• Comfortable with Git, Linux and Windows.

• Clear written communication — a lot of our work happens in tickets, PRs, and docs.

**Nice to have, not expected

**

• EKS specifically, or tooling like Karpenter, Argo CD, Atlantis, or Terramate.

• Observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, Sumo Logic, or similar).

• Scripting in Python or Go.

• Security or compliance work — vulnerability management, CIS benchmarks, certification programmes.

• Multi-region or multi-account AWS architecture.

**What Matters More Than The Checklist

**

• You’re curious and self-driven, while also knowing when to ask for help when needed.

• You finish things. Small, well-tested changes shipped consistently beat big ideas that stall.

• You care about the developers and customers using the platform, not just the platform itself.

On AI: experience with AI tooling is not a requirement. An interest in working with it is. We already use AI in our daily engineering work — including MCP servers and agents against our own platform — and we expect that to grow. We don’t expect you to have experience with this—but we do expect curiosity and a willingness to learn.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries — this is what we're looking for ideally, but if you're excited about this role and your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification, we still encourage you to apply.

**How You'll Grow Here

**We hire at this level expecting you to move beyond it, and we've structured the team so that happens on purpose rather than by accident.

• A rotation model that protects your focus. The team splits between operational duty and project work, so you're not permanently interrupt-driven. You get real blocks of time to go deep on something.

• Mentorship that's built in. Senior colleagues review your PRs and pair with you on incidents. Asking questions is the expected behaviour, not a sign you're struggling.

• Exposure to the big architecture work. You'll start with scoped pieces and take on more as you build context.

• A clear conversation about your development. Regular 1:1s that cover where you want to be, not just what you shipped last sprint.

**What We're Building Next

**Trackunit is moving from a SaaS company to a platform built on telemetry data from the construction industry worldwide. For SRE, that means going beyond delivering infrastructure to building the capabilities that let our developers and customers spin up environments tailored to their needs in the regions they need them.

Things on our roadmap include:

• Expanding the platform into a true multi-region architecture.

• Building self-service platform capabilities so developer teams move at their own pace.

• Making better use of AI in our own operations, through MCP servers and agents.

You won't be expected to lead these on day one. You will be in the room, and there will be pieces with your name on them.

**What Happens From Here — Recruitment Process Overview

**

• Virtual meet and greet. Meet with a member of our Talent Partner team

• Personality-based interview. You will be asked to complete an online personality assessment prior to the interview. There are no correct answers and we are not trying to categorise you — the aim is a dialogue about the results and Trackunit's culture, so you get to know us better as well.

• Assignment-specific interview. You will be given a case to prepare after the initial screening interview. You will present the case to relevant colleagues across Trackunit, who you will also work closely with in the role.

• Virtual meet and greet. Meet with Engineering Manager, Kåre Brandborg and an SRE team member.

• References and background checks (if needed). If required, we will obtain references from former employers and perform level-specific background checks, if you have not provided these yourself.

• Offer presentation and walk-through. We're lucky to have you!

**Coming Together To Connect Construction

**We're committed to construction — one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale.

We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products — it's a way of life at Trackunit. We're proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues get together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do it to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world.

The question is: Are you in?

jobs.occupation: Experienced Senior Lean Consultant for Project Excellence at Novo Nordisk Engineering
jobs.description:
If you’re energised by driving lean transformation at a company level and you thrive on turning complex challenges into tangible business impact, we’d love to hear from you!

Who we are

We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Lean Consultant to join our team of highly skilled colleagues in the Project Excellence department. In Project Excellence, we act as internal consultants grounded in Lean, supporting projects and leadership across NNE by strengthening performance management, structured problem solving and continuous improvement practices.

As a Senior Lean Consultant, you will work closely with project organisations and leaders to set direction for improvement initiatives, build Lean capabilities and drive performance. At the same time, you will take an active, hands-on role in facilitating problem solving and implementing improvements on our most critical projects, ensuring that ideas translate into real impact.

This role offers a unique opportunity to operate at the intersection of leadership, Lean transformation and project execution, contributing to building a strong and sustainable performance and improvement culture across NNE.

You’ll be based in our Virum Office, but the role requires you to visit our project sites in Kalundborg and around the Copenhagen area on a regular basis.

How you might spend your days

As a Senior Lean Consultant, you’ll be:

• Helping the Project Excellence department set direction for continuous improvement and Lean in NNE, aligned with NNE’s strategy

• Building Lean capabilities by developing and embedding structured problem solving, lean project management and continuous improvement practices

• Designing and delivering training in Lean tools, Lean principles and Lean ways of working across NNE

• Coaching leaders and teams to strengthen performance management and Lean leadership behaviours

• Facilitating and driving structured problem-solving on major projects, using A3 thinking as our core approach

• Advising on consistent implementation of improvements, ensuring solutions are anchored and deliver real impact

Who you are

We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you are:

• Passionate about Lean thinking and driven to create real lasting business impact

• Confident in engaging, challenging and developing leaders and teams at all levels

• Comfortable operating in complex environments, bringing clarity, structure and direction

• Pragmatic and execution-focused with a great drive to turn ideas into results

• A credible role model who takes ownership and leads by example

What you bring to the role

In all positions, there are some things that are preferred, and others, a bonus. If you do not meet all the qualifications listed below, you are welcome to offer alternative experience that you think would be valuable in this role:

• Extensive experience driving continuous improvement and lean transformations in complex organisations

• Proven ability to lead and implement change with measurable impact

• Solid experience working closely with senior leaders on performance and improvement agendas

• A relevant academic degree at Master level

• Excellent facilitation, coaching and stakeholder management skills across organisational levels

Life at NNE

NNE is short for Novo Nordisk Engineering. And for all of us who work here, NNE means so much more.

At NNE, you become part of a vibrant, project-based environment built on close day-to-day collaboration. The role is therefore primarily on-site, with physical presence at the workplace expected five days a week. Limited flexibility for occasional remote work may be accommodated in line with business needs.

We are, at our core, a people business and, as such, committed to continuously developing our people and the way we work together. We do not expect you to know it all from day one, and we truly believe a great start makes a real difference. We therefore welcome new colleagues with our award-nominated onboarding programme, supported by a range of in-house talent and development initiatives designed to support your long-term growth.

You can read more about the benefits we offer here.

Did we spark your curiosity? If you’re ready to join our passion, let’s hear from you.

Deadline of application is 13th November 2026

Questions before applying? Send us a quick text to arrange a convenient time to chat. Please Contact Director Daniel Iwarsson at +45 3075 7823 or Principal Consultant, Mikkel Bonne at +45 3191 8723 between 12.00-15.00 (12 AM-3 PM) on weekdays.

Please note:

• We only accept applications submitted through our online recruitment system

• You do not need to attach a cover letter, but please include a few sentences about why you are applying in your resume or CV

• We invite to interviews on a running basis.

Fair hiring:

At NNE, we are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equal opportunities for all job applicants. To maintain fairness, we request that you refrain from including a personal photo in your CV.

All Gravy is the AI-native people operating platform for hospitality and retail. 🥞

We're modernising how frontline teams work, replacing scattered tools and outdated systems with a single app that's actually built for the way people work & socialise today. Our AI Colleague gives staff instant answers & executes day-to-day tasks, freeing up managers to focus on people & customers instead of paperwork. We work with some of the most exciting brands in hospitality and retail, including Gail's, L'Osteria, Dishoom, Pizza Pilgrims, Ottolenghi, Q8 and 7-Eleven. Today over 2,000 restaurants and stores trust us to run their teams.

We've grown 10x in two years and are accelerating into new markets. Our team spans a wide range of nationalities and backgrounds, united by one mission: to create better work lives for the 80% of the world that do not sit behind a desk. 🚀

**🤩 About The Role

**We are looking for Senior Account Executive who loves the chase, the close and the craft. You’ll own a territory and build your own pipeline of high-value targets, and booming inbound channel feeding you qualified opportunities. You call the shots on where to hunt, who to warm, and how to win. We’ll back you with marketing air cover, product firepower, and leadership you can trust for support and development.

**🎯 What You Will Do

**

• Create and run your target list of dream logos in our ICP. Name them, map them, multi-thread them.

• Work a blended pipe: your self-sourced opportunities plus SDR-sourced meetings you turn into revenue.

• Full cycle everything: discovery → tailored demo → value proof → commercial design → close → high-five.

• Build business cases that make budget holders nod and sign (ROI, payback, the whole nine yards).

• Feedback like a pro: turn deal learnings into sharper messaging, better product bets, and smoother process.

• Beat targets without burning out.

🙌 **You’ll thrive here if you…

**

• You speak excellent English and are based in Copenhagen.

• 5+ years of SaaS sales under your belt, fluent in consultative selling, and MEDPICC. Psst... If you’ve sold into hospitality, we’re listening even harder.

• You’re curious, ambitious, disciplined, and self-driven.

• Are owner-minded. You don’t wait for leads, you create momentum and you love a clean CRM.

• Can navigate complex cycles and senior stakeholders, you’re credible in the boardroom and fun.

• Are data-curious and coachable. You test, learn, and iterate faster than most people.

**💎 Why All Gravy

**

• Grow fast, for real. We promote from within, move quickly, and give you real responsibility from day one.

• A culture that actually develops you. Honest feedback, active coaching, and the autonomy to experiment. We invest in you because your growth is our growth.

• Work that matters. Your work will directly impact the daily lives of millions of frontline workers.

• You'll work with people who've built, scaled, and won. Ex-founders, operators, all here because they want to do it again, bigger.

• The good stuff too. Prime office location, team lunches, Friday bars, padel tournaments, wine tastings, offsites, top-tier equipment, and a fridge that's always stocked. We work hard and celebrate harder.

Ready to roll? Curious, competitive, kind? Apply, even if you don’t tick every box. Attitude and growth mindset matter. Let’s build the future of frontline work together.

About ChemoMetec

ChemoMetec is a worldwide leading manufacturer of cell counting and analysis equipment. We specialize in developing and producing high-precision instrumentation, delivering consistent data for thousands of customers across biotech, pharma, and academic segments.

About the Role

We are seeking a highly organized and scientifically skilled Product Specialist - Technical Support & Documentation to lead technical support for ChemoMetec’s portfolio of analytical cell-counting instruments. In this support-centered role, you will handle technical inquiries from both customers and colleagues and act as the go-to reference for technically accurate and compliant solutions. The role combines life science, technical documentation, and QA collaboration, making it ideal for someone with a strong scientific background and a passion for structured problem-solving.

We are hiring two Product Specialists for our technical support team: one focused on documentation and one on data analysis. You will be part of the Product Management Department and work closely with QA, Field Application Scientists, and product teams to resolve customer complaints, complete technical documentation, and maintain our support infrastructure. A solid foundation in mathematics and validation methodologies, along with a strong understanding of GMP regulatory requirements, is essential to succeed in this role.

Key Responsibilities

• Provide technical support across all instrument platforms, with a focus on structured problem-solving and documentation.

• Collaborate with QA to complete technical questionnaires and support the resolution of customer complaints.

• Maintain and organize our support database platform, ensuring technical records are accurate and accessible.

• Proofread and write technical notes, user guides, and comparison studies.

• Develop and implement procedures to support both existing and new products.

• Ensure all support activities comply with GMP and relevant quality standards.

• Act as a subject matter expert on instrumentation and scientific applications, providing technical insight to internal teams.

Your Profile

• PhD in Biology, Physics, or a related scientific discipline.

• Solid foundation in mathematics and validation methodologies, and a strong understanding of GMP regulatory requirements.

• Strong understanding of microscopy, analytical instrumentation, and pharmaceutical workflows.

• Highly organized, structured, and detail-oriented.

• Excellent written communication skills, with experience producing technical documentation.

• Familiarity with support platforms or ticketing systems is a plus.

• Comfortable working cross-functionally in a fast-paced, technical environment.

Why join ChemoMetec?

At ChemoMetec, we believe that great people make a great workplace. We value both personal and professional development and offer an environment where you can grow, take responsibility, and make an impact. You will become part of a team of talented and supportive colleagues who enjoy working together in an informal and welcoming atmosphere. We also believe that strong relationships go beyond the workplace, which is why we regularly bring colleagues together through company-wide events to build connections and strengthen relationships across the organization.

Practical information

Both positions are on-site at our HQ in Allerød, Denmark. You will refer to Director, Ph.D. Product Management Bassam Tawfik.

Starting date is as soon as possible, and we conduct interviews on an ongoing basis. Deadline for applying is 20 November 2026.

If you have any further questions about this job opportunity, feel free to contact Frederikke Hvidberg, fhv@chemometec.com

Please attach a motivation letter and a resume.

**OrderYOYO | Copenhagen based

**What We Do At OrderYOYO

**We help restaurants succeed online by providing them with personalised branded mobile apps, websites and personalised marketing. We are ensuring that small to medium-sized restaurants and chains are not subjected to lofty commissions and giving the restaurant the ownership of their success.

**About The Role

**Commercial Data Analyst

Location: Copenhagen base

Hours: 40hours/ week

Salary: up to 40,000DKK/ month

We are looking for an analytical and commercially minded Commercial Data Analyst to join us, reporting to our CCO. You’ll turn data from across our commercial teams, covering sales, account management, customer success, B2B marketing, pricing and partner performance, into clear, actionable insight, giving our leaders one trusted view of performance across every OrderYOYO market. Working closely with market leads, Sales, Marketing, Finance and Product, you’ll help us understand what drives growth in each market and focus our efforts where they’ll make the biggest difference!

**Here’s a taste of what you’ll be doing:

**

• Analysing performance across all our commercial activities, including sales, account management, customer success, marketing and partnerships, in every market.

• Tracking and reporting on key commercial metrics such as new restaurant acquisition, revenue, order volumes, churn, retention and pipeline conversion.

• Owning our regular commercial reporting, including weekly, monthly and quarterly performance packs for leadership.

• Designing, building and maintaining dashboards that give a single, trusted view of performance and let teams self-serve their data.

• Comparing performance between our 11 markets, teams and channels to spot what’s working, where we can improve and where the risks are.

• Analysing the impact of pricing, campaigns and commercial initiatives on performance.

• Delivering ad hoc analysis to answer business questions and support commercial decisions, business cases and initiatives.

• Making sure commercial data is accurate and consistent across markets, working with CRM and system owners to close any gaps.

• Defining and documenting KPIs so everyone measures performance in the same way.

• Supporting forecasting, target setting and planning with Finance, and flagging variances against target early.

• Your success will be measured on the accuracy and timeliness of reporting, dashboard adoption, data quality, turnaround on ad hoc requests, forecast accuracy and stakeholder satisfaction.

**What We Are Looking For In You

**

• Proven experience in a commercial, sales, revenue or business analyst role.

• Experience building dashboards and reports in BI tools such as Power BI, Tableau or Looker.

• Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills, and experience working with CRM data (e.g. HubSpot or Salesforce).

• A strong understanding of commercial metrics such as revenue, pipeline, conversion, churn and retention, ideally within B2B SaaS.

• Analytical and curious: you can turn data into clear, actionable insight and recommendations.

• A confident communicator who can present findings to technical and non-technical stakeholders at all levels.

• Highly organised, with great attention to detail and a commitment to data accuracy.

• Comfortable in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

• Experience working across multiple markets, or with Python or R, is an advantage.

**Great to Have

**

• Experience working across multiple markets or countries.

• Experience with Python or R.

• Experience working in a high-growth, fast-paced business.

• Experience supporting forecasting, target setting or commercial planning alongside Finance.

• Experience defining KPIs or improving data governance and processes.

**About The Company Culture

**Who we are at OrderYOYO: Company culture is at the forefront of our minds creating an enjoyable, safe working environment where employee personal expression is supported. We are one team here at OrderYOYO and strive to help others succeed. Personal development and training plans are a key part of your journey within OrderYOYO, helping you be the best you can be by providing consistent and ongoing training for all aspects of the business. Our values (Passion, Action, Compassion, One Team) are what make us who we are and will be embedded in your day-to-day no matter what area of the business you work in.

**Benefits

**

• Monthly Friday Socials and regular ad-hoc socials.

• Quarterly Conferences and training days.

• Employee Awards.

• Holiday buying Scheme.

• Personal development plans and Genuine career development opportunities.

Your role

Bring your curiosity to work as our next Rental Desk Coordinator at our depot in Albertslund, outside of Copenhagen. You will be part of our Danish Rental Desk Team team reporting to our Operations and Service Lead. In this role, your mission is to deliver an outstanding customer experience, ensure operational excellence, and support profitable and sustainable rental activities. You will contribute directly to how we create high‑quality products and solutions for our customers.

Your day-to-day

• Handle customer inquiries, coordinate quotations, ensure optimal fleet planning, process work orders, and ensure accurate and timely invoicing

• Coordinate the tracking and transportation of rental equipment between customers and depots, ensuring timely availability and returns

• Handle rental contract administration including amendments and renewals with meticulous attention to detail

• Support the implementation of company processes, KPIs, and service standards, ensuring transparency, compliance, and continuous improvement across all rental activities

• Collaborate with the sales team to manage credit collection processes, ensuring financial accuracy and compliance

• Provide customers with accurate and timely documentation and information, supporting their rental experience effectively

• Support operations and rental team within Denmark and Norway

• You work closely with colleagues from Sales, Service, Logistics, Marketing, Accounting, and other Rental Desks, both locally and abroad.

Your skills and experience

• A secondary education diploma or equivalent professional experience

• Proficient communication skills in both Danish, English, and Norwegian, enabling clear and professional interactions across diverse stakeholders is a must

• Proactive approach to customer support, which enhances customer satisfaction and strengthen partnerships

• A problem-solving mindset and driven personality, through which you do everything you can to strive for continuous improvement and happy customers

• Strong understanding of business processes, administrative workflows, and safety procedures

• Demonstrated ability to prioritize tasks and manage time efficiently to meet operational targets and customer needs

• Proficiency with MS Office tools and experience with systems such as ERP, Salesforce, and Medius and a willingness to learn and adapt to new systems, ensuring smooth integration with internal processes

• A team player with strong communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills, contributing constructively while respecting diverse perspectives

• Basic knowledge or interest in logistics and understanding of equipment movement and planning is an advantage but not a must

We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every single requirement. We value diverse experiences and perspectives and are excited to see what you bring to the role.

Your compensation and benefits

At Atlas Copco Group, we are committed to fair and equitable compensation. Compensation is determined based on the position and its responsibilities, without regard to gender, race, ethnicity, religion, physical ability, sexual orientation, marital status, or any other protected characteristic. Our compensation offering is designed to be locally relevant, competitive, and aligned with the expectations of current and future talent.

Beyond compensation, we believe that a rewarding career is about having opportunities to learn, grow, contribute, and develop in an environment built on trust, collaboration, and continuous improvement. At Atlas Copco Group, we support our people in building long-term careers while making a meaningful impact through their work.

Your job location

This role requires you to work on-site at our depot located in Albertslund, where the offices are also located . You will be part of a dynamic team and enjoy the benefits of face-to-face collaboration. Some travel for training purposes will be required, mainly to Belgium where our head office is located.

Would you like to lead the Danish FP&A function in an international manufacturing company and help create greater financial transparency, stronger decision support and closer partnerships with operations and sales?

JELD-WEN is looking for a business-oriented Head of FP&A who can combine financial discipline with operational and commercial understanding. You will take a key role in the Danish organisation, where you will be responsible for strengthening the quality and credibility of financial information while developing FP&A into an increasingly proactive business partner.

Key finance role in an international manufacturing organisation

As Head of FP&A – Denmark, you will be a member of the Danish country leadership team and report to the Head of FP&A – Northern Europe. You will lead a team of two FP&A Analysts and work closely with leaders across operations, manufacturing and sales, as well as finance colleagues throughout Northern Europe and relevant stakeholders at headquarters.

Your initial focus will be to establish confidence in the Danish financial figures and ensure that reporting, forecasts and budgets are accurate, transparent and clearly explained. On this foundation, you will strengthen forward-looking analysis and decision support and bring the FP&A function closer to the commercial and operational organisation.

The position covers JELD-WEN’s two Danish manufacturing sites in Herning and Sønder Felding and requires regular presence at both locations. Working within an international matrix organisation, you will have a broad interface across functions, countries and organisational levels.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Leading monthly performance reporting, forecasting and budgeting for the Danish organisation

• Maintaining oversight of the Danish P&L, balance sheet and cash flow

• Ensuring the quality, transparency and credibility of financial information

• Explaining financial developments and the underlying operational and commercial drivers

• Ensuring compliance with relevant financial requirements, including US GAAP and local GAAP

• Acting as a financial business partner to leaders in operations, manufacturing, sales and the Danish country leadership team

• Translating financial and operational data into clear insights and recommendations

• Leading, developing and supporting two FP&A Analysts

• Improving and simplifying recurring reporting and FP&A processes

• Identifying opportunities to automate reporting and strengthen dashboard capabilities

• Contributing to the development of systems, data and FP&A practices across Northern Europe

Strong FP&A profile with business understanding

The ideal candidate brings a strong background within FP&A, business controlling or commercial finance, combined with broad experience in financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, performance management and business partnering. The position can be relevant both for an experienced finance leader and for a senior finance profile ready to take on broader responsibility for the FP&A agenda and leadership of a small team.

A good understanding of the operational and commercial drivers behind financial performance is important, together with the ability to take ownership of financial reporting, analysis and planning. Equally important is the ability to translate financial and operational data into clear insights and recommendations and to work closely with stakeholders across the business.

Experience from a manufacturing or operational environment is preferred, particularly where finance acts as a close business partner to operations and commercial functions. Experience from an international or matrix organisation will be an advantage.

You have strong analytical capabilities and are comfortable working with large datasets, financial models and Excel. Experience with ERP systems, dashboards and financial reporting or consolidation tools such as SAP, OneStream, HFM or Hyperion will be an advantage.

Previous people management experience is an advantage, but not necessarily a prerequisite. Leadership experience may also have been gained through project management, professional leadership or as a senior member of a finance team. What matters is the motivation and capability to lead and develop others while remaining close to both the numbers and the business.

As a person, you combine financial understanding with curiosity about the business. You are comfortable challenging assumptions, communicating financial topics to non-financial stakeholders and contributing to decision-making. You take ownership, create progress and are motivated by having a broad role that combines FP&A, business partnering and people leadership.You hold a relevant bachelor’s or master’s degree in finance, accounting, business administration or a related field and communicate professionally in both Danish and English.

**Shape the Future of Privacy

**

Usercentrics is a global leader in data privacy and privacy-led marketing solutions. We believe there is no need for a trade-off between growth and privacy compliance. Our vision is to unlock the potential of data privacy to empower a thriving digital ecosystem. We work with companies to create a healthy balance between data-driven business and privacy-led marketing for every size of enterprise. Our customers build trust with their users through improved transparency and control to drastically improve marketing and monetization, while achieving full privacy compliance.

**About the Office of AI

**

The Office of AI owns the strategy, governance, infrastructure, and enablement of AI across Usercentrics. We sit within the CTO office and work across all departments.

Mission: enable the entire organisation to adopt AI safely, responsibly, and effectively.

**About the role

**

You are the hands-on technical arm of AI adoption at Usercentrics. Finance, Legal, HR, Marketing, Customer Success, BI and every other department have real AI use cases, and your job is to turn them into governed, working software, not slide decks.

You will prototype and build department AI applications, run technical enablement sessions directly with the teams who will use them, and make sure everything you ship meets our governance standards before it goes live. You work from the use-case pipeline the AI Enablement Lead runs, and you report progress and adoption back into it.

This is not a support role bolted onto engineering. You are a full engineer, building with LLM APIs, MCP servers, and the internal AI platform, and you are expected to leave every pattern you build reusable by the next team. What you build feeds the platform layer: the AI Hub, MCP servers, Claude connector delivery, the Skill Hub. As that platform grows into its next layer, LLM access gateway, RAG infrastructure, model operations, and evaluation frameworks are the current candidates, you will contribute to that build alongside the rest of the Office of AI team, not just consume it.

On the shape of it: this is a small, senior team today, four to five people, and growing on both the engineering and enablement sides. You would be one of two engineers doing this work day to day, with a Staff AI Enablement Engineer setting the technical bar above you.

**Requirements

****What you will do

**

• Prototype, build, and hand over department AI applications, working directly with the business team that will own the outcome

• Run technical enablement sessions with non-engineering teams: walk them through what was built, how to use it, and how to ask for the next thing well

• Guide teams on tech stack choices, MCP servers, AI artefacts (Skills, Connectors, plugins), and integration patterns for AI in a business context

• Ensure every implementation you ship meets GRC standards before it reaches a business user

• Document reusable patterns and components and contribute them back into the platform layer: the AI Hub, MCP servers, Claude connector delivery, the Skill Hub

• Contribute to the platform's next layer as it gets built: LLM access gateway, RAG infrastructure, model operations, and evaluation frameworks

• Partner with the AI Enablement Lead on the use-case pipeline: help qualify requests, scope builds realistically, and report back on adoption

**What you bring

**

• 5+ years in software engineering, with a full-stack or solutions engineering background

• Genuinely hands-on with AI. You have built and shipped things with LLM APIs (Claude, OpenAI, or similar), not just prototyped them

• Strong communication with non-technical stakeholders. You can run a session with a Legal or Finance team and leave them able to use what you built, not just impressed by it

• Working knowledge of MCP servers, AI agent tooling, or integration patterns for AI in a business context

• Security- and governance-conscious engineering practice. You do not need to be told twice that this ships to a regulated business

**Nice to have

**

• Experience in consulting, solutions architecture, or embedded engineering

• Familiarity with the internal stack: Azure or GCP, and Usercentrics' own product platforms

• Exposure to model serving, RAG pipelines, or MLOps

• Background in AI governance or responsible AI deployment

**Benefits

****Why join Usercentrics?

**

• Joining Usercentrics means becoming part of a fast-growing, diverse and international team of tech enthusiasts and entrepreneurially-minded who build our success story

• together

• Company culture is important to us. We strive to continuously develop a positive, vibrant and inspiring environment that enables everyone to thrive both personally and professionally
