jobs.occupation: Chief Flight Instructor at GreyBird Pilot Academy - HQ located at Aarhus Airport, DK –  Ready to shape the future of pilot training? ✈️
jobs.description:
GreyBird Pilot Academy is more than a flight school. We are a fast-growing international business in an industry that never stands still – training the next generation of commercial pilots.

Since starting out in Aarhus in 2013, we have grown to seven bases across Europe – from Dublin in the west to Helsinki in the east. Our students fly under the Spanish sun and across European airspace. Today, more than 200 students are training to become commercial pilots with us, supported by over 40 flight instructors and a fleet of 12 Tecnam aircraft, with 13 more on the way.

This is where ambition becomes reality – where safety, people, technology, operations and training must all come together before the wheels leave the runway.

You have an aviation background and have instructed from the cockpit yourself. With us, you will join a highly skilled team with short decision-making lines and plenty of room to shape our development. We turn the dream of flying into a career – and you can help make that journey even better.

The role

The Chief Flight Instructor (CFI) is part of our ATO Core Team and holds overall responsibility for quality, standardisation and compliance in the flight and simulator training delivered by our flight instructors.

You are appointed by the Accountable Manager and report directly to the Head of Training, with whom you work closely to ensure consistent, high-quality training. The Head of Training may delegate tasks and authority to you within your area of responsibility.

Your key responsibilities include:

• 
Standardisation, supervision and training planning for the entire instructor team

• 
Developing and enforcing standard operating procedures for flight training

• 
Ensuring that all instructors hold valid licences, certificates and competencies

• 
Recruiting new instructors as well as guiding, mentoring and providing recurrent training for the existing team

• 
Assessing new bases as we expand into new countries

• 
Updating training materials and operations manuals on our in-house platform, SmartBird

• 
Taking part in ATO and management meetings, where you help set the direction for training

What we offer:

• 
Real decision-making authority over training quality and standards in a growing international organisation

• 
A direct reporting line to the Head of Training and close ties to management

• 
An established ATO with a clear, EASA-approved framework for the role

• 
Access to a modern and growing fleet

• 
An international working environment with colleagues and instructors from several countries

Requirements

The Chief Flight Instructor is a nominated post under EASA Part-ORA (ORA.ATO.210). In line with the regulation, the CFI must hold the highest pilot licence and at least one instructor certificate relevant to the courses the school offers. As GreyBird offers ATPL theory, several aircraft types and type rating-related training, we are looking for:

• 
CPL(A) or ATPL(A)

• 
Instructor certificate: FI(A)

• 
Additional instructor certificates such as CRI(A) and IRI(A) are considered an advantage

• 
A minimum of 1,000 hours as PIC, including at least 500 hours of instructional flying (industry practice is typically 1,500+ hours, and more experience counts in your favour)

• 
Ideally, you also have experience leading, standardising or developing other instructors

• 
Fluent English, spoken and written

How to apply

Ready to set the course for a role where you shape the standards for the next generation of pilots? Send us your application today – we look forward to hearing from you.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc Position: Endocrine Disruption in Fish with Focus on Histopathological Endpoint Development
jobs.description:
We invite applicants for a 3½-years Postdoctoral research position in Environmental Toxicology with a focus on histopathological and behavioral endpoints development in fish. The position is funded by the EU Partnership for Risk Assessment of Chemicals (PARC), the Danish EPA and University of Southern Denmark (SDU). The project will be carried out in the Ecotoxicology group at the Department of Biology, SDU. 

Qualifications: 
The successful candidate must hold a PhD degree in Environmental Toxicology. A strong background in chemical risk and hazard assessment and regulatory toxicology is highly appreciated. This includes knowledge of EU chemicals legislation and regulatory frameworks such as REACH, OECD test guidelines, AOP development, and/or pesticide and biocide risk assessment. Furthermore, the following experiences and skills are required: 

• 
Strong proficiency in English, both written and verbal. 

• 
Experience in teaching and supervision at the university level, including lectures, student examinations, and supervision of MSc students. 

• 
Hands-on experience in assessing endocrine disruption properties of chemicals using the Zebrafish (Danio rerio) model.  

• 
Strong documented knowledge of one or more endocrine pathways relevant to EU regulatory assessments (EATS modalities). 

• 
Extensive experience with OECD fish test protocols such as OECD TG 236 and OECD TG 210. 

• 
Documented experience in histopathology techniques, including tissue preparation, microtome sectioning, cryosectioning, H&E staining, microscopy, and image analysis. 

• 
Experience in behavioral assessment in zebrafish eleutheroembryos, e.g., using EthoVision XT or equivalent tracking and analysis software. 

The following qualifications are considered advantageous: 

• 
Experience with molecular biology techniques, including gene expression analysis (e.g., qPCR, transcriptomics). 

• 
Experience with immunohistochemistry and related imaging techniques. 

This position is particularly suited for a candidate with strong interest in bridging experimental ecotoxicology and regulatory chemical risk- and hazard assessment. 

Application deadline: 13. November 2026 at 23:59 hours local Danish time. 
Please see the full call, including how to apply, on www.sdu.dk

Good decisions start with good data. But good data does not just happen. At NORDEN, data comes from many places and is used across our business to understand markets, automate processes and make better decisions. Your job is to make sure that data is actually ready to be used.

As our new Data Engineer, you will build the pipelines and datasets that move data through our organisation and turn raw information into something people can trust and work with.

You will not be sitting far away from the business maintaining pipelines no one really talks about. You will work closely with digital and commercial colleagues, understand what they need and build the data foundation that helps them solve real problems.

And while shipping knowledge is something you will pick up along the way, curiosity about data and how to make it useful is something we hope you bring from day one.

Why this role?

Because there is a lot to build, improve and figure out.

You will join nine colleagues in our Data Engineering team in Copenhagen, working with large and varied datasets using PySpark, SQL, Azure DevOps and Microsoft Fabric. And our team is growing beyond Copenhagen. We are setting up a Data Engineering team in Singapore, starting with two colleagues, giving you an even broader team to work and share ideas with.

Some days will be about building something new. Others will be about improving what already exists, finding a smarter way to structure data or figuring out why something is not working quite as expected.

What connects it all is the purpose behind it: making data easier to trust, access and use across NORDEN.

You already know your way around data engineering. Now you are looking for a role where you can have more of a say in how things are built, not just build what has already been decided.

You will manage your solutions, contribute to technical decisions and collaborate closely with the business to understand what our data needs to do.

What you will be doing

You will work across the journey from raw data to reliable datasets that colleagues and systems across NORDEN can actually use.

You will:

• Build and maintain scalable data pipelines.

• Bring internal and external data together and turn it into trusted datasets.

• Transform raw data into useful features and insights.

• Improve how we capture, validate and enrich data.

• Build solutions that are reliable today without making life difficult for whoever needs to work with them tomorrow.

• Work with digital and commercial colleagues to understand what they need from our data and translate that into technical solutions.

What you bring

You know that good data solutions are not only about getting things to work, but about making them reliable, scalable and useful to others.

Besides this you likely have:

• Around 5 years of practical experience in data engineering or a similar role.

• A degree within data, IT, engineering or another analytical field.

• Eligibility to work in Denmark.

• Solid experience with Lakehouse architecture, for example in Microsoft Fabric or Azure Databricks.

• Experience designing and building data pipelines and working with how data is structured, transformed and made available to others.

• Experience contributing to technical decisions around data architecture and how data should be structured and used.

• The confidence to be responsible for your solutions, while still enjoying sparring with and learning from others.

• Good English communication skills, both written and spoken.

Application

Please upload your motivation letter, resume and relevant diplomas via our website as soon as possible and no later than 20 November 2026. Your motivation letter helps us understand what drives you, why you are interested in the role, and how your skills and experiences could contribute to the team. We are especially interested in your motivation and transferable skills, not a recap of your CV. It is your opportunity to tell us the story behind your application.

We review and interview candidates on an ongoing basis.

We will do our best to get back to you at least within ten working days after the application deadline, 20 November 2026.

In NORDEN we value a range of perspectives, educational backgrounds and professional experience and encourages all qualified candidates to apply.

Were you missing anything in this job ad? Please share your feedback with us here.

Our company

We are a global provider of ocean-based freight services for bulk and project cargo of all sizes. We integrate freight solutions with port logistics, helping our customers optimise and decarbonise supply chains. We provide tailored solutions built on flexibility, reliability, and intelligence.

Our agile business model ensures stability by continuously adapting our fleet to market developments and customer needs.

Founded in 1871, NORDEN is one of Denmark’s oldest internationally operating shipping companies. Incorporated in Denmark, we are listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen as part of the OMX Nordic Large Cap index.

With offices across 6 continents, we are a truly integrated part of global trade.

You know shipping. Now you can use that knowledge in a completely different way.

At NORDEN, our core business applications sit right at the heart of how our commercial teams work. But getting the most out of them is not only about the technology. It is about understanding how shipping actually works, how people use the systems every day and where things could work better.

As our new Business Application Manager, you will bring your shipping experience into that space.

You will work with colleagues across NORDEN to improve how we use our core business applications, optimise the processes around them and help turn business needs into better ways of working.

You do not need to come from IT or have worked as a Business Application Manager before. You understand shipping, likely from operations, control/finance or laytime and are curious about how systems and technology can make the business work better.

Why this role?

Because you get to use your shipping knowledge from a completely new angle.

You will join our Business Applications team of six colleagues across Copenhagen, Cyprus and Singapore, working closely with colleagues from the business as well as Digital Services and Solutions.

Your primary focus will be IMOS, but your work will also take you into applications such as SEDNA, PortLog, Shipfix and other tools used across NORDEN.

Some days you might be looking at how a process could work better in IMOS. Others you could be helping colleagues get more out of an application, supporting a new implementation or working with our commercial AI assistant tools.

What connects it all is understanding how people work today and finding ways for our systems and processes to support them better.

Your base will be our office in Hellerup, with occasional travel to other NORDEN offices.

What you will be doing

You will work where shipping, people, processes and technology meet.

You will:

• Analyse how our business applications and surrounding processes are used and identify opportunities to improve them.

• Participate in and lead projects implementing new applications, processes and integrations.

• Train and support colleagues in getting the most out of our applications.

• Work with teams across NORDEN to create better alignment between processes and systems.

• Support and develop the use of our commercial AI assistant tools.

• Work primarily with IMOS while also getting involved with SEDNA, PortLog, Shipfix and other business applications.

What you bring

You do not need to be an IT specialist. What matters most is your understanding of shipping and how these applications are used in practice. You may have used them as an end user up to now, and that experience could be exactly what makes you well suited for this role.

Besides this you likely:

• Have experience from shipping, from operations, control/finance or laytime.

• Have worked with shipping business applications and are familiar with IMOS.

• Are curious about technology, AI and digitalisation and how they can improve the way a business operates.

You are curious about how people work and what could make their day-to-day easier. You listen, ask questions and connect the dots between people, processes and systems, turning what you learn into practical improvements.

In NORDEN we value a range of perspectives, educational backgrounds and professional experience and encourages all qualified candidates to apply.

As Release Operations Manager, you will make sure every Novocare release reaches markets in a way that is consistent, scalable and compliant. You will lead the operational planning and rollout of Novocare V5 and ongoing releases across global markets, turning approved priorities into one clear, integrated plan. By keeping complex work visible and moving, you will help central teams, regions and affiliates launch with confidence, so Novocare support reaches each market reliably.

What you’ll bring

• A relevant degree in business, IT, engineering or project/programme management, or equivalent professional experience.

• Experience coordinating digital product or platform releases, multi-market rollouts or complex cross-functional programmes.

• The ability to manage integrated plans, dependencies, risks, readiness checks and stakeholder actions.

• A structured, dependable way of working that keeps complex work visible and moving.

• Clear communication and the ability to align teams without relying on line authority.

• A proactive, solution-oriented approach: you spot risks early, challenge stakeholders constructively when needed and escalate at the right time.

• A strong can-do mindset and a collaborative way of working.

• Familiarity with web/CMS or CRM environments.

Within approved priorities, you will own the operational plan, release calendar and readiness tracking, and you will recommend sequencing or a readiness hold when quality or market readiness is at risk.

• Own and continuously improve operational rollout procedures, so every market and release follows a consistent, scalable and compliant approach.

• Translate approved priorities into an integrated release plan with milestones, dependencies, readiness gates and rollout waves, and maintain the release calendar, dependency map, risk log and decision and action tracking.

• Facilitate planning and readiness reviews, confirming owners, evidence, actions and escalation paths.

• Coordinate rollout waves with Market Enablement and regional contacts, covering market readiness, localisation, training, communications, support and cutover.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Novocare within the newly established Consumer Care unit, reporting to Mathias Bauer Munk, Associate Director Novocare.

In PPS (Product & Portfolio Strategy), colleagues work across markets to serve people around the world and help improve health at scale.

Your remit is global. Working centrally, you will partner with Novocare leadership and capability leads; product, platform, content and GBS publishing teams; QA, Compliance, MLR, Privacy, Data and Consumer Care specialists; and delivery partners, Regional Market Enablers and affiliates. Your role is to bring everyone together around one plan, raise risks early and keep decisions moving. Some travel may be required.

We are looking for a Product Compliance Manager to join Veo's newly established Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) team.

As Veo continues to grow, we navigate a broad range of regulatory requirements across our products and business, from certifications, product safety, and environmental regulation to market access and broader compliance obligations.

In this role, you will focus on product-related regulatory compliance and certifications, while also working across Veo's broader compliance agenda. You will work closely with colleagues across Hardware, Product Development, Production, Procurement and other parts of the business to understand applicable requirements and help translate them into practical processes and solutions.

You will join a small GRC team with a broad mandate and significant exposure across Veo. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys understanding regulation, technology, and business.

**Key responsibilities:

**

• Coordinate Veo's product certification and market-access activities across relevant markets, working closely with Hardware, Production and other internal stakeholders.

• Monitor and assess new and changing regulatory requirements relevant to Veo and help determine their practical implications for our products and business.

• Develop and maintain a structured overview of regulatory and certification requirements applicable to Veo's products throughout their lifecycle.

• Drive and coordinate implementation of regulatory and compliance requirements across relevant business functions, ensuring clear ownership, appropriate documentation and timely follow-up.

• Work with regulatory frameworks relevant to Veo's products, including areas such as product safety, batteries, electrical and electronic equipment, environmental requirements, waste and recycling obligations and related product compliance requirements.

• Coordinate with external certification bodies, laboratories, consultants and other specialists where required.

• Maintain and develop compliance documentation, certification records, technical files, declarations and other evidence required to demonstrate compliance.

• Support the assessment of regulatory and compliance implications when Veo enters new markets, introduces new products or makes material changes to existing products.

• Support Veo's broader compliance activities, including policies, procedures, monitoring, due diligence, risk assessments and training.

• Support customer, auditor and other stakeholder requests relating to compliance and certifications.

• Contribute to the continued development of Veo's broader GRC framework and take part in cross-functional compliance projects as required.

**Your qualifications:

**

• Relevant higher education in engineering, technology, law, business, quality/compliance, or another relevant discipline.

• Relevant professional experience within product compliance, regulatory compliance, certification, quality/regulatory affairs or a similar area, preferably from an international company.

• Experience working with regulatory requirements affecting hardware or electronic products is an advantage.

• Experience with one or more areas such as product safety, product certifications, battery regulation, electrical/electronic equipment regulation, environmental product requirements, waste/recycling regulation or similar regulatory regimes.

• Experience coordinating certification processes, testing, technical documentation, declarations or interactions with certification bodies and laboratories is highly relevant.

• Broader compliance experience, for example within sanctions and export controls, third-party due diligence, anti-bribery and corruption or other corporate compliance areas, is an advantage.

• An ability to understand complex regulatory requirements and translate them into practical requirements for technical, operational and commercial teams.

• Strong project and stakeholder management skills, with experience coordinating initiatives across different functions and areas of expertise.

• A structured approach to documentation, monitoring and follow-up, combined with the ability to identify and prioritize material compliance risks.

• Strong business understanding and a pragmatic approach to compliance. You should be comfortable finding solutions that meet regulatory requirements while enabling the business to operate effectively.

• Comfortable working independently and taking ownership in an environment where processes and frameworks are still being developed.

• Strong communication skills and professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

At Veo, the Governance, Risk & Compliance team provides oversight, coordination and assurance across the company. We work closely with teams throughout Veo to ensure that regulatory requirements and risks are identified, appropriately owned and effectively managed.

You will report to the Head of Governance, Risk & Compliance and will have considerable opportunity to shape how Veo approaches compliance as the company continues to grow.

Contact Martin Eger Larsen one mel@veo.co if you have any questions

jobs.description:
Own the technical backbone for your workstream. As the Technical Workstream Lead for Procure to Pay you sit side-by-side with the Global Process Owner (GPO) and Global Process Leads (GPLs) to translate process design into robust and scalable technology across ERP, PLM, QMS procurement system solutions. You lead the technical scope for your workstream - architecture, build, environments, integrations, data migration, non-functionals, security/compliance, releases, and hyper-care – through stage gates to successful handover.

Ambu is transforming our core enterprise platforms (e.g., ERP, QMS, PLM), and each workstream needs a dedicated technical leader to ensure high-quality, compliant delivery that enables standardized, high-performing global processes.

**The role

**You are the end-to-end technical owner for one workstream. You co-lead the workstream together with the Business Workstream Lead/GPO, ensuring process-system alignment, decision-ready design, disciplined delivery, and operational readiness for your scope.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• 
Technical governance within your workstream

• 
Run technical governance for the workstream. Prepare decision-ready design packs and status for the Design Authority

• 
Own the workstream technical enablement of the Procure to Pay process. Assess run-time/architecture risks, define mitigations, and escalate with clear options

• 
Safeguard solution integrity against enterprise standards and non-functional requirements

• 
Design, build, environments, and release engineering

• 
Lead technical design for your workstream: integrations, extensions, data model, security roles, automation

• 
Define and manage environments for the workstream: branching strategy, CI/CD pipelines, and code quality gates

• 
Manage technical debt, versioning, and change control with impact analysis across upstream/downstream systems

• 
Data migration and cutover

• 
Plan and execute migration tooling, trial loads, reconciliations, and cutover steps for your workstream objects

• 
Security, privacy, and compliance

• 
Ensure cybersecurity, privacy, SoD, and validation/CSV compliance in collaboration with QA/Validation Lead

• 
Delivery orchestration and hyper-care

• 
Coordinate internal platform teams and external vendors for your scope

• 
Lead hyper-care triage and stabilization for the workstream. Complete documentation and knowledge transfer to run

• 
Program collaboration

• 
Partner daily with the GPO, GPLs, and Business Workstream Lead; align on scope, decisions, and adoption

• 
Work with PMO on stage gates, quality reviews, plans, and dependencies to other workstreams

**Your profile

**

• 8+ years delivering technical workstreams on enterprise platforms (ERP, QMS, PLM or similar) in global settings

• Proven leadership of architecture, integrations (API/iPaaS), data migration, and release management within a defined scope

• Strong command of non-functionals: performance, reliability, security, privacy, SoD, and validation/CSV

• Hands-on experience with CI/CD, environment strategy, branching, automation testing, and code quality

• Adept at partnering with GPOs/GPLs to translate future-state processes into scalable solution designs

• Skilled in vendor management and cross-team coordination. Clear, concise communicator in English

• Willingness to travel across Ambu’s footprint and collaborate across time zones

**Nice to have

**

• MedTech/life sciences background (GxP, ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 11, CSV)

• Exposure to Infor M3 or equivalent ERP, plus PLM, QMS, iPaaS/data platforms, and modern security frameworks

• Experience with Agile-at-scale combined with stage-gate governance

**Key stakeholders for your workstream

**

• Global Process Owner and Global Process Leads

• QA/Validation Lead

• PMO

• External implementation partners and software vendors

**Key Responsibilities Following The Transformation

**

• Participate in approved global projects

• Provide advice for standard systems and best practices of ERP and related systems

• Act as Service Delivery Manager and Subject Matter Expert in ERP in the IT Application Team

• Configure and maintain ERP systems, ensuring alignment with business requirements and best practices.

• Handle system configuration, unit testing, training, and documentation in accordance with standards in close cooperation with external partners.

• Manage Life Cycle Management & release management

• Coach and review work performed by peer professionals

• Work across functions and cultures to deliver high-quality global solutions

• Work independently to solve complex problems

• Train Business Process Owners and other key users

• Follow regulatory compliance

**Ambu – where your technical leadership matters

**Join a fast-growing, international company where your workstream leadership directly enables how we operate globally. We offer strong professional development and a competitive package of professional, social, and financial benefits.

**How To Apply

**Send your CV and a short note describing a program where you led the technical workstream for a specific domain from design through hyper-care, including how you de-risked integrations, data migration, and non-functionals.

We're looking for a marketing intern who wants to manage their own projects and develop creatives that get published.

Great camping experiences start long before guests arrive. At CompuSoft, we build the software that helps campsites turn that first booking into a memorable stay. We’re looking for a marketing intern who wants to take ownership of projects and create content that gets published.

Who We Are

We’re a Danish software company with roots in the camping industry and a story that began in 1987. Today, more than 600 campsites, holiday resorts, attractions, and other tourism businesses use our solutions.

Our technology brings together online booking, guest management, payments, guest apps, and self-service tools. We help businesses simplify daily operations, giving their teams more time to focus on their guests.

With development, sales, and support in-house, we work closely across teams and with our customers to keep improving our solutions.

Your Role:

Your work will cover content, communication, and digital marketing. We’ll shape the internship around your strengths and interests, so tell us what you enjoy working on.

You’ll have your own projects with clear goals and also support the team where needed.

Your tasks may include:

• Writing LinkedIn posts, newsletter articles, and customer stories.

• Creating photos, short videos, and simple graphics.

• Helping plan and run campaigns across our four markets, from trade fairs and webinars to customer events.

• Keeping our messaging clear and consistent across our website, emails, and sales materials.

• Working with our website, email flows, and HubSpot, and tracking results to understand what works.

• Testing new ideas, including ways to use AI tools in our daily marketing work.

...

Who we're looking for

You’re studying marketing, communication, journalism, digital media, or a related subject, and your programme includes an internship.

We hope you:

• Write well in Danish and English. Swedish, Norwegian, or German is a bonus.

• Are curious and enjoy figuring things out independently.

• Have some experience with content, social media, or digital marketing through your studies, work, or personal projects.

• Feel comfortable asking questions and sharing ideas.

You don’t need to know about campsites or software. We’ll teach you that.

What We Offer

You can expect:

• Real responsibility and work you can include in your portfolio.

• A dedicated contact person who makes time for you and provides honest feedback.

• Experience in a growing SaaS company with marketing activities across four markets.

• A place in a team that works closely with sales, product, and customer success.

• A relaxed workplace where we take the work seriously, but not ourselves.

How to Apply

Send a short application and your CV through the application form before December 10. Tell us who you are, what you’d like to work on, and show us one thing you’ve made: a post, an article, a video, or a campaign.

We review applications as they arrive and may fill the position before the deadline.

Do you have experience with Reference Standards and are you passionate about creating a broad collaboration with Contract Manufacturing Organizations and internal stakeholders? Ready for your next career move? If so, now is your chance to join Ascendis Pharma as our new Reference Standard Specialist.

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients' lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs in our Endocrinology Rare Disease portfolios. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

We are seeking a passionate Reference Standard Specialist to join our growing team. As a key member of the Reference Standard team, you will become point of contact in reference standard matters between Ascendis Pharma and Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs) on specified projects. You will work to ensure continuous good relations and alignment with CMOs worldwide and stay updated with insights into their methods and processes together with our QC specialists. It is expected that in the collaboration you will contribute to areas such as analytical testing and test methods as well as regulatory guidelines and requirements on reference standards. This is an exciting opportunity to work in a fast-paced environment, collaborate with cross-functional, global teams working together to achieve extraordinary results.

Your typical workday will consist of discussions and support together with a small team of highly experienced colleagues. You will report directly to Therese Lindin, Associate Director for Reference Standards,who is based in Hellerup, and you will also be working at our headquarters in Hellerup.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Plan, coordinate and document activities regarding establishment, maintenance, re-supply, recalibration and distribution/shipping of reference standards and critical analytical substances

• Establish and maintain overview of reference standards for all purposes and product phases (development and commercial manufacturing) including storage location, stock, stability, expiry etc. for current standards as well as standards needed in the future to ensure availability of required standards

• Establish and maintain internal guidance (SOP or guides) for reference standards

• Make sure relevant updates of external legislation and guidelines for reference standards are implemented in the Ascendis Pharma QMS

• Contribute as an author on regulatory documents, such as IMPD's, IND's, NDA's and BLA's and provide answers to questions from authorities - in writing or face to face during inspections. Further, contribute to assessment of inspection readiness of CMO's

Qualifications and Skills:

You hold a relevant academic degree - preferably a masters in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Chemistry, Engineering, or other relevant education - and a minimum of 5 years of experience from Biotech or Pharmaceutical industry working with reference standards.

Your knowledge and experience within the reference standard area will enable you to guide project teams at CMOs through conceptual as well as specific practical discussions. You have experience with coordination of reference standard activities, and experience with the commercial setup for resupply of reference standards. It will be an advantage if you have experience with analysis of large molecules, and preferably with polymers, proteins and/or peptides as well.

Furthermore, knowledge and practical experience in analytical sciences from the pharmaceutical industry within chromatographic analyses (HPLC) and bioassays, either from an analytical development laboratory or from a QC Laboratory will be an advantage.

Key competencies:

You have a structured and systematic approach to solving tasks and possess outstanding skills in collaboration and communication. As the job involves many stakeholders and coordination of activities both internally and externally, you thrive with being in contact with new people. You are a highly motivated individual who enjoys being challenged and working in collaborative environments. You possess a high energy level and focus on details.

To succeed in this role, we also expect you to have excellent abilities in terms of keeping an overview even with many active tasks at the same time. You are a strong team player, analytical, and have a can-do attitude. Criteria of success in the role will be to ensure efficient coordination of reference standard activities for development projects as well as post-approval resupply activities. FPRT is looking for a Senior Composite Process Technology Manager for our new composite production in Vojens, Denmark, and Moment Professionals manages the recruitment on our behalf. We are looking for a composite specialist with real depth in the technology who can convert transferred know-how into controlled, scalable and repeatable industrial processes. The role suits you if you want to build a production from the ground up and would rather build processes where little is written down yet than step into a production where everything is already in place.

Your everyday at FPRT

You report to the Chief Production Officer, Composite Manufacturing, and you build and lead the composite technology team of composite process engineers and materials and polymer engineers. You work closely with Production, Quality and NDT, HSE, Maintenance and Engineering, Planning and Supply Chain, and you support the competency and qualification standards for supervisors, technicians and operators together with Production and HR. You are the technical authority for composite manufacturing processes, with the mandate to define process parameters, technical standards and work instructions, and to require technical containment, a process review or a production stop when process integrity, product quality or safety is at risk.

Production starts from an existing process that is being transferred to Vojens, and experienced specialists from the group come to the site to hand it over. You lead the technical transfer and convert it into FPRT-controlled specifications, work instructions, training content and qualification requirements, and you define the technical requirements for equipment, tooling, fixtures, utilities and production conditions through trials, pilot builds and ramp-up. You make sure FPRT has clear local ownership of the critical processes and keeps the technical knowledge for the long term. From day one, you are expected to spot where a step can be done smarter and to have the composite understanding to back that view.

Your time is split between the desk and the floor. You own process flows, critical parameters, material requirements and process-control standards, and you define process qualification, inspection points, acceptance criteria and quality gates together with Quality and NDT. When a process starts to drift, you are the primary escalation point: you go to the floor, lead root-cause analysis, non-conformity investigations and corrective actions, and turn the lessons into updated standards and training. The weight of the role lies in the moulding stage and the material side of the process: resin systems, reinforcements such as carbon fibre, adhesives, curing and the conditions that decide whether porosity and voids are designed out or created. You need a sound grasp of finishing, but your depth is in why a part comes out of the mould as it does.

This is a greenfield site. New buildings are under construction on the site, systems are being selected, and support functions such as maintenance, IT and HR are being built in parallel. In the first period you will help shape how things are done well beyond your own field, and the composite team grows as production scales towards stable serial production.

The role is based in Vojens, and being on site is essential during the build-up. English is the working language in instructions and with colleagues across the group. Danish is a strong advantage in daily life on the floor, and if you are not fluent yet, your willingness to learn it counts.

And then there are the benefits:

Real authority over the processes you own, greenfield impact with no legacy to work around, a professional, international environment with a clear mission and purpose, a modern office with gym, sauna and social spaces, and top-of-market compensation for the right experience.

To succeed in the role…

…you do not need to have carried a manager title or to come from defence. What matters is that you know composite technology in depth: why a resin system behaves as it does, what creates strength and what creates defects, and how the environment affects the part. You may come from composite manufacturing in wind energy, marine, aerospace, defence or another high-performance industry, and work today in process or manufacturing engineering, production, materials or as a technical composite specialist. You also take pride in:

• challenging an established method, including one handed over by experienced colleagues, and agreeing on a better answer together.

• taking ownership and making decisions where little is written down yet.

• going to the floor when a process drifts and staying until the root cause is found.

• turning know-how into standards, instructions and training that engineers and operators can work from.

• developing engineers through technical reviews, coaching and structured problem solving.

What you need to bring:

• Either a relevant technical degree or equivalent strong industrial experience, and at least five years in composite manufacturing, process engineering, manufacturing engineering or materials engineering.

• Practical experience with industrial manufacturing of fibre-reinforced composite components and thermoset resin systems such as epoxy, phenolic or other thermosets, and hands-on experience with one or more of resin infusion or transfer processes, filament winding, lay-up, moulding, curing, bonding or composite machining and finishing.

• A proven track record of developing, transferring, industrialising, qualifying or stabilising manufacturing processes into repeatable production, with a solid grip on process control, documentation, process risk assessment, root-cause analysis, non-conformity handling and technical change management.

• Experience leading, mentoring or coaching engineers and production specialists, or acting as their technical authority.

• Fluent English, written and spoken. Danish is a strong advantage, or the willingness to learn it.

It is an advantage if you:

• come from advanced composite manufacturing in wind energy, marine, aerospace, defence, pressure vessels, automotive or another high-performance application.

• have worked with large or structurally critical components, such as aerospace and defence structures, casings, filament-wound products, UAV components or wind turbine blades.

• have taken part in a greenfield factory, a new production line, a technology transfer or a major ramp-up.

• live within commuting distance of 6500 Vojens, Denmark.

About the Role:

QuNorth is looking for a Quantum Error Correction (QEC) Lead to help develop and lead our collaborative Quantum Error Correction program, in addition to participating in other aspects of operationalizing Magne, QuNorth’s Neutral Atom quantum computer, in a fast-paced but stable startup environment.

QuNorth is a new Nordic Hub for quantum exploration, providing the region’s enterprises, researchers, and startups with the capability to test, learn, and build on Magne, a world-leading Level 2 quantum computer. With strong backing from EIFO and the Novo Nordisk Foundation, QuNorth will operate Magne as a shared platform for Nordic industries, research organisations, and start-ups. Our aim is to provide the access, tools, expertise, and support needed to explore new quantum applications across all relevant areas, including, but not limited to, life sciences, innovative materials, biochemistry, and AI.

Magne’s physical layer, developed by Atom Computing, includes 1200+ Ytterbium-171 atoms, serving as physical qubits with all-to-all connectivity. It can be operated seamlessly in logical mode enabled by Microsoft, providing tens of logical qubits depending on QEC code. Magne can also be operated in physical mode with mid-circuit measurement and feedforward, which in conjunction with its all-to-all connectivity at scale turns Magne into an excellent platform for exploration of novel QEC techniques, unconstrained by “chip topology”. We envision QEC projects and broader QEC-related partnerships to be a strong component of QuNorth’s portfolio. Working directly with the CTO, and interfacing with the CPO team and QuNorth’s users and partners, the QEC Lead will help shape this key component of the QuNorth portfolio. This role will, at least initially, be mostly a technical leadership role, rather than a managerial position.

We are a small and committed team working to build QuNorth from the ground up as a reliable and transparent organization that contributes to the long-term strength of the Nordic quantum computing ecosystem.

Your Responsibilities:

The successful candidate will eagerly engage in many of the following directions:

• Lead QuNorth’s technical work on quantum error correction, including strategy, architecture assessment, simulation, benchmarking, resource estimation, and roadmap development.

• Evaluate and compare QEC codes, decoding approaches, logical gate schemes, error models, and fault-tolerant architectures.

• Work with hardware, software, and theory collaborators to connect QEC requirements and assumptions to realistic device constraints.

• Help identify which QEC approaches are most relevant to QuNorth’s mission and which are not.

• Work closely with QuNorth’s CTO and Quantum Applications and Algorithms Lead to explore the interplay between applications, algorithms, QCVV, compilation, QEC, noise, error mitigation, and logical-mode operation, including opportunities for integration and co-design.

• Represent QuNorth in collaborations, including with universities, research institutes, startups, and enterprises.

• Contribute to proposals, grant applications, reports, publications, presentations, and internal documents.

• Help recruit, mentor, and coordinate future team members working on QEC, quantum architecture, simulation, and related topics.

• Participate in broader company-building work, including technical due diligence, collaborator or partner discussions, product strategy, documentation, and operational tasks.

• Use AI tools effectively and responsibly to accelerate research, coding, literature review, writing, planning, analysis, operations, and internal workflows.

• Help establish a high standard for scientific rigor, clear communication, and effective execution within the company.

Your Experience and Qualifications:

We expect strong candidates to have many of the following:

• A PhD or equivalent experience required in quantum information, quantum computing, physics, computer science, mathematics, electrical engineering, or a related field.

• 3+ years of experience in QEC beyond PhD.

• Deep understanding of quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

• Deep familiarity with topics such as surface codes, qLDPC codes, color codes, bosonic codes, subsystem codes, concatenated codes, holographic codes, and other conventional or emerging QEC approaches.

• ‘Hands-on’ experience with decoding algorithms, error models, threshold analysis, logical error rates, resource estimation, and architecture-level tradeoffs.

• Deep familiarity with QCVV techniques, including benchmarking approaches.

• Deep familiarity with protocols for mitigation and characterization of noise and error, and their relationship with QEC and relevant thresholds.

• Strong programming experience, preferably in Python or similar scientific computing environments, with experience developing simulations, analysis workflows, notebooks, benchmarking tools, or research software.

• Experience collaborating across disciplines with comfort, especially between theory, software, and experimental teams.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Comfort working in an early-stage environment where priorities evolve and everyone contributes beyond their formal job title.

• Practical experience using AI tools such as LLMs, coding assistants, literature tools, agentic workflows, and AI-enabled analysis environments.

• Good judgment about when AI tools are useful, when they are unreliable, and how to verify their outputs.

The Team:

The position is based in our new offices at Rønnegade 6 in Copenhagen, where Magne is also currently being built. You will be part of the Technology team under the CTO, and will interact closely with the Product team under the CPO and the rest of QuNorth as well.

Like many start-ups, we are building QuNorth as we go. You will join a very entrepreneurial team, driven by curiosity about the technology, with a desire to make an impact while working in a fun and engaging workplace. As an early employee, you will be an important contributor to building this environment along with us.

What We Offer:

A unique opportunity to be part of standing up and operating a quantum computing company with strong backers, in modern offices located centrally in the Innovation District Copenhagen with convenient public transport and lunch service.

Comprehensive remuneration package, including benefits that support an environment where people can grow and do their best work.

This position will be based in Copenhagen, which offers a rare combination of international outlook, strong quantum and deep-tech ecosystem, and excellent quality of life, consistently ranked amongst the most liveable cities in the world.

Application and Contact:

If you wish to know more about the position, please reach out to Dr. Kasra Nowrouzi, CTO at QuNorth, at kasra@qunorth.com

Please be aware that we will be reviewing applications on an ongoing basis.

All applications will be treated in the strictest confidence.

We look very much forward to receiving your application.

Job Description:

Drivetrain Engineer – Wind Power

Goldwind Denmark is looking for a Drivetrain Engineer to contribute to the development of wind turbine drivetrain systems. You will join an international engineering environment where colleagues in Denmark and China work together to develop mechanical concepts, evaluate design solutions and support their implementation.

This opportunity suits you if you enjoy combining component design with an understanding of the complete drivetrain. In a growing company with ambitious technology goals, you can influence new concepts and help turn them into practical solutions while broadening your expertise.

The role

You will develop and evaluate drivetrain concepts, balancing reliability, weight, cost and serviceability. Working with engineering specialists and suppliers, you will translate system requirements and turbine loads into mechanical solutions.

Your responsibilities include:

• Developing concepts for main shafts, bearing arrangements, housings, supporting structures and interfaces with gearboxes and generators.

• Developing mechanical designs supported by calculations, CAD models and technical specifications.

• Assessing load paths, stiffness, alignment, tolerances and component interactions alongside FEA specialists.

• Comparing solutions to improve performance, manufacturability, assembly and maintenance.

• Supporting colleagues in China during detailed design and participating in design reviews.

• Assessing suppliers’ component capabilities, resolving technical questions and supporting design verification and testing.

• Documenting recommendations, assumptions and design risks.

Your profile

You take a systematic, practical approach to engineering, develop concepts independently and challenge assumptions constructively. You involve specialists when needed, take responsibility for your work and communicate your findings clearly.

We expect you to have:

• A degree in mechanical engineering or a related discipline.

• At least five years of relevant experience in mechanical design and development.

• Practical knowledge of one or more drivetrain components, such as shafts, bearings, housings, couplings or gearbox support arrangements.

• A solid grounding in strength, fatigue, stiffness, materials and tolerances.

• Experience with 3D CAD, engineering drawings and mechanical calculations, together with the ability to interpret simulation results and use them to guide design decisions.

• Good written and spoken English and the ability to communicate effectively across teams and cultures.

Experience with wind turbine drivetrains or comparable large rotating machinery is preferred. Experience with rolling or plain bearings, large cast or forged components, drivetrain dynamics, prototype testing or wind turbine certification is an advantage. We also welcome specialists who want to broaden their understanding of the complete drivetrain.

What can you look forward to?

You will have the opportunity to influence drivetrain concepts and help develop them into practical engineering solutions. Your work will span concept development, component design, design reviews and validation, allowing you to see how technical decisions translate into working designs.

Through close collaboration with an international engineering team and specialist suppliers, you will exchange knowledge, explore different approaches and develop both your specialist expertise and your understanding of the complete drivetrain.

About Goldwind

Goldwind Energy ApS (also called Goldwind Denmark) is a R&D focused subsidiary of GOLDWIND SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD. (Goldwind), a world leading wind turbine technology and energy solutions provider headquartered in Beijing, China.

Through the implementation and investment in industry-leading turbine technology, water treatment solutions and other green energy technological ventures, Goldwind has been hailed as one of China’s most innovative companies.

Do you want to help build one coherent way for a global technology organization to deliver, bringing scaled product-centric ways of working project and program execution _together into a single system, rather than running them as separate worlds? Are you as comfortable helping shape that system and turning it into ways of working people actually use in the room with the people who'll actually use it?_We are hiring a Manager, Delivery Enablement to help shape and evolve how Pandora's D&T organization delivers. D&T spans the full range of technology that keeps Pandora running: from customer-facing platforms to manufacturing systems, ERP, logistics and operations, security, covering build, run, and operate across all of it. This role does not carry people-management responsibility. Your impact comes through the quality of what you build and how well it lands across the organization.

You'll join Delivery Enablement, a team combining operating-model design and implementation, coaching, and delivery tooling capability. It's built to make Digital & Technology (D&T) faster, clearer, and more coherent at scale. Delivery Enablement sits within Delivery Excellence, alongside the Scrum Masters, Delivery Leads, and Project and Program Managers. You will work with the wider team to shape ideas and turn them into practical ways of working across D&T.

**Your Role

**You will help harmonize and evolve how scaled agile delivery and more structured, plan-driven delivery work together, building on what already exists across D&T rather than replacing it, closing gaps only where they cause real friction. You will also advise on structuring new or reshaping delivery entities (product lines, programs, organizational changes, or other setups) as they take shape, and help teams and entities build the capability to adopt the model as it evolves.

**

• Lead workstreams that take new or improved delivery processes (for example dependency management or capacity planning) from idea through pilot, rollout, adoption and continuous improvement

• Build relationships, networks and communities that help change spread and stick across D&T

• Help translate high-level decisions about how delivery is prioritized, funded, resourced, and executed into practical structures and standards teams can use

• Help projects and programs connect into the wider D&T Operating Model, including common governance, planning, dependency management and delivery tooling

• Contribute to keeping the model coherent as it evolves, spotting where new structures overlap or conflict with what already exists

• Provide point-in-time advisory support where operating-model gaps are most costly

• Document how the operating model works and how it evolves over time

• Build strong relationships across the wider delivery community and leadership to ensure what gets built is genuinely adopted

**What Is Needed To Succeed

**

• Demonstrated experience working across both scaled/product-centric agile delivery and more structured, plan-driven delivery, with enough understanding to contribute credibly to how they work together

• Comfortable leading through organizational change: helping people, not just structures, adapt as delivery models shift

• Able to build trust, networks and momentum without relying on formal authority

jobs.occupation: Test Method Specialist, Quality Assurance Lifecycle Laboratory
jobs.description:
**_Imagine if robust test methods and reliable test equipment helped ensure the quality of both new and existing Coloplast products. That is where you come in.

**_As our new Test Method Specialist, you will become the technical focal point for selected test methods and related equipment in Coloplast Mørdrup, primarily supporting the QA Lifecycle Laboratory and Pilot SVS. This is a practical, hands-on specialist role in which you will work directly with laboratory equipment, including troubleshooting, service and calibration follow-up, qualification, and software and computer upgrades. You will support the full test method and equipment lifecycle, from implementation and qualification to maintenance, transfer and continuous improvement.

If you are motivated by hands-on technical problem-solving, equipment responsibility, quality assurance and data evaluation, this role offers meaningful responsibility and broad organisational impact. You will also work closely with many internal and external stakeholders, making clear communication, coordination and strong stakeholder management an important part of your success.

_“In this role, your technical judgement and ability to create robust solutions will help ensure reliable test results and compliant laboratory processes throughout the product lifecycle,” says Lotte Stoklund, Team Manager, QA Lifecycle Laboratory.

_**Join a skilled and collaborative laboratory team

**At our Coloplast Mørdrup site, you will join the Quality Assurance Lifecycle Laboratory. The team consists of laboratory technicians and test method specialists who work closely together to support ongoing production, process development, quality investigations and test method activities.

You will be part of an engaged team with a strong mix of practical laboratory experience and specialist knowledge. In our daily work, we collaborate closely with colleagues across Quality Assurance, Research and Development, Operations, Global Test Method teams and international manufacturing sites. We value curiosity, knowledge sharing, flexibility and a continuous improvement mindset.

**Own and develop test methods and equipment

**As Test Method Specialist, you will act as a one-point contact and technical superuser for selected test methods and test equipment. A significant part of the role is practical equipment responsibility. You will work hands-on with equipment and coordinate activities to ensure it is qualified, calibrated, serviced, maintained and performing as intended. You will also support software and computer upgrades connected to the equipment, as well as reliable data handling and traceability.

Your primary responsibilities will include:

• Acting as technical owner and one-point contact for selected test methods and related test equipment

• Planning, coordinating and performing qualification of test equipment, including relocation, capacity expansion and replacement of critical parts

• Preparing and maintaining qualification protocols, reports, procedures, test method documentation and one-point lessons when needed

• Performing hands-on troubleshooting of test equipment and methods, evaluating test results and leading root cause investigations when failures occur

• Taking practical responsibility for test equipment, including service activities, calibration follow-up, preventive maintenance and ensuring that equipment performs as intended

• Handling changes, nonconformities and CAPAs related to test methods, calibration and test equipment

• Supporting compliant storage and traceability of raw data before product release

• Planning and participating in transfers of test methods and equipment to international manufacturing sites

• Providing technical support and sparring to colleagues in the Pilot Plant, Global Operations and international manufacturing sites

• Collaborating with Global Test Method teams and contributing technical input to the development and improvement of test methods

• Training specialists, laboratory technicians, operators and other users in test methods, test principles and use of equipment

• Coordinating software and computer upgrades for test equipment, assessing their impact on qualification and documentation, and managing suppliers, service visits and relevant service agreements

• Participating in internal and external audits related to test methods, equipment and documentation

• Contributing to continuous improvement of laboratory processes, systems and ways of working

**Bring strong technical judgement and a quality mindset

**To succeed in this position, you combine technical depth with a structured, practical and hands-on approach. You enjoy working directly with equipment, take ownership and work systematically when resolving technical issues. You are comfortable making decisions based on data, risk and regulatory requirements.

The role involves close collaboration with many internal and external stakeholders, therefor you communicate clearly, coordinate effectively and are able to build strong working relationships across functions, sites and suppliers.

We imagine that you bring:

• A master’s degree within science, engineering, mechanics, physics, chemistry, pharmacy or a comparable technical field, or have at least five years of relevant experience with test methods

• Solid hands-on experience with test methods, measurement principles and qualification of laboratory or production test equipment

• Strong problem-solving skills and experience with structured root cause analysis

• Confident evaluating, analysing and presenting technical data skills, including the use of statistical methods

• Ability to write, review and understand technical documentation, protocols and reports

• Knowledge of quality systems and regulated environments; knowledge of ISO 9001, ISO 13485 and GMP is an advantage

• An understanding of validation, calibration, design control, specifications and process risk management

• Abitlity to plan and prioritise your work effectively and follow activities through to completion

• Strong stakeholder management skills and collaborate effectively across disciplines, functions, geographical locations and external suppliers

• Communicating skills professionally in English, both written and spoken; Danish is an advantage

jobs.occupation: Associate Director, Trial Delivery Team Lead
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**Overview

**The Associate Director, Trial Delivery Team Lead plays a key leadership role in overseeing Clinical Trial Managers (CTMs) and Clinical Trial Associates (CTAs) while supporting the broader Clinical Trial Management (CTM) organization. This individual ensures high-quality clinical trial execution by providing strategic guidance, mentorship, and operational oversight. The Line Manager is responsible for team development, resource allocation, process optimization, and ensuring alignment with organizational goals and regulatory standards. The Trial Delivery Team Lead may assume Global Trial Lead (GTL) responsibilities to address fluctuating demands.

**Roles & Responsibilities

****Leadership and Line Management:

**

• Directly manage, mentor, and develop Clinical Trial Managers (CTMs) and Clinical Trial Associates (CTAs), fostering professional growth.

• Conduct performance evaluations, provide feedback, and identify training and career development opportunities.

• Ensure adequate resourcing, workload distribution, and succession planning within the team.

• Facilitate cross-functional collaboration and knowledge-sharing within the clinical operations team.

• Collaborate with Global Trial Leads (GTLs) on trial activities for assigned direct reports.

• Support trial deliverables by facilitating progress, coaching, and mentoring CTMs and CTAs.

• Advise on resource needs and support overall clinical trial resource planning.

• Ensure team success through setting clear expectations, guiding performance, and leading competency development.

• Lead functional working groups; serve as process owner or Subject Matter Expert (SME) within Clinical Operations.

• Support training initiatives across Trial Operations as needed.

• Collaborate with senior leadership to define and implement best practices within the Development Operations organization.

**Process & Compliance Management

**

• Ensure team adherence to Good Clinical Practice (GCP), ICH guidelines, and regulatory requirements (FDA, EMA, etc.).

• Develop and refine Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to optimize trial efficiency and compliance.

• Support audits, inspections, and regulatory interactions by ensuring inspection readiness across clinical trials.

• Identify and drive process improvements to enhance trial execution and data quality.

• Lead cross-trial initiatives as needed, such as implementation of Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPAs) or new process rollouts across the program.

• Manages the execution and implementation of CTM and CTA tasks, ensuring operational success.

• Initiates and supports the development of processes within the CTM and CTA group, focusing on practical application and continuous improvement.

• Collaborates across functions to drive efficiencies and provide day-to-day guidance to the CTM and CTA groups.

**Requirements – What You Must Have

**

• Bachelor of science degree with relevant specialization; Master of science degree preferred

• Minimum requirement of 12 or more years of experience in clinical operations

• Significant experience in leading and managing complex global clinical projects/programs

• Significant experience managing/guiding internal (cross-functional) and external (CRO, regulatory authorities) teams

• Experience with operational management and budget planning

• Proven performance in earlier role/comparable role

• Global clinical program level experience required

• Experience within the field of oncology is preferred

• Minimum 2 years’ experience as Clinical Operations representative in Clinical Development Teams (CDTs) or Global Project Teams (GPTs) would be preferable

• Experience leading team members in global matrix environment, leveraging tools and technology to ensure business needs are met.

• Strategic thinking with ability to optimize organizational resources for successful program execution

• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken

**Moreover, You Meet The Following Personal Requirements

**

• Dedicated team player who enjoys leading teams and inspire trust among colleagues

• Quality mindset and able to prioritize your work in a fast paced and changing environment

• Result- and goal-oriented and committed to contributing to the overall success of Genmab

For US based candidates, the proposed salary band for this position is as follows:

$158,720.00---$238,080.00

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Also, certain positions are eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

When You Join Genmab, You’re Joining a Culture That Supports Your Physical, Financial, Social, And Emotional Wellness. Within The First Year, Regular Full-time U.S. Employees Are Eligible For

• 401(k) Plan: 100% match on the first 6% of contributions

• Health Benefits: Two medical plan options (including HDHP with HSA), dental, and vision insurance

• Voluntary Plans: Critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity insurance

• Time Off: Paid vacation, sick leave, holidays, and 12 weeks of discretionary paid parental leave

• Support Resources: Access to child and adult backup care, family support programs, financial wellness tools, and emotional well-being support

• Additional Perks: Commuter benefits, tuition reimbursement, and a Lifestyle Spending Account for wellness and personal expenses

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on role will be provided during the recruitment process

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Please note that if you are applying for a position in the Netherlands, Genmab’s policy for all permanently budgeted hires in NL is initially to offer a fixed-term employment contract for a year, if the employee performs well and if the business conditions do not change, renewal for an indefinite term may be considered after the fixed-term employment contract.

Spare Parts Coordinator

Are you passionate about customer service, coordination, and delivering results in an international environment? We are looking for a structured and service-minded Spare Parts Coordinator to join our Customer Service team. In this role, you will play a key part in ensuring the efficient handling of spare parts inquiries, quotations, and sales orders, contributing to an excellent customer experience through professional support, proactive communication, and reliable order execution.

As a Spare Parts Coordinator, you will be responsible for managing the spare parts process from initial customer inquiry through to final delivery. You will handle spare parts requests, prepare quotations, process sales orders, and proactively follow up with customers regarding availability, lead times, and order status. Working closely with procurement, planning, logistics, warehouse operations, and other internal stakeholders, you will help ensure smooth and timely order fulfillment while maintaining a high level of customer satisfaction.

As a person, you are service-oriented, structured, and proactive, with a strong sense of ownership and attention to detail. You enjoy working collaboratively across departments, are solution-oriented in your approach, and take pride in delivering excellent service to both customers and colleagues.

We offer an exciting and varied position in a growing international company where you will become part of a dedicated and professional team. You will have the opportunity to work closely with customers and colleagues across the organization while contributing to continuous improvements, operational excellence, and the company's ongoing growth and success.

Why Should You Join Körber Supply Chain DK?

We offer an exciting role in an international company in growth, where you will work with advanced technical solutions and be part of a strong professional environment characterized by collaboration and dedication. We offer a range of attractive employee benefits:

You will also be part of our lunch program, where our canteen provides healthy and exciting meals every day.

Social Events: We have a strong company culture that we invest heavily in maintaining and developing. This includes a wide range of events and an active employee association that organizes activities such as Friday bars, Christmas parties, an annual ski trip, cultural events, and much more!

Körber – Conquer Supply Chain Complexity
