We are therefore looking for someone who is comfortable not only producing high quality financial analysis, but also explaining, challenging and discussing it confidently with the business.

**Your Responsibilities Will Include

**

• Leading budgeting, forecasting, reporting and financial controlling activities for your primary business area

• Partnering closely with operational stakeholders to understand cost drivers, business requirements and future financial needs

• Supporting both OPEX and CAPEX planning, including the investment outlook for infrastructure in Kalundborg

• Preparing and presenting budgets and financial material to senior stakeholders and supporting Board-level financial discussions

• Identifying opportunities to strengthen, simplify and improve existing finance processes

• Contributing to broader API Business & Investment Finance deliverables, including budgeting, consolidated financial material and other cross-team priorities

The role requires a regular presence in Kalundborg, typically 2–3 days per week, with the remaining working days primarily based in Taastrup. Flexibility will be required depending on business and stakeholder needs.

**Your new department

**You will join API Business & Investment Finance, a team covering financial planning, budgeting and finance partnering for investment projects and operating factories across API.

We drive business insights and support senior management in financial processes and strategic resource allocation. API is the area in Novo producing the Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients for our patients worldwide.

In the team, we enjoy maintaining a humorous and ambitious environment, to which we all contribute. We are good at helping each other with complicated challenges and celebrating each other's victories. We look forward to welcoming you to the team and sharing our knowledge and experience.

**Your Skills And Qualifications

**To succeed in this role, you have a relevant academic background within Finance, Accounting, Economics or a related field, combined with practical finance experience.

More importantly, you have hands on experience with budgeting and are comfortable taking independent ownership of a financial process rather than simply contributing to one.

**Additionally, We Are Looking For Someone Who

**

• Has practical experience with budgeting, forecasting, financial planning or controlling, ideally within a line-of-business, operational or business-partnering environment

• Is comfortable preparing and presenting financial information to senior stakeholders

• Can explain complex financial information clearly and confidently and constructively challenge when required

• Brings a collaborative mindset and is comfortable contributing beyond their immediate area of responsibility

For candidates considered at Senior Finance Partner level, we will particularly look for evidence of independently managing complex finance partnering responsibilities, confidently influencing senior stakeholders and bringing a broader strategic perspective to financial decision making.

**Why Novo

**At Novo, we don’t wait for change. We drive it. We’re a dynamic company in an even more dynamic industry, and we know that what got us to where we are today is not necessarily what will make us successful in the future.

We embrace the spirit of experimentation, striving for excellence without fixating on perfection. We never shy away from opportunities to develop; we seize them. From research and development, through to manufacturing, marketing and sales we’re all working to move the needle on patient care.

**Working at Novo

**Novo is its people. We know that life is anything but linear and balancing what is important at different stages of our career is never easy. That’s why we make room for diverse life situations, always putting people first.

We value our employees for the unique skills they bring to the table, and we work continuously to bring out the best in them. Working at Novo is working toward something bigger than ourselves, and it’s a collective effort.

Novo relies on the joint potential and collaboration of its more than 63,000 employees. Together, we go further. Together, we’re life changing.

**Salary And Benefits

**The salary range for this role is 651,000 to 956,900.

On top of your base salary, you will receive a market leading benefits package.

**Incentives And Benefits

**You will also have access to a range of employee benefits and development opportunities designed to support your professional and personal wellbeing.

**More information

**For further information about the position, please contact Andreas Kjøller at AQKJ@novonordisk.com

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

At Novo we recognize that it is no longer good enough to aspire to be the best company in the world. We need to aspire to be the best company for the world and we know that this is only possible with talented employees with diverse perspectives, backgrounds and cultures. We are therefore committed to creating an inclusive culture that celebrates the diversity of our employees, the patients we serve and communities we operate in. Together, we’re life changing.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

jobs.occupation: Director, Governance, Languages, Communications and External Relations
jobs.description:
OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAMME

The European Region (EURO) of WHO is made of 53 countries, with over 880 million people. The diversity of people and health situations requires a solid understanding of the emerging socio-economic, epidemiologic, and demographic patterns and trends at regional, national and sub-national levels, with due sensitivity to disadvantaged populations and vulnerable segments of the society. It is equally crucial to have a solid understanding of the commonalities and divergences of the health systems, the circumstances and political economy under which they have evolved and operate. The Division of Programme Management ensures the technical excellence of WHO/Europe's work. It coordinates and ensures coherence across WHO/Europe's health programmes, country support and the Special Initiative on Primary Health Care (PHC).The division also leads planning and budgeting, resource mobilization and partnerships, communications and publications, governance and external relations and language services.

**Description Of Duties

**Under the direct supervision of the Director Programme Management and in close collaboration with the Director Business Operations and the Technical Directors, the incumbent:

• 
Leads the Regional Office's work in the areas of external relations, communications and publications, language services, and governing bodies.

• 
Provides high level strategic support through provision of policy, managerial and diplomatic advice to senior management.

• 
Promotes a culture of high performance, team work, ethical behaviour and integrity in accordance with the Organization's policies, rules and procedures.

• 
Provides support to the DPM in monitoring the implementation of the Global Policy Group of WHO (GPG) decisions and the strategic directions of WHO's work in the Region;

• 
Builds partnerships and contributes to effective and efficient three level coordination in the areas of responsibility, ensuring that countries benefit from the best possible support and advice from WHO headquarters, Regional Office and country office resources.

• 
Oversees and ensures rapid and clear information flows with other regions and WHO headquarters in areas of responsibility.

• 
Contributes to WHO regional coordination and serves as a member of EURO's Executive Council.

• 
Coordinates the work of the technical secretariat for WHO governing body meetings (World Health Assembly, WHO Executive Board, Regional Committee and the Standing Committee of the Regional Committee) and other senior management and advisory meetings.

• 
Interacts with technical directors to ensure implementation of policy decisions of WHO governing bodies

• 
Performs any other duties assigned by the 1st and/or 2nd level supervisor.

**Required Qualifications

**Education

Essential: Advanced university degree in public health, international relations, communications, social sciences or business management.

Desirable: Training in public health related issues.

**Experience

**Essential: At least 15 years of national and international experience with some years at the international level in a senior management position including experience in developing countries. Extensive writing and communications experience. Experience in multipartner health programme management and leadership. Experience guiding and interpreting WHO rules and procedures, including close familiarity with the work of the Regional Office and WHO governing bodies.

Desirable: Experience in the political and/or diplomatic arena.

**Skills

**

• 
Ability to exercise leadership and to work effectively with colleagues at national and international levels;

• 
Diplomatic skills;

• 
Ability to negotiate and engage in new partnerships;

• 
Ability to coordinate teams with different backgrounds in a multicultural environment;

• 
Excellent writing skills in English in a variety of styles and under tight deadline pressure;

• 
Ability to develop messaging and positioning for an international organization;

• 
Demonstrated networking skills, excellent interpersonal skills;

• 
Thorough understanding of public health and international development issues, with the ability to quickly understand, process and communicate new information;

• 
Proven ability to plan, execute, collaborate and work independently with donors, partners, etc.

**WHO Competencies

**

• 
Teamwork*

• 
Respecting and promoting individual and cultural differences*

• 
Communication*

• 
Producing results

• 
Moving forward in a changing environment

• 
Creating an empowering and motivating environment*

Use of Language Skills

Essential: Expert knowledge of English.

Desirable: Intermediate knowledge of French, German and/or Russian.

REMUNERATION

WHO salaries for staff in the Professional category are calculated in US dollars. The remuneration for the above position comprises an annual base salary starting at USD 117,953 (subject to mandatory deductions for pension contributions and health insurance, as applicable), a variable post adjustment, which reflects the cost of living in a particular duty station, and currently amounts to USD 6871 per month for the duty station indicated above. Other benefits include 30 days of annual leave, allowances for dependent family members, home leave, and an education grant for dependent children.

**Additional Information

**

• 
Staff members separated due to the 2025 Prioritization and Realignment Process will receive special consideration according to the applicable regulatory framework.

• 
This vacancy notice may be used to fill other similar positions at the same grade level.

• 
Only candidates under serious consideration will be contacted.

• 
A written test and/or an asynchronous video assessment may be used as a form of screening.

• 
In the event that your candidature is retained for an interview, you will be required to provide, in advance, a scanned copy of the degree(s)/diploma(s)/certificate(s) required for this position. WHO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU)/United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). The list can be accessed through the link: http://www.whed.net/. Some professional certificates may not appear in the WHED and will require individual review.

• 
According to article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. Due regard will be paid to the importance of recruiting the staff on as wide a geographical basis as possible.

• 
Any appointment/extension of appointment is subject to WHO Staff Regulations, Staff Rules and eManual.

• 
The Director-General retains the discretion to not make any appointment to this vacancy, to make an appointment at a lower grade, or to make an appointment with a modified job description, including shortening the duration of the appointment.

• 
Staff members in other duty stations are encouraged to apply.

• 
WHO is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. WHO recruits and employs staff regardless of disability status, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, language, race, marital status, religious, cultural, ethnic and socio-economic backgrounds, or any other personal characteristics.

• 
WHO is committed to achieving gender parity and geographical diversity in its staff. Women, persons with disabilities, and nationals of unrepresented and underrepresented Member States (https://www.who.int/careers/diversity-equity-and-inclusion) are strongly encouraged to apply.

• 
Persons with disabilities may request reasonable accommodations (modifications or adjustments to the application or recruitment process) to support their participation in the application and recruitment process. Please send an email to reasonableaccommodation@who.int with your full name, the vacancy number you are applying for, and specific details of the accommodation needed in your request.

• 
An impeccable record for integrity and professional ethical standards is essential. WHO prides itself on a workforce that adheres to the highest ethical and professional standards and that is committed to put the WHO Values Charter into practice.

• 
WHO has zero tolerance towards sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA), sexual harassment and other types of abusive conduct (i.e., discrimination, abuse of authority and harassment). All members of the WHO workforce have a role to play in promoting a safe and respectful workplace and should report to WHO any actual or suspected cases of SEA, sexual harassment and other types of abusive conduct. To ensure that individuals with a substantiated history of SEA, sexual harassment or other types of abusive conduct are not hired by the Organization, WHO will conduct a background verification of final candidates.

• 
Mobility is a condition of international professional employment with WHO and an underlying premise of the international civil service. Candidates appointed to a fixed-term position in the International Professional category (Grades P1-D2) are eligible for Geographical Mobility and may be assigned to any activity or duty station of the Organization throughout the world.

• 
WHO also offers wide range of benefits to staff, including parental leave and attractive flexible work arrangements to help promote a healthy work-life balance and to allow all staff members to express and develop their talents fully.

• 
The statutory retirement age for staff appointments is 65 years. For external applicants, only those who are expected to complete the term of appointment will normally be considered.

• 
Please note that WHO's contracts are conditional on members of the workforce confirming that they are vaccinated as required by WHO before undertaking a WHO assignment, except where a medical condition does not allow such vaccination, as certified by the WHO Staff Health and Wellbeing Services (SHW). The successful candidate will be asked to provide relevant evidence related to this condition. A copy of the updated vaccination card must be shared with WHO medical service in the medical clearance process. Please note that certain countries require proof of specific vaccinations for entry or exit. For example, official proof /certification of yellow fever vaccination is required to enter many countries. Country-specific vaccine recommendations can be found on the WHO international travel and Staff Health and Wellbeing website. For vaccination-related queries please directly contact SHW directly at shws@who.int.

• 
WHO has a smoke-free environment and does not recruit smokers or users of any form of tobacco.

• 
For information on WHO's operations please visit: http://www.who.int.

•

**Software Architect:

Agentic AI & Java, SitaWare Insight

**_Are you passionate about building sophisticated AI agents that solve real world problems? Join our Agentic AI team within SitaWare Insight, designing multi-agent workflows in Java and Python that power critical decision-making and help our customers get the job done faster and safer.

_**The job

**As Software Architect on this team, you will combine deep software architecture expertise in Java with strong LLM and AI engineering fundamentals to shape the technical foundation of our AI-driven solutions. You will define the technical vision and architectural strategy that enable our product, AI agents and multi-agent systems to scale, while also designing and implementing the software solutions that bring this vision to life.

In short, you can look forward to:

• Converting customer needs into robust software architectures for AI agents, multi-agent orchestration and RAG pipelines

• Designing and implementing AI agents, including tool definitions, action groups and knowledge base integrations

• Ensuring safe and predictable outcomes through human-in-the-loop design and guardrails, and building traceability and transparency into our AI-based solutions

• Writing production-grade Java code with full test coverage, structured logging and robust error handling

• Establishing and maintaining technology standards, and evaluating new technologies as they emerge

**Joining the team

**You will join a growing team within the SitaWare Insight program, close to 50 engineers, architects and testers across five Scrum teams, spanning Aarhus and Copenhagen. We are building a brand-new team around this role:

an architect, a data scientist, five to seven developers and a tester, working closely with our Product Manager and UX designer. Java is our primary backend language, and we also work in Python for our AI tooling, and we collaborate with researchers to give our LLMs geospatial situational awareness, the ability to understand tactical maps and follow events across an evolving timeline. If you enjoy figuring out how to make new AI capabilities work safely and reliably in a domain where the stakes are real, you will feel at home here.

**Your Qualifications

**

• 8+ years of software engineering experience, including significant experience in a software architecture role, designing and specifying system structures, interfaces and dependencies

• Strong backend development experience in Java, and familiarity with frontend architectures such as Angular or similar

• Strong understanding of microservices architecture, message queues and system integration patterns

• Experience with Docker and Kubernetes, and a solid grasp of how these fit into system architecture and deployment strategy

• A proven track record of defining technical vision and architectural strategy that supports product scalability and evolution

• Solid software engineering practices, including testing, logging, observability and version control, along with the ability to establish technology standards across a team

For more senior profiles, we are also looking for:

• At least two to three years focused on LLM or AI systems, including architecting and overseeing the deployment of AI-powered applications in Java and Python

• Deep understanding of orchestration frameworks, RAG architectures, vector databases, embedding models, hybrid search and tool-use/function-calling patterns

• Experience designing multi-agent systems, including orchestration patterns such as routing, delegation, parallelisation and result aggregation

• Familiarity with LLM evaluation frameworks and metrics, such as relevance, faithfulness and hallucination detection, and how to build evaluation and observability into system architecture

You should expect around two to four weeks of travel per year, giving you the chance to collaborate across our Aarhus and Copenhagen teams.

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

jobs.occupation: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy
jobs.description:
Declaration of interest regarding PhD project:

The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy, with background in one or more of the following areas: philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, phenomenology.
We are looking for a person with a relevant degree (M.A., MSc. etc.) in philosophy or a related field. Starting date is September 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is fully funded, full-time, for three years. The PhD degree will be awarded by the Faculty of Health Sciences.

 

Research environment

The PhD student will be based in the research group of Applied and Interdisciplinary Phenomenology in the Department of Psychology, SDU, at the Odense campus. The research group develops, disseminates, and applies methods to support cutting-edge research into subjectivity and the nature of human experience. Current group members have backgrounds in philosophy, psychology, anthropology, neuroscience, environmental studies, and pain research.

The group directly supports the professional development of its members, most of whom are postdocs or PhD students. In addition to receiving support from the project team, the PhD student will be supported by the broader group to develop their research, presentation, and teaching skills, as well as other academic skills, including those required for organizing academic activities such as workshops and conferences and for successful grant-writing. The PhD student will therefore be provided with the requisite knowledge and skills for pursuing an academic career in Europe or abroad.

The PhD student will also be provided with a work computer and a dedicated workspace at the Department of Psychology.

 

Project description

The PhD student will be part of the project, Understanding Experiences of Mood Disturbances in Depression (DEPMOOD), led by Anthony Vincent Fernandez. The project is funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark and runs for four years, starting September 1st, 2026. The PhD student will join the project for the final three years, collaborating with the PI, a psychology postdoc, and several external partners in Europe and the US, including philosophers, clinical psychologists, and psychiatrists.

The aim of the project is to establish a taxonomy of the variety of mood disturbances experienced by people diagnosed with depression, providing more precise characterizations of symptoms than those currently offered by concepts such as “depressed mood” or “anhedonia”. The project combines philosophical and qualitative methods, and includes in-depth interviews with people diagnosed with depression. The PhD student will not be expected to carry out interviews, as these will be conducted by the postdoc and external project partners. The PhD student’s primary role will be to help analyze the interview data using a combination of qualitative and philosophical methods. Their PhD thesis will therefore be a theoretical contribution, but will build upon the project’s empirical dataset.

In addition to producing a thesis, the PhD student will be required to take a variety of short PhD courses, carry out an international research stay, and fulfil light teaching duties.

The PhD student will be provided with DKK 10,000 per year for travel. Additional funds may be available.

 

Qualifications

Before the start date of September 1st, 2027, the applicant should have a master’s degree in philosophy or a related field and total course credits equivalent to 300 ECTS. Typically, this is a total of at least five years of education combined between bachelor’s and master’s degrees, with 60 ECTS obtained for every full year of study.

The candidate should have a background in philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, and/or phenomenology. Familiarity with qualitative research methods (especially analysis methods) is an advantage, but by no means required.

The candidate should be proficient in English. Proficiency in Danish or another Scandinavian language may be an advantage, but is not required.

For further information about the project, please contact:
Anthony Vincent Fernandez

Department of Psychology

University of Southern Denmark (SDU)

E-mail: afernandez@health.sdu.dk

Please note that while we are happy to provide answers to questions about the position and application process, direct feedback on application materials cannot be provided.

Applications must include (in English, or with a certified English translation):

 

• 
A letter stating the interest, motivation and qualifications for the project (max. 2 pages) - upload under “Application form”.

• 
Detailed CV, including personal contact information as well as any publications or presentations

• 
Certified copy of diploma and transcripts (Master’s degree in a relevant field). If the applicant is in the process of completing their master’s degree, they should provide transcripts along with a letter from their supervisor confirming expected completion of their degree before September 1st, 2027.

• 
Writing sample of maximum 10,000 words (e.g., publication, conference paper, selection from a master’s thesis). If the sample exceeds this length, please indicate which section should be read.

• 
A document listing 2-3 references, with contact information and a brief note about your relation to the reference. Note that reference letters will only be requested for candidates invited to interview.

 

At this stage, no project proposal is required. Candidates invited to interview will be asked to prepare a brief project plan.

Please do not use generative AI in the formulation of any application materials. The purpose of these materials is to gain a clear sense of you and your abilities.

Shortlisting and interviews may be used in the assessment process.
 

For purposes of evaluation and assessment, application materials may be shared with external members of the project team at Aarhus University and Amsterdam University Medical Center.

Further information about the PhD-study can be found at the homepage of the University.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated

 

Closing date January 15th, 2027

 

We expect to conduct interviews within two months of the application closing date.
Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students.
 

The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order)

 

Salary and Working Conditions at SDU

PhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement.

Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. The base salary (excluding 18.07% pension contribution) is DKK 374,912.98   per year.

The Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark is one of Denmark’s leading faculties of health sciences. With nine departments, internationally top‑class research, and a broad range of health‑related study programmes, we contribute to developing the knowledge, treatments, and healthcare system of the future.

As an employee at the faculty, you become part of an ambitious and interdisciplinary environment characterised by high academic standards, strong collaborations, and excellent opportunities for professional development. The faculty has activities in Odense, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. In Esbjerg and Copenhagen, strong academic communities provide the framework for research and education, while our modern faculty building in Odense brings research, education, and administration together under one roof and is directly connected to Odense University Hospital.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: Four-year Researcher position on Greenland marine ecosystems
jobs.description:
Four-year Researcher position on Greenland marine ecosystems
The Department of Ecoscience, Aarhus University, invites applications for a four-year scientist position on the biodiversity and coastal ecosystem status and trends along Greenland’s coast with a special focus on the use of eDNA for monitoring of marine macroalgae. The position is linked to multiple international projects, including the Greenland Ecosystem Monitoring Programme with an overarching theme of studying the impacts of climate change on coastal ecosystems in Greenland. The position requires active participation in developing and attracting funding for new projects including a special focus on developing and implementing eDNA tools for the ecological research and monitoring.

This is a four–year position available from 15 February 2027. 

Job description
The position focuses on the ecology of coastal marine ecosystems in Greenland and their responses to climate change, particularly warming and the ongoing loss of the cryosphere.

You are expected to participate in annual field campaigns in Greenland and contribute to the analysis and interpretation of monitoring and experimental data from coastal Greenland ecosystems. A particular focus will be on developing and applying environmental DNA (eDNA) methods for characterising and quantifying marine biodiversity, with an emphasis on marine macroalgae. This includes establishing high-quality biodiversity baselines and improving our capacity to detect changes in species distributions and the arrival of new species.

Your profile
Applicants must hold a PhD in biology or a closely related field. Documented experience with Arctic marine vegetation and ecosystem ecology is considered an advantage, together with expertise in eDNA-based approaches, including metabarcoding, quantitative PCR-based methods such as digital PCR (dPCR), bioinformatics and biostatistics.

Experience with marine fieldwork, DNA barcoding, experimental design and morphological species identification is also an advantage. The successful candidate is expected to have experience in developing research ideas and in contributing to research proposals and grant applications. A scientific diving certification is considered an advantage.

Fluency in spoken and written English is required. In addition, the candidate should enjoy working collaboratively in an interdisciplinary and international research environment and be motivated to contribute actively to fieldwork, research development and scientific publication.

Who we are
The Department of Ecoscience (https://ecos.au.dk/en/) is organised under the Faculty of Technical Sciences. The department’s research areas cover most aspects of biology and ecology, spanning all biological levels from genetics, physiological processes, individuals, populations and species to entire ecosystems. Strategic and applied research account for a large part of the research activities at the Department of Ecoscience. Geographically, the department works from the tropics to the poles, but with greater focus on Danish conditions. The department has an obligation towards the Ministry of Environment and Food of Denmark and the authorities in Greenland as national advisors on environmental issues. The department’s research, consultancy and teaching are linked to strong and active research groups. 

What we offer 
The successful candidate is offered:

• Access to a well-developed research infrastructure
• Office space and shared equipment
• a research climate inviting lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a working environment with teamwork, close working relations, network activities among young scientists and social activities
• a workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is the main University campus in Aarhus, C.F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C. 

Contact information

For further information, please contact Mikael Sejr (mse@ecos.au.dk) or Dorte Krause-Jensen (dkj@ecos.au.dk). 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range 
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.occupation: Head of the Nordic-Baltic Cyber Consortium (NBCC)
jobs.description:
About the position
The Danish Resilience Agency (SAMSIK) is seeking a highly experienced and strategic leader to serve as Head of the Nordic-Baltic Cyber Consortium (NBCC).

The NBCC is a Danish-hosted, EU-supported cybersecurity initiative established under the EU Cyber Solidarity Act. The consortium brings together Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania and Norway to build and operate a regional cyber hub that strengthens situational awareness and analytical capacity across the Nordic-Baltic region.

As Head of the NBCC, you will be responsible for establishing and leading a new international organisation of strategic importance to both regional and European cybersecurity. While formally employed by the Danish Resilience Agency, you will report to the NBCC Executive Board, composed of senior representatives from the participating national cybersecurity authorities, and operate in close coordination with EU institutions.

The position is based in Copenhagen, Denmark.

Key responsibilities

Strategic leadership and governance

• 
Provide overall strategic direction and leadership of the NBCC in line with EU objectives, consortium agreements and national mandates.

• 
Develop, implement and continuously adjust the NBCC’s strategic roadmap, including the phased build-up from initial deployment to full operational capability.

• 
Ensure alignment between the NBCC activities, EU cybersecurity policies and the strategic interests of participating member states.

Management, organisation and budget

• 
Act as head of the NBCC organisation, including direct line management of up to eight permanent staff based in Denmark and professional oversight of national analysts located in each participating member state.

• 
Build and lead a cohesive multinational organisation with a shared operational culture, while managing differing national frameworks and practices.

• 
Ensure sound financial management, reporting and documentation in accordance with EU and national requirements.

Operational responsibility

• 
Hold overall responsibility for the NBCC’s operational delivery, including the secure and reliable operation of platforms for cyber threat intelligence sharing, analytical collaboration and communication.

• 
Ensure structured and timely sharing of relevant cyber threat information and contribution to regional and European situational awareness.

About you
To succeed in this role, we expect that you:

• 
Have proven experience leading multinational or international cooperation involving multiple stakeholders and governance layers; experience from Nordic-Baltic cooperation is a strong advantage.

• 
Possess a strong understanding of cyber threat intelligence, incident response ecosystems and information-sharing mechanisms at national and international level.

• 
Have demonstrated experience with EU cooperation, preferably including EU-funded projects and engagement with EU institutions.

• 
Are able to operate confidently at senior political and administrative levels, nationally and internationally.

• 
Can demonstrate strong regional insight and experience, for example from a Nordic or Baltic cybersecurity authority or a comparable organisation.

 In addition, you:

• 
Exercise strong strategic judgement and are able to balance political, operational and technical considerations.

• 
Have excellent leadership and communication skills and are able to build trust across national and organisational boundaries.

• 
Are fully proficient in English; knowledge of one or more Nordic or Baltic languages is an advantage. Danish language skills are not required.

About the Danish Resilience Agency
The Danish Resilience Agency is under the authority of the Danish Ministry for Resilience and Preparedness. The agency is responsible for tasks related to cybersecurity, crisis management, physical security and protection of critical infrastructure.

We advise and support authorities, companies and key societal functions in preventing and managing incidents and crises. The agency currently employs approximately 300 staff members working across disciplines in a highly engaged and mission-driven environment.

About the NBCC
The NBCC is a Nordic-Baltic cybersecurity cooperation supported by the EU. Through the NBCC, the participating countries jointly establish and operate a regional cyber hub that enhances collective situational awareness and analytical capacity.

The NBCC will jointly procure cybersecurity capabilities with the EU, employ analysts in Copenhagen and across the member states, and contribute to the European Cybersecurity Shield. The NBCC is organised as a distinct entity within the Danish Resilience Agency and is accountable to its Executive Board.

As Head of the NBCC, you will be responsible for building this organisation from the ground up and for strengthening collective regional resilience against cyber threats.

Salary and terms of employment
Salary and terms of employment will depend on qualifications and experience and will be determined in accordance with the collective agreements applicable to employees in the Danish state. The area of employment is the Danish Ministry for Resilience and Preparedness.

Employment is conditional on obtaining and maintaining a Danish security clearance at SECRET (DK: HEMMELIGT) level for the duration of employment.

The position is a fixed-term appointment for a period of 4 years, with the possibility of extension.

The position is full-time 37-hours per week, and the duty station is Holsteinsgade 63, 2100 Copenhagen.

To be eligible for employment EU/EEA Citizens are required to obtain an EU residence document as proof of your right to reside and work in Denmark. Non-EU/EEA Citizens must hold a valid residence and work permit before you can begin working in Denmark. Citizens of Sweden, Norway, Finland, or Iceland do not require a residence or work permit to live and work in Denmark. For more detailed information regarding the regulations for your specific citizenship, please visit: New to Denmark and/or Info Norden | Nordisk Samarbejde

If the position is filled by an applicant not currently residing in Denmark, the Danish Resilience Agency is prepared to offer a relocation package of up to 45.000 DKK. Any other costs related to relocation or housing must be covered by the employee.

Are you interested?
Please submit your application via the “Apply” button on this page. Your application must be received by the recruitment system no later than 15th November 2026 and must include a CV and relevant diplomas of education.

For further information about the position, please contact Kia Slæbæk Jensen at +45 2134 1851 or Morten Bro at +45 2178 4257.

All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply regardless of personal background.

Applications may be shared with participants from the employment committee from all participating countries.

Your profile & qualifications 

We are looking for a commercially aware and structured tender professional who enjoys bringing people and specialist disciplines together around a shared deadline. You take ownership, maintain an overview when the process becomes complex, and communicate clearly with stakeholders at different levels of the organisation. 

You combine attention to detail with the ability to understand the bigger commercial picture. You are comfortable challenging inputs, following up on deliverables, and ensuring that the proposed solution is both competitive and operationally achievable. 

To succeed in this position, we imagine that you have: 

• Relevant experience in tender or bid management within offshore wind, renewable energy, maritime, oil and gas, engineering, or technical services. 
• Experience leading complex, multidisciplinary tenders involving several internal and external stakeholders. 
• A strong understanding of tender governance, compliance, cost estimation, pricing, contractual risk, approvals, negotiations, and handovers.

Additional languages relevant to our key markets will be considered an advantage. 

Welcome to Semco Maritime

At Semco Maritime, we create change. For people. For projects. And for the global energy sector. With us, you will join a community of over 2,300 of the most dedicated thinkers and doers in the energy industry who are driving real change and making their own personal mark on the global energy landscape.

Safety is at the core of everything we do, and we are committed to protecting our people, partners, and the planet as we work towards a sustainable energy future.

So yes, working for us will change the energy sector – and may well change you too. 

We know that our people are our greatest strength. We strive to build an inclusive workplace where everyone can be themselves, contribute their perspectives, and feel part of the team. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and believe that diverse teams help us find better solutions and move the energy transition forward.  

Care to join the movement?
Change. With us.

Semco Maritime is an international engineering and contracting company with 2,300 employees and 40 years of dedication rooted in both the conventional energy sector and the offshore wind industry. This puts us in a unique position to bridge today's and tomorrow’s solutions, constantly seeking clever and pragmatic ways to realise global energy ambitions. We do this through comprehensive project management across all phases of energy projects together with world-leading partners across the globe.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in fungal genomics and predictive modelling - DTU Food
jobs.description:
Fungi are increasingly causing health issues globally. Such infections are not only increasing in humans and animals, but also in crops and as contamination of food products with mycotoxins.

We have recently been awarded funding to develop online webservices for genomic characterization of all pathogens capable of infecting animals, humans and plants, which includes fungi. However, genomics methods and workflows have so far not gained enough attention in relation to plant infecting or mycotoxin producing fungi. 

Databases of genomes of known fungal species have already been developed, as has gene databases of mycotoxin producing gene clusters, but an extensive linkage to fungal taxa is poorly described. Furthermore, it is known that a number of fungi including some used in food production have the gene cluster for mycotoxin production but do not express them.

There is an urgent need to improve our understanding of the genomics of fungi, as well as to translate this into online services.

Thus, as part of our GPAP project (www.gpap.global) and our responsibilities as advise provider to the Danish Food Administration we are seeking a PhD-candidate in fungal genomics with a focus on correlating genomes to phenotypes and developing webservices. This will include whole genome sequencing of fungi, culturing and phenotypic characterization and implementing tools in our widely used online webservice.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your main responsibility will be to create a webservice for identifying fungal taxa, mycotoxin-producing gene clusters and predict phenotypes under different growth conditions. You will perform complete genome sequencing (including the analyses) of a selected range of fungal to create an improved database of reference genomes.

You will also:

• develop a web-based tool for species identification and detection of known toxin-gene clusters, virulence genes and regulatory genes.
• conduct phenotype to genotype association studies based on a large collection of phenotypically characterized Fusarium isolates and develop and improve the online tool.
• With assistant from other group members, you will analyse the output, draw conclusions and present the outputs. 
• communicate research results by presenting data at project meetings and international conferences and write reports and manuscripts for publication.
• engage in the general work carried out by the research group, including discussions and planning of strategies and projects, drafting research grant proposals, etc.
Daily work will be in close collaboration with other researchers in the Genomic Epidemiology group at DTU Food and the Applied Mycology group at DTU Bioengineering, as well as national and international partners.

The ideal candidate has experience in coding in python and experience with Unix-based systems and in machine and deep learning.

Other desired qualifications are:

• extensive knowledge in microbial genomics including phylogenetic analysis
• extensive knowledge of existing bioinformatic algorithms and tools.
• experience with DNA-based workload from microbes
It is a great advantage if you have experience in general microbiology and preferably fungal culturing.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years. Starting date is 1 February 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
The position is a collaboration between DTU Food and DTU Bioengineering, with the employment at DTU-Food. Further information may be obtained from Associate professor Christian Brinch, cbri@food.dtu.dk or Associate professor Jakob Blæsbjerg Hoof, jblni@dtu.dk.

You can read more about DTU National Food Institute at DTU National Food Institute and DTU Bioengineering at DTU Bioengineering .

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 10 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU National Food Institute
DTU National Food Institute conducts research into and disseminates - through advice, innovation and teaching - sustainable and value-creating solutions in the area of food and health for the benefit of society. The vision is to make a difference by generating future prosperity through research into food and health. The institute works to prevent disease and promote health, develop new and better food products for a growing population and create sustainable technological solutions, including biosolutions. The institute’s tasks are carried out in interdisciplinary collaboration within e.g. nutrition, chemistry, toxicology, microbiology, epidemiology, modelling, and technology. This is achieved through a strong academic environment of international top class with correspondingly skilled researchers and employees. The Institute employs approximately 390 staff members.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.description:
DANSK:

Timelønnet fuldtidsstilling på 37 timer om ugen – med faste arbejdstider søndag–torsdag og fri fredag–lørdag.

Har du øje for kvalitet, kan du holde overblik, og har du lyst til at tage ansvar for et mindre team? Så søger vi dig til vores fødevareproduktion i Hedehusene.

Hos FRISKSNIT søger vi en medarbejdende teamleder, som både deltager i det praktiske produktionsarbejde og koordinerer opgaverne for tre kolleger. Du skal sammen med teamet sikre, at produkterne bliver pakket korrekt, mærket rigtigt og færdige til tiden.

Vi er en fødevareproduktionsvirksomhed med cirka 75 fuldtidsansatte. Vi er medlem af Dansk Industri og omfattet af Industriens Overenskomst.

Dine arbejdsopgaver

Du bliver ansvarlig for den daglige koordinering i dit team og samarbejder tæt med den produktionsansvarlige. Du deltager selv i produktionen og følger op på, at teamet arbejder effektivt og overholder instruktionerne for kvalitet, hygiejne og sikkerhed.

Dine vigtigste opgaver er at:

• 
Koordinere og fordele arbejdet mellem teamets tre øvrige medarbejdere og følge op på dagens opgaver og effektivitet.

• 
Sikre korrekt pakning og mærkning, herunder kontrollere emballage, etiketter og datomærkning.

• 
Deltage i produktions- og pakkearbejdet samt støtte og oplære kolleger i de aftalte arbejdsgange.

• 
Reagere på fejl og forsinkelser og inddrage den produktionsansvarlige, når der er behov for hjælp eller ændrede prioriteringer.

Hvem er du?

Du arbejder omhyggeligt, tager ansvar og bevarer overblikket, når der er travlt. Du kan give tydelige instruktioner og bidrager til et godt samarbejde gennem en respektfuld og hjælpsom tilgang til dine kolleger.

Erfaring fra fødevareproduktion, pakkeri eller lignende er en fordel, men du behøver ikke have en bestemt faguddannelse. Erfaring med koordinering af opgaver eller oplæring af kolleger er også en fordel. Det er ikke et krav, at du tidligere har haft titlen teamleder.

Arbejdssproget er engelsk. Du skal derfor kunne forstå arbejdsinstruktioner og kommunikere tydeligt med kolleger og ledelse på engelsk.

Arbejdstid:

Stillingen er på 37 betalte arbejdstimer om ugen med følgende faste mødetider:

Søndag: kl. 08.00–16.00
Mandag–torsdag: kl. 12.00–20.00
Fredag og lørdag: fri

Mødetiderne omfatter samlet tre timers ubetalte pauser om ugen. Pauserne indgår ikke i de 37 betalte arbejdstimer. Den konkrete placering af pauserne fremgår af arbejdsplanen.

Arbejdstidens placering følger virksomhedens lokalaftale.

Løn og ansættelsesvilkår:

Du bliver timelønnet med grundtimeløn, et fast teamledertillæg og relevante tillæg, herunder tillæg for søndagsarbejde.

Ansættelsen sker efter Industriens Overenskomst og virksomhedens gældende lokalaftaler, med pension, feriepenge og fritvalg.

Fritvalg og søgnehelligdagsbidrag udbetales månedligt sammen med lønnen efter virksomhedens aftale.

Du får oplæring i arbejdsopgaverne, vores produkter og de kvalitetskrav, der gælder i produktionen. Du får en praktisk rolle med ansvar for den daglige koordinering og tæt samarbejde med både dit team og den produktionsansvarlige.

Ansættelsesform: Tidsubegrænset fuldtidsansættelse.
Arbejdssted: FRISKSNIT, Hedelykken 14, 2640 Hedehusene.
Tiltrædelse: Efter aftale.

Sådan søger du

Send dit CV og en kort ansøgning til Job@frisksnit.dk senest fredag den 13. november 2026. Skriv ”Teamleder – FRISKSNIT” i emnefeltet.

Fortæl gerne om din erfaring med produktion, pakning eller koordinering af kolleger, og hvorfor du er interesseret i stillingen. Du er velkommen til at skrive din ansøgning på engelsk.

Spørgsmål til stillingen kan også sendes til Job@frisksnit.dk.

Vi opfordrer alle kvalificerede ansøgere til at søge stillingen.

Your main tasks will be to:

• 
Ensure correct packing and labelling, including checking packaging, labels and date markings.

• 
Take part in production and packing, while supporting colleagues and training them in the agreed procedures.

Working hours

The position offers 37 paid working hours per week, with the following fixed schedule:

Pay and employment terms

This is an hourly-paid position with a basic hourly wage, a fixed Team Leader allowance and applicable supplements, including a supplement for Sunday work.

Employment is covered by the Danish Industrial Agreement (Industriens Overenskomst) and the company’s applicable local agreements, including pension contributions, holiday pay and flexible benefits.

Flexible benefits payments (fritvalg) and the public-holiday allowance are paid monthly together with wages under the company’s agreement.

You will receive training in your tasks, our products and the quality requirements that apply in production. The role combines practical work with responsibility for daily coordination and close cooperation with your team and the person responsible for production.

Employment type: Permanent, full-time employment with no fixed end date.
Workplace: FRISKSNIT, Hedelykken 14, 2640 Hedehusene, Denmark.
Start date: By agreement.

How to apply

Please send your CV and a short application to Job@frisksnit.dk by Friday, 13 November 2026. Use “Team Leader – FRISKSNIT” as the email subject.

Tell us about your experience in production, packing or coordinating colleagues, and why you are interested in the position. Applications in English are welcome.

Questions about the position can also be sent to Job@frisksnit.dk.

We welcome applications from all qualified candidates.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship/scholarship, Integrating Hormonal and Biomechanical Stimuli in Multi-scale Modelling of human Vascular cells

jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Mechanical and Production Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title:
Integrating Hormonal and Biomechanical Stimuli in Multi-scale Modelling of human Vascular cells

Research area and project description:
As part of the ERC Starting Grant project DISSEX, which aims at developing a sex-aware multiscale framework to predict vascular dissection risk, we are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to join our multi-disciplinary Cardiovascular Engineering (CareEng) group at Aarhus University. This PhD project specifically aims at quantifying how human coronary arteries respond to systemic hormonal fluctuations and biomechanical stress through both experimental and computational techniques. There are 2 objectives.

Objective 1: Experimental investigation of vascular adaptation
The candidate will use innovative microfluidic platforms and ex vivo human coronary arteries to recreate physiological and pathological vascular environments. By exposing vascular tissues to controlled flow, pressure, and hormone profiles representative of daily fluctuations in estradiol, cortisol, and testosterone, the project will quantify how endothelial and smooth muscle cells respond in terms of proliferation, apoptosis, signalling, and biomechanical function. Particular attention will be given to endothelial pathways involving nitric oxide and endothelin-1, providing a unique dataset on how systemic and mechanical stimuli jointly influence vascular health.

Objective 2: Development of a multiscale computational model
Building on the experimental findings, the candidate will develop a multiscale computational framework linking cellular activity to vessel-scale biomechanics. Combining agent-based modelling with computational fluid dynamics, the model will integrate hormonal regulation, cellular adaptation, and biomechanical stresses within the vascular wall. The resulting digital platform will enable mechanistic investigation of vascular remodelling processes and provide a foundation for understanding conditions that may predispose arteries to dissection.

The PhD candidate will join an interdisciplinary team bringing together expertise in vascular physiology, Cardiovascular biomechanics, microfluidics and fabrication; computational modelling, and clinical cardiovascular medicine. The project includes close collaboration with clinicians, biologists, and engineers and provides access to state-of-the-art laboratory and computational research facilities.

Qualifications and specific competences:
We are looking for highly motivated and independent candidates with the intention to complete a 3-year PhD at Aarhus University. The ideal candidate is expected to have most of the following qualifications:
 
• Master’s degree in Biomedical Engineering, Biomechanical Engineering, Biotechnology or relevant fields.
• In-depth knowledge in fluid mechanics and cardiovascular applications.
• Experience with cell culture and tissue engineering
• Familiarity with numerical modelling (CFD), and software such as COMSOL, SimVascular, or similar software
• (optional) Previous exposure to agent-based modelling or systems biology
• excellent written and spoken English (optional Danish).

Place of employment and place of work:
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering, Aarhus University, Katrinebjergvej 89F, 8200 Aarhus N.
Contacts:
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
• Mahdi Abkar, e-mail: abkar@mpe.au.dk (main supervisor)
• Monika Colombo, e-mail: mc@mpe.au.dk (co-supervisor)
For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:
• admission.gradschool.tech@au.dk
How to apply:
Please follow this link to submit your application.

Application deadline is 30 November 2026 at 23:59 CET.
Preferred starting date is 01 March 2027.

For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Please note:

• The programme committee may request further information or invite the applicant to attend an interview.
• Shortlisting will be used, which means that the evaluation committee only will evaluate the most relevant applications.
Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8. As a PhD fellow you will also receive a monthly non-pensionable allowance.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which everyone has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor in Global Health at The Research Unit of General Practice, University of Southern Denmark
jobs.description:
The Research Unit of General Practice at the Institute of Public Health, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a 2-year full time Assistant Professor position in Global Health. The position starts on April 1, 2027, and will terminate at the end of the appointment period unless otherwise agreed.

Beskrivelse til interne kandidater

The Research Unit of General Practice at the Institute of Public Health, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a 2-year full time Assistant Professor position in Global Health.

The position starts on April 1, 2027, and will terminate at the end of the appointment period unless otherwise agreed.

Job Description
The position involves research in global health with a particular focus on strengthening primary healthcare systems for vulnerable and underserved populations in low- and middle-income countries. The successful candidate will contribute to the international research project STRENGTHENing Gender-Responsive Health Systems for Addressing Non-Communicable Diseases in Climate-Affected Fishing Communities in Western Kenya (STRENGTHEN) and other upcoming global health projects. The STRENGTHEN project aims to improve the prevention and management of NCDs in climate-affected fishing communities in Western Kenya by making the health systems even more gender-responsive. The project will generate evidence on how community health promoters (CHPs) provide NCD care in FEDCs affected by climate change. It will address five key health systems building blocks: health information systems, health workforce, health service, medical technology, and policy and governance. The work will involve conducting implementation and health services research, and collaborating with researchers, healthcare professionals, policymakers, and community stakeholders across different country settings. The position involves travel to Kenya for short periods.

We offer a challenging position in a stimulating research environment with excellent opportunities for collaboration within SDU and with international research partners.

Expectations of qualifications
The successful applicant should have:

• 
A PhD degree (or equivalent) in Global Health, Public Health, Epidemiology, Health Services Research, Implementation Science, or a related discipline

• 
A strong background in health systems research, primary healthcare, chronic disease prevention and management, or health equity research in low- and middle-income countries

• 
A strong academic record

• 
Good collaboration and communication skills

• 
Interest in co-supervising BSc, MSc and PhD students

Following qualifications are preferred:

• 
Experience with mixed-methods research, including qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis

• 
Experience with implementation science, intervention development, and evaluation of community-based health programmes

• 
Experience with global health research conducted in low- and middle-income countries and/or humanitarian settings

• 
Experience with stakeholder engagement and collaboration with healthcare providers, communities, and policymakers

• 
Experience with writing research applications

• 
Experience in teaching and education

Further information
For further information please contact Prof. Jens Søndergaard, jsondergaard@health.sdu.dk, or Associate Prof. Trine Thilsing, tthilsing@health.sdu.dk 

Application deadline and interviews
The application deadline is November15th 2026 at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST)  

Terms of employment 
Appointment as an assistant professor is temporary and for an initial 2-year period, and the preferred start date is from 1. April 2027.

During employment, the assistant professor will complete the Lecturer Training Programme, if this has not already been completed.   

Appointment as an assistant professor requires academic qualifications at PhD level. 

Further information on the appointment procedure can be found in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities. 

The appointment is in accordance with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations .

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation.  

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”. 

Application 
Applications must be submitted electronically using the link “Apply now” - see below.  

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.  

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.  

Your application must include the following as PDF files: 

Please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total). 

• 
a motivation letter.  

• 
a detailed CV.  

• 
degree certificates (including a Ph.D.-diploma). 

• 
a complete and numbered list of publications.  

• 
3 to 5 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please note that a copy of each publication must be attached as a pdf file.  

• 
It is permitted to merge copies of the selected publications into a single PDF file. 

• 
a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy.  

• 
a research plan an explanation of other qualifications relevant to the position. 

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application.

Applications received after the deadline and/or incomplete applications will not be considered. 

If you experience technical problems, you must contact hcm-support@sdu.dk.

Assessment and selection process 
Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves. 

References will be obtained for the preferred candidate from their current and previous employers. Applicants invited for interview should expect to complete a work-related personality assessment.

Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. 

About Us
The Research Unit of General Practice is a collaboration between the Research Unit of General Practice in Odense-Esbjerg, which is organizationally affiliated with the Foundation for General Practice Research (FEA), and the Research Unit of General Practice at the Department of Public Health, University of Southern Denmark (SDU).

The primary objective of the Research Unit is to contribute to the improvement and development of health and healthcare for patients, with a particular focus on services provided in and around general practice. 

A cornerstone of our educational activities is the training of Master's and PhD students. In addition, we contribute to teaching across a range of health sciences bachelor's and master's degree programmes at the Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark, as well as within the Research Training Programme of the specialist training programme in general practice.

Further information about The Faculty of Health Sciences. 

Living and working in Denmark
Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. 

The International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. 

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

About Userlink

Userlink runs AI agents in production at several hundred Nordic webshops, including Bahne, XL-BYG, Coolshop and Bygma. The agents handle the customer dialogue before and after the purchase, and every conversation ends up as structured data on demand and purchase barriers. The team is based in Odense.

The brain

The agents are the arms. The next layer is a system that brings together every signal about a webshop and its customers: conversations on chat, email, phone and social, on-site behaviour, orders, returns and reviews.

The system identifies the moments where a sale is won or lost and intervenes while the session is still live. It scores answer coverage per product and closes the gaps, quantifies objections and unmet demand, and traces returns back to the expectation that broke.

Learning happens across all webshops, more than six million visits a month, where patterns become visible that no single shop has the traffic to see. Every intervention is measured against a control group. The patterns are shared, the data stays with each shop.

The hard problems are retrieval and evaluation of LLM output at scale, data isolation when patterns are shared across customers, latency in real-time flows, and attribution that holds up under scrutiny.

The stack

Java with Spring Boot, React and MongoDB, with language models and vector search on top. Moving the backend to C# and .NET is under consideration.

The role

You are one of the first engineers on the brain and own parts of it from idea to production: data model, retrieval, evaluation and the real-time flows that intervene in the session. You write the code yourself, ship it and follow it when it meets real customers.

The work is not split into tickets in advance. You help decide what gets built, and how, and your choices become the foundation the next engineers build on.

Decisions are made on arguments, not titles. Ideas get challenged regardless of where they come from, and the best one wins.

Why founding

You come in while the brain is taking shape. There is no finished architecture to follow, and the choices you make now are the ones everyone after you builds on.

That is why the role comes with equity. You help build the company, and you own part of what you build. In return we expect you to take responsibility like a co-owner, also when things are unclear or go wrong.

Profile

• 
Experience building and running SaaS systems in production

• 
Solid backend experience in Java or C#, and comfortable in React

• 
Has built LLM-based features and knows how to measure whether they work

• 
Owns what they build, also when it breaks in production

• 
AI-assisted development as part of the daily workflow

The person

• 
Dreams of owning and building a company

• 
Ideally has tried starting something and knows what it takes

• 
Thinks like a founder, not an employee

• 
Happily gives more than a regular job asks for, because it is fun

• 
Says things as they are, and can take the same in return

• 
Takes ownership and looks for solutions rather than excuses

• 
Curious, learns fast and has a positive mindset

What we offer

• 
Competitive salary

• 
Equity

• 
Short decision paths and a high degree of technical freedom

• 
Office at Storms Pakhus in Odense

Application process

We take the time it takes to find the right match.

• 
Introductory conversation

• 
Technical test

• 
Conversation about expectations and terms

Send a short description of something you built from scratch and put into production, and what you learned when it met real users, to jobs@userlink.ai.

The product and the direction

Today we sell chat. Email is rolling out now, and phone and social follow. On top of that we are building the brain: a system that brings together every signal about a webshop and its customers, understands why people buy, and why they do not, and acts on it while the buyer is still on the page. The effect is measured against a control group, so the shop can see what it means for revenue.

That moves the sale from a customer service tool to a conversation about growth, and revenue per customer can become several times what it is today.

There is no finished playbook. Pitch, customer profile and process take shape while you sell, and what works you write down, so the next salespeople can build on it.
