Click here to create an account and upload your resume and a short motivation. We look forward to getting to know you better!

jobs.occupation: Analyst (Student Assistant), Growth Markets Funds Investment Team
jobs.description:
Do you want to join a global leader in renewable energy infrastructure investments? If so, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) is the perfect place for you! We are currently looking for ambitious Analyst (Student Assistant) to join our Growth Markets Funds Investment Team in Copenhagen.

Team

The Growth Market Funds (GMF) invest in renewable energy infrastructure in high-growth middle-income markets with strong fundamentals for renewable development and significant impact potential. The funds target markets across Asia, Latin America and EMEA with strong fundamentals for renewable energy infrastructure investments with a combination of high economic and demographic growth including an expanding middle class leading to an accelerating electricity demand.

You will work closely together with highly experienced colleagues in an international and dynamic environment. We will constantly seek to inspire you, while focusing on your learning and personal development. Working with our skilled team members, you will build a solid commercial and contractual understanding of renewable energy infrastructure projects and how they are financed.

Role

As a Student Analyst, you will contribute to transaction processes, preparing for investment decisions, analyzing and reporting on investment performance and various other tasks.

Responsibilities will consist of but are not limited to:

• 
Preparation of Investment Committee materials

• 
Visualization and presentation of technical and financial data to stakeholders

• 
Financial modelling of large complex infrastructure assets including project finance

• 
Working together with industrial partners and advisors

• 
Ad-hoc analyses in close collaboration with other team members

The position is part-time and based in our headquarters in NordØ. The workload will vary depending on the numbers of projects you are working on, and you will be given the opportunity to influence your daily routine and schedule.

You

CIP is looking for 2nd and 3rd year BSc students in Economics, Business, Finance, Engineering, or any other relevant field.

We are looking for the following candidate:

• 
High academic achievements

• 
Great communication skills with fluency in written and spoken English

• 
Interest in corporate finance, strategy, and renewable energy

• 
Advanced skills in Excel and PowerPoint

• 
Strong analytical aptitude and structured and project-oriented approach to work

• 
Ability to deliver high quality output in a time-sensitive setting

• 
Curious and creative mindset and spirit of inquiry

• 
Ability to work with limited supervision, at the same time enjoying teamwork and engaging with colleagues at all levels of seniority

• 
Experience in energy and infrastructure is beneficial, but not a requirement

Please note that we do not offer a remote working opportunity, thus you must be a Danish resident to be eligible for this role. Students on exchange in Denmark are not considered eligible for this position.

The process

Please apply online as soon as possible as applications will be processed on an ongoing basis. For questions related to the role, please reach out to our Talent Acquisition team at recruitment@cipfs.com. We do not include CV's and Cover Letters sent by email.

As we continue to improve our candidate experience, diversity and avoid unconscious bias, please avoid having a photo in your CV. We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality for all applicants.

Please be aware that we will not accept speculative CV submissions for any of our roles from recruitment agencies, and any unsolicited candidate submissions will be exempt from any payment expectations and ownership.

---

Building value that matters

Founded in 2012, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners P/S (CIP) today is the world’s largest dedicated fund manager within greenfield renewable energy investments and a global leader in offshore wind. To date, CIP has developed and constructed more than +50 greenfield renewable projects around the world. CIP is developing a greenfield project portfolio of ~160GW total, and ~16 GW is in operation or under construction. CIP manages 13 funds and has to date raised approximately EUR ~35 billion for investments in energy and associated infrastructure from more than ~200 international institutional investors.

CIP has a multinational team of ~500 full-time employees with extensive experience and knowledge within the fields of renewable energy project development and regulated infrastructure. In addition, CIP has a broad range of competencies within corporate finance, mergers & acquisitions, engineering, construction, project development, and project management.

CIP has built a prominent investment team capable of originating proprietary investment opportunities and executing projects and investments based on the team’s industrial background, large industrial network, and extensive experience in structuring, executing, and managing investments within energy infrastructure. Headquartered in Copenhagen, CIP also operates from key locations across the globe, including offices in Hamburg, Munich, London, Utrecht, New York, Tokyo, Melbourne, Luxembourg, Kuala Lumpur, Seoul and Singapore. In addition, CIP has 17 local project offices globally.

For more information, visit www.cip.com.

jobs.occupation: Consultant, Procurement Advisory - KPMG Advisory Academy 2027
jobs.description:
Curious about how leading organizations make smarter buying decisions? Join our Procurement Advisory team and help clients transform the way they work with suppliers, use data, and leverage digital tools to create measurable business value. From day one, you'll be involved in projects that make a real impact, turning complex challenges into practical improvements.

About the role

Procurement is changing quickly. Organizations are using data, AI, automation and digital platforms to make better decisions, improve supplier collaboration and create more resilient operations. As a Consultant in Procurement Advisory, you will help clients navigate that change while building a solid foundation in consulting, sourcing and source-to-pay transformation.

You will work alongside experienced colleagues on projects across the entire sourcing process, from analysis and strategy to implementation and governance, contributing to impactful projects across both private and public organizations. You will help design and deliver solutions that improve procurement performance and support strategic objectives. You will play a key role in translating data and technology into actionable insights while becoming part of an environment where professionalism, innovation, and collaboration go hand in hand.

In this role, you will have the opportunity to:

• 
Analyze procurement processes, spend and supplier information, and turn findings into clear recommendations e.g. through business cases, sourcing strategies or outsourcing models.

• 
Support the design and implementation of procurement strategies, future-fit operating models, processes and digital solutions.

• 
Explore how AI, automation, analytics and procurement technologies can improve transparency, decision-making and performance across sourcing and procurement processes.

Perks of joining Procurement Advisory

Our team combines procurement expertise, business transformation and technology. This means you will not be limited to analyzing a problem or writing a strategy. You will also help translate recommendations into processes, operating models and solutions that can work in practice.

Learn by doing: You will take part in real client work from the beginning, with guidance from colleagues who will help you build confidence and increase your responsibility over time.

Work across disciplines: You will collaborate with procurement & sourcing specialists, technology consultants, data experts and international colleagues from across KPMG, giving you broad exposure while you develop a clear functional specialism.

Shape a growing area: You will join a close and motivated team where ideas are welcomed, knowledge is shared and junior colleagues are encouraged to contribute to client delivery, proposals and the continued development of our services.

About you, our new team member

You enjoy working with people and building strong relationships with clients, colleagues, and cross-functional teams. You thrive in a collaborative environment where knowledge sharing, teamwork, and mutual support are valued. At the same time, you appreciate a positive and social workplace where professional excellence and having fun go hand in hand.

More specifically, we are looking for someone who:

• 
Is curious about how organizations and their procurement functions operate.

• 
Enjoys turning complex information into clear and actionable transformation stories.

• 
Has an interest in sourcing, outsourcing, supplier management and/or procurement.

• 
Brings solid analytical skills and a structured approach to problem solving.

• 
Is motivated to learn, take initiative and develop your expertise over time.

• 
Is fluent in English, with Danish language skills considered an advantage.

• 
Holds or are expected to complete a relevant master's degree before Autumn 2027.

KPMG Advisory Academy

As part of your development, you will join the KPMG Advisory Academy, a 14-month development program designed to give you a solid foundation for your consulting career. Through a combination of professional training, personal development, networking opportunities, and practical client experience, you will build key consulting skills while expanding your network across KPMG Advisory.

Want to learn more about the KPMG Advisory Academy and how it supports your development from day one? Read more about the Advisory Academy here.

Are you ready to become part of KPMG? Send your application today!

The application deadline is 15 November, but we review applications on an ongoing basis and may close the process earlier - so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Interviews are expected to take place in November and December.

All we need from you is your CV, transcript, and a cover letter (a one-page document in which you answer the following three questions). How you choose to respond is entirely up to you - your answers will help us get to know you better and provide a basis for further discussion in a potential interview.

The questions are:

• 
Tell us about a situation where you used data or structured analysis to understand a complex problem. What did you do, and what did you learn?

• 
Procurement transformation often requires business, people and technology to work together. Which part interests you most, and why?

• 
Describe a time when you worked with others to deliver a result under changing priorities or an unfamiliar set of circumstances. How did you contribute?

If you have any questions or would like more information, please contact Senior consultant, Sascha Hjort at shjorth@kpmg.com.

Please note that we do not accept applications by e-mail to ensure GDPR compliance.

At KPMG, we are committed to developing diverse talents at all levels. We encourage all interested candidates to apply, regardless of age, race, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, religion, or ethnicity.

We can’t wait to hear from you!

We are looking for one in-house fit model for our menswear and one for our womenswear for minimum 2–3 full working days per month at MASCOT’s headquarters in Pårup. Are you interested in clothing, fit and functionality, and are you able to be flexible in your day-to-day schedule? If so, you could become an important part of developing our future collections. You do not need previous modelling experience. What matters is that your measurements match one of our base sizes, that you are patient, and that you can provide honest and constructive feedback.

About the role

As an in-house fit model, you will try on prototypes and production samples while our Pattern Designers and Designers assess fit, freedom of movement, comfort and functionality. Your feedback will help ensure that the garments perform well during an active working day.

This is not modelling work for photos, films or fashion shows. The fittings take place internally in a professional setting with our Product Development team.

Your primary responsibilities

• Try on garments and provide specific feedback on fit, comfort and movement

• Participate actively in fittings with Pattern Designers, Designers and Product Developers

• Be available for measurements and sample assessments

• Contribute patiently and constructively when a product needs to be tried several times

• By agreement, help with minor practical tasks relating to samples and collections (eg. tryout some garment functions, etc..)

Working hours and scheduling

The role involves approximately 2–3 working days per month and/or might be every 1 or 2 weeks (depending on the peak of development timing). The days will be agreed and scheduled well in advance, although requirements may vary in line with product development. You must be able to attend in person for a full or consecutive full working days at our headquarters in Pårup near Silkeborg (Silkeborgvej 14, 7442 Engesvang).

The role may therefore be suitable alongside studies or other flexible work, provided you are able to set aside full weekdays, from 8.00 to 16.30.

We are looking for someone who

• is reliable and flexible

• is patient and comfortable trying on clothes in front of a small, established team

• can describe how the garments feel and perform during movement

• has and can maintain reasonably stable body measurements over time

• can communicate in English

Measurements required

Size 40/L

What we offer

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Data-driven Critical Raw Material Supply Chain Resilience
jobs.description:
Do you want to investigate the resilience of critical raw material supply chains supporting low-carbon and digital technologies? Join us as a PhD student at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, University of Southern Denmark.

The Department of Green Technology at the University of Southern Denmark invites applications for a three-year PhD position in data-driven critical raw material supply chain resilience.

The position will be based at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, Department of Green Technology, Faculty of Engineering, at the SDU Odense campus. The expected starting date is 15 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

 

Project Overview

The deployment of low-carbon technologies, electrification and digital infrastructure is increasing global demand for critical raw materials. At the same time, the production and processing of many of these materials are geographically concentrated and exposed to geopolitical, economic, environmental and logistical disruptions.

Understanding how technology development affects material demand, in-use stocks, end-of-life flows and global supply dependencies is therefore important for assessing and strengthening the resilience of critical raw material supply chains.

The PhD position is jointly funded through research projects on critical raw material supply chains and material requirements for Denmark’s climate-neutral transition. The project will be embedded in an interdisciplinary research environment combining environmental systems analysis, supply-chain research and data science.

 

PhD Topic Description

The PhD project will develop modular and data-driven approaches for analysing critical raw material demand, supply-chain dependencies and resilience.

A central methodological contribution will be the development of transparent, reusable and reproducible computational modules for dynamic material flow analysis. The modules will support the integration of technology deployment scenarios, material intensities, product lifetimes, stocks and flows, end-of-life management, recycling, production, trade, facility and ownership data.

The developed approaches will be applied to selected technology systems, including Denmark’s wind-energy infrastructure and the rapidly expanding infrastructure supporting data centres and AI computing. These cases will be analysed within a common methodological framework to examine how infrastructure expansion and technological change influence demand for critical and scarce materials, in-use stocks, future waste flows, recycling potential and global supply-chain dependencies.

The project may also investigate overlapping material requirements and competition for materials across low-carbon and digital technologies. Particular attention may be given to supply concentration, host–by-product dependencies, trade and ownership structures, supply bottlenecks, cascading risks and potential resilience strategies.

Depending on the candidate’s academic background and the specific research questions, the project may include network analysis, geospatial analysis, scenario modelling, uncertainty analysis, machine learning and other AI-supported approaches.

The candidate will build on selected existing models, datasets and research activities in the group and further develop scientifically robust and reusable methods that improve transparency, comparability and reproducibility in material-system research.

The exact research focus and detailed PhD plan will be developed jointly with the successful candidate, taking into account the project objectives, academic background and research interests.

In addition to a PhD dissertation and high-quality scientific publications, the project is expected to produce reusable modelling methods, documented datasets and reproducible computational workflows.

 

PhD Position and Research Environment

As a PhD student, you will conduct independent research under the supervision of an interdisciplinary team, contribute to high-quality scientific publications and participate actively in a collaborative research environment.

You will join SDU Life Cycle Engineering, where research covers industrial ecology, material flow analysis, life cycle assessment, circular economy, resource systems and sustainability transitions.

The project connects expertise in engineering, data science, mathematics, business, supply-chain research and geological resources. The wider research environment includes competences in material flow analysis, critical raw material systems, data mining, network analysis, supply-chain science, finance, investment, ownership structures, geological resources and technology systems.

The position provides opportunities for collaboration across SDU faculties and with external research partners. It may also include participation in international conferences, research visits and collaboration with relevant industrial and public-sector stakeholders.

The PhD programme follows the Danish PhD framework and includes coursework, participation in active research environments, dissemination activities, and teaching or other knowledge-dissemination duties.

 

What We Expect

We are looking for a highly motivated, independent and collaborative candidate with a strong interest in critical raw materials, quantitative modelling, data-driven research and sustainability.

Applicants must hold a relevant master’s degree or equivalent by the time of enrolment. Relevant academic backgrounds may include engineering, industrial ecology, sustainability science, resource management, data science, computer science, applied mathematics, operations research, supply-chain management, geoinformatics, mining or geological sciences, or another relevant natural science or quantitative discipline.

The successful candidate should demonstrate:

• 
A solid academic foundation in quantitative analysis, system modelling, data science or related methods. 

• 
Experience with programming and data analysis, preferably using Python or a similar programming language. 

• 
Experience with data handling, including data cleaning, transformation, integration and exploratory analysis. 

• 
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. 

• 
The ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary research environment. 

• 
Good written and spoken English. 

• 
A strong interest in sustainability, critical raw materials and supply-chain resilience. 

Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage:

• 
Material flow analysis, industrial ecology or material systems modelling. 

• 
Network, supply-chain or geospatial analysis. 

• 
Scientific computing and reproducible research workflows. 

• 
Statistics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, optimisation, uncertainty or scenario analysis. 

• 
International trade, production facility or corporate ownership data. 

• 
Critical raw materials, wind energy, digital infrastructure or data centres. 

Applicants are not expected to possess expertise in all these areas. Prior experience with material flow analysis is an advantage but is not a requirement. Relevant training will be provided according to the candidate’s background and the needs of the project.

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

The application must be submitted in English through the SDU online recruitment system.

Assessment of applicants will be based on the submitted application material. The application must include:

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
A motivated application describing the applicant’s research interests, relevant qualifications and motivation for applying. 

• 
Documentation of academic qualifications, including bachelor’s and master’s degree certificates and complete transcripts of grades. 

• 
Official English translations of documents not issued in English or Danish. 

• 
Two letters of recommendation. 

• 
A list of publications and up to two examples of relevant publications, if available. 

• 
The completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
The completed TEK form for calculation of grade-point average. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
Official documentation describing the grading system of the awarding university, if the degree was not obtained in Denmark. 

• 
Examples of relevant thesis work, software, code repositories or other research outputs, where available. 

• 
Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

For administrative questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact our email support.

 

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position, and the monthly gross salary incl. pension is 37.075 DKK. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, you may be placed on a higher salary step. The place of employment is in Odense, Denmark and preferred starting date is February 15, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Applicants must hold a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. Enrollment will be in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order). Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for PhD fellows as described therein as well as the Protocol on PhD fellows signed by the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

 

SDU Life Cycle Engineering

The successful candidate will be affiliated with SDU Life Cycle Engineering at the Department of Green Technology. The research environment conducts interdisciplinary research on the global and systemic interactions between materials, technologies, energy, the environment and society.

The Department of Green Technology is located in Odense, the main campus of the University of Southern Denmark. Odense offers an international research environment and an open Scandinavian working culture.

 

Further Information

Further information about the scientific content of the position is available from:

Wu Chen
Associate Professor
Department of Green Technology
SDU Life Cycle Engineering
University of Southern Denmark
Email: wuc@igt.sdu.dk

Optimize the distribution network

We're looking for an experienced cyber and information security consultant in the GRC domain who has hands-on experience building automation and/or agentic tools into their work.

**What You'll Do

**We're scaling our GRC services team, a team dedicated to making governance, risk, and compliance of cyber and information security more efficient, effective, and valuable to organisations. We do this by automating processes through software and agentic tools, and by defining tasks, inputs, and outputs more clearly than is currently the norm.

As our client list grows, we need someone who can deliver GRC consulting from day one and open up new paths to delivery by developing and implementing our own tools and automations.

This role is open to being shaped by your own passions and talents, whether that's software development, sales and marketing, or deep industry knowledge.

**In This Role, You'll Definitely Be

**

• Helping companies implement and comply with laws, standards, and frameworks like NIS 2, ISO 27001, and the CIS Controls

• Driving projects independently and managing senior stakeholders

• Influencing decisions on cyber and information security at some of Denmark's leading companies and public institutions

**Depending on your experience and interests, you may also be:

**

• Developing your own client networks

• Programming and deploying your own agentic software tools

• Performing technical cybersecurity tasks in client environments

• Building new services from the ground up, targeting industries or problems you understand uniquely well

**What You'll Bring

**You may be a great fit for this role if you have delivered GRC consulting for at least three years, ideally across several clients at once. On top of that, you should have:

• Automated GRC tasks with software and LLMs, refining the output until it beats human work in at least some aspects

• Driven the delivery of software products in collaboration with developers

• Gotten up to speed on new regulatory requirements under tight deadlines

• Fought the least valuable and most dull parts of GRC work while defending the value of good GRC against sceptics and cynics

The ideal candidate must be fluent in English – Danish is a plus, but not required – and we value a relevant master's degree or equivalent hands-on experience.

**To Fit In At The Tech Collective, You Should

**

• Thrive among diverse colleagues, from highly technical security professionals to energetic commercial profiles whose common language is a mix of humour, sarcasm, and passion

• Know how to break down and structure complex assignments, and enjoy sharing your knowledge with your team

• Bring a startup mentality that helps drive the innovation and ingenuity of our GRC services

This role is based in Copenhagen. We combine remote work with meaningful in-person work, and you should expect to be physically present at our office or with clients most of the time.

**What We Offer

**On top of a competitive salary and bonus package, we offer the chance to join a unique team of experts and enthusiasts in your field. Our expectations are matched by our willingness to invest in your development, whether through training, conferences, or the opportunity to pursue research in areas you're passionate about.

**How To Apply

**We review applications on an ongoing basis and encourage you to apply ASAP, as the role will close once filled.

Please submit your CV and a short motivation. If you've built tools, automations, or agentic workflows you're proud of, make sure to include a link or short description as we'd love to see them.

**For Questions, Reach Out To

**

• Niklas Rendboe — nire@thetechcollective.eu

• +45 27 14 55 56

• Úlfur Sonjuson — ulso@thetechcollective.eu

• +45 25 53 19 98

**About Us

**The Tech Collective is a fast-growing consulting company powered by Implement Consulting Group. We're passionate about technology, and we have a genuine interest in people. We aim to make a positive difference in the consulting industry because we believe the ability to create change with impact and purpose is a prerequisite for success in a turbulent world. We're rapidly expanding our Cyber Tech Services team, and we're excited to meet people who want to build the future of GRC at the intersection of business and technology.

jobs.occupation: Senior Business Consultant - Fund Administration & Accounting
jobs.description:
**What Makes Us, Us

**Join some of the most innovative thinkers in FinTech as we lead the evolution of financial technology. If you are an innovative, curious, collaborative person who embraces challenges and wants to grow, learn and pursue outcomes with our prestigious financial clients, say Hello to SimCorp!

At its foundation, SimCorp is guided by our values : caring, customer success-driven, collaborative, curious, and courageous. Our people-centered organization focuses on skills development, relationship building, and client success. We take pride in cultivating an environment where all team members can grow, feel heard, valued, and empowered.

If you like what we’re saying, keep reading!

**WHY THIS ROLE IS IMPORTANT TO US

**As a Senior Business Consultant in Consulting, you will support our clients with best-practice market solutions and with services related to the use of SimCorp Dimension and beyond. You will work closely with local and global SimCorp teams, serving clients in their post-implementation phases. Drawing on your coordination skills and SimCorp Dimension expertise, you will collaborate with client and internal stakeholders on investment solutions, incident and problem management, and small changes or enhancements to current or future flows, all aimed at raising the level of automation and the end-user experience and satisfaction. Because the role is functional, Fund Administration & Accounting expertise is required. As part of your induction, you will work hands-on with our software and attend the three-week SimCorp Dimension® Academy, so you have steady support as you grow into the role.

**What You Will Be Responsible For

**

• Contribute to all aspects of SimCorp Dimension implementation projects.

• Advise on process improvements through better use of SimCorp Dimension, and help improve and document best practices for implementations.

• Map client needs to SimCorp Dimension functions and processes, and design and configure the setup.

• Lead the delivery of customised solutions with focus on Fund administration and Accounting.

• Assist clients in developing an overall test strategy and test plans, and support them in executing those plans.

• Drive the preparation and execution of test cases.

• Facilitate workshops to gather requirements for new and existing clients.

• Mentor, coach and enable colleagues to secure reliable project deliveries.

**What We Value

**

• Motivation to contribute and thrive in the position described above, which matters most.

• Proven skills in the areas below, however you gained them, as the route matters less than the capability.

• Investment accounting knowledge, some familiarity with any local GAAPS, IFRS9 would be an advantage

• Fund administration knowledge, including NAV calculation, Fund Structure and NAV Validation

• A strong background in effective consulting and project management.

• Demonstrated experience in software implementation projects.

• Enthusiasm for learning and using new software.

• A desire to act as a mentor and coach to less experienced colleagues.

• Good English, our corporate language, which is used in all communications.

• Knowledge of another European language is also appreciated. Danish is also an advantage

**Benefits

**SimCorp provides a range of benefits that may influence decisions regarding job offers. With operations in more than 30 offices globally, the benefits package can differ depending on the country. SimCorp implements a global hybrid work policy, requiring employees to be in the office two days per week and permitting remote work on other days. Additional information about location-specific benefits is available from the recruiter.

**NEXT STEPS

**Please send us your application in English via our career site as soon as possible, we process incoming applications continually.

Please note that only applications sent through our system will be processed.

At SimCorp, we recognize that bias can unintentionally occur in the recruitment process. To uphold fairness and equal opportunities for all applicants, we kindly ask you to exclude personal data such as photo, age, or any non-professional information from your application. Thank you for aiding us in our endeavor to mitigate biases in our recruitment process.

For any questions you are welcome to contact Launchpad user our Lead Talent Acquisition Partner. If you are interested in being a part of SimCorp and you can see yourself contributing and thriving in the position described above, but are not sure this role is suitable, submit your CV anyway.

SimCorp is on an exciting growth journey, and our Talent Acquisition Team is ready to assist you discover the right role for you. The approximate time to consider your CV is three weeks.

We are eager to continually improve our talent acquisition process and make everyone’s experience positive and valuable. Therefore, during the process we will ask you to provide your feedback, which is highly appreciated.

**Who We Are

**For over 50 years, we have worked closely with investment and asset managers to become the world’s leading provider of integrated investment management solutions. We are 4,000+ colleagues with a broad range of nationalities, educations, professional experiences, ages, and backgrounds.

SimCorp is an independent subsidiary of the Deutsche Börse Group. Following the recent merger with Axioma, we leverage the combined strength of our brands to provide an industry-leading, full, front-to-back offering for our clients.

SimCorp is an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, without regard to race, gender, age, disability, or any other protected status under applicable law. We are committed to building a culture where diverse perspectives and expertise are integrated into our everyday work. We believe in the continual growth and development of our employees, so that we can provide best-in-class solutions to our clients.

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

The Role

We’re looking for a proactive and curious student worker to join our Public Affairs Europe team. This is a unique opportunity to step into a highly visible role where personality, initiative, and strong interpersonal skills matter just as much as experience. In this role, you will support political engagement across multiple European markets, stakeholder coordination, and the operational excellence that makes strategic work possible.

You will gain direct exposure to a leading oncology biotech’s European policy landscape, develop insight into pharmaceutical policy and political strategy, and experience the dynamics of multi-market stakeholder engagement. At the same time, you will build hands-on experience in vendor management, procurement processes, and contract administration.

We are a small and agile team in Europe, currently the only Public Affairs presence in the region, working closely with colleagues in the US and across markets. This role is ideal for someone who is a self-starter, confident in sharing ideas, and not afraid to speak up. You enjoy working with others, building relationships, and navigating different stakeholders with empathy and strong communication skills. We offer flexibility around exams and study schedules, and an inclusive, supportive team environment where you are encouraged to grow and contribute from day one. Intended start date: 1 / 15 May.

Help us get to know you by submitting a comprehensive application, including your CV and motivational letter!

Responsibilities

Public Affairs

• Helping the team stay on top of political developments and initiatives across Europe.

• Supporting contact with different stakeholders like governments, patient organisations, and health authorities.

• Assisting in organising meetings and roundtables with external partners across European markets.

• Helping prepare clear and simple summaries, briefings, and communication materials.

• Supporting the organisation of events and conferences.

Operations & Administration

• Assisting with setting up and managing suppliers (vendors)

• Helping out with day-to-day administrative tasks where needed

• Supporting budget tracking and keeping an overview of costs

• Assisting with purchase orders and procurement processes

• Helping manage contracts and agreements

Requirements

• Actively enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s program with approximately 2 years remaining before graduation.

• Based in Denmark, with a background in Political Science, Business, Public Health, Communications, or a related social science.

• Motivated by both political engagement and high-quality administrative execution.

• Highly organized, detail-oriented, and self-directed.

• Comfortable working with spreadsheets and managing processes efficiently.

• Fluent in English, both written and spoken, as it's Genmab's primary language.

• Available for approximately 20 hours per week.

About You

• You are genuinely passionate about our purpose

• You bring precision and excellence to all that you do

• You believe in our rooted-in-science approach to problem-solving

• You are a generous collaborator who can work in teams with a broad spectrum of backgrounds

• You take pride in enabling the best work of others on the team

• You can grapple with the unknown and be innovative

• You have experience working in a fast-growing, dynamic company (or a strong desire to)

• You work hard and are not afraid to have a little fun while you do so!

Locations

Genmab maximizes the efficiency of an agile working environment, when possible, for the betterment of employee work-life balance. Our offices are crafted as open, community-based spaces that work to connect employees while being immersed in our powerful laboratories. Whether you’re in one of our office spaces or working remotely, we thrive on connecting with each other to innovate.

About Genmab

Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

About Us

Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose guiding its unstoppable team to strive towards improving the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For more than 20 years, its passionate, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and leveraged translational research and data sciences, which has resulted in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators, effector function enhanced antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates. To help develop and deliver novel antibody therapies to patients, Genmab has formed 20+ strategic partnerships with biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO™) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with locations in Utrecht, the Netherlands, Princeton, New Jersey, U.S. and Tokyo, Japan.

Are you passionate about recruitment and eager to gain hands-on experience in the field of People and Culture? Do you want to enhance your skills in recruitment while fostering employee engagement and well-being? Are you ready to join an international green-tech company where your ideas can truly make a difference for people?

Here is what your role entails

During your internship, you will play an important role in driving a people-focused recruitment process and ensuring a great experience for every candidate. Additionally, you will have the opportunity to explore other areas within People & Culture, based on your interests and career aspirations.

More specifically, you will be:

• Partnering with hiring managers throughout the recruitment process from A-Z

• Taking ownership of the for recruiting new the Interns for the Spring semester of 2027

• Conducting qualitative and quantitative surveys and providing the P&C with data-based insights

• Supporting onboarding activities, and helping create engaging internship experience in social events and courses throughout the internship program

You will experience the freedom to explore your interests and take ownership of your own projects, giving you valuable insight into how People & Culture works in practice. With a thorough onboarding and continuous guidance from your mentor, we will support you throughout your entire internship.

Meet your future team

In this role you will become a part of our P&C Global Excellence & Operations team consisting of 16 talented colleagues. We are a tight-knit group working collaboratively to attract and hire candidates while ensuring the smooth operation of our global P&C processes. You will be part of a skilled, dynamic, and diverse team that values personal development, initiative, and collaboration, supporting each other to bring out the best in both the team and the organization.

Did you know? We have a previous Danish champion in Pétanque on our team, and 6 of us started our journey in Kamstrup as Interns.

Less about us, more about you

We are looking for an Intern who is ready to contribute to Kamstrup’s recruitment efforts and help drive our global recruitment and P&C initiatives. You may not have much experience yet, but the most important thing is that you are motivated to make your mark within our people operations.

In order to succeed, we imagine that you:

• Are studying a master´s degree in Business Administration, Psychology, Educational Science or another relevant field

• Thrive in a communicating role, enabling you to establish good professional collaborations

• Have a structured and analytical approach to your work

• Can work independently, and like having responsibility for your own tasks

• Are curious and eager to learn, and bring a positive mindset to new challenges and collaborations

As we are an international organisation it is important that you are fluent in English and Danish.

Whilst you may not meet all the qualifications listed above, this is an internship position, and we value curiosity and a willingness to learn just as much as experience. If the role interests you and you are motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply.

We offer more than just an internship

At Kamstrup, your contribution as an intern is highly valued, and we cherish the good colleagueship. Therefore, you will experience an internship with a strong focus on your individual development through challenging tasks, career sparring, voluntary courses, as well as social events and a large network. We are proud, that our internship program has resulted in Studenterhus Aarhus granting us with the Mentor Award, the Internationalization Award, the Jury’s Special Award and the award for East Jutland’s Best Internship.

Besides the best program, we also offer:

• A gratuity which may be provided in recognition of your efforts if your place of study allows it as well as paid public transportation to and from work

• Multiple internship events and weekly internship lunches

• Employee benefits including a healthy canteen, fitness facilities, in-house dental clinic, hairdresser, and a free health clinic

• An active employee association, that fosters a collaborative and supportive workplace community

Do you want to be a part of Kamstrup?

The applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, but you can expect a response within six weeks. Any details about the internship will be individually agreed upon. However, the internship is expected to run from the beginning of February 2027 until the end of June 2027.

Kamstrup is located in Stilling south of Aarhus, and bus number 200 takes you right to the door.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact People Consultant, Emma Bak Andersen, on telephone nr.: +45 89 93 10 00.

Internship Duration: 2 February 2027 to 25 June 2027

Do you want to work for an Architectural Firm with sustainability at the heart of its strategy? Can you contribute with solutions from your academic studies? Are you currently studying to be an Construction Architecture (Bygningskonstruktør)? Then, join us to shape a sustainable and liveable world.

About us

Arkitema was established in 1969 making us one of Denmark's oldest architectural firms. Today, we are well positioned in Scandinavia with offices in Denmark, Norway and Sweden.

In our markets we provide wide range of competencies in our areas of expertise. We cover sectors and disciplines like healthcare, industry, transformation, landscape and residential construction.

Since 2019 Arkitema has been part of COWI, one of Scandinavia’s leading engineering and consultancy companies. Together with customers, partners and colleagues, we shape a future where people and societies grow and flourish. We do that by co-creating more sustainable and beautiful solutions that improve the quality of life for people today and many generations ahead.

Create Solutions that will enable a better tomorrow

As an intern at Arkitema, you will be part of a design team in one of Scandinavia's largest and leading architectural firms, where you will work with experienced architects, construction architects, urban planners and engineers to solve a wide range of professionally relevant tasks.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• To use your academic knowledge of technical fundamentals to contribute to our projects

• Gain valuable experience in the field of architecture and construction

Also, you will be included in a team and assigned an experienced colleague as a mentor who will guide you throughout your internship. We carry out architecture primarily throughout the Nordic region but also other parts of the world within the areas of; Housing, Learning, Business, Health, Urban, Culture and Infrastructure. Therefore, our assignments range from small preservation-worthy residential neighborhoods to complex super hospitals, bridges and cultural centers.

As an intern, you will have the opportunity to be involved in drawing the first lines, registering old building masses, supervising construction sites on ongoing projects, or modeling and detailing the many complex buildings. Our professional span will give you a broad understanding of the design profession and in-depth knowledge of the workflows in the construction industry.

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

The first step to success in this role is that you are eager to collaborate with the people around you, whether they are colleagues, partners, or customers. Developing ties with others is something you do by acting respectfully and delivering on your promises. And you never get set in your ways but keep exploring new insights and ways to improve.

On top of that, you’ll have:

• Actively pursuing a bachelor’s degree in architectural technology and construction management (Bygningskonstruktør)

• Have good problem-solving skills

• Be a creative and technical thinker

• Be able to demonstrate evidence of research and information gathering skills

Professional development

We strive to develop talented interns who graduate with a high level of professional skills. As part of the internship at Arkitema, there are ongoing presentations where our own specialists share their experience and best practices in topics such as:

• Sustainability, materials & reuse

• BIM, Revit, design & sketching

• Client consultancy & tendering

• Restoration & building preservation

• Competitions & visualizations

• Descriptions & quality assurance

• Urban Planning

These topics represent important knowledge and practical insights that will ensure you stand stronger in your future career.

A place to work and so much more

At Arkitema, we work together with our customers to shape sustainable and customized solutions. By making use of our collective knowledge and curiosity, we create opportunities that contribute to good solutions for a future with ever-changing needs.

We want to develop an environment where curiosity, belonging and good chemistry are in focus.

For us, it is important that the people we share everyday work with are allowed to be themselves, precisely because it is what brings out the best in you and those around us, both at work and at home.

Got more questions?

If you have any unanswered questions about the role, please reach out Jacob Faaborg-Simonsen – jafs@arkitema.com for Aarhus/Aalborg and Adrian Balch Petersen – adpn@arkitema.com for Copenhagen.

Get to know us even better at our website, Arkitema where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at Arkitema.

Diversity is fundamental to Arkitema, inclusion is key.

We focus on creating a respectful and fair work environment where all employees have a sense of belonging and equal opportunities to thrive and grow. We ensure that our leaders are role models for inclusive leadership by cultivating a culture where diverse perspectives and thoughts are considered valuable. We also take diversity and inclusion into account in all relevant decisions and processes when we put together teams and forums. We do it because it is part of our values and because it is simply the right thing to do.

NOTE

Kindly submit your CV, Cover Letter, and Portfolio. As only two attachment fields are available on the application page, please combine files where needed and upload them accordingly.

We only accept applications from active students who have not already completed an internship within their studies.

Do you want to play a key role in some of Denmark’s largest and most complex energy infrastructure projects? Are you an experienced planner who creates structure, transparency, and progress in complex projects? Then join us at COWI and help shape the future of sustainable energy infrastructure.

Become a vital part of our Energy team

As a Senior Planner, you will play a key role in planning and delivering large and complex energy and infrastructure projects. In this role, you will work at Energinet as part of a COWI team supporting some of Energinet’s important projects. You will take ownership of project schedules and work closely with project managers, technical specialists, contractors and suppliers to create transparency, manage dependencies and risks, and keep projects moving forward.

Furthermore, you will support projects throughout their lifecircle – from early development and design through tendering and execution. Beyond maintaining schedules, you will function as a trusted sparring partner to project management, using planning and schedule analysis to support informed decision-making, identify challenges and drive corrective actions. Through your work at Energinet, you will gain the opportunity to contribute directly to projects that are central to Denmark’s energy infrastructure and green transition.

Your official COWI office location will be either Lyngby, Vejle or Aarhus. However, your primary workplace will be at Energinet in Erritsø, but Ballerup could also be an option, with some travel to Erritsø. You will report to Head of Discipline, Ioana Nicoleta Tuglui, who is based at COWI's headquarter in Lyngby.

Your key responsibilities

As a Senior Planner, you will:

• Develop, maintain, and optimise integrated project schedules using Primavera OPC and MS Project.

• Monitor project progress together with project managers and technical leads, identify deviations and support corrective actions.

• Identify and manage critical paths, dependencies, interfaces, and schedule risks across project activities.

• Perform baseline management, what-if analyses and schedule risk assessments.

• Review and validate schedules from contractors, suppliers, and other project partners.

• Prepare clear progress and status reports, providing transparency on milestones, risks, dependencies, and deviations.

• Ensure schedules support effective progress, risk, and resource management.

• Contribute to the development and implementation of robust planning methodologies, processes, and tools across our projects.

• Provide planning expertise and constructive challenge to project management and project teams.

Your skills. Our team. Together, we design the future.

You are an experienced and proactive planner who is comfortable taking ownership of complex project schedules. You understand that good planning is about more than maintaining a programme – you use the schedule to create transparency, challenge assumptions, identify risks and support project management in making informed decisions.

You enjoy working across disciplines and are confident engaging with project managers, technical specialists, customers, contractors, and suppliers. You bring a structured and analytical approach while being able to communicate complex information in a clear and practical way.

On top of that, you will have:

• Extensive experience in project planning and project controls, preferably from large and complex energy, infrastructure, construction, or engineering projects.

• Strong experience developing, managing, and integrating complex project schedules.

• Strong working knowledge of Primavera and MS Project. Primavera OPC experience is a requirement.

• Experience with progress monitoring, critical path analysis, baseline management, schedule risk assessments and what-if analysis.

• Experience reviewing and validating contractor and supplier schedules.

• Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to turn complex schedule information into clear and actionable decision support.

• Excellent oral and written Danish skills.

Experience from major energy infrastructure, transmission, utilities or other large-scale construction projects in Denmark will be a strong advantage.

A place to work and so much more

At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility, and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide for our customers. We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home.

With offices primarily located in Scandinavia, the UK, North America, and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy, and environment into play.

Got more questions?

If you have any unanswered questions about the role or what we have to offer, please reach out to Senior Global Talent Acquisition Specialist Mette Gutte at mtgt@cowi.com or Head of Discipline, Ioana Nicoleta Tuglui at iatu@cowi.com

Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

Diversity is fundamental to COWI, inclusion is key.

We are committed to creating a respectful and fair work environment where all employees have a sense of belonging and equitable opportunities to thrive and grow. We ensure that our leaders are role models for inclusive leadership by cultivating a culture where diverse perspectives and thoughts are seen as strengths. And we take diversity and inclusion into account in all relevant decisions and processes and when setting up teams and fora. We do it because it’s a part of our values and because it’s simply the right thing to do.

Before you apply

All you need to include in your application is your CV - no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture. We will be conducting interviews on an ongoing basis.

jobs.occupation: Internship in Embedded Software Development for Electricity Meters
jobs.description:
Do you have a passion for software programming and are you up for new challenges? Would you like to be part of developing the future’s electricity meters for automated reading systems? Are you interested in an exciting and educational internship at an international green-tech company?

Here is what the job entails

During this internship you will become a part of a Scrum team working with embedded software for electricity meters, as well as the scripts and tools that tie the development process together. Your daily task includes improving and extending automated test software, maintaining test setups based on Raspberry Pi, and participating in proof-of-concept development projects.

The specific content of the tasks will be planned together with you based on your preferences, interests, and competencies. We work in a range of technical disciplines, but some tools you might be using are:

• Python

• Programmering i C

• C#

• GIT

• Automatic software test

• DevOps

Meet your future team

As an intern in Embedded Software Development - Electricity Meters, you’ll become an integral part of our meter development department. This department designs and maintains hardware and software for our metering systems. You will join a team of 8 skilled development engineers, all with a background in firmware development and testing. Collaboration is a key focus, and close interaction with experienced colleagues provides ample opportunities for daily discussions, professional growth, and a steep learning curve during your internship.

Did you know? Even though we are colleagues at work, we also value a bit of friendly competition, and we often take that competitive spirit to the padel court together.

Less about us, more about you

**Description

**Factbird helps manufacturers turn real-time production data into decisions they can actually act on. Since 2016, we've helped manufacturers in 28 countries cut waste, boost uptime, and run smarter — from the shop floor to the boardroom. Over 300 companies trust us to make sense of their operations, and we're a team of 80+ people across Copenhagen and the US who care about making complex things simple.

We're creating a new role at the top of our Engineering career ladder: Lead Architect. It's the senior end of our Technical Track — the rung above Tech Lead — and today it's a role we've deliberately left lightly defined, because we want the first person in it to help define it. You'll set Factbird's technical direction: architecture, tooling, and the multi-year technology bets that shape where the product goes next.

This is our most senior technical role, with no direct reports — your authority comes from judgment and track record, not the org chart. You'll work alongside our Tech Leads in Factbird's technical leadership group, partner closely with our Director of Engineering, and be the person other senior engineers go to when a decision is genuinely hard to reverse.

**About the Role

**As Lead Architect, you own Factbird's company-wide technical vision: the architecture our services run on, the tooling and standards our engineers use every day, and the multi-year technology strategy that ties it all together. You make — or sign off on — the high-stakes, hard-to-reverse architecture calls, and you're accountable for getting them right with the full context of where the business is headed, not just where the code is today.

You'll work across a team built on Rust, React, Node.js, and AWS, with AI-assisted development already a core part of how we ship. Some of what this role owns is already well-defined — reviewing RFCs, stewarding language and platform standards, setting the team's AI-tooling strategy. Some of it isn't yet: Factbird is still a growing company, and part of the job is helping us figure out what technical leadership at this level should look like as we scale.

You'll thrive here if you'd rather be trusted with genuinely hard calls than manage a team, and if you can hold both the technical detail and the commercial context — cost, risk, market direction — well enough to make a technology bet you can still defend a year later.

**

What you'll do

**Architecture & technical strategy

• Own Factbird's multi-year technology strategy, and make the high-stakes architecture calls that are hard to reverse — with cost, risk, and business context factored in, not just engineering elegance

• Author and drive major RFCs from proposal through to an actual decision, and review the highest-risk architecture changes across the team

• Act as steward for our core languages and frameworks — setting standards, library choices, and the platform's overall shape

• Make build-vs-buy calls for new technical capabilities, and bring a clear point of view on emerging technologies worth adopting

• Define the observability, reliability, and security posture the platform is held to

**

Tooling & standards**

• Set the team's technical tooling and platform standards, and keep them evolving as the stack and the company grow

• Define Factbird's strategy for AI-assisted development — which tools we adopt, how we balance velocity against code quality, security, and IP risk, and where we draw the line

• Shape engineering-wide quality philosophy and help set the technical bar used in hiring interviews

• Help define shared components and reference architecture that other engineers build on, rather than reinvent

• Give input into technical org design and team topology as Engineering scales

**

Technical leadership & mentorship**

• Act as the trusted technical advisor to our Director of Engineering and the technical leadership group, partnering with Tech Leads and Product Leads on cross-team alignment

• Mentor senior engineers and Tech Leads toward architect-level thinking, without formal ownership of their people management

• Communicate technical vision and trade-offs clearly to non-technical stakeholders, including leadership

• Identify technical risks to the business early, and say so before they become expensive

• Represent Factbird's technical thinking externally where it makes sense — a talk, a blog post, an open-source contribution — though this isn't a requirement on day one

**What we’re looking for

**We're looking for someone who's already earned this kind of trust somewhere else — someone whose technical opinions carry weight because they're right more often than not, and who'd rather solve the interesting, ambiguous problem than manage the team solving it.

**

The ideal background**

• 8+ years of hands-on engineering experience, including real time spent as an architect or equivalent senior technical authority, not just a senior engineer with a bigger title

• A track record of owning multi-year technology strategy or platform architecture decisions that other teams had to live with — and that held up

• Has led major RFCs or architecture proposals cross-team, through genuine pushback, to an actual decision

• Comfortable making build-vs-buy and technology-adoption calls that account for cost, risk, and where the market is heading, not just what's technically interesting

• Experience mentoring senior engineers or Tech Leads toward architect-level thinking, without needing formal authority to do it

• Practical, current experience with AI-assisted development, and a clear point of view on where it genuinely helps versus where it creates risk

**Why Factbird?

**People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

**

Here's what you can look forward to:**

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn't one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Thoughtful, human onboarding: We'll support you step by step, giving you the context, tools, and guidance you need to feel confident from day one.

• A career path that grows with you: Through bi-yearly Individual Development Plan conversations, we'll work together to shape a career journey that fits your ambitions.

• Company-wide gatherings & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what's next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We're proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.

**

We'd love to hear from you

**If this role feels like a match, we'd be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit — feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Composite Process Engineer for FirePoint Rocket Technology – Denmark

FirePoint Rocket Technology (FPRT) is building one of the most unique and strategically important industrial projects in Denmark – a brand new production facility for solid rocket propellant and advanced defense-tech components. Our ambition is significant: we are scaling from the early operational phase to 300+ employees within the next 18 months.

By joining our team now, you will become part of the core team shaping a new high-tech, safety-critical production environment from the ground up. We are looking for a Composite Process Engineer who will ensure that our composite manufacturing processes are safe, stable, repeatable, and ready for serial production. You will report directly to our Senior Composite Process Technology Manager and collaborate closely with Production, Quality, Materials, HSE, and Maintenance.

Duties and Responsibilities

• Translate composite technology and material requirements into practical production parameters, SOPs, and work instructions.

• Own day-to-day process stability by monitoring variation, investigating deviations, and defining corrective actions.

• Prepare and verify process readiness prior to production runs, including equipment settings, tooling, and environmental requirements.

• Lead and support technical trials, pilot builds, process prove-outs, and qualification activities.

• Support the commissioning and validation of production equipment, tooling, ovens, curing systems, and machining equipment.

• Drive continuous process improvement to reduce variability, scrap, cycle times, and material loss.

• Manage technical change control for changes to process parameters, tooling, equipment, or manufacturing methods.

Qualifications and Competencies

Professional and Operational Skills

• Degree in Engineering (BSc or MSc) in Materials, Mechanical, Chemical, Manufacturing, Composite Engineering, or equivalent strong industrial experience.

• 3–5+ years of experience in composite manufacturing, process engineering, or materials engineering.

• Practical experience with fiber-reinforced composites and thermoset resin-based processes (epoxy experience is highly desirable).

• Hands-on experience with processes such as resin infusion/transfer, filament winding, lay-up, prepreg, molding, curing, or composite machining/finishing.

• Proven experience creating or improving SOPs, work instructions, and manufacturing standards.

• Background in industrialization, production ramp-up, technology transfer, or process stabilization.

• Professional English language skills are a requirement; Danish language skills are considered an advantage.

Personal Attributes

• A hands-on, highly structured, and solution-oriented approach to your tasks.

• Strong problem-solving skills with a mindset for root-cause analysis (e.g., FMEA, 5 Whys).

• Ability to work close to shop-floor operations and maintain a clear overview under ramp-up pressure.

The Ideal Candidate

We are seeking a proactive engineer who combines strong technical capabilities with a practical understanding of production. You thrive on being close to the shop floor, working with operators to ensure that process standards are practical, understood, and followed. You are motivated by establishing structure and stability in a dynamic Greenfield environment, and you maintain a clear perspective—even when working under tight deadlines in an accelerating growth phase.

Why Apply for This Position

At FPRT, you are offered a rare career opportunity to shape one of Denmark's most unique industrial and defense-tech projects. You will take on a central role with real impact, where your expertise directly determines the integrity and manufacturability of safety-critical products. We provide a professional, international environment with a flat structure, high autonomy, and a clear mission. Additionally, we offer top-of-market compensation and modern office facilities including an on-site gym and sauna.

jobs.description:
Product Manager – Notifications | Help Dalux Users Focus on What Matters

Construction projects generate an enormous amount of information. Files change. Tasks are assigned. Deadlines approach. Comments are added. Reviews require action. Issues are reported. People are mentioned. Workflows progress. But more information does not necessarily make people better informed.

Dalux is looking for a Product Manager to take dedicated ownership of Notifications and help us answer a deceptively difficult product question:

How do we make sure users know what requires their attention – without overwhelming them with information?

Notifications exist throughout our products today, across email, mobile, and in-product experiences. As Dalux has grown, so has their complexity. We believe this area deserves dedicated product ownership and a coherent strategy across our products.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Notification Strategy: Define a coherent product direction for how Dalux communicates important events and required actions to users.

• Product Discovery: Understand when users need to be informed, when they need to take action, and when a notification simply creates unnecessary noise.

• Customer Insights: Research how different users manage information and attention across complex projects and busy working days.

• Cross-product Ownership: Map and improve notification experiences across Dalux products rather than optimizing individual notifications in isolation.

• Channels & Preferences: Develop experiences spanning in-app notifications, email, mobile push, notification preferences, subscriptions, following, mentions, reminders, and digests.

• Relevance & Prioritization: Explore grouping, prioritization, timing, and deduplication to ensure important information stands out.

• Actionability: Make notifications useful by ensuring users understand why they received them, what has changed, and what action they should take.

• Product Analytics: Use quantitative and qualitative insights to understand which notifications create value and which create noise.

• Shared Capabilities: Work with Development and other Product Managers to create common notification principles and platform capabilities that can be reused across Dalux.

About You

You probably don't currently have "Notifications Product Manager" as your job title – and that's perfectly fine.

We're looking for an experienced Product Manager who finds the underlying problem interesting and has the product and systems thinking required to solve it.

We believe you:

• Have strong Product Management experience, preferably from B2B SaaS, collaboration, productivity, workflow, communication, or similar software.

• Have excellent product discovery and UX instincts.

• Think systematically and can turn many individual use cases into coherent product concepts.

• Understand the tension between keeping users informed and creating notification fatigue.

• Are comfortable owning a horizontal capability spanning multiple products and development teams.

• Can combine user research with product analytics to understand behavior.

• Care about interaction details and understand how seemingly small product decisions can have a large cumulative impact on user experience.

• Can simplify complex systems involving events, recipients, relevance, timing, preferences, and communication channels.

• Communicate fluently in English, written and spoken.

Construction Technology Experience Is Welcome But Not Required .

Experience from collaboration, communication, workflow, or productivity software would be particularly relevant.

What To Expect At Dalux

At Dalux, you'll join a product-driven company where ideas quickly become reality and where you'll have a direct impact on the products we build.

We offer:

• A collaborative and informal work environment with flat hierarchies

• High ownership, trust, and the freedom to drive initiatives

• Talented and dedicated colleagues in an international team

• A central Copenhagen office, flexible work hours, and no dress code

• Monthly social events and an active community

• Attractive benefits including health insurance, lunch, fitness facilities, and free parking

• Opportunities for professional growth and development

Ready for the next step?

We are reviewing applications on an ongoing basis, so please submit your resume and application as soon as possible.

About Dalux

Founded in 2005, Dalux is a Danish Contech company revolutionizing the construction industry with innovative software built on geometric processing and 3D computer graphics.

Over the past years, we’ve grown by 40% annually and now have over 900 employees across 50+ offices in more than 25 countries. All product development takes place in our Østerbro, Copenhagen office, where we focus on building the future of construction technology. We place great value on our strong social community and close collaboration with colleagues, which is why we primarily work from our Copenhagen location.

Application deadline:

As soon as possible
