jobs.occupation: Senior Frontend Engineer - with an interest in fullstack
jobs.description:
About Cardlay
Cardlay is a Danish fintech building white-label card and spend management solutions. Banks, issuers and financial partners in Europe and the US offer our platform to their business customers using their own brand.

We are a small dedicated team with short decision paths. We make bold decisions, turn them into results by helping each other, and give people the mandate to own what they build.
About the job
Our web portal is where companies run their spend: cards, expenses, accounting and people management. Every bank offers it under its own brand.

Some of the core capabilities include

• Cards: card programs, card orders and requests, and funding accounts
• Expenses: transactions, receipts, mileages and expense policies
• Accounting: categories, cost dimensions, GL accounts and exports to external accounting systems
• People and teams: onboarding, invitations, roles and company settings
Under the hood, it's React, TypeScript, pnpm workspaces and Vite.

Every new bank brings its own brand and requirements, and AI agents now write a growing share of our code. We need a senior engineer who builds the product and keeps the shared components and patterns behind them consistent, so new screens, whether built by people or AI agents, look and work like the rest of the product.

This is a hands-on product role with significant ownership: you will build features every day and help set our frontend direction.

What success looks like after a year

• Customers use features you built and shipped end to end
• A new feature takes less code and fewer review rounds than it does today
• New screens are built from shared components by default, by people and AI agents alike
• The core libraries are up to date with latest security updates and we are on a clear upgrade path going forward
The challenge

Customers rely on the platform every day, and it has grown over several years:

• Some pages use our new design system and some don't yet. Deciding what to migrate, and when, to keep the experience consistent is ongoing work
• You work closely with our UI/UX Lead. That takes the confidence to push back on designs that hurt the user experience, and the taste to know when you're right
• There are several ways of handling data and state in the codebase, and picking the right one for each case directly affects what customers experience
• We're a small team, and other developers contribute a lot to the web portal. As the senior frontend engineer, you decide what's good enough to merge and where our code style and stack go next
• You look beyond your own domain. When the answer is on the other side of the API, you read the backend code and unblock yourself where you canWhat you'll do
As a Senior Frontend Engineer, you will own the frontend of our web portal. You take responsibility for what we ship, make decisions others can build on, drive projects forward and help the people around you grow.

You will be the primary frontend engineer in an engineering team of 10 people across frontend, backend, mobile and DevOps. You will work closely with Product and our UI/UX Lead, and report to our Head of Engineering.

Your responsibilities will include

• Take responsibility for the frontend as a whole: its quality, performance and direction
• Make the key frontend decisions and stand by them: architecture, what goes into the design system and when to say no
• Drive projects from idea to production with Product and our UI/UX Lead, and own them until customers are using them
• Build reusable components and patterns as part of your product work, not one-off solutions
• Move legacy screens onto the design system as you work on them, without silent visual regressions
• Set up component APIs, lint rules and docs so AI agents produce code that fits
• Mentor other engineers and share what you know through reviews, docs and pairingWho you are
We are looking for an experienced frontend engineer who loves building a product and cares about the quality and consistency behind it.

You likely bring

• Deep experience with React and TypeScript
• You have shipped complex features in a web product that customers rely on
• You use AI coding tools every day and know where they go wrong
• A good eye for UX and product quality
• You speak up when something could be done better, and you see your work through to production
• You have driven projects with other engineers and helped them grow through mentoring and reviews
Bonus if you have

• Experience building component libraries or design systems
• Design tokens or white-label theming
• Interest in fullstack work, so you can help out on the backend when you can
• Experience from fintech or complex B2B products
You will work with the technologies below. We don't expect experience with all of them; we are looking for engineers who learn quickly.

• React, TypeScript
• Vite, pnpm workspaces, Biome
• MUI, styled-components, Storybook
• TanStack Query, TanStack Table, Redux Toolkit
• React Hook Form, react-intl
• Vitest, MSW, CypressWhy Cardlay
You will join at a point where our platform is proven, our customer base is growing and AI is changing how we build software. You will have a real say in how Cardlay builds the frontend, in a team where senior engineers set the direction.

• Permanent employment, freelance or consultancy, with salary or rate matching experience
• Hybrid work from our offices in Copenhagen or Odense
• English as our main working language, with Danish spoken too. You don't need to speak Danish to join
• Flexible working hours, and the option to work from home when it suits you and the team
• Company-paid phone and home internet
• Lunch, coffee, fruit, drinks and snacks at the officeHow to apply
Go ahead and hit "apply" and upload your résumé, application and other relevant information through our HR system.

Any questions about the position can be directed to our Head of Engineering:

Magnus Biolzi Hansen, Mail: mbh@cardlay.com, Telephone: +45 42 28 62 42

Application deadline: We review applications as they come in and will close the position once we've found the right person.

This is your opportunity to join an international group on an exciting transformation journey and play a key role in shaping the tax agenda at operational level.

We are looking for a Direct Tax Manager to join our Global Tax team. You will report directly to the Head of Global Tax and become part of a highly skilled team of colleagues covering Direct Tax, Transfer Pricing and Indirect Tax.

You are most likely a technically strong tax professional with a hands on approach. You will have a broad operational responsibility with a strong focus on Danish corporate income tax within a joint taxation group, Direct Tax across the group and an interest in tax digitalisation.

Your Role And Responsibilities

As Tax Manager, you will work closely with the Head of Global Tax, other team members and internal stakeholders across finance and the business. Your main responsibilities will include:

• Responsibility for Danish corporate income tax compliance, including joint taxation (sambeskatning)

• Preparation and review of tax calculations and tax returns

• Participation in dialogue with tax authorities, including audits and enquiries

• Monitoring tax legislation and assessing impacts on the group

• Contributing to process optimisation, automation, digitalisation and development of tax governance

• Acting as a sparring partner to finance functions and other stakeholders in the organisation

• Contribution to transfer pricing compliance and documentation

• Contribution to Pillar Two compliance

The role combines technical depth with practical execution, and you will have significant exposure to both national and international tax matters.

Your profile

We are looking for a strong tax professional who thrives in a collaborative environment.

You Likely Have

• A bachelor’s or master’s degree within Tax, Accounting, Finance or a related field

• Solid experience with Danish corporate income tax, including joint taxation

• Experience with tax reconciliations, including reconciliation between tax calculations, tax reporting and financial accounts

• Knowledge of cooperative taxation (andelsbeskatning) is considered an advantage

• Experience working with multinational organisations and shared service centers is considered an advantage

• A structured and analytical mindset with attention to detail

• The ability to work independently while being a strong team player

• Strong communication skills and the ability to explain complex tax matters clearly

• Fluent in Danish and English (written and spoken).

The team and working environment

You will join a dedicated Global Tax team with high professional standards and a pragmatic, solution oriented mindset. We work closely together across tax disciplines and value trust, openness and knowledge sharing.

The position is based at our office in Randers, offering flexible working conditions.

Why join us?

We offer an exciting and visible role in a complex international group undergoing transformation.

You Will Have The Opportunity To

• Work with a broad tax scope and real business impact

• Develop your technical and professional skills in close collaboration with experienced colleagues

• Being part of a company that values trust, openness and personal development

• Enjoy attractive employment conditions, including a competitive salary, pension and health insurance

Interested?

If you are motivated by responsibility, complexity and collaboration, we would be pleased to hear from you. If you have any questions about the role, please contact Director, Head of Global Tax, Merete Rousing Glob at +45 41 15 55 10.

Please submit your application and CV as soon as possible.

We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.description:
Would you like to combine your engineering studies with practical experience in project management and learn how technical solutions and business priorities come together?

At Gram Equipment, we develop and deliver equipment for industrial ice cream production worldwide. We are looking for an engineering student to join our Project Management team in Kolding, either as an intern or a student worker.

You will work alongside experienced colleagues and gain insight into how we coordinate projects, from technical requirements and planning to delivery. Along the way, you will learn how mechanical solutions, customer expectations, budgets and deadlines influence project decisions.

What you will be doing
You will support our project managers in their daily work, with tasks adapted to your skills, interests and study requirements. Your tasks may include:

• Supporting project planning and following up on milestones, deadlines and outstanding actions.
• Preparing and updating project documentation, status reports and meeting materials.
• Participating in project meetings and following up on agreed actions.

jobs.description:
We are extra[not]ordinary

*(ex· tra· not· or· di· nary |\ ik-ˈstr-not-ȯr-də-ˌner-ē)

Adjective: A unique word for Genmab meaning to go way beyond what is

usual; to be remarkable; proudly unique and authentic

Back to search results

Previous job Next job

JOB DESCRIPTION

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

The Role

Genmab is searching for an energized Senior Associate to be part of Global Clinical Supply Manufacturing in Copenhagen within commute distance from our office locations to work according to your hybrid work arrangement.

With an impressive pipeline and many ongoing clinical trials, you will have a central role in supporting inspection readiness across our late-stage clinical development portfolio. Your work will help ensure that documentation is complete, compliant and readily available to support the successful execution of business-critical GMP and GCP inspections.

You will support inspection readiness activities within Global Clinical Supply, collecting, organizing and performing completeness and compliance checks of trial-specific documentation. During inspections, you will participate in back-office activities and help ensure timely retrieval and follow-up of requested information.

The role also offers an opportunity to develop beyond inspection readiness. You will work closely with the Head of Global Clinical Supply Manufacturing and support selected functional initiatives, providing exposure to broader activities across the organization and our CMO and vendor network. In parallel, you will have the opportunity to build your GMP and clinical supply knowledge by learning and supporting selected operational activities related to outsourced packaging and labelling of IMP and AxMP.

The position reports to the Director, Head of Global Clinical Supply Manufacturing based in Copenhagen.

Responsibilities

• Support inspection readiness across late-stage clinical trials by collecting, organizing and maintaining relevant clinical supply documentation.

• Perform completeness and compliance checks of trial-specific documentation against applicable procedures and inspection-readiness expectations.

• Participate in back-office activities during GMP and GCP inspections, including document retrieval, request coordination and tracking of responses and follow-up items.

• Support preparation for mock inspections, audits and health authority inspections, including compilation and review of supporting documentation for completeness and readiness.

• Support the Head of Global Clinical Supply Manufacturing with selected functional initiatives and tasks across the organization.

• Support activities related to our external CMO and vendor network, including coordination, follow-up and preparation of relevant material and documentation.

• Build knowledge of GMP and clinical supply activities within Global Clinical Supply Manufacturing and learn and support selected operational tasks related to outsourced packaging and labelling of IMP and AxMP.

• Participate in maintenance and continuous improvement of procedures, tools and ways of working supporting inspection readiness and clinical supply activities.

• Responsible to be compliant with Genmab´s quality system.

Requirements

• Minimum a bachelor’s degree or equivalent.

• Some experience working with documentation, quality or compliance activities in the pharmaceutical, biotech, clinical research or another regulated environment is an advantage.

• Knowledge and understanding of GMP and GCP; experience with inspection or audit readiness is an advantage.

• Strong interest in documentation, quality and compliance, with a structured and detail-oriented approach to your work.

• Ability to coordinate activities, maintain structure and follow up on actions involving multiple stakeholders.

• Ability to work successfully under pressure in a fast-paced environment and with tight timelines, including during inspections.

• Ability to be proactive, enthusiastic, curious and goal orientated, with a willingness to learn new GMP-related activities.

• A team player with demonstrated ability to work effectively with internal and external stakeholders, including CMOs and vendors.

• Strong communication skills in English - both oral and written.

The Team

You will be part of a highly competent team focused on GMP applicable to packaging and labelling of supplies for clinical trials, with a strong focus on quality, inspection readiness and successful collaboration with our internal stakeholders and CMOs.

Together with Global Clinical Supply Portfolio & Project Delivery and Global Clinical Supply Systems, the teams make up the Global Clinical Supply department.

We have an international and informal working environment with a high pace, strong one-team spirit and close collaboration across functions.

Application

Has this sparked your interest? Then we encourage you to upload your CV and cover letter including your motivation for this position. We screen candidates on a continuous basis and call in for interviews.

Fully remote applicants will not be considered, so please indicate if you are willing to relocate if you’re not currently living in commute distance.

The proposed gross annual/hourly base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK544.000,00---816.000,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

About Genmab

Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Besides the best colleagues you could imagine, we also offer:

• Employee benefits including a healthy canteen, fitness facilities, in-house dental clinic, hairdresser, and a free health clinic

• An active employee association that fosters a collaborative and supportive workplace community

• Beneficial health care and insurance package

**Do you want to be a part of Kamstrup?

**Please submit your motivated resume by using the link below. Applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, and you can expect a response within six weeks.

The position is located at Kamstrup's headquarters in Stilling, Denmark, between Aarhus and Skanderborg.

**_Get to know us

_**_At Kamstrup, you'll become part of a close-knit community that genuinely cares about one another, fostering connections both in and out of the workplace. Our team comprises innovators, dreamers, and doers, united by an unyielding passion to challenge the status quo, find better solutions, and constantly push the boundaries of what's possible by being driving by our purpose: We Make What You Measure Matter. With an unwavering commitment to growth, we offer opportunities for you to leverage your skills and drive our business to new heights, empowering you to leave your mark on our future and grow with us.

_Explore more on our website, see our annual report, and stay updated through LinkedIn for the latest news and job openings.

**System Architect (Principal) – Shape the Future of Medical Device Innovation

**Would you like to help drive the transformation from product-centric to platform-centric development in global innovate medtech company?

Then we offer you an opportunity to join a highly skilled R&D environment where collaboration, learning, and innovation go hand in hand. Your role will drive how we work with system architecture, requirements, modularization, and platform building across the organization – while contributing to products that make a difference for our users every day.

day.

At Coloplast, we work every day to improve the lives of people with intimate healthcare needs. And you will play a key role in bringing our strategy to life by helping shape the future of how we develop innovative medical devices.

**Join a team shaping the future of R&D

**You will become part of our Requirements Engineering Team, which forms an essential part of our new Centre of Excellence in R&D, bringing together almost 500 talented colleagues.

In your new team, you will meet 7 colleagues who are global process owners of regulated medical device processes and our system architects driving our large strategic development projects.

Together, we define and improve ways of working across R&D to enable ambitious innovation to reach our users faster through a more structured and scalable development approach.

And of course, we make sure to have fun along the way.

**Lead the development of the System Architecture discipline

**As our new Principal System Architect, you will lead the development of the system architecture discipline and help position it for the future. This means you will lead Coloplast’s journey from developing individual products towards platform building and building up competences within system architecture discipline.

Specifically, you will:

• Lead and support the implementation of platform-based product development and manufacturing process development.

• Strengthen and mature the system architecture discipline by defining and evolving processes, methods, and best practices.

• Contribute to building system architecture capabilities across the organisation through training, sparring, coaching and knowledge sharing.

• Shape and communicate the value of system architecture as part of ongoing transformation initiatives.

• Build alignment across stakeholders in a complex, cross-functional environment by engaging, listening, and creating shared understanding.

• Driving results through colleagues, including other system architects, project managers, program managers and system engineers, in a motivating and engaging way.

• Contribute hands-on to development projects as a trusted architecture resource, working closely with teams to define and deliver system architecture artefacts (e.g. system design, interface specifications, functional analysis and impact analysis)

• Translate inputs from across the business (e.g. commercial, regulatory, manufacturing) into clear and usable system architecture decision and artefacts, ensuring different perspectives are reflected

• Ensure system architecture is effectively integrated with related development disciplines such as requirements engineering, test, and documentation management

**Solid Experience In System Architecture For Physical Product Development

**You are a team player, with strong communication skills and the ability to communicate clearly and concisely as you manage stakeholders across a complex and large organization. Moreover, you have the ability to balance and consider cross-functional concerns in decision-making, and you take a coaching leadership approach to support and develop colleagues and stakeholders.

While experience from the medical device industry is valuable, we also welcome candidates with a strong systems engineering and architecture background from other complex product development industries such as aerospace, defense, industrial automation, robotics, windmill industry or advanced consumer products.

**What We Expect From You

**

• 7+ years of experience in system architecture, preferably for physical products and hardware-based systems, not solely software.

• Strong stakeholder management skills and a proven ability to drive alignment across functions, disciplines, and organizational levels.

• Comfortable working across engineering, product management, quality, regulatory, manufacturing, and other key functions.

• Experience leading or influencing organizational change, including the implementation of new ways of working, processes, or engineering practices.

• Ability to provide technical leadership, coaching, and architectural guidance to teams and stakeholders.

• Extensive hands-on experience with systems engineering for complex products, including system architecture, requirements management, interface management, verification, and validation.

• Proven experience establishing, evolving, and governing system architecture and systems engineering practices.

• Experience with modular architecture, product platforms, and reusable architecture strategies.

• Strong knowledge and practical application of systems engineering principles, methods, and best practices, including recognized industry frameworks such as INCOSE.

• Experience contributing directly to development projects and delivering architecture artefacts from concept through implementation.

• Proven experience operating in regulated product development environments and balancing technical, quality, risk, regulatory, and design control requirements.

• Ability to translate diverse business, user, and technical needs into clear architecture decisions and system-level solutions.

• Strong architectural judgement and ability to balance commercial, technical, regulatory, manufacturing, and user considerations.

• Experience defining system boundaries, interfaces, and reusable architectural building blocks that support platform-based product development.

• Motivated by both shaping long-term architectural direction and contributing to successful day-to-day product delivery.

**You might also bring

**

• Experience from medical device development or other highly regulated industries.

• Knowledge of relevant standards and frameworks such as ISO 13485, ISO 14971, IEC 62304, IEC 62366, or equivalent.

• Understanding manufacturing, industrialization, and production processes, ensuring architectures are scalable, manufacturable, testable, and cost-effective throughout the product lifecycle.

• Experience supporting product strategy through platform thinking, technology roadmaps, and long-term architecture planning.

Please note: Seniority level will be determined based on your experience (principal, senior principal)

jobs.occupation: Deciphering host-pathogen interplay by utilizing biostructure prediction and New Genomic Techniques (NGTs) to engineer durable disease resistance in plants
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Agroecology programme. The position is available from 01 February 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Deciphering host-pathogen interplay by utilizing biostructure prediction and New Genomic Techniques (NGTs) to engineer durable disease resistance in plants

Research area and project description
The Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University is offering a PhD position focused on genetic modification of plants for higher resistance to pathogens. The position is available from 01-02-2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

The PhD is part of the project that aims to develop novel and durable disease resistance in cereals by targeting key protein–protein interactions between plants and pathogens. Using hexaploid wheat (Triticum aestivum) and diploid barley (Hordeum vulgare) as model systems, the project will focus on
powdery mildew disease caused by Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici (Bgt) and B. hordei (Bh).

The PhD student will establish and optimize an AI-based structural biology modelling and prime editing toolbox and apply it to introduce genome modification in vitro culture. These edits are designed to disrupt critical plant-pathogen protein interactions, thereby enhancing disease resistance without relying on classical resistance genes. Computational prediction tools, including AlphaFold-based protein-protein interaction modeling, will be used to guide target selection and interpret the molecular effects of the edits. Wheat transformation will be carried out in three varieties with contrasting resistance profiles, and barley transformation will be done in Golden Promise. Disease resistance will be assessed through controlled inoculation experiments. Edited and wild-type plants will be inoculated with Blumeria graminis isolates and evaluated at the whole-plant level.

Overall, the project aims to establish a new resistance concept based on blocking essential plant-pathogen interactions rather than relying on single resistance genes. This strategy has the potential to deliver more robust and durable disease resistance and to open new avenues for precision breeding in cereal crops.

The position is funded by a project supported by the DFF, in collaboration with Copenhagen University and will last 3 years.

Qualifications and specific competences
Applicants to the PhD position must hold a relevant MSc degree within molecular biology, plant or agricultural sciences, biology, biotechnology or similar.
• Knowledge in plant transformation and in vitro culture
• Experience with Alphafold and/or structural biology.
• Be fluent in English (written and spoken).
• Have scientific writing and communication skills.
• Have the ability to manage your own tasks and collaborate in an international research team.
Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Agroecology, Forsøgsvej 1, 4200 Slagelse, Denmark.

Contacts
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
• Associate Professor Kim Hebelstrup, e-mail: Kim.hebelstrup@agro.au.dk (main supervisor)
• Tenure Track Assistant Professor Olga A. Oxholm, e-mail: olgaa@agro.au.dk (co-supervisor)For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:
• admission.gradschool.tech@au.dk

Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8. As a PhD fellow you will also receive a monthly non-pensionable allowance.

**Turn complexity into one plan the business can act on.

****What if planning could shape the future, not just react to it?

**Across the Nordics, demand is shaped by tenders, contracts, launches and changing customer needs. The opportunity is to bring those signals together early, translate them into clear choices and create a healthier balance between product availability and inventory. That is where you come in.

As our Demand & Supply Manager Nordics, you will create one reliable view of demand and supply across Denmark, Sweden, and Finland. You will own the Nordic Sales and Operations Planning cycle, lead a distributed planning team and help move the organization from reactive expediting towards confident, forward-looking decisions.

**Your impact

****Role

**This is not a role where you simply maintain a forecast. You will set the direction for how the Nordics plan, decide and improve. You will:

• Own one Nordic demand and supply plan, bringing tender and contract intelligence into the forecast early enough to influence decisions.

• Lead the full S&OP cycle, from portfolio and demand reviews through supply and management review, with clear monthly decisions and ownership.

• Take accountability for inventory health, availability and the working-capital effect of the plan, while preventing excess and risk stock from rebuilding.

• Lead and develop four planners and one analyst across Denmark, Sweden and Finland, creating one way of working that is resilient across countries and absences.

• Connect sales, category, tender, sourcing, finance, warehouse and transport around the same facts, priorities and actions.

**What Will Make You Successful

**You combine strong planning craft with practical leadership. You are comfortable moving between item-level detail and senior stakeholder decisions, and you know how to challenge constructively when the numbers tell a different story.

**You Are Likely To Bring

**

• 8-12 years in supply chain, including at least five years in demand and supply planning or S&OP.

• Experience owning a full S&OP or IBP cycle and leading a planning team, ideally across more than one country.

• Strong knowledge of inventory, working capital, forecast quality and excess or obsolete stock.

• Hands-on experience with an advanced planning system such as Slim4, o9, Kinaxis, SAP IBP or a comparable platform, plus strong Excel or BI skills.

• Professional English and, preferably, Danish or Swedish.

• A relevant Bachelor or Master degree. APICS, IBF or an equivalent certification is an advantage.

**The environment you will step into

**The scope is genuinely Nordic and the mandate is broad. You will have the space to shape the process while keeping the daily business moving.

You will work closely on standards, tools and the group excess and risk stock process. Your influence will reach well beyond your direct team, so trust, clarity and follow-through will matter as much as technical expertise.

**Ready to build what comes next?

**If you want to lead a cross-border team, create one Nordic planning approach and turn better demand and supply decisions into stronger service and healthier inventory, we would like to hear from you.

Location: Copenhagen Denmark or Kungsbacka Sweden. Travel: Regular travel within the Nordics and Europe is part of the role.

jobs.occupation: Senior AI Engineer for The Tech Collective
jobs.description:
Job Description

We're looking for a senior AI engineer with hands-on experience in generative AI, API integrations, and advanced agent-based applications. The ideal candidate brings a mix of full-stack, AI, and cloud engineering experience.

What you'll do

This role cuts across multiple tech stacks and is a central part of how we deliver AI solutions for our clients.

In this role, you'll:

• Translating early ideas into working prototypes and iterating them into production-ready solutions using modern full-stack frameworks

• Designing and deploying generative AI applications and autonomous agents using LLM APIs and established agent frameworks

• Integrating AI capabilities into client systems and managing deployment pipelines in cloud environments

• Collaborating with engineering, product, and business stakeholders to build solutions that address real needs

• Mentoring junior engineers and keeping pace with emerging AI and software engineering paradigms

What you'll bring

We're looking for someone with at least five years of software development experience, including at least two in generative AI and agent-based applications, and a master's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field.

Beyond that, you'll bring:

• Full-stack capability across TypeScript (React, Next.js, Vite) and Python, with experience shipping production systems

• Hands-on experience with agent frameworks such as LangChain/LangGraph, CrewAI, Agno, or DSPy

• Proficiency with RESTful APIs, cloud environments (AWS, Azure, or GCP), and containerisation tools such as Docker and Kubernetes

• Strong communication skills across technical and non-technical stakeholders

Relevant AI or cloud certifications are a plus. English is our corporate language; however, proficiency in one or more additional languages is a plus for this role.

What we offer

You'll join a fast-growing team backed by Implement Consulting Group — nerdy by nature, genuinely curious about both technology and people, and serious about craft. You'll have real autonomy, a strong culture of learning, and meaningful AI challenges across industries.

Ready to shape the digital future with us? We review applications on an ongoing basis and will close the role once filled, so apply ASAP.

We look forward to hearing from you!

About The Tech Collective

The Tech Collective is a fast-growing consulting company powered by Implement. We help organisations unlock the immense potential of data, AI and analytics, ensuring that they are fit for the digital future. Through co-creation and passionate advisory, we aim to make our clients’ data easy to handle and provide useful insights.

In our collective, you will find people with a combination of nerdiness and infectious energy. We are passionate about technology, but we also have a sincere interest in people.

The Role

Our Purpose

Scheduling isn’t simply filling shifts. It’s finding the sweet spot that enables businesses to grow and team members to enjoy the perfect work/life balance.

At Planday from Xero, we aim to use Agentic AI to build a future where managers seamlessly can free up invaluable time for their business and teams. We’re not just building software; we’re on a mission to make shift work more human, to change work/life balance from a luxury to a reality for all shift workers. We’re using advanced technology to help humans reach their full potential. At work and in life.

Founded in 2004, Planday is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark and helps create perfect schedules for hundreds of thousands of users across the world. Planday was acquired by Xero in 2021.

How you’ll make an impact

We are introducing customer marketing as a dedicated discipline at Planday, and this is the role that will build it.

This is a builder's role: you will define how we market to our existing customers, establishing the strategy, the programmes, and the ways of working from the ground up. Across the UK, Nordics, and Germany, you will design and deliver 1:many marketing that drives adoption, deepens engagement, and turns customers into long-term advocates and expansion opportunities.

You will sit at the heart of our commercial ambition: as we target growth in the UK, defend our leadership in the Nordics, and build momentum in Germany, customer marketing is one of the key levers that connects product value to commercial outcomes. This is a role for someone who is energised by creating from scratch, earns trust through execution, and knows that the best customer marketing is grounded in deep empathy for the people you are marketing to.

What You'll Do

jobs.occupation: Professor of Geological Mapping and Mineral Resources
jobs.description:
The Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland (GEUS) seeks excellent candidates with a strong research profile in one or more disciplines related to igneous and sedimentary rock geology, geologically applied geophysics and geochemistry, ore geology, remote sensing, tectonics and structural evolution to fill a new full professor position. The professorship focuses on Greenland and the surrounding Arctic.

  You are expected to contribute to GEUS’ overall strategy by strengthening and further developing our knowledge of the geological evolution of Greenland from a combined field geology, laboratory analysis and modelling approach. An important element is advancing the understanding of the various geological settings in Greenland with a broad scientific focus spanning from paleogeography, sedimentary basins, mountain belts and rift zones to tectonic features and associated mineral systems.

  Furthermore, you are expected to promote our ideas, expertise and concepts to the surrounding societies, to deliver research output at a high international level, and to successfully obtain funding for and lead larger research projects. Moreover, the position aims to strengthen and profile our research, public sector consultancy and advisory activities.

  The position is in the Department for Mapping and Mineral Resources, which is located at GEUS’ main office in Copenhagen.

  About the position
 The candidate is expected to establish and further develop a strong and coherent research group in the Department for Mapping and Mineral Resources, which will closely cooperate with the other departments in GEUS as well as with Danish universities and relevant international research institutions. Many of GEUS’ activities in this research field are focused on the geology of Greenland and the surrounding Arctic, and fieldwork in Greenland will be a key activity. Moreover, development and application of new, innovative methods for efficient data analysis are expected to continuously contribute to the advancement of the research field, and the professor is expected to play a central role in this context.

  Candidates for professorships at GEUS must have a strong research profile in the field and have a strong publication track record in international research journals with high impact in the research field. Moreover, candidates are expected to have played and have the ambition to play a key role in advancing the research field, for example by taking part in the organisation of international conferences and by editing relevant journals and/or book series.

  Research activities are to a large extent dependent on external funding. GEUS has a strong tradition for attracting research funding from e.g. Danish research councils, the European Commission, private foundations and authorities. GEUS also leads and acts as a partner in internationally funded research projects such as EU Horizon projects. Professors at GEUS should have a strong track record of research funding and play a leading role in research funding applications and project management.

  Professors at GEUS are expected to set the direction for GEUS’ research within their field of expertise and related fields to develop and advance research and make new ideas thrive in an open and welcoming research environment. Furthermore, professors at GEUS play an active role in career planning for early-career scientific staff and take responsibility for the supervision of PhD students and postdoctoral researchers. They are also expected to have a collaborative spirit and actively engage with other professors, project managers and staff to contribute to a dynamic research environment. Moreover, professors may become members of GEUS’ research committee and act as sparring partners for management decisions on strategic planning and hiring plans for scientific staff.

  GEUS is an independent research institution under the Danish Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities. GEUS provides research-based public sector consultancy for Danish governmental institutions and research-based advice to private companies. Professors are expected to take part in such public sector consultancy and act as sparring partners for colleagues and management in such matters.

  Who are you? 
 We seek candidates with an excellent international profile. Consideration will be given to your international network, your ability to engage and motivate staff, as well as your openness, drive and interpersonal skills.

  You have a research profile in the field, and you have visions and ideas for developing the research field. You are experienced in creating and establishing research projects with different partners, obtaining external funding, and in leading and managing large research projects.

  Experience with supervising MSc and PhD students as well as early-career researchers is a prerequisite.

  We also expect you to have experience with public sector consultancy, advisory activities (or similar), and fieldwork. Especially, experience with fieldwork in Greenland and/or another Arctic/Antarctic environment is considered advantageous.

  The Department for Mapping and Mineral Resources
 In the Department for Mapping and Mineral Resources, we conduct research on rocks, their mineralogy and chemical composition, and their genesis and evolution. We use this insight to provide the geological background for investment opportunities in exploration for mineral resources and data for responsible natural resource management. For this work, we have considerable in-house analytical facilities, including instruments for analysis of major and trace elements, isotopic composition and analytical microscopy.

  One of the department’s important tasks is the continuous geological mapping of Greenland. In addition to the above-mentioned tools, we acquire and analyse high-resolution stereographic images of mountain walls in our photo laboratory, which provides our geologists with a powerful tool for the development of 3D geological mapping on metres to tens of kilometres scales. Finally, the department hosts D-MIC (Danish Mineral Intelligence Centre), which analyses raw materials’ value chains, thereby linking geological knowledge to society’s need for mineral raw materials.
 
 A working environment with a focus on professional development and well-being

  There are many good reasons why you should choose a working life at GEUS.

  We are a diverse staff of about 300 committed employees. Trust and flexibility are keywords. The working environment is lively, informal and international. Our tasks are versatile and there are plenty of opportunities for you to influence the development of your task portfolio.

  We prioritise professional development, among other things by offering access to courses and other relevant activities. Socialising is also very important at GEUS, and we have a rich social life with a staff club, an art association and more.

  At GEUS, we prioritise the well-being of every single employee. We prioritise that the Heads of Departments are close to the employees, and we have flexible working hours that allow you to organise your life so that there is time for what matters to you. If you need to work from home occasionally, that is also possible.

  Furthermore, we have a gym with associated physiotherapists.

  Salary and conditions of employment
 The position as Professor is permanent. Salary and terms of employment are in accordance with the relevant trade union agreement. Supplements can be negotiated according to skills.

  The appointment area is the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities and its institutions.

  The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities considers diversity to be an asset and encourages anyone regardless of gender, age, religion or ethnicity to seek the position.

  Additional information
 If you would like additional information, please contact the Head of Department, Mikael Pedersen on telephone +45 22 21 65 75, e-mail mp@geus.dk, or Managing Director, Lars Nielsen, on telephone +45 91 33 38 70, e-mail larni@geus.dk.

  If you are an international applicant, you can read more about living and working in Denmark on GEUS’ website.

  Are you interested?
 Please write the application in English and include a letter of motivation, your PhD diploma and CV incl. your ORCID, as well as a complete list of publications with 1) a separate indication of peer-reviewed journal articles and 2) an indication of publications where you have been either the lead or senior author.

  Please include in the application the relevant academic works that you wish to be included in the professor assessment (max. 10). Please enclose other material that documents your research and teaching qualifications.

  You are requested to include a 2-3-page account that refers to your most important academic work with relevance to the position. Finally, you are encouraged to write a one-page explanation of your plans for the development of the field. In addition to the material that you would like to be included in the assessment, the assessment committee may choose to include further material in their assessment. It is your responsibility to send the material to the committee upon request.
 
 It is mandatory to include your updated ResearcherID and/or ORCID, which will be used to assess your publication record in Web of Science. Any recently accepted or submitted publications may be added separately to the list of publications.
 
 We must have your application at the latest on Monday 9 November 2026 (Danish time).

  Applications or other material received after the deadline will not be considered.

  The appointment procedure
 A professional assessment committee consisting of one internal and two to four external assessors at minimum professor level will carry out an individual assessment of all applicants’ professional qualifications, and the applicants will be assessed as qualified or unqualified for the position. Afterwards, an internal employment committee will decide which of the professionally qualified candidates will be invited for a job interview. This procedure is in accordance with the “Order on employment and assessment of scientific staff at the Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland § 4 and 7”.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Coastal Engineering (Wave-Vegetation Interaction) - DTU Construct
jobs.description:
How can coastal vegetation help protect our coastlines from waves and flooding? Understanding how waves interact with vegetation is key to exploring its potential for coastal protection and climate adaptation. Are you interested in combining fluid mechanics, mathematical analysis and numerical modelling to help answer this question.

Then join us for a 3-year PhD fellowship in coastal engineering at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering, Section for Fluid Mechanics, Coastal and Maritime Engineering.

Your PhD research will play an integral part in the project “Marine advection and dissipation in the vegetated coastal environment”, financed by the Independent Research Fund Denmark.

You will collaborate with researchers at DTU and DHI in Denmark, as well as at University College Dublin, Ireland and Northeastern University, USA.

Responsibilities 
Your primary tasks will be to develop analytical and numerical models for waves interacting with coastal vegetation. Particular emphasis will be placed on the wave-averaged flow generated by surface waves and on the changes introduced by vegetation canopies.

The research will include:

• Development and validation of models for wave-induced mean velocity profiles over vegetated beds under regular waves.
• Extension of these models to irregular wave fields, including derivation of wave-averaged shear-stress distributions and mean velocity profiles.
• Investigation of undertow and circulation currents above vegetated beds in the surf zone under breaking waves.
• Development of a cross-shore momentum balance describing wave-induced changes in mean water level and the potential reduction of storm-surge flooding by coastal vegetation.
• Numerical simulations using computational fluid dynamics 
• Application of advanced turbulence models for surface-wave flows, modified to account for vegetation.
• Validation of the developed models against existing high-quality laboratory datasets.
• Development of practical parameterizations suitable for implementation in larger-scale coastal and hydrodynamic models.
The project combines fundamental fluid mechanics with applications directly relevant to coastal protection and climate adaptation. A major scientific objective is to move beyond conventional empirical vegetation models and instead explicitly account for the modification of the wave-induced velocity field within and above vegetation canopies.

Qualifications
We are looking for candidates with a strong background in one or more of the following areas:

• Coastal or ocean engineering
• Fluid mechanics or hydrodynamics
• Computational fluid dynamics
• Environmental hydraulics
• Applied mathematics or a closely related field
Experience with numerical modelling, programming and/or CFD is highly desirable. Experience with turbulence modelling, wave mechanics or coastal hydrodynamics would be advantageous, but is not essential. Strong mathematical skills and an interest in combining theoretical analysis with numerical modelling are important.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. Starting date is anticipated as 1 February 2027, or according to mutual agreement. The position is a full-time position. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Professor David R. Fuhrman (drfu@dtu.dk).

You can read more about Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at www.construct.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 10 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Civil and Mechanical Engineering develops and utilises science and technical knowledge for the benefit of society and the sustainable development. We undertake research, education, innovation, and scientific advice of the highest quality within building design and processes, building construction and safety, building energy and technical services, solid mechanics, fluid mechanics, coastal and maritime engineering, materials technology, manufacturing engineering, engineering systems design, design for sustainability, and thermal energy.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: AI Red Team Specialist – Lead Researcher in Agentic Security
jobs.description:
We’re looking for an experienced red teamer with proven credentials in agentic red teaming to join our advanced product and research team.

What you’ll do

You’ll join the team dedicated to building and developing a tool that dynamically tests and evaluates large language models (LLMs) and their native application context for vulnerabilities.

You’ll be working with seasoned reverse engineers, application pentesters, red teamers, and data scientists, bridging multiple digital disciplines by creating a unique suite that gives our clients the capability to test, remediate, and harden their agentic workloads.

What you’ll bring

Most of all, we value ingenuity, curiosity, and drive. You may be a great fit for this role if you have experience with:

• Building or contributing to tools used for dynamic application testing

• Working extensively with open source or proprietary tools used for web and application pentesting

• Actively adopting LLMs and Model Context Protocol (MCP) in automating and enhancing your penetration tests

• Spending time researching agentic vulnerabilities and attending relevant trainings or conferences

To fit right in here at The Tech Collective:

• You should be genuinely curious about new developments within the red teaming domain

• You possess the willingness to tackle new and technical challenges as they arise

• You know how to break down and structure complex assignments and enjoy sharing your knowledge and insights with your team members

• You possess a startup mentality to help drive the innovation and ingenuity of our red team products

• You can cooperate seamlessly with different profiles in a highly diverse team of researchers, developers, consultants, and red teamers

We don’t expect you to know everything – after all, agentic security is a rapidly evolving field! In this role, we’re looking for someone who wants to own, develop, and innovate the product modules related to testing the application context (e.g., API security, cryptographic implementation, broken authentication, RBAC) and supporting infrastructure (e.g., misconfigurations, server-side vulnerabilities) for the agents that we test.

To succeed in this role, your experience and competencies should include:

Professional experience

• A minimum of five years’ progressive experience in enterprise red teaming or offensive research

• A proven track record of web application pentesting with an emphasis on remediation and hardening

• Experience defining and driving product roadmaps for red team tools (not required, but highly valued)

• Demonstrated ability to evaluate complex technology stacks, including common cloud platforms (M365/Azure, Google, or AWS), CI/CD pipelines, and AI-powered platforms and systems

• Experience communicating technical findings to non-technical stakeholders and the ability to bring technical assessments to life

Technical competencies

• Familiarity with both Mitre and OWASP frameworks, and experience applying them in client reporting

• Relevant security certifications (e.g., OSCP, OSCE, OSEP, GIAC GPEN/GXPN, etc.) are a plus, indicating solid foundational knowledge and commitment to the offensive security field.

• Prior experience developing agent-specific attack types such as prompt injection, memory & context poisoning, or jailbreaking

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Arctic fjord food webs under glacial retreat - DTU Aqua
jobs.description:
Greenland Institute of Natural Resources (GINR), the Greenland Climate Research Centre (GCRC) and DTU Aqua invite applications for a joint PhD position investigating how glacial retreat affect the structure, functioning, and stability of Arctic fjord food webs.

The position offers an excellent opportunity to combine Arctic field ecology, laboratory analyses, quantitative trophic ecology, and ecosystem modelling while working in Greenland and Denmark. You will become part of an interdisciplinary research environment spanning GINR, DTU Aqua, and the wider EDGE project.

The PhD project focuses on two contrasting fjord systems near Nuuk, Greenland, which differ in their degree of glacial influence. It is part of the Independent Research Fund Denmark project “Fjords on the EDGE: Resilience of Greenland Coastal Food Webs in a Warming Arctic”.

The overall aim is to understand how changes at the glacier–ocean interface propagates through the coastal ecosystem, from primary production to benthic communities, fish, and marine mammals. In particular, you will investigate the relative importance of benthic and pelagic energy pathways for key consumers using stable isotope analyses and stomach-content data. These observations will be integrated into an ecosystem model to explore how deglaciation tipping points may alter food-web structure and ecosystem functioning.

The position is jointly hosted by GINR in Nuuk and DTU Aqua in Lyngby. You will be based in Nuuk during the first two years and at DTU Aqua in Lyngby during the final year. Fieldwork, courses, project meetings, and collaborations will take place at additional locations throughout the PhD. You will be enrolled as a PhD student at DTU Aqua and work closely with researchers at both institutions and with collaborators in the EDGE project.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your primary responsibilities will be to:

• Conduct fieldwork in Nuup Kangerlua and Ameralik during 2027, collecting benthic and pelagic samples.
• Prepare and analyse samples for stable isotope analysis and use isotope mixing models to quantify the relative contribution of benthic and pelagic food sources to key consumers.
• Conduct fish stomach-content analyses to characterise diets and trophic interactions.
• Integrate new observations with existing datasets to develop and parameterise an ecosystem model based on the StratE2E framework.
• Use the model to investigate how glacial retreat and associated changes in pelagic production may affect fjord food-web structure, functioning, and stability.
• Publish results in international peer-reviewed journals and present findings at scientific conferences and to relevant local stakeholders.
We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with a strong interest in Arctic marine ecosystems and interdisciplinary research. You should have:

• A two-year master’s degree (120 ECTS) in marine biology, marine ecology, fisheries science, ecosystem modelling, or a related field, with good academic results.
• A strong interest in fieldwork and laboratory-based research, including the ability to work effectively on ocean-going research vessels in Arctic environments.
• Demonstrated experience with quantitative data analysis and scientific programming in R, Python, or MATLAB.
• Knowledge of marine ecosystem dynamics and trophic or food-web ecology.
• Strong analytical and scientific communication skills.
• Fluency in written and spoken English.
The following qualifications are considered an advantage:

• Experience with ecological or ecosystem modelling, including StratE2E or similar frameworks.
• Experience with stable isotope ecology and/or mixing models.
• Experience identifying benthic organisms.
• Experience with fish diet or stomach-content analyses.
• Experience with Arctic marine ecosystems.
• A published or submitted peer-reviewed scientific publication.
• Fluency in Danish and Greenlandic.
We recognise that candidates may bring different combinations of these skills and do not expect applicants to have prior experience in all components of the project. Particular emphasis will be placed on scientific potential.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Professor Teunis Jansen (DTU Aqua and GINR) and Researcher Sandra Maier (GINR).

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The position is a full-time, three-year PhD appointment administered by DTU. The expected starting date is 1 February 2027. You will be based at GINR in Nuuk during the first two years and at DTU Aqua in Lyngby during the final year. GINR will assist the successful candidate with finding accommodation in Nuuk.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
For further information, please contact Professor Teunis Jansen, DTU Aqua and GINR (tej@aqua.dtu.dk), or Researcher Sandra Maier, GINR (sama@natur.gl)

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 30 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

About DTU Aqua
DTU Aqua – National Institute of Aquatic Resources – works for well-functioning oceans, rivers, and lakes where biodiversity can thrive. Our research, advisory service, and education contribute to the development of a sustainable blue bioeconomy, robust aquatic ecosystems, and reduced effects of climate change. We have a large national and international network and cooperate with research partners, public authorities, industry, and NGOs. We have state-of-the-art research facilities and Denmark’s only ocean- and arctic-going research vessel. The Institute has about 400 employees, one-half being scientific staff, including about 45 PhD students. About 40 nationalities are represented at the institute, and we support an equal gender distribution. We are located in Lyngby, Hirtshals, Nykøbing Mors, and Silkeborg and have regular activities in Greenland. Learn more on aqua.dtu.dk

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Tenure Track Assistant Professor in Infectious Animal Disease Modelling for Sustainable One Health Actions
jobs.description:
Tenure Track Assistant Professor in Infectious Animal Disease Modelling for Sustainable One Health Actions  Department of Veterinary and Animal Sciences
 Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences
 University of Copenhagen

  The University seeks to appoint a tenure track assistant professor to commence 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

  Information on the department can be found at: http://www.sund.ku.dk/. 

  Subject area: Infectious disease epidemiology, modelling, animal health, One Health, and sustainable health systems

  The Tenure-Track Assistant Professor will lead research on the dynamics of infectious disease spread in health systems, with particular emphasis on how changes in environmental conditions, animal populations, production systems, and management practices influence disease emergence, transmission, and control. The position will combine infectious disease epidemiology, mathematical and statistical modelling, data science, and economic analysis to generate evidence supporting disease preparedness, prevention, and control.

  The successful candidate will:

   	
• Lead independent research on the dynamics of infectious disease spread in health systems, including the influence of environmental and production system changes. 	
• Develop and apply simulation, epidemiological, and statistical models to assess disease and spillover risks, evaluate mitigation and control strategies, and quantify their economic implications. 	
• Demonstrate strong programming skills in R and other relevant programming languages, including experience in managing, processing, and analysing large and complex datasets. 	
• Have experience in developing and applying epidemiological disease-spread models, including model calibration, validation, parameter estimation, and calculation of epidemiological indicators such as the basic reproduction number (R₀) across different animal species and production systems. 	
• Design and implement epidemiological modelling frameworks. 	
• Validate and calibrate models using large-scale national datasets, ensuring scientific robustness, methodological validity, and relevance for policy and decision-making. 	
• Translate research findings into evidence supporting risk-based disease prevention, preparedness, and control.  	
• Establish and maintain collaborations with key stakeholders, including the Danish Veterinary and Food Administration, industry partners such as SEGES and Landbrug & Fødevarer (L&F), and international organisations such as the FAO. 	
• Lead and secure independent research funding through competitive national and international funding calls. The position requires demonstrated experience in securing external funding, as well as the ambition to develop research ideas into externally funded projects and provide scientific leadership for such projects within the TIPTON Research Group. 	
• Contribute to the development and delivery of One Health and sustainability teaching, with a particular focus on infectious diseases, disease preparedness, and the interactions between animal, human, and environmental health. 	
• Contribute to teaching in data science, including data management, dataset preparation and handling, statistical analysis, programming, and the analysis of large-scale and complex datasets. 	
• Supervise students and contribute to research capacity building within infectious disease epidemiology, disease modelling, data science, and One Health. 	
• Contribute to the delivery of government services undertaken by the Department, including research-based advice, preparedness activities, risk assessments, and other activities relevant to infectious disease modelling and control.   The position is expected to combine methodological excellence in infectious disease modelling and data science with applied epidemiological research, generating evidence that is directly relevant to disease preparedness, private and public bodies, sustainable production systems, animal health and resilient health systems.

  The tenure track assistant professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of: 

   	
• research, including publication/academic dissemination 	
• research-based teaching  	
• sharing knowledge with society  	
• participation in formal pedagogical training programme for assistant professors    The tenure track assistant professor’s performance will be evaluated through annual evaluations. Furthermore, the tenure track assistant professor will be evaluated in a mid-track appraisal. 

  After no more than six years of employment and on condition of a positive final appraisal, the tenure track assistant professor will be employed as associate professor. Find more information about tenure track at the University of Copenhagen.

  Required qualifications 
 To be qualified for an assistant professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion.

  Furthermore, each applicant must be able to document:

   	
• a PhD degree or similar qualifications within the subject area  	
• research experience within the field of the position    The tenure track assistant professor must have an academic standing showing internationally competitive research, and/or have internationally recognized high potential to make a future impact. 

  The assistant professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills. 

  Salary and employment conditions
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is permanent. 

  Employment is as Tenure Track Assistant Professor under the applicable collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations. 

  There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector at www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025. 

  Questions 
 For further information, please contact Research Group Leader: Professor Beate Conrady, bcon@sund.ku.dk

  Foreign applicants may find the university’s International Staff Mobility useful.

  Application 
 The application must be submitted in English, and must include the following documents: 

   	
• Application (Including motivation for applying for this position (Maximum 2 pages)) 	
• Curriculum vitae (Including information about external funding) 	
• Diplomas (Master’s, PhD and other relevant diplomas) 	
• A complete list of publications  	
• Research plan (2-4 pages) 	
• Teaching plan 	
• Uploads of maximum 5 publications to be considered in the assessment  	
• Teaching portfolio, if applicable (Guidelines)   Please note: It is mandatory to upload a teaching plan in the online application form. Should you not be able to produce a teaching plan, please upload a blank document in this box instead.

  Application procedure
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee.  All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at the university's Job Portal.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation. 

  The application will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities. 

  The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested in this post to apply. 

  Please submit the application with the required attachments. Only online applications will be accepted. The closing date for applications is 23.59 p.m. CET, 18 November 2026.

  Interviews for this position are likely to be held on 7 April 2027.
