**WHO WE ARE?

**For over 50 years, we have worked closely with investment and asset managers to become the world’s leading provider of integrated investment management solutions. We are 3,000+ colleagues with a broad range of nationalities, educations, professional experiences, ages, and backgrounds.

SimCorp is an independent subsidiary of the Deutsche Börse Group. Following the recent merger with Axioma, we leverage the combined strength of our brands to provide an industry-leading, full, front-to-back offering for our clients.

SimCorp is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to building a culture where diverse perspectives and expertise are integrated into our everyday work. We believe in the continual growth and development of our employees, so that we can provide best-in-class solutions to our clients.

jobs.occupation: Kickstart your Career with Deloitte’s Finance Consultancy Programme
jobs.description:
Company Description

Are you interested in working in an exciting and challenging consulting role, where you can deploy and develop your skills and competencies within the CFO domain of companies? Do you hold a business-related Master’s degree by the summer of 2027, and are you ready to embark on a life-long learning journey in a leading global consulting firm? If yes, then we might have the perfect opportunity for you!

Who we are

Joining our Finance Consultancy Programme, you will get to collaborate with experienced consultants on a wide variety of assignments and development opportunities. At Deloitte, we work with different project sizes across finance disciplines and industries, but the foundation is always the same: Our genuine passion for the CFO area and creating value together with our clients.

Finance Transformation is part of Deloitte Technology & Transformation (former Consulting) consisting of more than 350 consultants in Denmark who work across all areas of the CFO function. We engage with clients to operate, advise, optimize, and transform their finance functions. Our clients range from domestic to international, from private to public, across various industries, sizes, and time horizons.

You will join a team that emphasizes collaboration, collegiality, coaching, and talent development. At Deloitte, we value diverse skills, experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, encouraging an inclusive and collaborative environment.

Job Description

Exciting tasks await you

As an Analyst in Deloitte Finance Transformation, you will experience that no workdays are the same. You will face a wide range of tasks, both in the form of interim-based roles and project-based assignments. Projects and tasks will vary across finance disciplines (e.g., operational finance or business finance) and industries (e.g., private or public), and within the first years of your career, you will be assigned to as many different projects and tasks as possible to expand your toolbox and build on your financial craftmanship.

Based on the specific client's needs and your interests, experiences, and competencies, typical assignments and projects could be within the scope of:

• Finance operations optimization and transformation, e.g., controlling, month-end closing, and reporting

• Transformation and digitalization of finance functions, e.g., process optimization, closing excellence, internal controls advisory, and leveraging technology solutions

• Enterprise performance management, e.g., analytics, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting

• ERP-enabled finance transformations and finance systems implementation, e.g., outlining the ERP-strategy, defining business requirements and ensuring consistent data migration

• Finance strategy and operating model, e.g., designing service delivery models, outlining roles and responsibilities and conducting assessments

• M&A readiness and finance post-merger integration

• Global business services transformations, e.g., assessing, developing and implementing shared service functions and aligning service delivery with corporate strategy

• Internal business development and leadership support, e.g., assisting on client proposals, facilitating events and developing material to strengthen our market offerings.

Onboarding and learning

When joining us, you will participate in our onboarding programme designed with the purpose of giving you the best foundation for kickstarting your career in Deloitte. During your first two weeks, you and your peers will attend our Finance Transformation Nordic Bootcamp and our Consultant Academy, where the content is tailored to match your competencies as recent graduates. The Finance Transformation Bootcamp helps you in building your finance craftmanship and toolbox, while the Consultant Academy prepares you for your consulting role in Deloitte Technology & Transformation. Also heavily focused on social activities and team-building, the onboarding programme provides a smooth transition from university as it offers a unique opportunity to connect and build strong relations with your fellow new joiners from day one.

At Deloitte, we believe in life-long learning, and we are committed to investing in your individual development, both professionally and personally, throughout your career. You will experience this with our Finance Consultancy Programme, which is a highly structured learning programme, aimed at equipping you with the appropriate skillset and the right level of competencies needed to succeed in your role.

Leadership and culture

To support your learning, you will also be assigned a People Leader as your closest leader and go-to sparring partner. Your People Leader will help you set the overall direction of your journey in Deloitte and provide guidance across projects to make sure that your individual aspirations and professional development goals are met. Every career path is unique, and together with your People Leader you get the chance to shape your own.

We believe in leadership at all levels, and we have committed ourselves to creating and maintaining an inclusive and psychologically safe culture, where you are encouraged and empowered to take responsibility while leading both yourself and others. We combine this with a substantial focus on continuously staying relevant and being a meaningful social community to our people. We are a people’s business, and therefore we strongly believe that this is an essential prerequisite for making an impact that truly matters – for ourselves and for our clients**.

Qualifications

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for you, who are passionate about consulting and the CFO-area and who are willing to go the extra mile to deliver sustainable impact that truly matters to our clients. You show an eagerness to make a difference for both clients and colleagues and you are able to see the opportunities and potential in all types of assignments. As our business can be highly changeable, it is important that you are curious by nature, and that you face challenges with an open-minded and solution-oriented approach.

In addition to this, you:

• Have completed a master’s degree within the fields of finance, economics, business, accounting, social sciences, IT, or similar areas in the summer of 2027 or before

• Have achieved academic results from your bachelor’s and master’s degree that you are proud of

• Demonstrate a flair for both oral and written communication and are fluent in English

• Have a legal working permit in Denmark

Although relevant job experience might be an advantage, this is not a requirement.

Additional Information

Want to know more?

Click the "I'm interested"-button above and upload your CV and grade transcripts from your bachelor’s and master’s degree if you are interested and ready to join our team**. Instead of an application letter, we would like you to answer the questions you will be presented with on the next pages** (please only consider the required (*) fields). As we process applications and arrange interviews on an ongoing basis, we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

Application deadline: Hiring on an ongoing basis.

Please do not hesitate to contact Giulio Marano (gimarano@deloitte.dk / +45 30 93 64 11) or Maria Banke (mbanke@deloitte.dk / +45 20 97 64 15) if you have any questions about the position.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

About Hemab

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These are therapies designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage - with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

As Director, Clinical Sciences, you'll help turn Hemab's science into well-designed clinical studies and clear evidence about how our treatments perform in patients. You'll take scientific ownership across protocol development, study execution and data interpretation, working closely with Medical Directors and colleagues across clinical development, regulatory and other functions.

What you'll do

• Lead the clinical science contribution to study strategy, design and execution, keeping the scientific questions and patient needs at the centre of decisions.

• Drive protocol development with the Medical Director, including amendments as emerging data or study needs require.

• Own the scientific review of clinical study data, identify discrepancies and trends, and turn emerging safety and efficacy data into clear questions and actions for the team.

• Shape study documents and plans, including informed consent forms, eCRFs, medical monitoring plans and data review plans.

• Guide sites and vendors on protocol requirements, eligibility criteria and participant management so studies are executed consistently and to the intended design.

• Partner across clinical development to analyse and interpret study results and build a clear understanding of what the data mean.

• Translate study findings for internal and external audiences alongside the Medical Director.

• Develop clinical content for regulatory documents, including investigator brochures, annual safety reports, clinical study reports and registration submissions.

What you'll bring to Hemab

• Substantial clinical science or clinical research experience in drug development, with direct responsibility for clinical studies.

• Experience developing clinical protocols and interpreting safety and efficacy data from interventional studies.

• A strong working knowledge of ICH-GCP, clinical study design and drug development in a regulated environment.

• The scientific judgement to interpret clinical information, literature and changing treatment approaches and apply it to study and development decisions.

• Experience working effectively with investigators, vendors and cross-functional clinical, medical and regulatory colleagues.

Nice to have

• Experience in haematology, rare disease or bleeding disorders.

• Experience contributing to development programmes through later-stage studies and registration.

• An advanced scientific or clinical degree.

What to expect, honestly

Hemab is still building a lot of its own structure. Systems here tend to get created as we need them, not handed down in advance. Whoever takes this role will likely build some of their own process instead of inheriting a finished one. We work across two hubs and multiple time zones - bridging that well takes real, deliberate effort. And because we're growing quickly, priorities can shift with less notice than they would at a larger, more established company.

This is the actual shape of working somewhere at this stage: It's genuinely energising for the right person and genuinely frustrating for the wrong one. If you want a place where the operating manual is already written, this might not be it – but if you want to help write it, this might be exactly it.

Why Hemab

At Hemab, your work ultimately connects back to something simple. People living with serious bleeding disorders get something they've never had before - the chance to prevent a bleed, instead of reacting to one after it happens. You'll be joining at a stage where individual decisions still carry real weight, and where your work can help turn promising science into a preventative treatment that actually reaches patients.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty, and respect. We're still building the consistency to back that up across every hiring process, every time. We'd say that plainly instead of pretending otherwise. If any part of your experience with us falls short of it, tell us.

Hemab builds balanced candidate slates and assesses everyone against a single standard. If you need a reasonable adjustment at any stage of the hiring process, please tell us.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Hemab Therapeutics is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, seeking to create a welcoming and diverse environment. All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, sex, marital status, gender expression or identity, genetic information, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

Our purpose to help people and businesses help each other is a tall order, but we keep it real. We’re a great bunch of humans, doing awesome stuff, without fuss or pretense. A successful Trustpilot future is driven by you –– we give you the autonomy to shape a career you can be proud of. If you’re ready to grow, let’s go.

Join us at the heart of trust.

Trustpilot is committed to creating an inclusive environment where people from all backgrounds can thrive and where different viewpoints and experiences are valued and respected. Together, we are the heart of trust.

We're looking for senior consultants to take a leading role in complex ERP transformation projects across ERP strategy, programme management, solution architecture, and functional consulting.

You will take a leading role in some of the largest ERP transformations across Europe. Depending on your profile and development goals, your responsibilities may include:

You will work across R&D, manufacturing, supply chain, commercial, and corporate functions. **

jobs.occupation: Associate Professor (non-tenured) in archaeometry at SDU in Odense
jobs.description:
A position as non-tenured Associate Professor in archaeometry is available from 1 May 2027 until 31 March 2030 at the Department of Physics Chemistry and Pharmacy, Faculty of Science, SDU in Odense.

About the research group and the project
The research group at which this position is posted is called CHART (Cultural Heritage and Archaeometric Research Team). Cultural Heritage and archaeometric research deal with investigations of samples originating from all sorts of culturally important artefacts: those procured by archaeologists in excavations, medieval buildings, handmade artefacts of all kinds, pieces of art, written materials. Only, the objects must have survived and be preserved today to some tangible degree. The study of cultural heritage is not exclusively for the humanities. In the last four or five decades, natural sciences have been increasingly involved in untangling the events of the past by studying cultural heritage objects to an ever-increasing degree of complexity. 

 

In CHART we take up the challenge of investigating cultural heritage objects on an international level using chemistry and physics. We aim at making a difference on the international scene by inventing new analytical methodologies, investigating objects of national and international interest, and by always securing collaboration between natural science and the humanities.

We do not claim to produce final or stand-alone answers; instead, we strive to achieve solutions together with colleagues from the humanities. In our research laboratories we daily cross the line between natural science and the humanities.

 

The present position is aimed at executing the already financed CIPP Center (Center for the Interior of Parchment and Paper), which involves the investigation of the Dead Sea Scrolls (https://www.sdu.dk/en/om-sdu/fakulteterne/naturvidenskab/nyheder-2026/erc-dead-sea-scrolls-archaeometry), the development of new methods for analysing paper and parchment, and a new project on poisonous books conducted in collaboration with the Royal Academy in Copenhagen, Pisa University, and the Library at SDU (https://www.nature.com/articles/s40494-019-0334-2 ).   

 

About the candidate
The successful candidate is expected to hold a PhD in archaeometry, analytical chemistry, or a closely related field, with a research profile centred on the application of analytical and physical-chemical methods to archaeological and heritage materials. A demonstrated expertise in a wide range of archaeomaterials (e.g., ceramics, bricks, pigments, and parchments) spanning diverse chrono-cultural contexts will be considered an asset. 

 

Tasks

• 
The candidate must partake in the execution of the research at the CIPP Center conducted by the CHART research group and contribute to the overall research theme of CHART. 

• 
The candidate must be able to support the ongoing collaboration with ADBOU at the SDU Health Faculty.

• 
The candidate is expected to obtain external funding for independent research, to foster internal collaboration at the Department, and to build and lead an internationally recognized research group. 

• 
The candidate should contribute to public outreach and communication activities.

• 
The candidate should teach (broadly) in degree programmes at the department, as well as participate in departmental administration, strategy development and educational programme development. 

• 
The candidate is expected to mentor undergraduate, graduate, and research students. 

 

Skills

• 
The candidate must have a strong and independent research profile, documented by an excellent track record of peer-reviewed publications in international journals. Hands-on experience with advanced analytical chemical instrumentation, experience with luminescence-based dating methods, and a demonstrated ability to develop or adapt analytical chemical methods will be highly valued.

• 
Experience with international collaboration, of partnerships with museums and cultural-heritage institutions, and of collaboration with the private sector will be an advantage.

• 
The successful candidate should have a strong teaching record. This includes experience with teaching courses within a chemistry curriculum at bachelor and master level as well as experience of project supervision across all levels, from bachelor to PhD. Experience with interdisciplinary, practical, and laboratory-based teaching, and with modern teaching methods, e-learning, flipped classroom, and online learning methods will be an advantage. A teaching CV should be included in the proposal. Teaching at the department includes first year teaching held in Danish, and the successful applicant may be expected to be involved in first year teaching. However, teaching in English is accepted from the start of employment, and the successful applicant is expected to learn basic Danish within 5 years. The university offers language courses.

The candidate will be part of the chemistry section. 

Application deadline: 15. November 2026 at 23:59 hours local Danish time

Please see the full call, including how to apply, on www.sdu.dk

Job Description

Are you ready to make a difference on a global scale? If you have a commercial background in the field of Operation & Maintenance from a relevant technical industry or a technical background in intralogistics, material handling or baggage handling solutions and a passion for working internationally, this is your chance to step into a high-impact role.

As a member of the Operations & Maintenance Partner Programs Centre of Competence, you will become a trusted expert and valued specialist in our global organisation. Expect international travel as required to support business operations, customer projects, and development activities. Depending on business needs, travel may amount to up to 60 days per year, collaborating with colleagues worldwide to develop new business opportunities, support contract extensions, and help local teams deliver best-in-class services to our airport and logistics customers. This position combines technical expertise, commercial insight, and operational support in a dynamic international environment.

Facilitate great global service

At BEUMER Group, we deliver intralogistics solutions such as mission critical baggage handling systems for airports and parcel handling systems for a variety of logistic customers all over the world. We have the leading product on the market, and the office in Aarhus is an international Centre of Competence. From here, you support 29 Beumer Group Companies around the world and help carry the strategic responsibility for our global service contracts.

Support colleagues and customers globally

Working with our colleagues in 29 Group Companies around the world, you will support Operation & Maintenance solutions for their regions by driving quotations and price calculations and defining the right winning strategy. You will also support a pool of over 100 existing O&M contracts worldwide. Although most of your interactions will be internal, at times you will also be working closely with our customers, via online or physical meetings and presentations. The role, however, is quite broad and dynamic, with the main responsibilities listed below:

• Analysing customer requirements in tender documents from a commercial, operational and organizational perspective to establish the right O&M service solutions

• Identifying, analysing and mitigating risks of new opportunities and existing contracts

• Close cooperation with project teams, sales teams and all departments within the organization

• Monitoring existing contracts so as to verify that they are performing well and adhering to the global O&M processes and company strategy

• Acting as single point of contact for all O&M contracts and Group Companies as well as facilitating work in all O&M contracts while promoting know-how sharing and best practice across O&M sites globally

• Overall planning on the implementation of new service contracts, including the resources, time and commercial aspects as well as the coordination with the customer and Group Companies

• As custodians of our global O&M processes and tools, constantly reviewing and enforcing them

• Following up on the implementation and the continuous optimisation of the service concepts

People person with experience managing and quoting maintenance solutions

Responsibility, communication and collaboration. These are three skills that are essential in this outgoing role, where you act across sites and cultures. You need to be able to talk to everyone – from service technicians to CEOs – communicating convincingly and persuasively. With no direct reports, your internal networking is highly important in this role as there is constant interaction with internal departments. At the end of the day, we are looking for your clout, energy and motivation to participate in global teamwork and collaborations. The requirements for the role are:

• A commercial background in a relevant technical field or a technical background from a similar industry. Experience with managing and quoting maintenance solutions is a strong advantage but not a must.

• A great communicator, fluent in English -spoken and in written-, who can talk and challenge people at all levels of the organisation

• Excellent skills in MS Office, especially Excel.

We offer you the opportunity to become part of a family-owned global industry leader, where quality in everything we do is essential for us. We are extremely customer-driven and team-oriented, and we are only successful, when everybody participates and help each other out. Our O&M-contracts are crucial for not just our business, but also for the many airports and logistics sites we support all over the world and by joining us a our new Operations & Maintenance Sales & Service Manager, you will not just help our company and customers, but also help making sure that parcels and baggage arrive quickly and in the right hands every time.

Interested?

Job Description

Join BEUMER Group Innovation & Development in creating solutions that power the next level of logistic sortation systems worldwide. As a Robotics Software Engineer at BEUMER Group, you’ll design innovative solutions that drive efficiency and reliability in sortation and handling systems for logistic sites around the globe.

Our logistics customers seek innovative solutions to improve the efficiency of their sites. This includes automating manual processes through technologies such as mobile carrier robots, articulated robots, and computer vision software. More broadly, digitalization is a key driver of efficiency improvements.

To meet these needs, we are intensifying our focus on innovation and investing more in bringing new products to the market to address our customers’ evolving needs, making this an exciting time to join BEUMER Group.

Global innovation team

As our new Robotics Software Engineer, you will join a local, cross-functional Innovation & Development team consisting of highly skilled professionals in computer vision, robotics, user experience design, software architecture, and software development. The team operates in a global setup and collaborates closely with colleagues across locations and disciplines. The team's mission is to develop innovative products and systems for the logistics industry.

In your role as Robotics Software Engineer, you will:

• Develop, maintain, and debug software on industrial PCs and robotic platforms, including communication and computer vision applications.

• Configure, program, and integrate industrial robots and motion control systems.

• Work with geometric and spatial calculations related to robot motion, object positioning, and vision-guided applications.

• Participate in the development of new products, from early prototypes to market-ready solutions.

• Collaborate with colleagues and stakeholders across disciplines and locations in a global organization.

Driving business value

You have a strong background in designing and implementing automation solutions across a range of software platforms. You are innovative, proactive, and capable of developing automation systems and software that enhance efficiency and create business value.

You bring the following qualifications to the role:

• A degree in computer science, engineering, physics, or a related field.

• Experience with robotics and automation technologies, preferably from a similar or related industry.

• Experience developing near real-time software and solid knowledge of C#. Experience with Python, Docker, and microservice architecture is an advantage.

• Interest in robotics software and technologies, particularly in combination with computer vision applications.

• Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work in a dynamic environment.

• Strong understanding of geometry and spatial reasoning, including the ability to model and calculate physical dimensions, positions, and movements in real-world systems.

We are looking for a Director (or Partner) with a track record of helping leading organisations turn strategy into execution to join our team. We are seeking a commercially driven, delivery-focused leader who can confidently bridge business and technology and bring industry and consulting perpsectives to create real impact for our customers. In this role, you will act as a commercial, professional and cultural leader within our Strategy & Transformation service offering, working closely with the leadership team to strengthen our market position. You'll take ownership of engagements from first conversation to final delivery, shaping the approach, guiding the customer and mobilising the right people to get things done. To be succesful in this role, you will need to be a sharp and credible communicator - both in writing and in person. You will need to be structured and take a high level of ownership. You will combine and balance deep advisory work with driving forward our Strategy & Transformation service offering, helping to define how we work, what we offer, and where we are headed.

What you'll be doing:

• Lead and deliver strategic transformation initiatives across business and IT, from framing the challenge with the customer to mobilising teams and driving execution.

• Advise executives on IT strategy, digitalisation and operating model design.

• Drive strategic prioritisation and enterprise-wide capacity planning, helping customers make hard choices about where to focus and how to sequence change.

• Lead organisational design initiatives, including carve-outs and post-merger integration.

• Build and expand customer relationships through trusted advisory and commercial ownership.

• Turn customer needs into proposals, pitches and new engagements, and develop and grow long-term accounts.

• Contribute to Unify Partner's growth as a company through thought leadership, market positioning and helping shape our Strategy & Transformation service offering.

Qualifications, we hope you will bring

• A minimum of 8+ years working within Strategy & Transformation - either within an external management consulting house or with a mix of industry and consulting experience

• Please note that experience working as an external consultant is a requirement for this role.

• A relevant Master's degree.

• The ability to work in both Danish and English (it's our internal language).

• Deep expertise in strategic transformation planning and execution, portfolio management, prioritisation and operating model design.

• A track record of delivery complex transformation initiatives across a range of different industries, transferring patterns and insights across contexts to create measurable impact.

On top of the hard requirements above, we are seeking a candidate with:

• proven experience in leading teams and developing others

jobs.description:
Implementation Consultant with expertise in social services – Columna Cura

Do you know municipal case management in social services inside out – VUM, FFB, service catalogues, rates and citizens' co-payments – and would you like to help municipalities get the most out of their IT support for social services? Then seize this unique opportunity to put your professional insight to use in a company with high ambitions, and help our customers get the greatest value from Columna Cura!

Join a collaborative and ambitious team

As our new Implementation Consultant, you'll work with Columna Cura, our IT solution for the health and social care sector, which supports staff, citizens and relatives throughout the citizen's entire care journey. The solution is already live in 38 Danish municipalities, and we're growing in social services, where case management, service provision and collaboration between authority and provider place specific demands on how the system is configured and used.

You'll join the Cura Projects & Services team, made up of dedicated colleagues – consultants, solution architects, service developers and more.

The team's main responsibility is project and service delivery, and your tasks will include implementation projects, training and professional guidance on configuration.

Play a key role and contribute to Systematic's growth

As our new Implementation Consultant on Columna Cura, you'll play a key role in helping municipalities get off to a strong start with Cura in social services – and continue to get optimal value from the Cura product suite afterwards. You'll bridge the gap between the municipality's case management practices, providers' needs and the system's setup, translating assessments, service catalogues, rates and workflows between authority and provider into a well-functioning Cura setup.

Your insights from customer dialogue also feed into our product and service development.

Your key tasks will include:

• advising municipalities on how to configure Cura to support case management in social services, including VUM (the Adult Needs Assessment Method) and the process from assessment and decision to service delivery

• setting up and maintaining service catalogues (FFB – Denmark's Common Professional Concepts framework – and municipal services), rates and rules for citizens' co-payments in collaboration with the customer

• supporting collaboration between case workers and internal and external providers in Cura, including ordering, follow-up and billing of services

• training system administrators and super users to use and configure Cura

• producing and maintaining functional documentation that helps customers configure Cura to their needs

• taking part in tender responses for new customers

• working closely with your colleagues in Cura Projects & Services, Product Management and Domain Advisors, and feeding valuable customer insights from social services into our product development

You should expect around five travel days a month to customers in Denmark and Norway.

Put your social services expertise to use

Our new colleague knows social services inside out – either as a social worker with hands-on experience in case management or with providers, or as a system administrator or super user of Columna Cura or a similar IT solution for social services. You're a strong communicator who's motivated by helping others and committed to laying the groundwork for customer success and satisfaction.

We expect you to have in-depth knowledge of municipal case management in social services – particularly the VUM method, FFB and service catalogues, services, rates, citizens' co-payments, and collaboration with internal and external providers. Experience with Columna Cura or a similar specialist system for social services is a strong advantage, but the right professional insight matters more to us than the exact system you know.

It would be a huge plus if you also know the provider side of social services – for example residential care, supported housing, and activity and employment services – and understand how orders, goals, documentation and follow-up move between authority and provider. That understanding is exactly what enables you to help a municipality set up Cura so that case workers and providers work as one connected process.

We also imagine that you:

• can translate legislation and case management practice into concrete system setup and clear guidance for users

• enjoy coordinating and collaborating with customers and stakeholders – from case workers and providers to system owners and management

are proactive and take the initiative

• speak and write Danish and English fluently - Non Danish Speakers need not apply

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO/EU country for the past seven years as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

Welcome to Systematic Aarhus

At our Aarhus office, you can look forward to joining our Employees Club, which offers nearly 100 social/professional events a year. Here, you can take advantage of a range of on-site perks from physiotherapist-led massages and an in-house hairdresser to sports clubs, games tables and even our own padel court. Our canteen is a standout feature, serving a daily selection of delicious and healthy dishes. Beyond the office, you will also enjoy benefits like free ARoS +1 access and various shopping discounts.

Never stop developing

Systematic is truly international, proudly Danish and uniquely people-centric. Together, we write intelligent and innovative code to drive progress and improve lives. We develop IT solutions that make a real difference where it matters most – this is why we never stop developing. Here, there is room to be professional and personal. Systematic is not just a place to work but a place to belong.

You can look forward to joining our Employees Club, which offers almost 100 events of both social and professional character a year, so there is plenty to choose from. Our colleagues also highlight our canteen, which serves a variety of delicious and healthy dishes each day. In addition, we offer several employee benefits such as paid Home Internet, health insurance and a company pension scheme. Finally, we are always up for a friendly game of padel at our new padel court in Aarhus!

Start your development here

We will be assessing applications on an ongoing basis as we wish to welcome our new colleague as soon as possible, so click Apply Now and send us your CV today. If you have any questions, you are always welcome to contact us on tel. +45 8943 2000 and ask for Mette Skylvad, Program Manager.

Imagine working with cutting-edge machine learning models, crunching high frequency data sets and sparring with exceptional and fun colleagues, all while taking part in scaling our business even further.

Does this sound highly appealing to you? Then you might be our new Senior Quantitative Researcher in the Equity Statistical Arbitrage wing of Alipes Capital!

At Alipes Capital, we have been a market leader in equity and electricity algorithmic trading since starting in 2008.

This position is focused on

Elevating our predictive modeling standards to the highest levels in the area of statistical arbitrage of traded funds.

Creating a world class modeling workflow, enabling the team to turn massive data sets of financial information into mathematical models that accurately predict movements in the markets.

In doing so, you will get a chance to tackle a variety of software infrastructure challenges, such as:

• 
Development and optimization of calibration and benchmarking frameworks.

• 
Building out and implementing best practices for data preparation and dataset generation pipelines.

Prototyping and releasing novel predictive architectures, especially with respect to time-series models.

A scientific and inquisitive mind.

Programming experience with languages like C# and C/C++.

PhD or MSc degree in engineering, physics, computer science, mathematics or economics.

A valued role with unique responsibilities and plenty of room for creativity.

3Shape are creating a new role in R&D for an experienced Wi-Fi specialist to help ensure reliable, high-performance wireless connectivity for our scanner systems. Job Description

We’re looking for a senior full-stack engineer with a strong interest in building AI-first products who enjoys owning problems end-to-end – from vague client needs and early hypotheses to production-grade systems that actually get used.

What you’ll do

You’ll join The Tech Collective (our Data & AI hub, specifically), where we help organisations design, build, and operationalise data- and AI-driven solutions.

This role is tailor-made for a systems thinker and builder – someone who has shipped real products, taken responsibility for technical direction, and is motivated by creating pragmatic solutions that combine data, software, and AI.

You’ll work closely with experienced AI specialists who bring deep model and ML expertise, while you focus on building robust products and software around those capabilities.

Your responsibilities will include:

• End-to-end solution ownership: designing and implementing full-stack applications from early concepts and prototypes to scalable, production-grade systems, including architecture decisions across frontend, backend, data, and cloud

• Modern full-stack development: building high-quality frontend and backend services, applying sound software engineering principles, and using AI-assisted development tools thoughtfully and critically

• AI-enabled product building: collaborating with AI specialists to integrate LLMs, retrieval pipelines, and agentic patterns into real products, and translating AI potential into solutions that make sense for organisations

• Data and systems thinking: designing data models, reasoning about distributed systems and trade-offs, and implementing event-driven or real-time features where they add value

• Observability and evaluation: experience setting up the right observability and eval tooling to establish traceability and iteratively improve on products

• Cloud, delivery, and collaboration: deploying and operating solutions in cloud environments, balancing speed, robustness, and security, and working closely with clients and stakeholders to create tangible business impact

What you’ll bring

We’re looking for someone with an AI builder mentality and 5+ years of hands-on full-stack experience, who is comfortable owning applications end to end – from frontend and backend to data and deployment.

You don’t need to tick every box, but you should recognise yourself in most of the following:

• Strong full-stack foundation: solid skills in TypeScript and/or Python, with experience building and shipping production systems

• Mentoring experience: helping other developers through technical sparring and code reviews

• Outward curiosity: actively seeking to understand client problems in detail and working in close collaboration with them to solve them

• Ownership and leadership: a track record of building substantial solutions from scratch (e.g., startup, scale-up, or personal ventures), taking responsibility for outcomes, and leading technical direction without relying on formal authority

• System-level thinking: the ability to reason about architecture, data flows, trade-offs, and failure modes across the stack, and to make pragmatic decisions in ambiguous contexts

• Critical technical judgement: a keen eye for identifying weaknesses in existing architectures and tech stacks, and knowing where and how to improve them

• Communication and collaboration: the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders, work across disciplines, and learn from – and share knowledge with – others in the team and across Implement

• Tool agnostic: capable of choosing the right tool for the job

What we offer

We offer a role with technical ownership and influence, working in a 20-person team that feels much closer to a nerdy startup than a large corporation – while being firmly backed by Implement Consulting Group.

You’ll gain exposure to a wide range of data- and AI-driven problems across industries, all within a culture built on trust, curiosity, humility, resilience, and impact. You’ll also have great freedom to shape your own role, deepen your expertise, and grow in exactly the direction that motivates you.

Ready to shape the digital future with us? Apply ASAP.

About The Tech Collective

The Tech Collective is a fast-growing consulting company powered by Implement Consulting Group. We aim to make a positive difference in the consulting industry, believing that the ability to create change with impact and purpose is a prerequisite for success in a global and turbulent world.

We’re expanding our team and look forward to meeting talented people who are curious about a career in information systems and management consulting at the intersection of business and technology.

We're looking for an experienced Microsoft Purview specialist with a proven track record of delivering compliance projects for clients who’s ready to own and develop our Purview capability as the agentic landscape evolves.

What you'll do

You'll be the person who drives the Purview agenda on behalf of an ambitious team, working across industries with organisations that are serious about data security and compliance.

In this role, you'll own:

• 
Design, deployment, and optimisation of Microsoft Purview solutions, including Data Classification, Information Protection, Data Loss Prevention, and Insider Risk Management

• 
Development of data protection policies, automation workflows, and compliance reporting tailored to client requirements

• 
Assessment and reporting on the maturity of client data security and compliance deployments

• 
Definition and creation of operational and executive compliance dashboards and reports

• 
Integration activities across Microsoft Purview and the broader Microsoft 365 compliance ecosystem

You'll also collaborate closely with other engineers on the team, contribute to R&D activities, and support managed service customers in maintaining and maturing their data security practices.

What you'll bring

We're looking for someone with at least three years of hands-on experience enabling security and compliance technologies in a Microsoft environment. Beyond that, you'll bring:

• 
Strong experience with Microsoft Purview across Data Classification, Information Protection, DLP, and Insider Risk Management

• 
Hands-on experience implementing sensitivity labels, retention policies, and DLP rules

• 
Knowledge of data governance principles within the Microsoft ecosystem

• 
Current Microsoft certifications in compliance and security – or a willingness to obtain them within 90 days

• 
Strong communication skills and confidence in client-facing settings

We don't expect you to know everything. Purview and the agentic space are moving fast, and that's part of what makes this role interesting. What matters most is that you want to own it.

To be a great fit for The Tech Collective, it will be a bonus if you bring:

Knowledge of LLMs and agentic workflows, including cybersecurity risk considerations

• 
Understanding of Zero Trust principles as applied to data security

• 
Experience with risk assessment methodologies and compliance reporting

• 
Microsoft Certified: Information Protection Administrator Associate, Security Administrator Associate, or equivalent

What we offer

On top of a competitive salary and bonus package, you'll join a tight team of experts and enthusiasts who take both craft and collaboration seriously. We invest in your development – through training, conferences, and the space to pursue research in areas you're passionate about.

We combine remote work with meaningful co-working at our offices in Copenhagen and will provide you with the tooling and hardware required to reach our goal of building a unique red team platform.

For questions, contact Anders Rømer Skøtt at anrs@thetechcollective.eu or +45 31717487.

Job Description

Would you like to shape Denmark’s pension solutions of tomorrow? As our new Consultant, you’ll use your actuarial expertise to turn complex models and business logic into tangible solutions, creating value for clients and society. Join a major IT project and turn theory into practice.

Responsibilities

As a Consultant within the life and pensions industry, you will become part of a specialised team contributing to the development of a new, unified IT system for pension solutions in Denmark.

You will work at the intersection of deep expertise in actuarial mathematics and technical implementation in a dynamic, and ambitious environment. Your expertise will be at the heart of our work, and you will see your analyses, business insights, and models create direct value for our clients and their businesses. Your work will involve developing and implementing complex calculation models and ensuring that solutions meet both business and regulatory requirements.

In addition, you will gain broad insight into different companies within the pensions industry and develop expertise in delivering large-scale IT projects. You will work closely with actuaries and pension experts at our clients and contribute to building actuarial and pension-specific capabilities at Netcompany.

Your responsibilities will typically include:

• 
Developing and implementing calculation models for life and pension products.

• 
Quality assurance and testing of pension products, as well as bridging the gap between actuarial expertise and technical implementation.

• 
Ensuring that solutions comply with applicable legislation and standards.

• 
Communicating complex analyses and results to colleagues, developers, testers, and clients.

• 
Contributing to the design and customisation of insurance and pension products within our solutions.

Are you the one who brings structure when things get complex, and who walks over to ask why something has stalled rather than waiting for an email? Then you might be the Student Assistant we are looking for!

At JYSK, our Operational Centre of Excellence helps teams across IT and the business units it supports work in more stable and measurable ways. We are looking for a Student Assistant for 15 hours a week to work with data and stakeholder coordination at JYSK Head Office in Aarhus.

You start as soon as we have found the right candidate. For the first six weeks you work about one day a week, then 15 hours a week over two days, with at least one of them at the office. We start with a three-month contract and hope you stay at least 12 months. We are flexible around exams and holidays.

WHAT WE OFFER YOU

You work directly with the Manager of IT Operational Excellence and get real responsibility from day one. Within your first three months, you will have delivered your first piece of reporting that the IT leadership team uses.

Furthermore, we offer you:

• Insight into how IT operations and continuous improvement work in an international retailer with more than 3,700 stores in 49 countries, more than 35,000 colleagues and an IT organisation of more than 400 people

• Room to shape your own role - this is a new area we are designing, and what you lean into will help define it

• A dedicated mentor, regular sparring and a network across IT that few students get

• Hands-on experience with ITIL, Lean, structured change management and the agile framework SAFe, which is how our teams work

• The option to use real cases for projects or your thesis

• Flexible hours that fit your studies and exams

• Engaged colleagues, a lunch programme with healthy and varied meals, and Friday bars

WHAT YOUR NEXT JOB WILL BE ABOUT

You help us turn improvements into results, and most of that happens in conversation with people. Your tasks and responsibilities in the job include:

• Data and insight: Collect and analyse data, build dashboards, and explain what the numbers show and how our initiatives are working.

• Following up on improvement actions: Keep track of our actions, check with the owners that they are delivered, and find out why when something stalls.

• Making larger initiatives easy to join: One example is our CMDB, a map of how applications and servers connect. You create templates, plan the steps with the teams and help remove what blocks them.

• Working with people: Talk to colleagues instead of hiding behind the screen. Join a stand-up, send a Slack message or walk over, and make it easy for people to help.

WHAT SHOULD YOU BRING

You do not need experience. We are looking for a new colleague who:

• Is curious about data and what it tells you, with Excel as a good starting point

• Enjoys bringing structure to messy tasks

• Likes talking to people and following up until things get done

• Is motivated to learn, not least how IT runs a large retail business

• Is enrolled in a relevant higher education programme with at least 12 months of studies left

• Communicates fluently in English. Danish is a plus

• Can be at the office in Aarhus at least one day a week

jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Civil and Architectural Engineering programme. The position is available from 1 February 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title:
AI-augmented Physiological Modelling for Prediction and Mitigation of Heat Stress in Pigs

Research area and project description:
Heat stress is an increasing challenge to pig production and animal welfare, particularly during hot seasons. Effective mitigation requires not only the detection of elevated heat load, but also the ability to predict how animals respond dynamically and to determine when and how cooling interventions should be applied. Existing mechanistic thermal models provide an important basis for representing animal heat balance and physiological responses. However, their ability to incorporate real-time physiological observations, account for model assumptions and environmental stochasticity, and support timely intervention decisions remains limited. At the same time, purely data-driven black-box approaches are challenging to develop and validate when high-quality physiological datasets are limited, as is often the case in controlled animal experiments.

This PhD project aims to develop a physics-informed digital model for predicting and mitigating heat stress in pigs. Building on conventional mechanistic models of pig physiological responses, the project will investigate how physiological modelling can be combined with AI approaches to develop a more robust and interpretable representation of the pig’s thermal state. To further enhance the accessibility and practical use of the model, the project will also explore how large language models (LLMs) can be integrated with the physiological model to facilitate interactive exploration of model behaviour and predictions.

Qualifications and specific competences:
We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with:
• A MSc degree in Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, or Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or related filed.
• A strong academic background and interest in HVAC systems in buildings, and fluid and thermal systems modelling.
• Proven experience in data analytics, machine learning, and optimisation.
• Ability to program using Python, R, MATLAB or similar platforms.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in interdisciplinary teams.
• Excellent written and spoken English skills.It is considered an advantage if you have:
• Knowledge of animal heat stress and animal welfare.
• Knowledge of Large Language Model, stochastic modelling, system identification.
• Experience with CFD simulations.
Place of employment and place of work:
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering, Inge Lehmanns Gade 10, 8000 Aarhus C., Denmark.

jobs.description:
Are you a collaborative and ambitious master's graduate with strong intercultural awareness and a curiosity for exploring sustainability challenges across different contexts and disciplines? Would you like to help shape the next generation of sustainable and regenerative global supply chains through a unique collaboration between the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) and the University of Nairobi, Kenya? DTU Management (Department of Technology, Management, and Economics) invites applications for a three-year PhD scholarship at the intersection of supply chain management and organization studies. Focusing on global agricultural commodity chains, the project explores how supply chains can create positive environmental and social impacts rather than simply reducing negative ones. It examines regenerative approaches that renew ecological and social systems while being collectively organized with local communities.

The PhD position is anchored at DTU Management and contributes to the department's strategic focus on developing viable and sustainable systems. You will join an international research environment at the forefront of sustainable supply chain management and organization studies, collaborating with researchers and partners in Denmark and Kenya. The project combines literature-based and empirical research on regenerative agri-food supply chains with fieldwork and data collection in Denmark and Kenya. The project will be supervised by Associate Professor Lærke Højgaard Christiansen and Assistant Professor Lara Schilling at DTU and will include an extended research stay at the University of Nairobi under the co-supervision of Senior Lecturer Thomas Ombati and Lecturer Veronica Wambui Mwangi. 

Based in Copenhagen – consistently ranked among the world's most livable cities – you will enjoy a high quality of life, a safe and sustainable urban environment, and a thriving cultural scene. At the same time, you'll be part of a vibrant, interdisciplinary research community at one of Europe's top technical universities, known for its commitment to innovation, societal impact, and diversity.

Responsibilities and qualifications
As a PhD candidate, you will investigate how global agricultural commodity chains, such as tea or coffee, can be managed based on regenerative principles. The project offers a unique opportunity to develop an international and interdisciplinary research profile at the intersection of organization studies and supply chain management. As part of the DTU Management PhD Program, you will follow a structured research and training program that combines independent research, academic coursework, teaching, and professional development.

Mandatory requirements:

• You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.
• An educational background in the social sciences 
• A familiarity with supply chain management, organization studies, or related fields such as (human) geography
• Have a strong interest in sustainability, regenerative systems, and the organization of global supply chains
• Strong speaking and writing skills in English
Further, the following qualities will be valued highly in the assessment:

• Research vision and potential 
• Evidence of academic accomplishment (e.g., high grades, timely graduation)
• Knowledge and experience with qualitative research methods and empirical fieldwork 
• Scholarly/academic writing skills

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarships in Economics at the Department of Economics, University of Southern Denmark
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for one fully funded PhD scholarship at the Department of Economics, University of Southern Denmark. The position is based at SDU’s Esbjerg campus.

The successful candidate will be enrolled in the 5+3 PhD programme. The programme includes a research stay abroad, typically of six months’ duration, and offers a competitive full-time salary.

We aim to appoint the successful candidate as soon as possible, ideally with a start date of 15 January 2027, while remaining flexible regarding the exact timing.

About the Department and Research Environment

The Department of Economics is an international department with a strong tradition of excellence in research and teaching across a wide range of fields within economics. Research, teaching, and outreach activities are organized within five research groups: Econometrics and Data Science; Economic History; Macroeconomics; Microeconomics; and Environmental and Resource Economics. Further information about the department and its research groups is available on the department website.

The PhD student will be affiliated with the Environmental and Resource Economics (ERE) group, which focuses on Environmental and Natural resource economics on a variety of topics, namely ecosystem conservation and use, marine resource use, management and conservation, energy transitions, climate regulation, and interdisciplinary research at the interface between economics and the natural sciences. The group applies economic theory and tools to policy and analysis to provide guidance for more efficient use of environmental and natural resource goods and services.

The position

The successful candidate will become part of an international research environment and work closely with Associate Professors Ana Faria Lopes and Melina Kourantidou.  Part of the work will contribute to the BRAVE (Biological Invasions Resolved through Adaptable, Versatile, and Engaging Nature-Based Solutions) project, a Biodiversa+ -funded project that investigates the complex ecological and societal challenges associated with invasive species and their management. In particular, the research will contribute to the Danish BRAVE case study on the invasive Pacific oyster in the Wadden Sea, including work on stakeholder preferences, economic values, and trade-offs associated with its management. For further information about the project, please see this link or this link.

The project relies on the application of economic theories, namely non-market valuation and bioeconomic modelling, to investigate the management of invasive species. We welcome candidates with strong quantitative and analytical skills from economics or related disciplines, including candidates with interdisciplinary backgrounds and an interest in environmental and resource management.  There will be considerable scope for the PhD student to develop their own research questions within the broader themes of the project.

The successful candidate is expected to contribute to high-quality research within the scope of the project, through both collaborative research and independent work, including a single-authored paper. In addition, the candidate will be involved in teaching and supervision within economics at both undergraduate and graduate levels.

The PhD student will be supervised by Associate Professor Ana Faria Lopes as the main supervisor and will join a research group that includes postdoctoral researcher and research assistants, with access to an international network of collaborators.

Applicants’ profile

Applicants should have completed a relevant master’s degree in Environmental and Resource Management, Economics, Mathematics and Economics, or related disciplines. Furthermore, we expect applicants to:

• 
Have solid quantitative and analytical skills, with experience in data analysis and applied quantitative methods using R, Stata, or similar tools, and be eager to learn and apply new methods.

• 
Be dedicated, capable of working independently and collaboratively as part of a research team.

• 
Have strong English skills, both spoken and written. 

• 
Have willingness to participate in stakeholder engagement activities and communicate research findings to different audiences. 

• 
Have good interpersonal skills, be interested in engaging with national and international researchers.

The following qualifications are an advantage

• 
Have an interest in, or potentially experience with, non-market valuation, press analysis, GIS and/or bioeconomic modelling.

• 
Experience conducting empirical research.

• 
Demonstrated interest in environmental and resource economics.

• 
Knowledge of Danish or another Scandinavian language would be an advantage for stakeholder engagement and work with locally relevant material but is not a requirement.

We are an international department, and the working language is English.

Further information about the position can be obtained from Head of Administration Astrid Holm Nielsen, e-mail: astni@sam.sdu.dk. For general questions regarding relocation, housing, taxes etc., contact the SDU’s International Staff Office. 

How to apply for this position

Employment as a paid PhD fellow takes place in accordance with the circular of 20 December 2021 on the collective agreement for academics in the state – appendix 5, protocol on PhD fellowships.

For more information on the department guidelines for qualification and recruitment please see our Appointment Guidelines.

The application must include (all attachments must be in Adobe PDF format): 

• 
Detailed CV - the education and work history must be month and year specific.

• 
A certified copy of your master’s degree certificate, including transcripts of all examination results.  Foreign diplomas that are not in Norwegian, Swedish or English must be accompanied by a translation into Danish or English, as well as a translation of the official description of the marking scale used.

• 
A motivational letter describing why the applicant is a good match for analyzing the topic and how the applicant’s skills provide a solid foundation to do so (max. 5 pages incl. reference list).

• 
A project description (max 5 pages of 2400 characters each, including spaces, notes, appendices, bibliography etc.).

• 
When applying for a PhD scholarship, please fill in the application form available on our web page. 

On the webpage of the PhD-school, you can find the guidelines for preparing your project proposal.

All non-Danish documents must be translated into English.

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material.

Once the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicant will receive the portion of the evaluation that pertains to them.

Applications that are incomplete regarding the above requirements will not be assessed by the committee.

Shortlisting and tests may be used in the assessment process.

As part of the overall assessment of the applicant’s qualifications, an interview may be applied.

Documents should not contain a CPR number (civil registration number) – in this case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

The application and CV must not exceed 10 MB.

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, 23.59 CET/CEST.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now" on our website. Uploaded files must be in Adobe PDF (unlocked) or Word format.

We recommend that you read the guideline for applicants. If you experience technical problems, you must contact hcm-support@sdu.dk before the application deadline.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

Salary and employment terms

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements.

As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process.

SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.

We're looking for our 4th team member!

Do you thrive creating structure in chaos?

Would you like to be a part of shaping the data infrastructure in a growing startup?

Does your Python code run like a well oiled machine, handling massive datasets with ease?

Then proprty.ai might be just the place for you!

The Product

We're building an exciting product to help property owners maintain buildings in a timely, cost-effective, and sustainable manner. We integrate public and private data sources, statistical models, and AI to deliver a modern consumer grade user experience in our app.

The software we’re building includes tools for condition assessment of individual building parts on a property, gathering public data for a building portfolio overview and creating ML & AI models for predicting remaining lifespan and forecasting maintenance cost.

The product went live in 2024, and is solving real problems for real people, and there's SO many things we can do to make it even better!

About you

We won't pretend there's a perfect checklist, but here's who we imagine joining us:

• 
You have a couple of years of professional experience building data pipelines, backend services, or similar setups.

• 
You take personal pride in your work. You want your work to matter.

• 
You're a startup type more than a corporate type: you prefer short decision paths over steering committees, you'd rather ask "why not?" than wait for a mandate, and you're comfortable when the answer to "who owns this?" is sometimes "you do, as of now".

• 
You create structure rather than wait for it. Ambiguity doesn't paralyze you.

About Us

The team consists of three people, two Data Scientists and one Data Engineer, working closely with our app team of five. We’re looking for a Backend Developer/Data Engineer to join us in developing and optimizing our data pipelines, backend services, and integrations. Most of our setup is in Databricks on Azure, using Python and SQL for the tasks.

We're expanding into Norway, the Netherlands, Germany and Switzerland, and we need more hands on creating a globalized and scalable setup for the years to come!

The job

Our team is creating an analytics heavy backend both serving the development and implementation of AI & ML models, and providing foundational data for our app team.

You’ll be the second in proprty.ai in this specific area of expertise and should have at least a couple of years of experience from developing similar setups.

Your main responsibilities will be:

• 
To evaluate and improve our tech-stack, database structure, and data flow.

• 
Creating structured data using a collection of data from multiple sources.

• 
Integrating new data sources in the current data flow.

• 
Ensuring that data pipelines run flawlessly.

• 
Connect our database and data science setup to both our frontend and external systems.

• 
Develop API integrations

• 
Help drive tech and AI adoption across the teams in proprty.ai

Most of the tasks above should be familiar to you.

proprty.ai is building a service to help Danish property managers leverage machine learning technology to create better condition assessments and maintenance plans. We're creating an AI powered web platform, that allows property managers to create condition assessments and maintenance plans in a fraction of the time they're using today, by mixing output from our machine learning models with boots on the ground input. jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in High-Speed Hyperspectral and Super-Resolution Terahertz Imaging - DTU Electro
jobs.description:
Are you interested in pushing terahertz (THz) imaging beyond today’s limits in speed, bandwidth, and spatial resolution? 

At DTU Electro, you will work at the interface of ultrafast THz photonics, nonlinear optical detection, coherent imaging, and machine learning to develop a new generation of high-speed hyperspectral THz imaging technology.

The PhD project is part of the DFF-funded INSPIRING project (High-speed hyperspectral and super-resolution terahertz imaging). INSPIRING will combine broadband THz-to-near-infrared upconversion with CMOS-array detection to enable high-speed THz imaging. Your main role will be to establish the imaging platform and develop hyperspectral and machine-learning methods for super-resolution imaging and material identification.

You will work in an international, interdisciplinary team at DTU Electro. The project includes a planned 3–6-month research stay in Prof. Xi-Cheng Zhang’s group at the University of Rochester, USA.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your research will focus on high-speed coherent THz imaging with machine learning. 

You will:

• Develop and operate a broadband coherent THz imaging platform using optical rectification and/or laser-induced plasma THz sources.
• Implement wide-field imaging based on THz-to-NIR upconversion and CMOS focal-plane-array detection.
• Acquire and analyze time-domain hyperspectral THz data with a target bandwidth above 10 THz.
• Apply machine-learning methods, including CNN and autoencoder-type architectures, for super-resolution reconstruction and material identification.
• Study semiconductors, polymers, multilayer structures, and industrial test samples, and collaborate with project partners in Denmark and abroad. 
• Publish your results in peer-reviewed journals and present them at international conferences.
We are looking for a highly motivated and curious candidate with a strong background in experimental photonics, optics, applied physics, electrical engineering, or a closely related field. Experience with THz spectroscopy, ultrafast laser systems, nonlinear optics, or optical imaging is highly desirable. Experience with scientific programming, data analysis, image processing, or machine learning will be considered an advantage. You should have a strong interest in experimental research and be comfortable working with complex optical setups as well as analyzing large multidimensional datasets. We value creativity, independent problem-solving, and the ability to work effectively in an interdisciplinary and international research environment. You should also have good communication skills and be able to present and communicate your scientific results clearly in written and spoken English.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Associate Professor Binbin Zhou, Professor Peter Uhd Jepsen, and Associate Professor Francesco Da Ros. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures. 

The period of employment is 3 years. The start date is 1 January 2027 (or by mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Binbin Zhou at zhou@dtu.dk. 

You can read more about DTU Electro at www.electro.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 30 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Electro  
DTU Electro employs more than 300 skilled researchers with competencies in electrical and photonics engineering. As a department, we strive towards creating sustainable energy and a greener internet, as well as strengthening cyber security and health technology. Working with industry and public organizations is one of our top priorities to find and implement new solutions to our society. We aim to offer education, research, and innovation of the highest standard, and our focus on application-oriented research enables us to work across many engineering disciplines and research areas, such as IT and the medical and health sciences. We have a close collaboration with researchers from all over the world, just as we collaborate with industry and public authorities about the dissemination of solutions based on electrical and photonics engineering as their key enabling technologies. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.
