jobs.occupation: Postdoc position in the intellectual history of corporate politics
jobs.description:
Copenhagen Business School invites applications for a postdoc position in the field of the intellectual history of corporate politics at the Department of Business Humanities and Law. The expected starting date is 1 May, 2027 or as agreed upon by consultation. The postdoc position is a non-tenured full-time position of 2 years, with the possibility of 1 additional year of teaching obligations.

The research will be conducted as part of the Independent Research Fund Denmark Sapere Aude Grant project Visions of corporate politics: Intellectual histories of the state-firm analogy. The project team will consist of the PI, one postdoc and one PhD.
Read more about the project here: https://dff.dk/en/our-funded-projects/meet-the-researchers/research-leaders/eksterne-personer-en/research-leaders-2025/mathias-hein-jessen/

The central objective of the research project is to analyze contemporary contestations over the state-firm boundary as well as mobilizations of analogies between state and firm in projecting political and economic visions. The project analyzes the constitution of the state-firm distinction as well as what it terms contemporary ‘visions of corporate politics’ represented by ideologically distinct answers to the crisis of liberal democracy which both contest the state-firm boundary and mobilize the state-firm analogy to legitimize their vision: On the one hand attempts to democratize or politicize the firm and on the other hand attempts to build political communities on principles of corporate governance. The postdoc project will focus on one of the two contemporary visions of corporate politics.

Examples of potential research topics: the democratization of the firm; democratic or economic planning; employee ownership; platform cooperativism or socialism; network states; gov-corps; start-up governments; freedom cities.

The research conducted will be team-based and oriented towards delivering on the project objectives. Taking the project framework into consideration, applicants are required to outline their reflections on how to approach the study.

The position is mainly in-place. The candidate should be able to be regularly present and attend meetings in Copenhagen.

For more information about the position, please contact PI of the project Associate Professor Mathias Hein Jessen (mhj.bhl@cbs.dk). 

Research environment
The Department of Business Humanities and Law is dedicated to an integrated approach to the contemporary challenges facing business and society drawing on the humanities, interdisciplinary social sciences, and law. The core research areas of the Department of Business Humanities and Law are organized into different research Units: Governance, Culture and Learning; Entrepreneurship, Ethics and Leadership; and CBS Law. Faculty within these groups have research backgrounds in areas of political science, sociology, philosophy, history, anthropology, law, theology, aesthetics, design and innovation, tourism and leisure management, cultural economics, leadership and strategy, pedagogic study, and other areas. What unites faculty in our department is an overriding concern for the organization of the human within its multiple environments: work, nature, economy, civil association, the state, and corporation. 

Teaching responsibilities of the Department comprise undergraduate and graduate teaching as well as teaching in post-experience and doctoral education. Some programs are taught in Danish, some in English.

Within the Department of Business Humanities and Law, the position will be located in the Governance, Culture and Learning Unit, an interdisciplinary research environment connecting governance studies at all levels of global society. 

Qualifications
The ideal candidate will have completed a PhD in intellectual history, history, political sociology, political theory or political philosophy. The candidate will be committed to an academic career, have the capabilities to conduct internationally recognized research and be able to communicate findings clearly. 

The assessment of the candidate will be based primarily on the following qualifications:

• Excellent academic track record
• Research within the history of political, economic or legal thought, political theory, or political philosophy.
• The ability and desire to work autonomously and as part of a team
• Excellent organizational and communication skills (both oral and written); proficiency in English is required
• Ability to engage with others in a way that reflects a collective commitment to diversity, equality, and inclusion. 
The application (see link below) must include a 3-5-page project description. The project description must include:

• a presentation of an original research question
• a description of the initial theoretical framework and method
• a presentation of the proposed material
• a work plan for the project
Application procedure
All applications must be sent via the electronic recruitment system, using the link below. The application must include:

A complete, numbered list of publications and work in progress (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review.

The application must include:

• Cover letter outlining motivation, fit, and qualifications
• A project description
• Transcripts (Master's and PhD) and a full CV
• A complete, numbered list of publications (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review. A maximum of 5 publications for review is allowed. Applicants are requested to prioritise their publications in relation to the field of this job advertisement.
• Copies of the publications marked with an *. Only publications written in English (or another specified principal language, according to research tradition) or one of the Scandinavian languages will be taken into consideration)
• Any relevant information indicating experience in research management, industry co-operation, and international cooperation.
• Documentation of pedagogical qualifications or related material.
Closing date: 15 December 2026

Recruitment procedure
The Recruitment Committee will shortlist a minimum of two applicants. If possible, five or more applicants will be shortlisted. The shortlisted applicants will be assessed by the Assessment Committee. All applicants will be notified of their status in the recruitment process shortly after the application deadline. The applicants selected for assessment will be notified about the composition of the Assessment Committee and later in the process about the result of the assessment. An appointment committee will invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview. Once the recruitment process is completed each applicant will be notified of the outcome of their application.

Appointment
Appointment and salary will be in accordance with the Ministry of Finance’s agreement with the Central Academic Organization. Information about CBS as a workplace is available at www.cbs.dk/en/about-cbs/jobs-cbs. 

For further information, please contact: PI of the project Associate Professor Mathias Hein Jessen, email: mhj.bhl@cbs.dk, or Head of Department Pia Bramming, e-mail pib.bhl@cbs.dk. Information about the department may be found at www.cbs.dk/bhl. Information about Copenhagen Business School is available at https://www.cbs.dk/en.

Copenhagen Business School must receive all application material, including all appendices (see items above), by the application deadline.

Copenhagen Business School invites all qualified candidates to apply for the position. An appointment committee will review the applications and invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview.

One of CBS’ strategic goals is the promotion of diversity, which is why every effort has been made to ensure a recruitment process that reduces potential bias. Applicants are therefore encouraged not to include a photo or unnecessary personal information in their application.

Details about Copenhagen Business School and the department are available at www.cbs.dk.

Design for the people in the tiny chairs

At Famly, we build software that takes admin off the plates of early-years educators, so they can spend their time where it matters - with the children. And we make it easier for over a million parents to stay close to their child's day, even while they're at work.

We're looking for a design system builder to join the design team - responsible for the design system, prototyping tools and all other infrastructure with the goal of driving consistency and coherence across the entire product.

About Famly

We’re on a mission to stop admin stealing the joy of working with young children. We do that with our platform, the world’s first proactive assistant for educators and staff that handles admin for them so they can get back to what they love. And we do it with our content (like The Tiny Chair Podcast), reminding educators of the joy and meaning that got them into working with children in the first place.

About the role

You live where design and code meet. With a small team, you'll own Famly's design system: the components, patterns, and documentation that product teams (and increasingly, AI agents) build on every day.

The team's job is coherence. Every feature and every domain should feel like it came from the same place. You'll give builders what they need to design and build to our standards, and keep the conversation going so the system keeps getting better.

You'll bring deep technical knowledge of design systems, and you'll care just as much about how the product feels to the people using it.

The team is based in our Copenhagen office, but we are open to you being based somewhere else.

What you'll be doing

• 
Build production-quality React and TypeScript components for Famly's design system.

• 
Design component APIs that are hard to misuse, and version them so upgrades don't break product teams.

• 
Write the documentation that makes those components self-serve, so a new engineer or an AI agent can pick one up and use it correctly without asking anyone.

• 
Keep the system trustworthy: tests, visual regression, and a release process people don't dread.

• 
Learn Famly's frontend deeply enough to know where a pattern lives, who depends on it, and what breaks if it changes.

• 
Audit and evolve the components we already have, for consistency, accessibility, and reuse across the product.

• 
Own the code side of the design standard with a small team, so design intent survives the trip into production.

• 
Push back when a design won't hold up in code - too many states, no empty case, a pattern that already exists - and say what you'd do instead.

• 
Work with PMs, designers, and engineers across product teams, and bring them ideas before they ask.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

• 
You have 5+ years of frontend experience in B2B SaaS, including design system work.

• 
You're strong in React, TypeScript, and CSS.

• 
You have taste for craft: spacing, motion, states, and the details that make a component feel finished.

• 
You think in systems: reusable, documented, maintainable components over one-off fixes.

• 
You get from a rough idea to a working prototype fast.

• 
You own your work end to end, from discovery through testing to shipping.

• 
You care about the difference between "works" and "is right," and you'll say so and set the direction.

The interview process looks like:

• 
Short meet and greet with Lead People Partner

• 
A logical test

• 
1st interview: Meet and greet with our Senior Director of Product Design

• 
Take-home assignment

• 
2nd interview: Assignment presentation with Senior Director of Product Design and Lead Designer

And who are Famly?

You’re probably wondering at this stage, and Famly are...? Well, it all began when our co-founder Henrik’s daughter was ready to start at daycare. He couldn’t believe the amount of work being done on paper - and how distant he felt from his first child during the day. The paper ‘parent’ books they exchanged once a month just weren’t cutting it. Together with his friend, our co-founder and CEO Anders, they set about solving that.

These days, about 180 of us build Famly for more than 10,000 institutions and over 1 million parents.

We handle admin stress so they can get back to what matters, and we make it easier than ever to connect home, and nursery so parents can play a part in their child’s day. If you join us, you’ll be building, selling, or support customers with everything from staff rotas and invoices, to child development and parent communication.

How we work

Famly prides itself on a few principles; we choose simplicity, we believe friendliness is a superpower, we set the pace, and we want everyone to be surrounded by talent.

It all adds up to a culture that refuses to make employees choose between a place that is ambitious and sets the pace for what good looks like - and one that is a nice place to work. We think you can be ambitious and kind and when you get to meet our team, we hope you’ll agree.

What we expect of you, is that you make others shine, that you believe in being better than yesterday, and you are not afraid to just ‘get it done’. Finally, we want you to value ‘sitting in the tiny chair’ - which means you look at your work through the impact it has on our customers: the people sitting in tiny chairs in childcare settings all over the world.

What’s in it for you?

• 
Competitive pension, private health insurance, and paid maternity/paternity leave.

• 
A clear career framework and coaching to make sure you’re growing, a $1000 personal development budget and a ‘We’ll buy you any book you want’ policy.

• 
We guarantee we’ll create the time, space and leadership (as well as the budget) to make sure you grow and develop.

• 
We want to set the pace, and don't cut corners when it comes to investing in tooling and technology that you need to be at the frontier of tech.

• 
We’re all about hiring clever people who are good humans too. It means Famly is full of top thinkers and generous teammates waiting to help you shine.

• 
We like to give a lot of ownership both in terms of responsibility and freedom to try new, challenging tasks.

• 
Top-notch work equipment (including noise cancelling headphones for those focus periods!).

• 
We believe collaboration happens best in person, so we have the default of four days a week in office - but with plenty of flexibility for when life happens outside the office too.

We're looking to fill the position as soon as possible, so get your application in today by sending us:

Your CV

Short and precise cover letter to tell us what you can bring to the role

• 
Portfolio (attached or linked) showcasing your work

Looking forward to hearing from you!

The Aarhus Institute of Advanced Studies (AIAS) is pleased to announce an exclusive fellowship opportunity for a researcher who holds a position at a Swedish research institution. The fellowship is made possible through a collaboration with Riksbankens Jubileumsfond in Sweden.The purpose of the AIAS-RJ fellowship is to strengthen the ties and expand collaborations between the Swedish and Danish research communities.

Why apply for an AIAS-RJ Fellowship

AIAS is a haven for intellectual exploration, hosting excellent researchers eager to develop their work in an interdisciplinary, international and collaborative environment. AIAS nurtures an innovative atmosphere where breakthroughs emerge through transparent, inclusive and reflective discussions, offering a space for engagement and creativity.

The AIAS-RJ fellowship gives the selected fellow the opportunity to concentrate on their own research interests while also being an active member of the AIAS research community and participating in and contributing to seminars and activities beyond their own field of expertise. The fellow must be eager to engage in the interdisciplinary community at AIAS and expand research collaborations with colleagues at Aarhus University.

Who can apply for an AIAS-RJ Fellowship

The call is open to curiosity-driven researchers who:

• are of any nationality who hold a tenured position at a Swedish research institution

• work within the humanities and social sciences

• have a research experience of minimum 4 years after completion of the PhD

A unique interdisciplinary platform at AIAS

AIAS fosters connections, sparks ideas and dissolves boundaries as fellows engage with researchers from different disciplines within the Institute and across departments and research hubs at Aarhus University. Therefore, the call welcomes applications from all research areas and themes.

With a location within the unique campus of Aarhus University, AIAS functions as an interdisciplinary platform that connects researchers across Aarhus University and international scholars. AIAS has fellows who work in thematic groups or in individual fellowships, and hosts events and activities, which AIAS-RJ fellows are welcome to join and contribute to.

AIAS and Aarhus University strive to create a multidisciplinary, inclusive academic environment and to be an inspiring workplace for all by fostering a culture in which the individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The fellowship includes

The AIAS-RJ Fellow is offered:

• a salary based on seniority (employment conditions and wages are regulated through the Danish collective union agreements)

• travel costs to and from Aarhus

• relocation assistance

• a moderate budget for research-related costs

The AIAS-RJ Fellow will have office space at AIAS and can participate in academic training activities, conferences and workshops at AIAS. They will also be affiliated with the relevant research environments at Aarhus University.

How to apply: Application process and deadline

Applications must be submitted online via the system: GrantOne.

In the ‘Guide for Applicants,’ you can find the detailed application requirements and more information on the structure of the application system, the selection criteria and the selection process.

Timeline of the application process

• Opening of call: August 2026.

• Deadline for applications: 24 November 2026 at 12.00 (noon) CET.

• Evaluation and selection period: December 2026 - March 2027.

• Applicants will receive answers: Ultimo March 2027.

• Fellowship begins: 1 September 2027.

About AIAS

As an 'Institute for Advanced Study,' AIAS brings researchers together across disciplines, seniority and nationality. AIAS offers fellowships for excellent researchers from all academic disciplines to pursue cutting-edge research projects for the benefit of society and humankind in optimal research conditions.

The daily encounter with colleagues from diverse research disciplines at AIAS provides fellows with fresh and different insights, methods and perspectives on their own research, leading to new and unexpected research questions and ideas.

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These therapies are designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage, with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

As Director, Medical Writing, you will be dedicated to one of our compounds under clinical development, taking ownership of the clinical and regulatory writing that helps move this compound through development. You will turn complex clinical and scientific evidence into clear, accurate documents that regulators can act on - connecting the science, data and development strategy into one coherent story.

This is a hands-on role. You will write, shape and drive documents yourself while bringing physicians, scientists, biostatisticians and regulatory colleagues together around high-quality outputs and demanding timelines.

What You'll Do At Hemab

• Own medical writing for one of our leading compounds, from document strategy and planning through drafting, review and finalization.

• Lead development of clinical documents, including clinical study protocols, clinical study reports, Investigator’s Brochures, and clinical submission documents appropriate to the program’s stage.

• Contribute to clinical content of regulatory and safety documents, such as briefing documents, regulatory responses, and DSURs.

• Translate complex clinical and statistical data into clear, scientifically accurate narratives for regulatory reviewers.

• Partner closely with clinical development, regulatory, biostatistics, safety, and other scientific colleagues to align document content with the program strategy.

• Drive cross-functional document reviews, resolve comments constructively and build alignment without compromising scientific accuracy.

• Apply relevant regulatory requirements and guidance, including ICH E3, ICH E6 and applicable FDA and EMA expectations.

• Build writing plans and practical frameworks that keep interdependent documents moving against development and submission timelines.

• Maintain document quality, consistency and version control while adapting quickly as data, priorities and timelines evolve.

• Identify writing or documentation risks early, take ownership of solutions and give the program team a clear view of what is needed next.

• Collaborate with internal cross-functional teams and external vendors to manage public disclosure activities in compliance with transparency rules.

What You'll Bring to Hemab

Essential:

• Bachelor’s degree or higher in a scientific discipline, with at least 10 years of hands-on medical writing experience in biotechnology, pharmaceutical or CRO clinical research environments.

• Significant experience authoring clinical and regulatory documents across drug development.

• Strong working knowledge of ICH E3, ICH E6 and relevant FDA and EMA requirements.

• Scientific fluency and the ability to interpret clinical trial data and statistical outputs accurately.

• Excellent written English, with the ability to make complex science clear, structured and precise.

• Strong cross-functional communication skills and experience bringing multiple expert reviewers to alignment.

The Department of Accounting invites applications for a PhD position in Auditing. The Department of Accounting is one of the oldest and largest accounting departments in Europe. We have a growing and flourishing research environment within financial accounting, management accounting and control, auditing, and corporate governance.

We especially welcome PhD proposals that adopt qualitative research methods and suggest novel approaches to the study of

• The making of the audit profession, especially regarding emerging technologies in auditing, such as generative artificial intelligence, with an emphasis on how they may reshape the audit profession, including the training and socialization of auditors, the exercise of professional judgment and the relevance of the traditional audit model in responding to evolving societal demands.
• Audit firm ownership, including the emerging role of private equity firms acquiring ownership interests in audit firms. Proposals within this research theme may explore implications for, for example, the partnership model, audit firm governance, how audits are conducted, talent management, client portfolios, audit market competition, and how these developments may reconfigure the audit profession.
• The role of auditing and assurance in sustainable development. Within this theme, candidates are encouraged to explore alternative forms of auditing and assurance that contribute to sustainable development and to propose empirical work that goes beyond simply examining the current compliance-oriented role associated with the verification of sustainability reports. Proposals should aim to develop research that provides a basis for debate about how auditing and assurance can play a meaningful role in sustainability.
• Regulator-auditor interaction, with a focus on challenges and potential pathways in public oversight practices, including, for example, the role of firm-level oversight practices and dialogue, as well as the role of ad hoc regulatory investigations alongside routine quality inspections.
• Client-auditor interaction, with a focus on, for example, the governance role of audit committees, the negotiation of accounting issues, professional and commercial conflicts, or the role of client technology adoption in the performance of audits.
• Auditing in the context of audit firm organization and governance, with the aim of understanding how increasingly intensive and sophisticated audit firm-level systems (e.g., quality management, incentive systems, performance measurement, and culture/tone at the top) operate to manage and control auditor behavior within audit firms. Within this theme, candidates are encouraged to propose research that can inform reflections on how bureaucracy in audit firms can be balanced, how tendencies toward defensive behavior might be reversed, and how professional judgment at all levels, from junior auditors to partners, might be encouraged.
The project should speak to contemporary concerns in auditing and aim to contribute to academic, public, professional, and company-level debates. The PhD project should therefore be informed and enriched by engagement with firms and professionals as part of both the research process and the dissemination of research findings, and we encourage proposals to demonstrate the potential for such engagement.

The PhD position is based in the Department of Accounting, and the candidate will be part of the department’s auditing research group. We welcome applicants with degrees or experience in accounting and auditing. We also welcome applicants from other social sciences who are interested in engaging with auditing as a research domain. The auditing research group consists of researchers with backgrounds in accounting and auditing, as well as researchers from other academic fields who have a strong interest in auditing. The PhD candidate will work in close collaboration with the supervisors and benefit from the international research environment in the Department of Accounting and at CBS. Candidates are encouraged to contact Professor Thomas Riise Johansen (trj.acc@cbs.dk) for informal discussions and information about the position before submitting the application.

About the PhD programme
The three-year PhD programme at CBS gives you the opportunity to conduct research under the supervision of CBS’s associate professors and professors, supported by research related PhD courses. The programme is highly international, and you are expected to participate in international research conferences and to spend time at another research institution as a visiting PhD student. See the CBS homepage for more information about the PhD programme, https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programmeme. 

CBS PhD graduates are held in high esteem not only in academia and research institutions but also in government and business where their research qualifications are in high demand.

CBS is committed to ensuring excellence, transformative and relevant teaching and research. Candidates who wish to join us must be interested in working in an organisation of this type and it is expected that the applicant will show an interest in joining the department's research environment. You can read more about the department's research here: www.cbs.dk/acc

Application and admission requirements
The department will give priority to applicants with high grades from their universities. To be considered the applicant must:

• have a basic education at master's level (corresponding to the 3 + 2 Bologna process)
• have received the grade of 10 (or equivalent) for the master's thesis according to the Danish 7-point grading scale (https://ufm.dk/en/education/the-danish-education-system/grading-system)
• have a weighted grade point average of at least 8.2 on the Danish 7-point grading scale for the bachelor's and master's degree combined or alternatively a weighted grade point average must be at least 9.5 for the master's degree alone. If the grade point average is not met, documentation for being in the top 40% of the class is also accepted. In rare cases, the grade requirement can be waived.
• have completed the master's programme before starting the PhD programme at CBS
• master academic English at a high level in writing and speaking
The application (see link below) must include a five-page project description. The project description must include:

• a presentation of an original research question
• a description of the initial theoretical framework and method
• a presentation of the proposed empirical material
• a work plan for the three years
More information can be found here: https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programmemes/admission

In addition to the project description, copies of the following must be included:

• diploma for bachelor's and master's degree or other certificates at an equivalent level as well as the grade transcripts
• documentation for being in the top 40% of the class (if grade requirements are not met)
• a concise curriculum vitae (CV)
• a list of articles and publications (if applicable)
• one example of a selected written work (e.g. master's thesis)
The PhD student is enrolled in the CBS PhD School. Further information about PhD scholarships and the PhD programme can be found at https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programmeme.Information about the department can be found at https://www.cbs.dk/forskning/institutter-centre/institut-regnskab.

For additional information regarding the PhD position, feel free to contact Professor, Thomas Riise Johansen, trj.acc@cbs.dk.

Employment and salary
A PhD scholarship runs for a period of three years and includes teaching obligations corresponding to 416 work hours. The scholarships are fully salaried positions, according to the national Danish collective agreement. The monthly salary is currently approximately DKK 30,264 up to DKK 36,877 depending on seniority and a pension contribution totaling 18.07%. The scholarship includes tuition fees, office space, course and travel costs (according to the current CBS agreement). 

Salary level and employment take place in accordance with the Ministry of Finance's agreement with the Academics' Central Organization.

Applicants selected for assessment will be notified about the composition of the Assessment Committee and will receive their personal assessment later. Selected applicants will be invited for an interview. Please note that a positive assessment does not automatically result in an interview. Once the recruitment process is completed each applicant will be notified of the outcome of their application. 

The application must be sent via the online link below.

Copenhagen Business School invites applications for a vacant PhD scholarship within the field of the intellectual history of coporate politics at the Department of Business Humanities and Law. Expected starting date is 1 May 2027.

The PhD position is a non-tenured full-time position of 3 years, with teaching and course work obligations.

The research will be conducted as part of the Independent Research Fund Denmark Sapere Aude Grant project Visions of corporate politics: Intellectual histories of the state-firm analogy. The project team will consist of the PI, one postdoc and one PhD.
Read more about the project here: https://dff.dk/en/our-funded-projects/meet-the-researchers/research-leaders/eksterne-personer-en/research-leaders-2025/mathias-hein-jessen/

The central objective of the research project is to analyze contemporary contestations over the state-firm boundary as well as mobilizations of analogies between state and firm in projecting political and economic visions. The project analyzes the constitution of the state-firm distinction as well as what it terms contemporary ‘visions of corporate politics’ represented by ideologically distinct answers to the crisis of liberal democracy which both contest the state-firm boundary and mobilize the state-firm analogy to legitimize their vision: On the one hand attempts to democratize or politicize the firm and on the other hand attempts to build political communities on principles of corporate governance. The PhD project will focus on one of the two contemporary visions of corporate politics.

Examples of potential research topics: the democratization of the firm; democratic or economic planning; employee ownership; platform cooperativism or socialism; network states; gov-corps; start-up governments; freedom cities.

As a Business Consultant, you will help ensure that Netcompany’s IT projects are successfully anchored within our clients’ organisations and business processes. You will also play a key role in making sure users have the right capabilities and readiness, so that both users and the organisation are fully prepared when new solutions go live.

The role is diverse and dynamic. Your responsibilites will typically include:

• Supporting clients with change management initiatives.

• Preparing user guides and training materials, as well as conducting user training sessions.

• Performing analyses and reporting on organisational change readiness.

• Mapping processes and facilitating workshops with clients.

• Defining benefits tracking models and preparing communication plans.

• Building strong domain knowledge by participating in and facilitating analysis work, testing, and refinement activities.

About you

You actively seek understanding by asking questions and encourage learning through curiosity and dialogue. Deadlines do not intimidate you and you are willing to go the extra mile when needed. To succeed in this role, you:

• Are either a recent graduate or have a few years of experience — ideally working at the intersection of IT, business, and organisation, for example as an IT project manager or consultant.

• Have an interest in IT and digitalisation.

• Hold a relevant master’s degree, such as Cand.merc., Cand.it., Cand.scient., or similar.

• Have strong written and verbal communication skills and are fluent in both Danish and English.

• Have experience working professionally with PowerPoint and Excel.

• Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken) is a must.

Continue developing with us

At Netcompany, we focus on your personal and professional development.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will guide you through your development and help you achieve your goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague helps ensure the well-being of each employee and provides you with concrete insights into the many different career opportunities as you build your experience.

Additionally, you will be enrolled in our internal training programme, Netcompany Academy, where you are offered courses and seminars on everything from technologies to customer management. All courses are taught by experienced Netcompany colleagues, ensuring that all content is highly relevant and builds upon your professional skills, preparing you for various tasks and continuously improving your expertise throughout your career with us.

Join an inclusive community

At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand and build a network early in your career.

Send us your application

Upload your resume and a motivational letter to our recruitment system via the link. If you have unanswered questions, feel free to write to hr.dk@netcompany.com.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment. Our recruitment processes are based on individual merit. If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support during the interview process, please email our recruiters at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com for assistance. #LI-SA1

We seek professionals who are passionate about the intersection of technology and finance. If you enjoy solving complex challenges and creating value for clients, and have specific experience with OneStream, AMCO Solutions offers an ideal environment for you to thrive. Experience in other CPM software solutions is also a relevant background.

Job Description

As a Senior Consultant, your responsibilities will include:

•   Engaging in all phases of the project lifecycle, from gathering requirements to building solutions and supporting client’s post-launch.

•   Collaborating with a skilled, diverse team to address challenging business needs and deliver effective solutions, ensuring OneStream is utilized to its full

•   potential.

•   Leading project tasks and ensuring timely, high-quality delivery in accordance with project scope.

•   Mentoring and coaching colleagues while contributing to the overall knowledge-sharing within the team.

•   Actively participating in internal initiatives to help AMCO maintain its position as a leader in implementation of OneStream solutions.

Requirements and Qualifications

•   A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in economics, Finance, Information Systems, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).

•   3-4 years of CPM implementation experience, including system design, project management, and change management. Specific knowledge of OneStream

•   Software is an advantage.

•   A solid understanding of accounting & finance principles (preferred).

•   OneStream certification is a strong plus, and experience with the software is highly preferred for this role.

Perks and Benefits

•   Professional Development: Access to training and certifications in OneStream, and continuous learning opportunities.

•   Work-Life Balance: Flexibility in working hours and the opportunity to collaborate with a global team across various time zones.

•   Competitive Compensation: We offer a competitive salary package, comprehensive benefits, and opportunities for career advancement.

Do you get a small, slightly nerdy kick out of working out why a conversion stopped firing three weeks ago and nobody noticed?

At Helion B2B we don't just "run ads" for our clients. We build data-driven growth engines for some of the most ambitious B2B companies in Europe. But an engine is only as good as its sensors. That's where you come in.

You won't just keep the engine running. You'll help build it.

You'll join our tracking team in Aarhus, working day to day with our Tracking Lead. Real ownership early, someone who has done all of it sitting right next to you, and a direct hand in how the practice develops. We have standards, and we like them being challenged. If you think we're doing something the hard way, we'd rather hear it in week two than in year two.

You'll work across all of it: new implementations, server-side setups, multi-market containers, consent, QA, troubleshooting, and the measurement plans that hold it together. Real clients, and real responsibility for whether their measurement holds up.

Some of that is building something new. A lot of it is taking a setup that already exists and making it better than you found it, which is where data quality actually comes from. Your scope over the clients you look after grows from there.

The job doesn't stop when the data arrives. Part of the work is reporting and analysis: helping a client see what their numbers are telling them, and noticing when a number is telling them something wrong. Mostly technical work, then, but not only

Your playground

• 
Google Tag Manager: Web containers from day one, server-side (sGTM) as you grow into it.

• 
GA4: Event design, debugging, and making sure the numbers actually mean something.

• 
HubSpot: we're an Elite HubSpot partner, so tracking data and CRM data have to meet properly.

• 
Consent management: Cookiebot and Cookie Information, Consent Mode, and the GDPR reality behind them.

• 
Data Studio and reporting: Turning all of the above into something a client can read and act on, and being able to say what it means.

• 
AI-assisted tracking: We're actively building agent-supported auditing, monitoring and insight workflows. You'll use them, break them, and help shape where they go next.

What you need on day one

• 
You can build and debug tags, triggers and variables in a web GTM container on your own. Preview mode and Tag Assistant are familiar territory.

• 
You can configure and debug GA4, and you know what to start checking when a dimension comes back as (not set).

• 
You're a finisher. "Done" means tested and verified, not deployed.

• 
You think for yourself. When you hit a wall, you research, test and come back with a proposal rather than waiting for instructions.

• 
You're curious about where AI is taking this field. You don't need experience with it. You need to want to poke at it.

Somewhere around three to five years of hands-on tracking experience, from an agency or in-house, is the usual shape. It's a guide, not a gate.

What you'll learn here

Server-side GTM and Conversions API. Consent Mode in depth. HubSpot data flows. BigQuery. Multi-market container architecture. Reporting and analysis on top of GA4 and BigQuery. B2B lead cycles, and why they make tracking a harder problem than e-commerce.

Experience with any of these is an advantage. None of them are requirements. You'll have a lead who would rather teach you properly than do it twice.

The practical bits

• 
Where: Our Aarhus office, with a minimum of three days a week on site.

• 
Language: We work in English. Danish is an advantage, not a requirement.

• 
Right to work: You must already hold the right to work in Denmark: EU/EEA citizenship, or a valid Danish work and residence permit.

• 
Everyday life: Lunch scheme and flexible hours. We care that the work lands, not that you were at your desk at 08:30.

• 
Pension and insurance: Company-paid pension and health insurance (sundhedsforsikring).

• 
Growing here: We back training and certifications, and you'll have a lead who would rather you learned something new than closed one more ticket.

• 
The social side: fredagsbar, summer party, julefrokost and a yearly off-site. If you're new to Denmark, ask about the julefrokost.

> Earlier in your career than the above, but the rest of this sounds like you? Apply anyway and tell us where you're at. We'd rather shape the level around the right person than miss them.

Business-to-business, person-to-person

Helion B2B is a fast-growing, Elite HubSpot partner that helps B2B companies build growth engines.

We are an ambitious, curious team genuinely passionate about our work. We are eager to learn, value great social relationships and are not afraid of challenging ourselves and our clients if we feel that there is a better way to solve a challenge.

You can read more about us, our customers and what we do on helionb2b.com or on our HubSpot Directory page.

Let's talk business-to-business, person-to-person

Dansk:

Kort beskrivelse

Support a 9-year-old boy in Skævinge

Jobbeskrivelse

Do you have experience working with children with special needs, and do you enjoy an active one-to-one role? Then you could become an important source of support for a 9-year-old boy who loves movement, play and safe, predictable routines.

About the role

You will provide regular one-to-one support for a 9-year-old boy with autism and an intellectual disability. He needs close support, clear structure and a calm approach that helps create predictability.

The boy is energetic, enjoys being active and particularly likes outdoor play, trips to the playground and running in the woods. He also enjoys activities such as puzzles, music, bubbles, balloons and sensory toys. Your role is to plan and take part in activities that match his pace and needs. As he has limited awareness of danger, it is important that you stay close to him and remain attentive to his surroundings.

The role includes assistance with personal care, including bathing, changing diapers and toilet training. You will also provide support at mealtimes, with a focus on motivating and guiding him towards gradually becoming more independent.

The boy does not communicate verbally and uses only a few English words. It is therefore important that you are able to communicate in English, including with his parents, who do not speak Danish.

The boy has food allergies and has an EpiPen, which must be used in the event of an allergic reaction. The family will provide thorough instructions on its use. He also has asthma, and his parents are responsible for all medication management.

About you

You may be a qualified pedagogue/social educator or have relevant experience working with children with special needs. You approach the child with calmness, patience and clarity, and you enjoy an active working environment where you take part in play and physical activities.

At the same time, you are able to create structure and a sense of security, be attentive and provide clear boundaries when needed. As communication with the family takes place in English, you must be able to communicate confidently in English.

A driving licence is an advantage. Alternatively, you must be comfortable using the family’s cargo bike, which will be provided.

Working hours

The position is for 16 hours per week. The working hours are:

Two weekdays per week: 3 hours after school, from 2:30 pm to 5:30 pm

Thursdays: 9:30 am to 1:30 pm (4 hours)

Sundays: 11:00 am to 5:00 pm

What we offer

You will become part of a family-owned company with many dedicated employees. You will have a dedicated adviser who is available for guidance and support. Outside office hours, a staffed emergency phone line is always available, so you are never on your own.

Salary and pension are provided in accordance with the national collective agreement between FOA and the Danish Chamber of Commerce (Dansk Erhverv). You are covered by DUOS’ liability and occupational injury insurance, and health insurance is included as part of your pension scheme.

We offer a wide range of courses, and as a DUOS employee, you will receive relevant induction and ongoing professional development. Working with people at DUOS also gives you the opportunity to develop both personally and professionally.

Would you like to become our new colleague?

Please submit your application via the link. You must have a profile on mit.duos.dk and be logged in to apply. We conduct interviews on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. The position is available for an immediate start.

If you have any further questions, please contact Recruitment Consultant Trine Ankær Johansen on +45 36 34 49 90. You can also find answers to general questions in our FAQ.

We are people helping people

At DUOS, we help people in their everyday lives, support them through challenging situations and contribute to their well-being and quality of life. As one of Denmark’s largest and longest-established welfare service providers, we strive to be there where support is needed.

We understand the importance of combining empathy with the right professional expertise, and we know that finding the right match between an employee and the person receiving support is essential for our services to make a meaningful difference.

Join the DUOS team and make an important difference in another person’s life.

Learn more about DUOS at www.duos.dk.

**About Bolt

**Bolt is shaping a future where cities are built for people, not cars. What started as an ambitious project of a 19-year-old in 2013 has grown into a global mobility platform used by more than 200 million customers and 4.5 million driver and courier partners across 50 countries.

From ride-hailing and food delivery to scooters, e-bikes, and car-sharing, Bolt helps people move through cities every day. Small, autonomous teams drive this work, combining the speed and ownership of a startup with the scale of a global technology company backed by more than €1bn in funding.

And we're just getting started.

**Why join Bolt?

**

• Build the future of mobility and help transform how people live and move in cities.

• Tackle challenges at scale that span technology, operations, regulation, and growth.

• Take real ownership early. Small, lean teams mean your decisions matter from day one, and you'll learn fast alongside some of the best people in the industry.

• Join one of Europe's leading technology companies, backed by world-class investors including Sequoia.

**About The Role

**Bolt for Business is scaling fast — and corporate mobility is one of the biggest opportunities ahead of us. As Regional Sales Manager, you'll lead up to 8 country-based sales teams, owning the strategy and execution behind how businesses of all sizes manage employee mobility and ground transportation. This isn't just team management — it's building and scaling a B2B sales engine across multiple markets, with real autonomy to shape how we win.

_Please note that this role can be based in one of the following locations: Denmark, Sweden, Finland, Norway, or Germany.

_**Main Tasks And Responsibilities

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Public Sector Management Accounting and Control
jobs.description:
The Department of Accounting invites applications for a PhD position in Public Sector Management Accounting and Control. The Department of Accounting is one of the oldest and largest accounting departments in Europe. We have a growing and flourishing research environment within financial accounting, management accounting and control, auditing, and corporate governance.

Public sector organizations continuously face demands for high service quality under increasingly tighter budget constraints while simultaneously being held accountable for their performance. Several attempts have been made to strengthen management accounting and control practices such as introducing new costing techniques, performance-based budgeting, benchmarking, and performance management. But despite these initiatives, public organizations still struggle to realize political objectives, which is further complicated by the development of new technologies and societal demands for sustainability. Within this context, the PhD application should reflect an independently formulated research project that addresses questions related to the role and effects of management accounting and control practice in public sector organizations at state, regional and/or municipal level. Potential research areas are:

• 
Developing and using performance measurement and management to create public value

• 
The influence of new technologies on management accounting and control practices

• 
The use of financial/non-financial information by public officials and politicians

• 
The development and/or use of budgeting for public sector decision-making

• 
The role of accounting in strategic development and public organization management

The PhD candidate will be part of the department’s management accounting research group. We focus on examining various subjects related to management accounting and control within both private and public sectors. For this PhD position, we welcome all forms of research methodologies and theoretical approaches, but we prioritize research inquiring specifically into organizational practices. We are open to candidates from different academic backgrounds both within and outside business administration.

The candidate will be expected to teach within management and control. As many courses are taught in Danish, priority will be given to candidates with language proficiencies in Danish, Swedish or Norwegian.

About the PhD programme
The three-year PhD programme at CBS gives you the opportunity to conduct research under the supervision of CBS’s associate professors and professors, supported by research related PhD courses. The programme is highly international, and you are expected to participate in international research conferences and to spend time at another research institution as a visiting PhD student. See the CBS homepage for more information about the PhD programme, https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programmeme. 

CBS PhD graduates are held in high esteem not only in academia and research institutions but also in government and business where their research qualifications are in high demand.

CBS is committed to ensuring excellence, transformative and relevant teaching and research. Candidates who wish to join us must be interested in working in an organisation of this type and it is expected that the applicant will show an interest in joining the department's research environment. You can read more about the department's research here: www.cbs.dk/acc. 

Application and admission requirements
The department will give priority to applicants with high grades from their universities. To be considered the applicant must:

• 
have a basic education at master's level (corresponding to the 3 + 2 Bologna process)

• 
have received the grade of 10 (or equivalent) for the master's thesis according to the Danish 7-point grading scale (https://ufm.dk/en/education/the-danish-education-system/grading-system)

• 
have a weighted grade point average of at least 8.2 on the Danish 7-point grading scale for the bachelor's and master's degree combined or alternatively a weighted grade point average must be at least 9.5 for the master's degree alone. If the grade point average is not met, documentation for being in the top 40% of the class is also accepted. In rare cases, the grade requirement can be waived.

• 
have completed the master's programme before starting the PhD programme at CBS

• 
master academic English at a high level in writing and speaking

The application (see link below) must include a five-page project description. The project description must include:

• 
a presentation of an original research question

• 
a description of the initial theoretical framework and method

• 
a presentation of the proposed empirical material

• 
a work plan for the three years

More information can be found here: https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programmemes/admission

In addition to the project description, copies of the following must be included:

• 
diploma for bachelor's and master's degree or other certificates at an equivalent level as well as the grade transcripts

• 
documentation for being in the top 40% of the class (if grade requirements are not met)

• 
a concise curriculum vitae (CV)

• 
a list of articles and publications (if applicable)

• 
one example of a selected written work (e.g. master's thesis)

The PhD student is enrolled in the CBS PhD School. Further information about PhD scholarships and the PhD programme can be found at https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programmeme.

Information about the department can be found at https://www.cbs.dk/forskning/institutter-centre/institut-regnskab.

For additional information regarding the PhD position, feel free to contact Associate Professor, Tim Neerup Themsen, tnt.acc@cbs.dk.

Employment and salary
A PhD scholarship runs for a period of three years and includes teaching obligations corresponding to 416 work hours. The scholarships are fully salaried positions, according to the national Danish collective agreement. The monthly salary is currently approximately DKK 30,264 up to DKK 36,877 depending on seniority and a pension contribution totaling 18.07%. The scholarship includes tuition fees, office space, course and travel costs (according to the current CBS agreement). 

Salary level and employment take place in accordance with the Ministry of Finance's agreement with the Academics' Central Organization.

Recruitment procedure
The Recruitment Committee shortlists at least two-five applicants to be assessed by the Assessment Committee. Applicants are informed whether their application has proceeded for assessment.

Applicants selected for assessment will be notified about the composition of the Assessment Committee and will receive their personal assessment later. Selected applicants will be invited for an interview. Please note that a positive assessment does not automatically result in an interview. Once the recruitment process is completed each applicant will be notified of the outcome of their application. 

The application must be sent via the online link below. 

Copenhagen Business School must receive all application material, including all appendices (see above), by the application deadline.

Details about Copenhagen Business School are available at www.cbs.dk/en.

Application due 11/11/2026

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in Natural Language Processing
jobs.description:
PhD Project in Cultural Reasoning with Language Models

The AI Section at the Department of Computer Science invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in computational modelling and evaluation of cultural interpretation with language models. The position is part of the research project “CuRe: Cultural Reasoning for Responsible Language Model Development” (DFF project 5334-00088B), funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark.

The expected start date is February 1st, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The project

Language models can produce fluent interpretations of texts while obscuring the cultural assumptions, uncertainty and alternative readings underlying their answers. CuRe investigates how language models understand and reason about culture, ambiguity and interpretation, and how these capabilities can be evaluated and improved to support responsible language model development. Literary texts provide a demanding testbed: their interpretation depends on historical and cultural knowledge, close attention to textual evidence and the ability to accommodate several plausible readings.

The PhD candidate will develop computational methods and evaluation resources for culturally grounded interpretation. Working closely with researchers in natural language processing and literary studies, the candidate is expected to:

• 
construct datasets and benchmarks linking literary passages, relevant cultural and historical context, textual evidence and expert or reader interpretations;

• 
analyse what cultural knowledge and interpretive strategies language models use, where their interpretations fail and how confidently they present uncertain conclusions;

• 
develop methods for grounding interpretations in evidence and for representing uncertainty, ambiguity and multiple plausible interpretations;

• 
evaluate the resulting methods through automatic experiments and studies with literary scholars and other readers; and

• 
publish the results in leading venues in natural language processing, artificial intelligence and computational humanities.

 The exact research questions will be refined together with the successful candidate. Relevant methodological directions include language model evaluation and probing, retrieval and retrieval-augmented generation, explicit representations of interpretive evidence and uncertainty, data annotation, human-centred evaluation and multilingual or cross-cultural analysis. The empirical work will primarily use modern Scandinavian literary texts, while aiming to develop methods and findings that generalise beyond literature. The project includes a planned research stay at McGill University.

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for candidates with a strong computational background and an interest in how language, culture and interpretation can be studied rigorously. Applicants may have a background in natural language processing, computational linguistics, computer science, machine learning, artificial intelligence, data science, digital humanities or a closely related field. Formal training in literary studies is not required, but the successful candidate must be motivated to work across disciplinary boundaries and to engage seriously with humanities research questions.

Our group and research- and what do we offer?

The PhD fellow will join the CoAStaL research group and the AI Section at the Department of Computer Science. The research environment brings together faculty, postdoctoral researchers and PhD students working on multilingual and cross-cultural NLP, multimodality, language model training and evaluation, responsible AI and computational humanities. The section collaborates broadly with leading research groups in Denmark and abroad.

CuRe is an interdisciplinary collaboration with the Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics at the University of Copenhagen. The project builds on established joint work in computational literary studies and provides access to large literary corpora, domain expertise and relevant annotation resources. The PhD fellow will therefore be part of both a technically strong NLP environment and a close collaboration with literary scholars.

The group is part of the Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. We are located in Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern GPU computing resources, shared data and annotation infrastructure and access to relevant text corpora.

Principal supervisor: Associate Professor Desmond Elliott, Department of Computer Science, de@di.ku.dk.

Co-supervisor: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor Daniel Hershcovich, Department of Computer Science, dh@di.ku.dk.

Co-supervisor: Associate Professor Jens Bjerring-Hansen, Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics, jbh@hum.ku.dk.

The PhD programme

The position is offered as a three-year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme).

Qualifications needed
To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. [relevant educations]. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

Terms of employment 

The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 31,800 DKK/approx. 4,200 EUR (August 2026-level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18,07 % to your pension fund.

Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

Responsibilities and tasks

• 
Carry through an independent research project under supervision

• 
Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE

• 
Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad

• 
Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities

• 
Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals

• 
Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project

We are looking for the following qualifications:

• 
A master’s degree or equivalent qualification relevant to the PhD project.

• 
Strong programming skills, preferably in Python, and experience with machine learning or natural language processing tools.

• 
Knowledge of modern NLP and language models and an ability to design, implement and evaluate computational experiments.

• 
Experience with one or more of the following is an advantage: language model evaluation, retrieval or retrieval-augmented generation, data annotation, interpretability, multilingual NLP or computational humanities.

• 
Relevant research experience, publications, thesis work or professional activities.

• 
Ability to work independently, formulate research questions and collaborate across computer science and the humanities.

• 
A curious and critical mindset with a strong interest in culture, interpretation and responsible AI.

• 
Excellent written and spoken English. Knowledge of a Scandinavian language or experience with literary analysis is an advantage but not a requirement.

Application and Assessment Procedure

Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

Please include: 

• 
Motivated letter of application (maximum one page) explaining your motivation for the project, your relevant qualifications and the research directions that particularly interest you.

• 
Curriculum vitae including information about your education, research or work experience, language skills and other skills relevant to the position.

• 
Original diplomas for bachelor’s and master’s degrees and transcripts of records in the original language, including an authorised English translation if issued in a language other than English or Danish. If the master’s degree has not yet been completed, a certified or signed recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.

• 
Publication list, if applicable.

• 
Reference letters, if available.

Application deadline: 

The deadline for applications is November 8th, 2026, 23:59 CET

jobs.description:
PhD Position in Computational Mass Spectrometry Imaging and Spatial Metabolomics
Applications are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at the Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Roskilde Campus, Denmark, within the Environmental Science and Toxicology department. The position is available from February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Title
PhD Position in Computational Mass Spectrometry Imaging and Spatial Metabolomics

Research area and project description
Spatial metabolomics enables the study of biochemical processes and human–environment interactions at micrometer to cellular resolution (single cell metabolomics). Mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) is increasingly used to investigate how environmental stressors and micropollutants affect biological systems across space and time. However, data processing, image segmentation, multimodal image registration, reproducible computational workflows and biological interpretation remain major challenges.

This project will develop computational methods and open-source tools for processing, analyzing and interpreting MSI and spatial metabolomics data. The methods will be applied to microbial communities, environmental samples and tissues to uncover spatially resolved biotransformation processes and metabolic responses to environmental stressors.

The successful candidate will work at the interface of computational science, biochemistry, microbiology and analytical chemistry. The project will combine computational method development with experimental spatial metabolomics including signal preprocessing, machine learning, spatial statistics, image registration and interactive software development. The PhD student will join an interdisciplinary team of chemists, microbiologists, biologists and computational scientists and contribute to both methodological development and biological applications.

The position includes:
• Developing batch-processing workflows for MSI and metabolomics data, including normalization, quantification and feature alignment.
• Developing spatial segmentation methods, including uncertainty-aware and spatially regularized clustering.
• Collaborating with experimental scientists, mass spectrometrists and biologists to validate methods against experimental and biological datasets. Ensure reliable implementation of automated quality control, testing, documentation and reproducibility reporting.
• Communicating computational results clearly to interdisciplinary and non-computational re-searchers. Processing and analyzing imaging datasets and presenting results at internal and international scientific meetings.
• Publishing methodological and application studies and releasing well-documented open-source software.
• Close supervision and collaboration with dedicated researchers and senior investigators.
Project description
For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please simply copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Qualifications and specific competences
We are seeking highly motivated candidates with a strong interest in interdisciplinary research. Applicants should hold a master’s degree (or equivalent) in computer science, bioinformatics/ cheminformatics, AI/ML, data science, chemistry, computational biology, chemometrics, analytical chemistry or a related discipline.

Essential qualifications:
• Solid background in computational chemistry, image processing, omics data analysis and/or mass spectrometry
• Strong interest in spatial metabolomics and its applicationsDesirable qualifications:
• Experience with mass spectrometry, microscopy, microbial systems, or analytical chemistry
• Ability to work independently as well as in collaborative, interdisciplinary teams
Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Environmental Science, Roskilde Campus, Frederiksborgvej 399, 4000 Roskilde, Denmark.

Location: Farum, Denmark | Level: PhD / Postdoc / Experienced Engineer

The Mission: Build the Next Generation of SBC Systems

At Ibsen Photonics, we are developing Spectral Beam Combining (SBC) modules for high-power laser architectures. We are looking for creative, hands-on Optical Design Engineers to take full ownership of designing, building, and optimising our SBC platform.

This role bridges the gap between theoretical physics and industrial reality. You won’t just design on a screen; you will spend significant time in the lab, iterating rapidly from proof-of-concept to robust, production-ready, scalable systems.

Key responsibilities:

• Design & Assemble: Develop compact, efficient SBC modules using Ibsen’s world-class transmission gratings, while considering optical beam paths, thermal effects and mechanical constraints.

• System Optimisation: Drive performance by refining optical alignment, mechanical stability, and complex thermal management for high-power loads in a reiterative process: design – experiment – optimise.

• Characterisation: Use advanced diagnostics to maintain beam quality (low M²) during power scaling, including wavefront sensing and spectral analysis.

• Full Lifecycle Ownership: Source optical/mechanical components and manage the transition from experimental prototypes to scalable, volume-ready designs.

• Global Collaboration: Work closely with an internal team and international partners, including potential overseas visits for joint prototyping and testing.

What you bring

You are a proactive problem-solver who thrives in a “build-test-learn” environment. Ideally, you possess:

• Education: A PhD or Postdoc in Optics, Photonics, Laser Physics, or a related field.

• Expertise:

• Hands on experience with (high-power) fibre and free-space optical systems, precise alignment, and experimental troubleshooting.

• Understanding of (and ideally experience with) SBC and CBC beam combining techniques.

• Beam quality measurement and analysis.

• Mechanical design of low-tolerance devices

• Technical Knowledge: Deep understanding of Gaussian optics, beam propagation, and high-power laser effects (thermal lensing, runaway-effects, mitigation strategies).

• Software Skills: Proficiency in optical simulation tools (e.g., Zemax) and familiarity with mechanical CAD.

• Mindset: Independent enough to drive a project and work on your own, but collaborative enough to thrive in a flat-hierarchy, cross-functional team, sharing insights and discussing projects/next steps. The role is highly experimental and hands-on, requiring independence and a strong drive to make systems work in practice, not just on paper.

• Security Clearance: You are a European citizen with no family ties to Russia or Russian allied territories, and you have a clean criminal record.

Why join Ibsen Photonics?

• High Impact: Your designs will directly shape the future of high-brightness laser systems for manufacturing, defence, telecommunications, and science.

• Freedom to Innovate: We value experimental drive—if you have a better way to align or stabilise a system, we want to see it.

• Danish Engineering Culture: Enjoy a supportive environment with fast decision-making, real ownership, and a healthy work-life balance.
