jobs.occupation: Research Associate – Peptide Chemistry Discovery Platform
jobs.description:
Research Associate – Peptide Chemistry Discovery Platform

Location: Copenhagen, Denmark

Employment type: Full-time

Are you passionate about practical chemistry?

Are you an early-career chemist or laboratory technician with strong hands-on laboratory skills? Would you like to develop your expertise in peptide chemistry, automation and modern analytical techniques while contributing directly to innovative drug-discovery programmes?

We are looking for a motivated and detail-oriented Research Associate to join a Platform Chemistry team in Copenhagen.

This is a laboratory-based position for someone who enjoys experimental work, operating advanced equipment and producing reliable, high-quality results. You will work with automated synthesis workflows, generate linear and macrocyclic peptide libraries, and use modern purification and analytical technologies to support the discovery of potential future medicines.

Direct experience with peptide chemistry is an advantage, but it is not essential. Candidates with a strong practical chemistry background and a genuine interest in learning peptide chemistry are encouraged to apply.

About the organisation

You will join an innovative and growing biotechnology organisation developing a new generation of orally available macrocycle therapeutics.

The organisation combines artificial intelligence, automated chemistry, high-throughput experimentation and real-compound data to design molecules capable of addressing challenging biological targets. Its ambition is to develop oral alternatives to medicines that are traditionally administered by injection, particularly within inflammation and immune-driven diseases.

The Copenhagen research site includes a modern laboratory environment and an experienced multidisciplinary team of chemists, scientists and technology specialists.

About the role

As a Research Associate in Platform Chemistry, you will help deliver the experimental chemistry that drives the organisation’s drug-discovery platform.

You will work alongside experienced peptide chemists and scientists to execute automated synthesis workflows, produce compound libraries and evaluate experimental results. You will also operate, optimise and troubleshoot laboratory equipment such as peptide synthesisers, liquid-handling systems and LC-MS instruments.

The role offers an excellent opportunity to build specialised knowledge in peptide and macrocycle chemistry. You will receive training in automated synthesis, purification, analysis and platform operation while contributing directly to active discovery programmes.

This position is particularly well suited to someone who enjoys spending time in the laboratory, takes pride in accurate experimental work and is motivated by learning new techniques and technologies.

Your responsibilities

As part of the Platform Chemistry team, you will:

• Execute automated workflows for the synthesis of linear and macrocyclic peptide libraries.

• Operate peptide synthesisers, liquid-handling systems, purification equipment and LC-MS instruments.

• Prepare reagents, samples and laboratory materials for experimental workflows.

• Monitor experimental performance and identify deviations or technical issues.

• Optimise and troubleshoot automated laboratory methods and instrumentation.

• Purify and analyse compounds using modern chromatographic and analytical techniques.

• Interpret experimental and analytical data accurately.

• Document methods, observations, results and deviations in a clear and structured way.

• Communicate findings to colleagues across Platform Chemistry and drug-discovery teams.

• Support the delivery of high-quality compounds for research programmes.

• Contribute to the continuous improvement of laboratory workflows.

• Help maintain reliable and efficient day-to-day platform operations.

• Work according to relevant laboratory, quality and safety procedures.

Your background

You may hold one of the following qualifications:

• A bachelor’s or master’s degree in chemistry, chemical engineering or a related scientific field.

• A laboratory technician or laboratory technologist qualification.

• Another relevant scientific qualification combined with strong practical laboratory experience.

Your skills and experience

We are looking for someone who has:

• Strong practical laboratory skills.

• Experience with common synthetic chemistry, purification or analytical techniques.

• Experience operating laboratory equipment and instrumentation.

• Familiarity with equipment such as automated synthesisers, liquid handlers, HPLC, UPLC or LC-MS systems.

• A structured and careful approach to experimental work.

• A strong understanding of the importance of reproducibility and data quality.

• The ability to follow established methods while recognising opportunities for improvement.

• Confidence working independently with laboratory procedures after appropriate training.

• Good written and verbal communication skills.

• The ability to collaborate effectively in a multidisciplinary scientific team.

Experience with peptide chemistry, solid-phase peptide synthesis or macrocycle chemistry is desirable, but not required.

Your personal qualities

You are likely to succeed in this role if you:

• Genuinely enjoy practical laboratory work.

• Are curious and motivated to learn new chemistry, instrumentation and software.

• Take ownership of the quality of your experimental results.

• Pay close attention to detail.

• Approach technical problems in a structured and patient way.

• Are comfortable working with both routine workflows and experimental optimisation.

• Communicate unexpected results or technical issues openly.

• Enjoy working in a collaborative and fast-developing environment.

• Are adaptable and comfortable learning new technologies.

• Want your laboratory work to contribute directly to meaningful scientific progress.

What you can expect

This opportunity offers:

• A hands-on role in an innovative biotechnology environment.

• Training in peptide synthesis, macrocycle chemistry, purification and analysis.

• Experience with advanced automation and high-throughput laboratory technologies.

• The opportunity to become an expert user of a sophisticated discovery platform.

• Direct involvement in active drug-discovery programmes.

• Close collaboration with experienced scientists and peptide chemists.

• A modern laboratory environment in Copenhagen.

• Significant opportunities for technical and professional development.

• The chance to contribute to technologies designed to improve how future medicines are developed and delivered.

Why this role matters

The molecules designed by a drug-discovery platform only become valuable when they can be produced, analysed and tested reliably.

Your work will help transform digital molecular designs into real compounds. By delivering accurate, reproducible experimental chemistry, you will provide scientists with the materials and data they need to identify promising therapeutic candidates.

In this role, your contribution will be practical, visible and directly connected to the wider discovery pipeline.

Application

Please submit your application or contact Black Swans Exist to express your interest or learn more about the position and recruitment process.

Applications will be reviewed continuously.

Black Swans Exist

jobs.occupation: Team Lead & Field Service Engineer, EMEA
jobs.description:
Introduction

We are looking for an ambitious and talented Team Lead & Field Service Engineer based in Ballerup, Denmark. The ideal candidate has a minimum of 10 years of experience in servicing and maintaining scientific, analytical, biomedical, or laboratory equipment.

About the Role

The Team Lead for the 1st Level Service and Support Team plays a critical role in leading and developing the regional Field Service Engineering and Technical Support function across Europe. The role combines people leadership, hands-on technical support, and customer-facing field activities, working closely with the team to ensure a high level of customer satisfaction and operational excellence.

With a strong focus on customer experience, the Team Lead works in close collaboration with the Application Science Manager for the region and Regional Account Managers to ensure seamless service delivery, proactive customer engagement, and successful resolution of technical challenges.

In this position, you should expect approximately 50% travel. Travel within Europe will typically involve up to two overnight stays per trip, while overseas travel may involve longer stays. We expect 80 to 100 overnight travel days per year.

About Us

Sophion Bioscience is a leading global life science company founded in 2000 by a group of passionate electrophysiologists with the aim of making patch clamping objective and independent of user skill.

We specialize in developing and manufacturing automated patch clamp and cell line solutions. Through our comprehensive technical, biological, and application support, we help our partners advance ion channel research and drug discovery. We take the voodoo out of patch clamping, enabling faster, more accurate, and objective results for our users.

Through the continued development of our QPatch, Qube 384 and Ethica M platforms, we offer uncompromised data quality in a user-friendly environment, from assay setup to advanced data analysis.

We are headquartered in Denmark and have subsidiaries in the United States, Japan, and China.

What You'll Do

Team Leadership

• Supervision: Oversee the daily operations of the 1st Level Service Team, ensuring efficient workflows and adherence to service standards.

• Motivation: Foster a positive team environment, encouraging collaboration and professional development among team members.

• Performance Management: Conduct regular performance evaluations, provide constructive feedback, and set goals for team members.

Technical Expertise

• On-Site Service: Actively participate in on-site installations, service visits, and breakdown support activities, demonstrating technical expertise and leadership.

• Remote Support: Actively participate in remote support sessions with customers related to installations, system maintenance, and breakdown support.

Customer Interaction

• Customer Relations: Act as the primary point of contact for key customers, addressing concerns and building strong relationships.

• Feedback Collection: Gather customer feedback during service visits to identify areas for improvement and enhance customer satisfaction.

Coordination and Communication

• Escalation Management: Act as a liaison between the 1st Level Team and 2nd Level Support, ensuring effective communication and timely escalation of unresolved issues.

• Best Practices: Identify and implement best practices to improve service delivery and operational efficiency across the team.

Who You Are

You are an experienced service professional with a passion for customer success, technical excellence, and team leadership. You thrive in a hands-on environment where no two days are the same and enjoy balancing strategic leadership responsibilities with direct customer engagement.

We imagine that you:

• Have a minimum of 10 years of experience servicing and maintaining scientific, analytical, biomedical, or laboratory equipment.

• Have previous experience leading, mentoring, or coordinating technical service teams.

• Possess strong troubleshooting and diagnostic skills across hardware, software, and integrated instrument systems.

• Are highly customer-focused and motivated by delivering exceptional service experiences.

• Communicate effectively with customers, colleagues, and stakeholders at all levels of an organization.

• Have the ability to remain calm and solution-oriented in high-pressure situations.

• Enjoy working independently while also collaborating closely with cross-functional teams.

• Are organized, proactive, and capable of managing multiple priorities simultaneously.

• Are willing and able to travel extensively throughout Europe and occasionally overseas (approximately 80 to 100 overnight travel days per year).

• Are fluent in English; additional European languages are considered an advantage.

How to Apply

Please apply via LinkedIn.

If you have questions about the role, you are welcome to contact the hiring manager, the General Manager & Commercial Director, EMEA & RoW.

Questions

Please submit your questions through the LinkedIn application process (or to your internal recruiting contact, if applicable).

Start Date

As soon as possible.

We review applications on an ongoing basis and close the recruitment process once we have found the right candidate. If this opportunity excites you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

jobs.occupation: Software Manager – Life Science Instrument Software | Copenhagen/Ballerup, Denmark
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Software Manager to lead a team of software engineers building software for automated life science instruments. This role is for a leader with clarity, drive and curiosity — someone who can help people grow, make delivery more predictable, and shape how we use AI in everyday development. You may already be an experienced manager, or ready for your next leadership step; what matters most is your ability to create direction, build trust, and turn ambition into progress.

About the role

You lead a team of eight software engineers (frontend, backend and DevOps), report to the VP of R&D, and join the R&D management team. You own the software roadmap together with Product Management and hold budget responsibility for the function. The role is based in Ballerup, in the Copenhagen area.

Day to day you work closely with Product Management, System Engineering, Hardware, Bioscience, Quality and Technical Support. A lot of the work happens in the room rather than in documents: quick alignment at a desk, a shared look at test data, and a decision taken the same afternoon. That closeness is what makes our pace possible, and protecting the energy and team spirit that comes with it is part of your job.

What matters most to us

• Execution and structure. You know software development best practice and can turn priorities into a clear and structured plan the team understands and believes in.

• Leadership. You lead eight engineers with care and structure - performance conversations, motivation, team building - and you enjoy helping people grow.

• AI ambition. You want to change how a software team works with AI. Hands-on experience is welcome; genuine ambition and curiosity matter just as much.

What you'll do

You lead the software work from roadmap to release and set the tone for how the team collaborates:

• Own the software roadmap and release planning together with Product Management, balancing scientific priorities and business goals.

• Set the technical direction and the quality standards that keep our software robust and maintainable.

• Keep delivery predictable with clear scope, realistic timelines and visible progress.

• Lead the team day to day - hiring, onboarding, mentoring, feedback and career development.

• Shape how we use AI in software development, and share what works with the rest of the company.

• Manage the software budget and resources.

Your background

You do not need to match every point below, but we would like to hear from you if you bring a strong software foundation, leadership drive and the ambition to keep learning:

• Software engineering, computer science or similar background — either through education or equivalent practical experience.

• Solid software development experience - ideally with instruments, hardware-related or other complex product software.

• Experience guiding and mentoring engineers — formally or informally — and a strong ambition to grow into a broader leadership role over time.

• Curiosity about AI and modern ways of working, with the ambition to help the team improve how software is built and deployed.

• Fluent English.

About us

Since 2000 Sophion Bioscience has pioneered Automated Patch Clamping for ion channel research. Today, we specialize in automated solutions for pre-clinical life sciences.

We work closely with academic institutions, contract research organizations, and leading biotech and pharmaceutical companies to create effective assays for screening and characterization. Our solutions empower the study of drug targets and candidates at the bench, reducing development time in discovery and reducing risk in clinical trials.

Through the continued development of our Automated Patch Clamp portfolio (QPatch & Qube) and our new Organ On a Chip platform (Ethica), we offer uncompromised data quality in a user-friendly environment, from assay setup to advanced data analysis. We are headquartered in Denmark and have subsidiaries in the United States, Japan and China.

What we offer

• Real ownership, short decision paths, and visible impact across the company.

• A collaborative, international R&D environment with flexibility in how and when you work.

• Room to shape both the technology and the way the team works, including our use of AI.

• Close interaction with colleagues across R&D - scientists, hardware engineers, product managers - and an informal tone where people help each other out.

• The energy of a scaleup: fast decisions, visible results, and a product portfolio that is still taking shape.

• A team that enjoys working together, celebrates releases, and takes team spirit seriously.

We are committed to an inclusive workplace and welcome applicants of all genders and backgrounds. If you are unsure whether you tick every box, please apply anyway - we would rather have the conversation.

How to apply

Apply via LinkedIn. If you have questions about the role, you are welcome to contact the hiring manager (VP R&D).

Start date: as soon as possible. We review applications on an ongoing basis and close the process once we have found the right match.

Do you have a strong eye for design, and do you enjoy turning creative ideas into tangible experiences?

In collaboration with Actief Hartmanns, Axlab is looking for a Graphic Designer & Event Coordinator who wants to play a key role in shaping and strengthening our visual identity.

This is a newly created position where you will have the opportunity to make a real impact. You will be responsible for developing visual content across digital, print, and event channels while helping bring the Axlab brand to life through trade shows, conferences, and other customer-facing activities. Essential to this role are a proven track record and interest in design execution.

You will join a dynamic Marcom team that is responsible for building Axlab into the most recognized brand for bringing innovation and automation to pathology laboratories.

The role is primarily focused on graphic design, which will account for approximately 70% of your time. The remaining 30% will involve coordinating and supporting events in close collaboration with colleagues and external partners.

The role

The Graphic Designer & Event Coordinator is responsible for leading creative direction, executing graphic design, and ensuring the quality of all visual assets across digital, print, and event media. The role will bring Axlab’s graphic design capability fully in-house for the first time, owning the brand’s visual identity, building scalable asset libraries, and co-creating with external agencies where needed. Alongside design, this person works closely with the Events & Digital Platforms Manager on delivering standout experiences at trade shows, conferences, and hosted events. This role will also spend up to 30% of the time on event coordination, so there must be an interest in working on event execution.

Your responsibilities:

Graphic Design

• Contribute to creative strategy and visual concepts.

• Apply the CVI and ensure consistent brand evolution and strategy while adapting visuals to meet campaign objectives and country differences, where needed.

• Design creative assets for campaigns, events, and country requests across digital and print channels.

• Design based on knowledge of customer segmentation, journey mapping, and value proposition frameworks.

• Work with agencies, the CMO, and the Director, Marcom to evolve the brand and marketing materials, as needed.

• Create asset libraries to support scalability and efficiency.

• Maintain updated files across our systems.

• Use relevant AI and digital design tools to improve creativity, efficiency, and workflows.

Event Coordination

• Planning & logistics: managing the end-to-end event timeline from brief to debrief, coordinating booth/space bookings, A/V, catering, and floor logistics. For trade shows specifically: managing exhibit builds, shipping, and setup/teardown.

• Vendor & supplier management: sourcing and briefing vendors (printers, fabricators, AV, promotional items), negotiating contracts, and holding suppliers accountable for timelines and budgets.

• Budget tracking: tracking spending against actuals, reconciling invoices post-event.

• Marketing & materials coordination: create and deliver event assets on time (signage, collateral, giveaways, digital screens, presentations).

• Stakeholder coordination: Work with Events & Digital Platforms Manager on aligning internal teams (sales, product, marcom) on event goals, speaker/demo needs, and who's attending from the company.

• Post-event reporting: capturing leads, attendance metrics, and ROI data; documenting lessons learned for next time.

The primary working language for this role is English, but Danish is a plus. The candidate should expect to travel up to 30% during certain periods.

What we are looking for

We are looking for a creative and proactive designer who enjoys turning ideas into clear and engaging visual communication.

• A bachelor’s degree or higher in Graphic Design, Visual Communication, or another relevant design field

• 3-5 years of graphic design experience (healthcare industry or other regulated industry, or marketing agency experience preferred)

• Design Expertise: Strong understanding of composition, color, hierarchy, and design best practices, along with a portfolio showcasing diverse projects across digital and print formats.

• Technical Proficiency: Mastery of Adobe InDesign, Illustrator, and Photoshop. Experience with AI design tools is a plus.

• Brand Stewardship: Proven ability to apply and assist in the evolution of a Corporate Visual Identity, maintaining consistency across a wide range of asset types while allowing for project-level creative flexibility.

• Commercial & Business Mindset: Understanding of marketing goals, customer value propositions, and how visual design supports pipeline, brand awareness, and commercial objectives.

• Openness to Event Execution (required): Genuine interest in spending up to 30% of the time on event coordination, including hands-on execution, occasional travel, and learning new processes and tools on the job.

A role with both creativity and impact

This is an opportunity to make a visible impact. You will be the first dedicated graphic design resource in-house and will therefore have considerable influence over how we develop and manage our visual identity.

You will combine creative freedom with ownership and structure, working across various projects and collaborating with colleagues, suppliers, and agencies.

The role also offers the opportunity to develop your skills beyond traditional graphic design, particularly within event execution, project coordination, digital tools, and AI-supported creative workflows.

We are Playdead, an independent game company based in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. We have made two critically acclaimed titles, LIMBO and INSIDE. Our current project is a 3rd-person science fiction adventure set in a remote corner of the universe.

We are seeking an experienced Level Architect with strong artistic skills to join our team in Copenhagen. As our process is very visually driven, we expect layout artists to have a strong eye for visual composition and broad experience in the creation of 3D environments.

Your responsibility as our new colleague will be in designing, blocking out, and in some cases modeling locations for a third-person, open-world game. jobs.occupation: Backend Developer, Data Collection and Infrastructure
jobs.description:
What we are building

Someone researching a purchase might start in ChatGPT, compare options in Perplexity, run a Google search, then go back to an AI assistant to decide. The companies being compared have little idea where they show up in that chain or what gets said about them, and very few can measure it today.

We build the infrastructure that measures it. Every platform we track changes under us, and none of them offers a feed, so we collect the data ourselves. The collection is the hard part, and it is most of this job. Three products run on it:

• AccuRanker is the rank tracking and SEO analytics platform. Rankings, competitor movement, keyword research, dashboards, forecasting.

• AccuLLM tracks brand visibility inside ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overview, and AI Mode.

• AccuSERP is a search data API we sell to other companies in the industry.

On a normal day that means 27 billion rows inserted, 85 million web requests collected, 80 million background jobs run, and 64 million analytical queries served. Eight people build and run all of it.

What you will work on

• The collection and ingestion pipeline behind those numbers, together with the engineers who run it today.

• Add coverage for new search surfaces as they appear, and fix the ones we already cover when they change shape.

• Write and tune queries against very large time series data, across columnar and relational stores.

• Start with scoped changes to existing services, and grow into owning services yourself, from design through deployment to how they behave in production.

What you bring

Must have:

• Solid programming fundamentals. You write clear code and can reason about what it costs at runtime.

• Code of yours running somewhere real. A production system at work, a service you host yourself, or a side project with actual users.

• Comfort in Linux. You can read logs, follow a request through a system, and find out why something is slow.

• Ownership. You take a problem, decide how to attack it, ask when you are stuck, and follow through.

Good to have:

• Distributed systems fundamentals. Queues, workers, backpressure, etc.

• Python and its common frameworks (Django, Celery, pandas/polars). Our stack runs mostly on Python, but it is not a must if the fundamentals are strong.

• ClickHouse or another columnar store.

• The network layer. Connection lifecycle, timeouts and retries, TLS, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.

• Web scraping or browser automation.

• AI agents. Tool and context design, structured output and evals.

• Kafka.

All of it can be learned here.

Who does well here

People who set a high standard for their own work, and who care about performance, reliability, cost, and operational simplicity.

You want to own a feature end to end, from idea to production. The problems we hand you will be scoped at first, and less so over time, and a month after something ships, you are still the one who cares about it.

You move fast when speed is what the problem needs, and you know when stability, safety and maintainability matter more.

This field moves fast right now. We expect you to read, try things, and form your own view of what is worth using, without waiting to be told what is new.

The job is wide. In one week you might tune a database, debug a proxy network, and design an agent.

This role is not for you if you want a narrow technical scope or a large team around you. We are small, the problems change, and you will get real responsibility earlier than most places give it. The senior engineers sit next to you, and asking them is part of the job.

AI at AccuRanker

AI is a big part of the product and of how we build it. AccuLLM sends queries to LLMs all day, customers use our MCP server, and agents and tool design are real engineering problems here.

Being effective with coding agents is becoming a core engineering skill, and it is part of this job. You should be good at giving agents the right context, breaking work into pieces they can execute well, reviewing what they produce, and knowing when to take over yourself. The bar is more high-quality engineering done without outsourcing your understanding and judgment, which is a different thing from using AI a lot.

How we work

• You own services, not tickets. You decide how to solve the problem, make the tradeoffs, and deploy it yourself.

• We ship many times a day. A change can go from idea to production the same day.

• We argue about designs, in writing and in the room. Correctness, cost, and latency are worth arguing about out loud.

• We share what we know and help each other own unfamiliar parts of the system.

What we offer

• Salary set individually on skills and experience.

• Pension, health insurance, flexible working hours, and paid parental leave.

• Hardware of your choosing.

• Office in central Aarhus on Åboulevarden, top floors, panoramic views over the city. The role is on-site, with hybrid options planned for later this year.

• Great lunch.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note to pet@accuranker.com, in Danish or English. A link to something you have built counts for a lot.

We review applications as they come in and hire as soon as we find the right person, so send yours when it is ready.

Questions about the role are welcome. Call our CTO, Peter Emil Tybirk, on +45 61 41 77 41.

At Körber Supply Chain DK, we design and deliver advanced automated material handling solutions to customers worldwide. As our business continues to grow across Europe and North America, we are strengthening our capabilities within machine safety and compliance and are looking for an experienced Senior Safety & Compliance Engineer.

This newly established position offers significant influence across the organization. You will become our internal subject matter expert within machine safety and compliance, ensuring that safety requirements are effectively integrated into projects and business processes.

Your Role:

As Senior Safety & Compliance Engineer, you will be responsible for driving machine safety and compliance activities throughout the project lifecycle, from concept and design to commissioning and customer acceptance.

You will work closely with Engineering, Project Management, Commissioning, Service teams, customers, and external stakeholders to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and industry standards.

Key responsibilities include:

•    Conducting risk assessments and hazard analyses

•    Developing safety concepts and Safety Requirement Specifications (SRS)

•    Supporting design reviews, FATs, SATs, commissioning, and customer acceptance

•    Ensuring compliance with European and international standards

•    Driving continuous improvement initiatives within machine safety and compliance

•    Acting as the go-to expert for safety-related questions across the organization

The position includes approximately 15-20 travel days per year, primarily related to customer meetings, project activities, factory and site acceptance testing, and commissioning support.

Professional Competencies

We expect you to have solid experience within:

•    CE marking and conformity assessment of machinery and automated systems

•    Risk assessments according to EN ISO 12100

•    Functional safety according to EN ISO 13849 and IEC 62061

•    Development of Safety Requirement Specifications (SRS)

•    Validation and verification of safety-related control systems

•    Safety PLC solutions and safety architectures

•    Technical documentation, declarations of conformity, and technical files

•    Machine safety for automation, robotics, and material handling equipment

•    Machinery lifecycle compliance requirements

Experience with TÜV Functional Safety Engineer, TÜV Machinery Safety Expert, CMSE, or similar certifications is considered an advantage.

Knowledge of the EU Machinery Regulation (EU 2023/1230), IEC 62443, and related machine safety or automation certifications is highly valued. As an increasing number of our projects are delivered to North America, experience with U.S. regulations and standards is highly desirable, including OSHA requirements, NFPA 79, ANSI B11 standards, UL standards and certified components, North American approval, documentation, and customer acceptance processes. Experience working with Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) is also an advantage.

Your Profile

You hold a degree in Engineering, Automation, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field, combined with at least 5-10 years of experience within machine safety, functional safety, or compliance engineering.

You combine strong technical expertise with the credibility and confidence to influence decisions across a complex project organization. You are comfortable challenging solutions when safety requirements are at stake and thrive in a role where you can take ownership, drive initiatives, and lead through expertise.

You are proactive, analytical, and self-driven, with strong communication skills and the ability to build trust across all levels of the organization. Most importantly, you understand how to balance compliance requirements with practical business needs while maintaining a strong customer focus.

jobs.occupation: Senior Specialist, Retail Operations - Sales Floor Excellence
jobs.description:
Do you combine extensive hands-on store experience with the ability to lead complex global initiatives? Are you skilled at turning strategic priorities and operational challenges into practical solutions that work in stores? Then, keep on reading!

About the Role

As Senior Specialist, Retail Operations - Sales Floor Excellence, you will shape global operating principles, standards, and solutions that improve store productivity, operational consistency, and customer experience across Pandora’s retail network. You will lead complex, cross-functional workstreams from initial problem definition through implementation and adoption. Operating with a high degree of autonomy, you will structure ambiguous operational topics, establish the recommended approach, and bring together stakeholders across functions and markets to drive solutions forward. You will make recommendations within your area of responsibility and retain ownership of the operational assessment and direction.

Your Key Responsibiltiies will include:

• Shape and continuously improve global Sales Floor operating principles, standards, frameworks, and ways of working.

• Translate strategic priorities, store needs, and operational insights into practical, scalable solutions that improve productivity, consistency, and customer experience.

• Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, or redesign Sales Floor activities, balancing global consistency with relevant cluster, market, and store requirements.

• Lead complex, cross-functional operational initiatives from problem definition through implementation, adoption, and follow-up.

• Independently structure ambiguous topics by defining the scope, priorities, stakeholders, governance, and recommended approach.

• Anticipate risks, dependencies, implementation challenges, and operational trade-offs, driving mitigation actions and escalating decisions with broader strategic, financial, or organizational implications.

• Define the operational approach, tools, guidance, and communications required to embed new standards and ways of working successfully across stores.

• Assess adoption and performance using operational data, reporting, store feedback, and cross-market learnings.

• Identify root causes and improvement opportunities, translate insights into clear recommendations, and drive follow-up actions that strengthen execution and long-term sustainability.

• Define relevant success measures and shape reporting requirements to ensure insights are useful, actionable, and aligned with operational needs.

• Act as the primary operational partner for assigned programs, building alignment across Global Labor, Global Retail Training, Global Inventory Process & Control Excellence, Global Strategy, clusters, markets, and other relevant stakeholders.

• Influence decisions and constructively challenge proposals based on store realities, operational requirements, and available evidence.

• Represent Sales Floor Excellence in relevant forums and working groups, ensuring solutions remain practical and executable at store level.

What is needed to succeed

Experience

• Minimum 3 years of hands-on experience in store operations, store leadership, or field management roles, with a strong understanding of day-to-day retail operations, customer experience, and sales floor execution.

• Minimum 1 year of experience partnering with regional, corporate, or global stakeholders in a retail environment to drive operational initiatives, business priorities, or process improvements.

• Proven experience leading cross-functional initiatives involving multiple stakeholder groups and functions.

• Experience translating operational challenges and business priorities into practical, scalable solutions that improve store execution.

• Experience managing initiatives from problem identification through implementation, adoption, and follow-up.

• Experience working in a complex, international, or multi-market retail organization is strongly preferred.

Skills

• Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to drive alignment without direct authority.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate operational insights and performance data into actionable recommendations.

• Ability to navigate ambiguity, define a recommended approach, and drive progress where solutions are not yet fully established.

• Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to engage effectively with both frontline teams and senior stakeholders.

• Ability to balance strategic thinking with practical execution and operational realities.

Did we get your attention?

We hope you got all your questions answered and feel confident applying for this position. If you see yourself in the role and would like to become a part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply! We are an international team, so please make sure to send us your application in English to be considered. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

Icing on the cake

You will be working out of our Head Office in Copenhagen V. Besides our beautiful interior design, we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

About Pandora

Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

jobs.occupation: Senior Manager Global Rewards - Exec. Rem.
jobs.description:
We are looking for an analytical profile with in-depth Rewards experience to join our Global Rewards & People Analytics team.

About the team

Our team brings together expertise across Global Rewards, Mobility, People Analytics, People Technology & Data, and Danish Payroll & Benefits.

In Rewards, we are responsible for the design, governance and continuous development of our global reward programmes and frameworks. You will be a key partner to the Senior Director Global Rewards & People Analytics on Executive Rewards, supporting analyses, market insights, presentations, remuneration governance and the development of future reward solutions.

“We are an ambitious and engaged team focused on developing solutions that are relevant, engaging and aligned with business needs, while ensuring successful implementation across the organisation”, says Wandunia Pontoppidan, Senior Director, Global Rewards.

The job

You will build a strong network across the organisation and work closely with colleagues across functions and countries from specialists to people partners and senior leaders.

In preparation for our Remuneration Committee meetings, you will partner closely with Senior Director, Global Rewards & People Analytics on executive remuneration and the ongoing evolution of our variable pay programmes. You will analyse current practices, assess market trends and alternative approaches, and develop recommendations that help ensure our reward programmes remain competitive, effective and aligned with our strategic priorities.

In close collaboration with Reward colleagues, people partners and business leaders, you will be responsible for:

•    Supporting Remuneration Committee activities, including benchmarking, analytics, presentation materials and recommendations related to executive remuneration.

•    Supporting annual Executive Leadership Team reward reviews and reporting activities.

•    Reviewing and designing short and long-term incentive programmes, including implementation planning and change communications.

•    Partnering with leaders and people partners on position evaluations and salary recommendations for new hires and promotions at ‘Director’ level and above.

jobs.occupation: Senior Backend Developer, Product and Data
jobs.description:
What we are building

Someone researching a purchase might start in ChatGPT, compare options in Perplexity, run a Google search, then go back to an AI assistant to decide. The companies being compared have little idea where they show up in that chain or what gets said about them, and very few can measure it today.

We build the infrastructure that measures it. Every platform we track changes under us, and none of them offers a feed, so we collect the data ourselves. Three products run on it:

• AccuRanker is the rank tracking and SEO analytics platform. Rankings, competitor movement, keyword research, dashboards, forecasting.

• AccuLLM tracks brand visibility inside ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overview, and AI Mode.

• AccuSERP is a search data API we sell to other companies in the industry. On a normal day that means 27 billion rows inserted, 85 million web requests collected, 80 million background jobs run, and 64 million analytical queries served. Eight people build and run all of it.

This job is on the product side: the backend, the data models, and the query paths that run on top of what we collect.

What you will work on

• Build features across AccuRanker and AccuLLM: Django APIs, background jobs, and the data models behind them.

• Design ClickHouse schemas and query paths, and keep the 64 million daily analytical queries fast as the data grows.

• Work across Postgres and ClickHouse, and decide what lives where.

• Own services end to end, from design through deployment to how they behave in production.

• Take features into the React frontend if you want to. Fullstack is welcome, not required.

What you bring

Must have:

• Python and a major web framework (we run Django and Celery), or equivalent depth in another stack.

• Database and API design. Schemas, indexes, migrations, and APIs that hold up under load.

• Comfort in Linux and close to production. Debugging incidents, understanding system behavior, improving observability, making services more reliable.

• Ownership and initiative. You take a problem, you decide how to solve it, and you follow through.

Good to have:

• React and TypeScript, for the optional frontend part of the job.

• ClickHouse or another columnar store at scale.

• Kafka.

• AI agents in production. Tool and context design, structured output and evals.

• Data infrastructure at scale. The ingestion, storage, and query-performance problems our numbers imply.

Who does well here

People who set a high standard for their own work, and who care about performance, reliability, cost, and operational simplicity.

You own a feature end to end, from idea to production. You can make progress while the problem is still half defined, and a month after it ships, you are still the one who cares about it.

You move fast when speed is what the problem needs, and you know when stability, safety, and maintainability matter more.

This field moves fast right now. We expect you to read, try things, and form your own view of what is worth using, without waiting to be told what is new.

The job is wide. In one week you might tune a query, ship a customer-facing feature, and design an agent.

This role is not for you if you want a roadmap handed to you, a narrow technical scope, or a large team around you. We are small, the problems change, and you will often be the person deciding both what to build and what “done” means.

AI at AccuRanker

AI is a big part of the product and of how we build it. AccuLLM sends queries to LLMs all day, customers use our MCP server, and agents and tool design are real engineering problems here.

Being effective with coding agents is becoming a core engineering skill, and it is part of this job. You should be good at giving agents the right context, breaking work into pieces they can execute well, reviewing what they produce, and knowing when to take over yourself. The bar is more high-quality engineering done without outsourcing your understanding and judgment, which is a different thing from using AI a lot.

How we work

• You own services, not tickets. You decide how to solve the problem, make the tradeoffs, and deploy it yourself.

• We ship many times a day. A change can go from idea to production the same day.

• We argue about designs, in writing and in the room. Correctness, cost, and latency are worth arguing about out loud.

• We share what we know and help each other own unfamiliar parts of the system.

What we offer

• Salary set individually on skills and experience.

• Pension, health insurance, flexible working hours, and paid parental leave.

• Hardware of your choosing.

• Office in central Aarhus on Åboulevarden, top floors, panoramic views over the city. The role is on-site, with hybrid options planned for later this year.

• Great lunch.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note to pet@accuranker.com, in Danish or English.

We review applications as they come in and hire as soon as we find the right person, so send yours when it is ready.

Questions about the role are welcome. Call our CTO, Peter Emil Tybirk, on +45 61 41 77 41.

About us:

Founded in Copenhagen, Denmark, in 2014, Templafy’s success is built by our 60+ employee nationalities found at offices around the world. We believe that when people feel valued, heard, and empowered, they perform at their best—creating a win for all. Our unique product and dedication to innovation and excellence have raised over $200 million in funding from top investors like Insight Venture Partners, Seed Capital, Dawn Capital, Damgaard Company and Golub Capital.

About the role and company:

I'm using AI to write the job posting, and I asked Codex to use the Slack connector to collect some "cultural proof points" about what it's like working at Templafy. This is what it came up with:

Templafy engineering culture comes across as pragmatic, product-close, technically opinionated, and unusually open about trade-offs.

· Engineers are expected to think like product builders, not just implementers. Threads often connect technical work to customer demos, pilots, product quality, adoption, and user feedback

· Pragmatism is a real value. There’s repeated language around simple/explicit code, logical PR chunks, avoiding feature creep, solving the 80% case first, building MVPs, and getting something testable into users’ hands quickly

· Quality matters, but in a practical way. Tests, E2E coverage, evals, pipeline health, flaky tests, feature-flag cleanup, and technical health all show up as shared concerns

· Engineers are candid and trusted to challenge scope. I saw people questioning whether work should be bugs vs feature requests, whether backlog items are clutter, when to pause work, and when a “quick fix” is acceptable

· Cross-functional collaboration is very present. PMs, design, solutions, support, security, platform, and product engineering are all in the same threads negotiating quality bars, customer urgency, UX, risk, and ownership

· AI/tooling curiosity is strong, but not naive. The AI guild and engineering channels show people experimenting with code review agents, AGENTS.md, evals, Codex/Claude workflows, guardrails, and agentic SDLC, while also worrying about learning, friction, false positives, security, and long-term maintainability

· There’s a bias toward async feedback and shared learning. Moving sprint review-style updates into short videos and Slack feedback is a good culture signal: fewer meetings, more continuous visibility

· Ownership is distributed. People jump in to unblock, sanity-check, investigate, create PRs, clean up flags, or hand over work when someone is away. The tone is informal but accountable

Small caution: I would avoid selling the culture as “perfectly polished.” The honest version is stronger: Templafy looks like a place where engineers have real agency, real product context, and real technical messes to improve.

The rest of this job posting is probably more like what you'd expect.

What You’ll Do

In Product Engineering, you will help build and improve product experiences used by Templafy customers. You will work with product managers, designers, and other engineers to understand customer problems, shape solutions, and deliver features from idea through production.

You will:

• 
Build, improve, and maintain customer-facing product features

• 
Collaborate with Product and Design to turn ambiguous problems into usable solutions

• 
Use AI-assisted development tools thoughtfully as part of your everyday engineering workflow

• 
Make technical decisions within your area and contribute to broader architecture discussions

• 
Write reliable, maintainable code that fits existing patterns and systems

• 
Use tests and fast feedback loops to support confident delivery

• 
Build early versions of ideas to evaluate real behavior instead of debating hypotheticals

• 
Help simplify product paths, remove complexity, and make features easier to test and maintain

• 
Debug issues, improve performance, and support production systems

• 
Help the team balance delivery speed, technical quality, and customer impact

• 
Contribute to engineering practices, code reviews, and technical discussions

What We’re Looking For

We’re looking for someone who enjoys product context and wants to be part of shaping what gets built, not only how it gets built.

You probably have:

• 
Strong experience building production software in a product engineering team

• 
Experience using AI-assisted engineering tools in real development work

• 
The judgment to use AI tools without outsourcing your understanding of the system

• 
Good technical judgment and the ability to make pragmatic trade-offs

• 
Experience with modern web application development

• 
A solid understanding of software design, testing, and maintainability

• 
Comfort working across frontend, backend, or full-stack

• 
Strong communication skills, especially in async and cross-functional settings

• 
A bias toward making discussions concrete through prototypes, tests, and working software

• 
A sense of ownership over outcomes, not just assigned tasks

• 
The ability to challenge scope constructively and keep work focused

Nice To Have

• 
Experience with SaaS or B2B software

• 
Experience with cloud platforms, CI/CD, observability, distributed systems

• 
Experience building AI-enabled products, agentic workflows, evals, or prompt/tooling systems

• 
Interest in improving developer experience, technical health, and team practices

What You’ll Join

You’ll join a product engineering team that cares about building useful software, learning quickly, and keeping the systems healthy enough that we can keep moving. We value people who can ask good questions, make things simpler, and help the team find the right trade-off when there is no perfect answer.

This is a good role for someone who wants meaningful product ownership, close collaboration with non-engineering colleagues, and enough technical complexity to make simplification genuinely valuable. We are looking for someone who can move fast, but who also knows that the fastest teams are usually the ones that keep their systems understandable.

Backend: C# / .NET, ASP.NET Core, Entity Framework Core, SQL Server

Frontend: TypeScript, React, HTML/CSS/SCSS

AI: LLM integration & agentic AI (tool-calling, multi-agent)
